modules.title: The bracket of adjoint families
modules.doc:
Families of symbols with one adjoint index, valued in an arbitrary algebra, and their bracket.

## i. Overview

A gauge field in an algebra `B` of local expressions is a family of symbols `A^φ`, indexed by a
dual vector `φ` of the gauge algebra, that is a linear map
`Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B`. Such an adjoint family is assembled into a field in
`B ⊗ G.lieSubalgebra` by `dualPairEquiv`, so that its adjoint index can be contracted with the
Lie bracket. This gives the bracket of two families, `bracketFam`, the physicists'
`f^a_{bc} f^b g^c`, and the derived commutators `commutatorFam`, the Leibniz convolutions
`∂_s ⁅A_μ, A_ν⁆` of the derivative symbols.

Nothing here assumes that `B` is commutative, and no gauge action is part of the data. The
gauge action enters only in `repGauge_bracketFam`, for an action by multiplicative maps. The field
strength and the covariant derivative in the adjoint are built from these formulas in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GaugeBoson.AdjointFamily.CovariantDeriv`.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeBoson.dualPairEquiv`, `GaugeBoson.tensorBracket` : the tensor bookkeeping of the
  adjoint index.
- `GaugeBoson.bracketFam` : the bracket of two adjoint families.
- `GaugeBoson.commutatorFam` : the derived commutators `∂_s ⁅A_μ, A_ν⁆`.
- `GaugeBoson.repGauge_bracketFam` : the gauge transformation of a bracket of two families with
  affine transformation laws.
- `GaugeBoson.bracketFam_adjointDualCoeff` : the bracket against the dual adjoint Taylor
  coefficients of a jet.
- `GaugeBoson.massWeightEigenspace`, `GaugeBoson.anticommuteSubmodule` : the submodules through
  which the mass weights and the statistics of covariant towers are checked term by term.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Pure-tensor computations for `dualPairEquiv` and `tensorBracket`
- B. The bracket of general component families
- C. Antisymmetry and order of the derived commutators
- D. The gauge transformation of a bracket
- E. Iterated Leibniz expansions
- F. The bracket of families against the adjoint coefficients
- G. Mass-weight eigenspaces and anticommutants

## iv. References

* None.

## C. Antisymmetry and order of the derived commutators

The bracket of two families is antisymmetric as soon as the values of the two families
commute, and every derived commutator is a polynomial in symbols of no higher order.

## G. Mass-weight eigenspaces and anticommutants

A covariant tower is a sum of products of symbols, so its mass weight and its statistics
can be checked term by term once each property is a submodule. The weight-`w` eigenspace of
an algebra map `P : B →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial B` and the elements anticommuting with a fixed one
are both submodules, and the bracket of two families lands in any submodule containing the
products of their components.

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.dualPairEquiv
declarations.doc:
The canonical equivalence, through finite-dimensional duality, between
algebra-valued fields `B ⊗ G.lieSubalgebra` and their component families `φ ↦ A^φ`, the element
`b ⊗ a` corresponds to the family `φ ↦ φ(a) b`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def dualPairEquiv :
    (B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.tensorBracket
declarations.doc:
The bracket of two algebra-valued fields, multiplication in `B` on the first
factors, the Lie bracket of the gauge algebra on the second, so that on pure
tensors `⁅b₁ ⊗ a₁, b₂ ⊗ a₂⁆ = (b₁ b₂) ⊗ ⁅a₁, a₂⁆`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorBracket :
    (B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) →ₗ[ℝ] (B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) →ₗ[ℝ] B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commutator
declarations.doc:
The commutator term `⁅A_μ, A_ν⁆` of the field strength, as a component family. It is
the physicists' `f^a_{bc} A_μ^b A_ν^c` contracted with a dual adjoint vector, without a
basis. The two fields are assembled into `B ⊗ G.lieSubalgebra` by `dualPairEquiv.symm`,
bracketed there by `tensorBracket`, and read back out as components.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def commutator
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.dualPairEquiv_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquiv_tmul (b : B) (a : G.lieSubalgebra) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    dualPairEquiv (b ⊗ₜ[ℝ] a) φ = φ a • b

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.tensorBracket_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorBracket_tmul (b₁ b₂ : B) (a₁ a₂ : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    tensorBracket (b₁ ⊗ₜ[ℝ] a₁) (b₂ ⊗ₜ[ℝ] a₂) = (b₁ * b₂) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] ⁅a₁, a₂⁆

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.dualPairEquiv_map_left
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquiv_map_left (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B) (t : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    dualPairEquiv ((TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) t) φ = Φ (dualPairEquiv t φ)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.dualPairEquiv_map_right
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquiv_map_right (T : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra)
    (t : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    dualPairEquiv ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id T) t) φ =
      dualPairEquiv t (T.dualMap φ)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.symm_comp_left
declarations.statement:
lemma symm_comp_left (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B) (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    dualPairEquiv.symm (Φ ∘ₗ f) =
      (TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) (dualPairEquiv.symm f)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.symm_comp_right
declarations.statement:
lemma symm_comp_right (T : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra)
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    dualPairEquiv.symm (f ∘ₗ T.dualMap) =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id T) (dualPairEquiv.symm f)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.tensorBracket_map_left
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorBracket_map_left (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂) (s t : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) :
    tensorBracket ((TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) s)
        ((TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) t) =
      (TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) (tensorBracket s t)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.tensorBracket_one_right
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorBracket_one_right (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (s : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) :
    tensorBracket s ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] c) =
      -(TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra c)) s

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.tensorBracket_one_left
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorBracket_one_left (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (t : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) :
    tensorBracket ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] c) t =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra c)) t

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.dualPairEquiv_one_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquiv_one_tmul (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    dualPairEquiv ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] c) φ = algebraMap ℂ B (φ c)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam
declarations.doc:
The bracket of two arbitrary component families, generalizing `commutator` (which
is the case of two field symbols). The families are assembled into `B ⊗ G.lieSubalgebra`
by `dualPairEquiv.symm`, bracketed by `tensorBracket`, and read back out as components.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bracketFam (f g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commutator_eq_bracketFam
declarations.statement:
lemma commutator_eq_bracketFam
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : commutator A μ ν = bracketFam (A 0 μ) (A 0 ν)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commutatorFam
declarations.doc:
The derived commutator family, the `s`-derivative of the commutator term, given
by the Leibniz convolution of the derivative symbols over the multiset antidiagonal.
With the derivative symbols as primitives this convolution is the definition. For
`s = 0` it is the commutator itself (`commutatorFam_zero`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def commutatorFam
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commutatorFam_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma commutatorFam_zero
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : commutatorFam A μ ν 0 = commutator A μ ν

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_add_left
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_add_left (f₁ f₂ g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam (f₁ + f₂) g = bracketFam f₁ g + bracketFam f₂ g

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_add_right
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_add_right (f g₁ g₂ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam f (g₁ + g₂) = bracketFam f g₁ + bracketFam f g₂

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_smul_left
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_smul_left (c : ℝ) (f g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam (c • f) g = c • bracketFam f g

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_smul_right
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_smul_right (c : ℝ) (f g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam f (c • g) = c • bracketFam f g

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_apply_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The bracket of two component families expanded through a basis of the gauge
algebra, the physicists' `f^a_{bc} f^b g^c`, with `φ⁅e_j, e_k⁆` the structure
constants contracted with the dual vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_apply_eq_sum (f g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    bracketFam f g φ = ∑ j, ∑ k,
      φ ⁅Module.Free.chooseBasis ℝ G.lieSubalgebra j,
          Module.Free.chooseBasis ℝ G.lieSubalgebra k⁆ •
        (f ((Module.Free.chooseBasis ℝ G.lieSubalgebra).coord j) *
          g ((Module.Free.chooseBasis ℝ G.lieSubalgebra).coord k))

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_apply_eq_zero_of_map_lie
declarations.doc:
A dual vector vanishing on every bracket of the gauge algebra, such as the coordinate of an
abelian factor, vanishes on the bracket of any two families. Every structure constant
`φ⁅e_j, e_k⁆` it sees is zero.

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_map
declarations.doc:
The bracket of families is natural in the algebra. A multiplicative linear map carries
the bracket of two families to the bracket of their images.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_map {B' : Type} [Ring B'] [Module ℝ B'] [SMulCommClass ℝ B' B']
    [IsScalarTower ℝ B' B'] (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B') (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂)
    (f g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam (Φ ∘ₗ f) (Φ ∘ₗ g) = Φ ∘ₗ bracketFam f g

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commutatorFam_map
declarations.doc: The derived commutator family is natural in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma commutatorFam_map {B' : Type} [Ring B'] [Module ℝ B'] [SMulCommClass ℝ B' B']
    [IsScalarTower ℝ B' B'] (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B') (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    commutatorFam (fun p ρ => Φ ∘ₗ A p ρ) μ ν s = Φ ∘ₗ commutatorFam A μ ν s

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.tensorBracket_map_left_derivation
declarations.doc:
`tensorBracket` is a derivation in the algebra factor. For `Δ` satisfying the
Leibniz rule on `B`, applying `Δ ⊗ id` to a bracket distributes over the two
arguments.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorBracket_map_left_derivation (Δ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (hΔ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Δ (b₁ * b₂) = Δ b₁ * b₂ + b₁ * Δ b₂) (s t : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (TensorProduct.map Δ LinearMap.id) (tensorBracket s t) =
      tensorBracket ((TensorProduct.map Δ LinearMap.id) s) t +
      tensorBracket s ((TensorProduct.map Δ LinearMap.id) t)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_derivation
declarations.doc:
The bracket of families under a derivation of the algebra, the Leibniz rule, in
family form.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_derivation (Δ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (hΔ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Δ (b₁ * b₂) = Δ b₁ * b₂ + b₁ * Δ b₂)
      (f g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    Δ ∘ₗ bracketFam f g = bracketFam (Δ ∘ₗ f) g + bracketFam f (Δ ∘ₗ g)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_swap_of_commute
declarations.doc:
The bracket of two component families with commuting values is antisymmetric. In
the basis expansion the structure constants are antisymmetric in the two gauge
indices, and the two field factors of each term may be exchanged.

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commutatorFam_swap
declarations.doc:
The derived commutator term is antisymmetric in its two directions when the symbols
of the gauge field commute. Swapping the two parts of the antidiagonal matches the
Leibniz convolution with the swapped one termwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma commutatorFam_swap
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (hA : ∀ (s s' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ μ' : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (ψ ψ' : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), Commute (A s μ ψ) (A s' μ' ψ'))
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    commutatorFam A ν μ s = - commutatorFam A μ ν s

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_neg_right
declarations.doc: The bracket of families is odd in its second argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_neg_right (f g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam f (-g) = - bracketFam f g

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commutatorFam_mem
declarations.doc:
Every derived commutator term is a polynomial in derivative symbols of order at
most that of the derivative. Each Leibniz splitting contributes a product of two
lower-order symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma commutatorFam_mem
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (s' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (ν lam : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    commutatorFam A ν lam s' φ ∈
      Algebra.adjoin ℂ {b : B | ∃ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
        (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), p.card ≤ s'.card ∧ b = A p μ φ}

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.map_dualPairEquiv_symm_of_affine
declarations.doc:
An affine transformation law of a family, read on the field it assembles. If `Φ` sends
each component `f ψ` to `f' ψ + ψ(c)·1`, then `Φ ⊗ id` sends the field of `f` to the field of
`f'` plus `1 ⊗ c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_dualPairEquiv_symm_of_affine (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    {f f' : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B} {c : G.lieSubalgebra}
    (hf : ∀ ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra, Φ (f ψ) = f' ψ + algebraMap ℂ B (ψ c)) :
    (TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) (dualPairEquiv.symm f) =
      dualPairEquiv.symm f' + (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] c

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.tensorBracket_add_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
The bracket of two fields shifted by constant fields `1 ⊗ c_f` and `1 ⊗ c_g`. It is the
bracket of the unshifted fields, two `ad` cross terms, and the constant bracket.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorBracket_add_one_tmul (s t : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) (cf cg : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    tensorBracket (s + (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] cf) (t + (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] cg) =
      tensorBracket s t
      + (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra cf)) t
      - (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra cg)) s
      + (1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] ⁅cf, cg⁆

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.repGauge_bracketFam
declarations.doc:
The gauge transformation of the bracket of two component families with affine
transformation laws `f ↦ f' + φ(c_f)·1` and `g ↦ g' + φ(c_g)·1` is the bracket of the
transformed families, two `ad` cross terms, and the constant bracket `⁅c_f, c_g⁆`.
Pure bilinearity, with `tensorBracket_add_one_tmul` computing the cross terms. Only the
multiplicativity of the action of `U` is used.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_bracketFam
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (hmul : ∀ b₁ b₂ : B, repGauge U (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge U b₁ * repGauge U b₂)
    {f g f' g' : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B}
    {cf cg : G.lieSubalgebra}
    (hf : ∀ ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra,
      repGauge U (f ψ) = f' ψ + algebraMap ℂ B (ψ cf))
    (hg : ∀ ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra,
      repGauge U (g ψ) = g' ψ + algebraMap ℂ B (ψ cg))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    repGauge U (bracketFam f g φ) =
      bracketFam f' g' φ
      + g' (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra cf)
      - f' (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra cg)
      + algebraMap ℂ B (φ ⁅cf, cg⁆)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_zero_left
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_zero_left (g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam 0 g = 0

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_zero_right
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_zero_right (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam f 0 = 0

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_sum_left
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_sum_left (S : Multiset (Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B))
    (g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam S.sum g = (S.map fun f => bracketFam f g).sum

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_sum_right
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_sum_right (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (S : Multiset (Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)) :
    bracketFam f S.sum = (S.map fun g => bracketFam f g).sum

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_finset_sum_left
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_finset_sum_left {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι)
    (f : ι → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam (∑ i ∈ S, f i) g = ∑ i ∈ S, bracketFam (f i) g

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_finset_sum_right
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_finset_sum_right {ι : Type*} (S : Finset ι)
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (g : ι → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    bracketFam f (∑ i ∈ S, g i) = ∑ i ∈ S, bracketFam f (g i)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.tensorBracket_map_right_antidiagonal
declarations.doc:
`tensorBracket` under an antidiagonal family of transports on the Lie factor. If `T x`
distributes over the bracket as the antidiagonal convolution of the
`T m`, so does `id ⊗ T x` over `tensorBracket`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorBracket_map_right_antidiagonal
    (T : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (hT : ∀ a b : G.lieSubalgebra, T x ⁅a, b⁆ =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p => ⁅T p.1 a, T p.2 b⁆).sum)
    (s t : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      tensorBracket ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (T p.1)) s)
        ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (T p.2)) t)).sum =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (T x)) (tensorBracket s t)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_adjointDualCoeff
declarations.doc:
The bracket of families against an iterated dual adjoint coefficient is the
antidiagonal convolution of the brackets against the coefficients of the two factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFam_adjointDualCoeff (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (f g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    bracketFam f g (G.adjointDualCoeff U x φ) =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        bracketFam (f ∘ₗ G.adjointDualCoeff U p.1)
          (g ∘ₗ G.adjointDualCoeff U p.2) φ).sum

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFam_apply_mem_submodule
declarations.doc:
The bracket pairing of two adjoint families lands in any submodule containing the
products of their components. It is the sum of the structure constants against them.

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.massWeightEigenspace
declarations.doc:
The weight-`w` part of `B` for a mass-weight algebra map `P`, the elements on which `P`
is the monomial `X ^ w`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightEigenspace (P : B →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial B) (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.mem_massWeightEigenspace_iff
declarations.doc: Membership of the weight-`w` part is the eigenvector equation itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightEigenspace_iff {P : B →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial B} {w : ℕ} {b : B} :
    b ∈ massWeightEigenspace P w ↔ P b = Polynomial.monomial w b

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.mul_mem_massWeightEigenspace
declarations.doc:
The mass weight is additive on products. `P` is an algebra map and monomials multiply by
adding their degrees.

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.anticommuteSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The elements of `B` anticommuting with a fixed element. It is a submodule, which is what
lets the anticommutation of a tower be checked term by term.
declarations.statement: def anticommuteSubmodule (x : B) : Submodule ℂ B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.mem_anticommuteSubmodule_iff
declarations.doc: Membership of the anticommutant is the anticommutation relation itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_anticommuteSubmodule_iff {x y : B} :
    y ∈ anticommuteSubmodule x ↔ x * y = -(y * x)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.anticomm_symm
declarations.doc: Anticommutation is symmetric in its two arguments.
declarations.statement: lemma anticomm_symm {a b : B} (hab : a * b = -(b * a)) : b * a = -(a * b)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.mul_mem_anticommuteSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Multiplying an anticommuting element on the left by a commuting one keeps it
anticommuting.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_mem_anticommuteSubmodule {x a b : B} (ha : Commute x a)
    (hb : b ∈ anticommuteSubmodule x) : a * b ∈ anticommuteSubmodule x

modules.title: The classification of gauge invariants of a gauge field
modules.doc:
A gauge-invariant polynomial in the symbols of a gauge field, and in further generators fixed
by the pure jets, is a polynomial in the covariant derivatives of the field strength and those
generators.

## i. Overview

Let `A` be a family of gauge-field symbols in an algebra `B` that transforms as a gauge field
under a multiplicative action of the jet gauge group, and whose symbols commute with each
other. The classification `invariant_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength` says that a gauge-invariant
element of the subalgebra generated by the symbols and a set `S` of elements fixed by the pure
jets lies in the subalgebra generated by the covariant derivatives of the field strength and
`S`. The elements of `S` need only commute with the symbols. No algebraic independence of
the symbols is assumed, and nothing about the rest of `B`.

By the generation theorem the symbols may be traded for the symmetrized derivatives and the
covariant field-strength tower. Pure jets fix the tower and act on the symmetrized derivatives
by translations, and every translation is realized by a pure jet, since the pure jets are free
coordinates. The ring-theoretic extraction principle `mem_of_translationInvariant` then strips
the symmetrized symbols order by order, by a Vandermonde argument.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeBoson.exists_translation_of_support` : every top-order translation is realized by a
  pure jet.
- `GaugeBoson.mem_of_translationInvariant` : the ring-theoretic extraction principle.
- `GaugeBoson.invariant_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength` : the classification of invariants.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Translations by pure jets
- B. Translation invariance in a ring
- C. The classification of invariants
  - C.1. The order-`m` subalgebra
  - C.2. The top-order coordinates and their translations
  - C.3. The descent
  - C.4. The classification

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Translations by pure jets

Every family of shifts supported at a single order is realized by a pure jet trivial below that
order. The gauge action of a jet is also recorded here as a ring endomorphism.

## B. Translation invariance in a ring

The extraction principle behind the classification is pure ring theory: if a family of ring
endomorphisms fixes a subalgebra `R` pointwise and translates finitely many central
elements `y i` by arbitrary prescribable scalars, then an element of the subalgebra
generated by `R` and the `y i` that is invariant under the whole family lies in `R`. The
proof chooses any polynomial representation and kills its top coefficient by evaluating the
invariance at enough shifts.

## C. The classification of invariants

The goal is the classification theorem: a gauge-invariant element of the subalgebra
generated by the gauge-field symbols together with a set `S` of elements fixed by the pure
jets lies in the subalgebra generated by the covariant field-strength tower together with
`S`, assuming only that the gauge-field symbols are central (bosonic), with no
algebraic-independence hypothesis.

The strategy, by downward induction on the top symmetrized order `m + 1` present in `x`:

* By the generation theorem, `x` is a polynomial in the symmetrized symbols of order at most
  `m + 1`, the covariant tower, and `S`.
* By freeness of the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data, there are pure jets whose data are
  supported at exactly order `m + 1`. Triangularity places them in the deep truncation
  kernel `truncationKer m`, so they fix every generator of order at most `m`, the covariant
  tower and `S`, and act on the order-`m + 1` symmetrized symbols by pure translations with
  arbitrary prescribable scalars.
* The extraction theorem `mem_of_translationInvariant` then places `x` in the subalgebra of
  order at most `m`.

### C.1. The order-`m` subalgebra

The subalgebra generated by the symmetrized symbols of order at most `m`, the covariant
tower and `S`. It is fixed by the pure jets trivial to order `m`, and its elements commute
with every symmetrized symbol.

### C.2. The top-order coordinates and their translations

The symmetrized symbols of order exactly `m + 1` are indexed, in a basis `bv` of the gauge
algebra, by a multiset of `m + 1` directions and a basis index. A real function `t` on that
index set prescribes a shift family supported at order `m + 1`, hence a pure jet
translating each coordinate by the corresponding value of `t`.
### C.3. The descent
### C.4. The classification

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.exists_translation_of_support
declarations.doc:
Every top-order translation is realized by a pure jet. Any coefficient family supported
at exactly order `N` is the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of a pure jet trivial to order
`N - 1`, by freeness of the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data together with Maurer–Cartan
triangularity.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_translation_of_support (N : ℕ)
    (c : {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0} → G.lieSubalgebra)
      (hcN : ∀ r, r.1.card ≠ N → c r = 0) :
    ∃ U : G.truncationKer 0,
      G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U⁻¹ = c ∧
      ∀ x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), x ≠ 0 → x.card < N →
        G.adjointDualCoeff (U.1)⁻¹ x = 0

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.repGauge_one
declarations.doc: The gauge action fixes the unit, being multiplicative and invertible.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_one (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    repGauge U (1 : B) = 1

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.repGaugeRingHom
declarations.doc:
The gauge action of a jet as a ring endomorphism of the algebra of local
expressions.
declarations.statement: def repGaugeRingHom (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) : B →+* B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commute_of_mem_adjoin
declarations.doc: Commutation with a generating set extends to the generated subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_of_mem_adjoin {X : Set B} {y : B} (hX : ∀ x ∈ X, Commute x y)
    {r : B} (hr : r ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ X) : Commute r y

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commute_symmetrizedDeriv_right
declarations.doc:
Anything commuting with all gauge-field symbols commutes with the symmetrized
symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_symmetrizedDeriv_right {y : B}
    (hy : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra),
      Commute y (A p μ φ))
    (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    Commute y (symmetrizedDeriv r A φ)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commute_symmetrizedDeriv
declarations.doc: For a bosonic gauge field the symmetrized symbols commute with each other.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_symmetrizedDeriv
    (hcomm : ∀ (p q : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (φ ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), Commute (A p μ φ) (A q ν ψ))
    (r r' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ φ' : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    Commute (symmetrizedDeriv r A φ) (symmetrizedDeriv r' A φ')

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.exists_polynomial_rep
declarations.doc:
Any element of the subalgebra generated by a subalgebra `R` and a single element `y`
commuting with `R` is a polynomial in `y` with coefficients in `R`. The subalgebra is the
image of `R[X]` under evaluation at `y`.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_polynomial_rep (R : Subalgebra ℂ B) (y : B) (hy : ∀ r ∈ R, Commute r y)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ R ⊔ Algebra.adjoin ℂ {y}) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (r : ℕ → B), (∀ k, r k ∈ R) ∧ x = ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, r k * y ^ k

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.map_mul_pow_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The binomial expansion of the translate of a single monomial `r * y ^ k` under an
endomorphism fixing `r` and shifting `y` by a real scalar `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_mul_pow_eq_sum (Φ : B →+* B) {r y : B} (hr : Φ r = r) {t : ℝ}
    (hy : Φ y = y + algebraMap ℂ B (t : ℂ)) (k : ℕ) :
    Φ (r * y ^ k) =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (k + 1), t ^ j • ((k.choose j : ℂ) • (r * y ^ (k - j)))

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.map_sum_mul_pow_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The translate of a polynomial `∑ r k * y ^ k` under an endomorphism fixing the
coefficients and shifting `y` by a real scalar `t`, expanded in powers of `t`. The coefficient
of `t ^ j` collects the binomial terms `(k choose j) • r k * y ^ (k - j)` over `j ≤ k`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_sum_mul_pow_eq_sum (Φ : B →+* B) {r : ℕ → B} {y : B} (hr : ∀ k, Φ (r k) = r k)
    {t : ℝ} (hy : Φ y = y + algebraMap ℂ B (t : ℂ)) (n : ℕ) :
    Φ (∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, r k * y ^ k) =
      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, t ^ j • ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n,
        if j ≤ k then (k.choose j : ℂ) • (r k * y ^ (k - j)) else 0

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.sum_range_ite_choose_top
declarations.doc:
The top coefficient of the expansion `map_sum_mul_pow_eq_sum` is the top coefficient of the
polynomial.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_range_ite_choose_top (r : ℕ → B) (y : B) (m : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (m + 2),
      if m + 1 ≤ k then (k.choose (m + 1) : ℂ) • (r k * y ^ (k - (m + 1))) else 0) =
      r (m + 1)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.mem_of_translationInvariant_single
declarations.doc:
The single-variable extraction. An element of `R[y]` invariant under a family of ring
endomorphisms fixing `R` pointwise and translating `y` by arbitrary real scalars lies in
`R`. Invariance forces the top coefficient of any chosen polynomial representation to
vanish, by expanding the translated polynomial in powers of the shift.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_translationInvariant_single (R : Subalgebra ℂ B) (y : B)
    (hy : ∀ r ∈ R, Commute r y) (Φ : ℝ → B →+* B)
    (hΦR : ∀ t : ℝ, ∀ z ∈ R, Φ t z = z)
    (hΦy : ∀ t : ℝ, Φ t y = y + algebraMap ℂ B (t : ℂ))
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ R ⊔ Algebra.adjoin ℂ {y}) (hinv : ∀ t, Φ t x = x) : x ∈ R

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.mem_of_translationInvariant
declarations.doc:
The extraction theorem. If a family of ring endomorphisms fixes a subalgebra `R`
pointwise and translates finitely many commuting elements `y i`, each commuting with
`R`, by arbitrary prescribable scalars, then an element of the subalgebra generated by
`R` and the `y i` that is invariant under the whole family lies in `R`. The variables are
eliminated one at a time by `mem_of_translationInvariant_single`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_translationInvariant {ι : Type} [Fintype ι]
    (R : Subalgebra ℂ B) (y : ι → B)
    (hyR : ∀ i, ∀ r ∈ R, Commute r (y i)) (hyy : ∀ i j, Commute (y i) (y j))
    (Φ : (ι → ℝ) → (B →+* B)) (hΦR : ∀ t, ∀ z ∈ R, Φ t z = z)
    (hΦy : ∀ t i, Φ t (y i) = y i + algebraMap ℂ B (t i))
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ R ⊔ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (Set.range y)) (hinv : ∀ t, Φ t x = x) :
    x ∈ R

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.repGauge_eq_of_mem_adjoin_symSymbolsLE
declarations.doc:
A pure jet trivial to order `m` fixes every generator of order at most `m`, namely the
symmetrized symbols with at most `m` derivatives, the covariant tower and `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_eq_of_mem_adjoin_symSymbolsLE {U : G.truncationKer 0}
    (hU : ∀ x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), x ≠ 0 → x.card ≤ m →
      G.adjointDualCoeff (U.1)⁻¹ x = 0)
    (hUsym : ∀ (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (hr : r ≠ 0), r.card ≤ m →
      G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U⁻¹ ⟨r, hr⟩ = 0)
    {z : B} (hz : z ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symSymbolsLE A m ∪ (tower A ∪ S))) :
    repGauge U.1 z = z

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commute_symmetrizedDeriv_of_mem_adjoin_symSymbolsLE
declarations.doc: Every element of the order-`m` subalgebra commutes with every symmetrized symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_symmetrizedDeriv_of_mem_adjoin_symSymbolsLE
    {z : B} (hz : z ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symSymbolsLE A m ∪ (tower A ∪ S)))
    (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    Commute z (symmetrizedDeriv r A φ)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.topCoord
declarations.doc:
The top-order coordinates, the symmetrized symbols of order `m + 1` in the basis
`bv`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def topCoord : Sym (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m + 1) × ι → B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.shiftFamily
declarations.doc: The shift family supported at order `m + 1` with coordinates `t` in the basis `bv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def shiftFamily (t : Sym (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m + 1) × ι → ℝ) :
    {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0} → G.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.shiftFamily_eq_zero_of_card_ne
declarations.statement:
lemma shiftFamily_eq_zero_of_card_ne (t : Sym (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m + 1) × ι → ℝ)
    (r : {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0}) (hr : r.1.card ≠ m + 1) :
    shiftFamily m bv t r = 0

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.coord_shiftFamily
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_shiftFamily (t : Sym (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m + 1) × ι → ℝ)
    (ps : Sym (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m + 1)) (hp0 : (ps : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) ≠ 0) (j : ι) :
    bv.coord j (shiftFamily m bv t ⟨ps, hp0⟩) = t (ps, j)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.commute_topCoord_of_mem_adjoin_symSymbolsLE
declarations.doc: The top-order coordinates commute with the order-`m` subalgebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_topCoord_of_mem_adjoin_symSymbolsLE (p : Sym (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m + 1) × ι)
    {z : B} (hz : z ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symSymbolsLE A m ∪ (tower A ∪ S))) :
    Commute z (topCoord A m bv p)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.mem_sup_adjoin_range_topCoord
declarations.doc:
An element of the order-`m + 1` subalgebra lies in the sup of the order-`m` subalgebra
and the subalgebra generated by the top-order coordinates.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sup_adjoin_range_topCoord {z : B}
    (hz : z ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symSymbolsLE A (m + 1) ∪ (tower A ∪ S))) :
    z ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symSymbolsLE A m ∪ (tower A ∪ S)) ⊔
      Algebra.adjoin ℂ (Set.range (topCoord A m bv))

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.repGauge_topCoord
declarations.doc:
The pure jet realizing the shift family `t` translates each top-order coordinate by
the corresponding value of `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_topCoord {U : G.truncationKer 0}
    (t : Sym (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m + 1) × ι → ℝ)
    (hU1 : G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U⁻¹ = shiftFamily m bv t)
    (hU2 : ∀ x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), x ≠ 0 → x.card < m + 1 →
      G.adjointDualCoeff (U.1)⁻¹ x = 0)
    (p : Sym (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (m + 1) × ι) :
    repGauge U.1 (topCoord A m bv p) = topCoord A m bv p + algebraMap ℂ B ((t p : ℝ) : ℂ)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.mem_adjoin_symSymbolsLE_of_repGauge_eq
declarations.doc:
The descent. An element of the order-`m + 1` subalgebra fixed by all pure jets lies
in the order-`m` subalgebra. The pure jets realizing the shift families at order
`m + 1` fix the order-`m` subalgebra and translate the top-order coordinates by arbitrary
real scalars, so `mem_of_translationInvariant` applies.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_adjoin_symSymbolsLE_of_repGauge_eq {z : B}
    (hz : z ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symSymbolsLE A (m + 1) ∪ (tower A ∪ S)))
    (hzinv : ∀ U : G.truncationKer 0, repGauge U.1 z = z) :
    z ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symSymbolsLE A m ∪ (tower A ∪ S))

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.invariant_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength
declarations.doc:
The classification of invariants. A gauge-invariant element of the subalgebra
generated by the gauge-field symbols and a set `S` of `truncationKer 0`-fixed
elements is a polynomial in the covariant derivatives of the field strength and the
elements of `S`. Requires only that the gauge-field symbols commute with each other
(the gauge field is bosonic) and with the elements of `S`, nothing about the rest
of `B`, and no independence hypothesis.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariant_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength (S : Set B)
    (hcS : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), ∀ y ∈ S, Commute y (A p μ φ))
    (hS : ∀ y ∈ S, ∀ U : G.truncationKer 0, repGauge U.1 y = y)
    {x : B} (hx : x ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symbols A ∪ S))
    (hinv : ∀ U : G.gaugeJetGroup, repGauge U x = x) :
    x ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (tower A ∪ S)

modules.title: The field strength and the covariant derivative of an adjoint family
modules.doc:
The field strength of a family of gauge-field symbols, the covariant derivative in the
adjoint, and the gauge law of an adjoint gauge tensor.

## i. Overview

Let `A` be a family of gauge-field symbols `∂_s A_μ^φ` in an algebra `B`, indexed by a
derivative multiset `s`, a direction `μ` and a dual vector `φ` of the gauge algebra. Its field
strength is
```
  F_{μν} = ∂_μ A_ν − ∂_ν A_μ + ⁅A_μ, A_ν⁆
```
with `⁅·,·⁆` the gauge-algebra bracket, which carries the physicists' factor of `i` (on the
matrix factors `⁅a, b⁆ = i(ab − ba)`). In terms of the plain matrix commutator this is
`F_{μν} = ∂_μ A_ν − ∂_ν A_μ + i [A_μ, A_ν]`, the sign forced by the convention
`ω_μ(g) = i (∂_μ g) g⁻¹` for the Maurer–Cartan form. With the derivative symbols as primitives
the field strength is itself a family of derivative symbols `s ↦ [∂_s F_μν]`. The derivative
terms shift the multiset index, and the commutator term is the Leibniz convolution
`commutatorFam`.

The covariant derivative of an adjoint family `F` is `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + ⁅A_ρ, F⁆`, and
`iteratedCovDerivAdjoint` iterates it along a list of directions. All of these are formulas in
an arbitrary algebra `B`, natural under multiplicative linear maps (`fieldStrength_map`,
`iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_map`).

A family transforms in the adjoint, `TransformsInAdjoint`, when every derivative symbol
transforms by the Leibniz convolution of the dual adjoint coefficients of the jet, with no
inhomogeneous term. That the field strength and its covariant derivatives transform in the
adjoint is proved in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GaugeBoson.AdjointFamily.GaugeLaw`.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeBoson.fieldStrength` : the field strength of a family of gauge-field symbols.
- `GaugeBoson.covDerivAdjoint`, `GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint` : the covariant derivative
  of an adjoint family and its iterates.
- `GaugeBoson.sum_bracketFam_conv_eq` : the derived bracket against the dual adjoint
  coefficients, regrouped by the exchange of the four-fold splitting.
- `GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_fieldStrength_map` : the covariant field-strength tower
  is natural in the algebra.
- `GaugeBoson.TransformsInAdjoint` : a family transforms in the adjoint.
- `GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_mem_massWeightEigenspace` : the mass weight of an adjoint
  covariant tower.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The field strength
- B. The covariant derivative in the adjoint
- C. Iterated covariant derivatives
- D. Families transforming in the adjoint
- E. Mass weights

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.fieldStrength
declarations.doc:
The field strength `F_μν = ∂_μ A_ν − ∂_ν A_μ + ⁅A_μ, A_ν⁆` of a family of
gauge-field symbols, as a family of derivative symbols. The `s`-th derivative has
the derivative terms through the shifted symbols `A (μ ::ₘ s) ν`, and the commutator
term through the Leibniz convolution `commutatorFam`. This is the physicists'
`F_μν^a = ∂_μ A_ν^a − ∂_ν A_μ^a + f^a_{bc} A_μ^b A_ν^c`. The gauge-algebra bracket
already carries the physicists' factor of `i`, so no explicit factor appears. This is
the normalization of the structural equation of the Maurer–Cartan form, which makes the
field strength transform without inhomogeneous terms
(`TransformsAsGaugeField.repGauge_fieldStrength`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fieldStrength
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.fieldStrength_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_apply
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    fieldStrength A μ ν s φ = A (μ ::ₘ s) ν φ - A (ν ::ₘ s) μ φ + commutatorFam A μ ν s φ

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.fieldStrength_zero
declarations.doc:
The underived field strength, derivative symbols on singletons, plus the plain
commutator.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_zero
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    fieldStrength A μ ν 0 = A {μ} ν - A {ν} μ + commutator A μ ν

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.pair_eq_fieldStrength_sub_commutatorFam
declarations.doc:
The antisymmetrized pair of derivative symbols is the field strength minus its
commutator term.
declarations.statement:
lemma pair_eq_fieldStrength_sub_commutatorFam
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (ν μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    A (ν ::ₘ s) μ - A (μ ::ₘ s) ν = fieldStrength A ν μ s - commutatorFam A ν μ s

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.fieldStrength_swap
declarations.doc:
The field strength is antisymmetric in its two covector indices when the symbols of
the gauge field commute. The two derivative terms swap outright, and the commutator term
swaps by `commutatorFam_swap`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_swap
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (hA : ∀ (s s' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ μ' : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (ψ ψ' : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), Commute (A s μ ψ) (A s' μ' ψ'))
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    fieldStrength A ν μ s = - fieldStrength A μ ν s

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.fieldStrength_map
declarations.doc:
The field strength is natural in the algebra. A multiplicative linear map carries the
field strength of a family to the field strength of its image.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_map {B' : Type} [Ring B'] [Module ℝ B'] [SMulCommClass ℝ B' B']
    [IsScalarTower ℝ B' B'] (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B') (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    fieldStrength (fun p ρ => Φ ∘ₗ A p ρ) μ ν s = Φ ∘ₗ fieldStrength A μ ν s

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFamConv
declarations.doc:
The derived bracket family `⁅A_ρ, F⁆`, the `s`-derivative of the bracket of the
gauge field against a family, given by the Leibniz convolution of the derivative
symbols over the multiset antidiagonal.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bracketFamConv
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.covDerivAdjoint
declarations.doc:
The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + ⁅A_ρ, F⁆` of an adjoint-valued family
of derivative symbols, the extra derivative on the symbol plus the derived bracket
against the gauge field. The gauge-algebra bracket carries the physicists' `i`, so
in matrix terms this is `∂_ρ F + i [A_ρ, F]`, the adjoint-representation covariant
derivative in the same `D = ∂ + i A` convention as the field strength. It preserves
`TransformsInAdjoint` (`TransformsInAdjoint.covDerivAdjoint`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def covDerivAdjoint
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.covDerivAdjoint_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivAdjoint_apply
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    covDerivAdjoint A F ρ s φ = F (ρ ::ₘ s) φ + bracketFamConv A ρ F s φ

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.covDerivAdjoint_apply_of_map_lie
declarations.doc:
At a dual vector vanishing on every bracket the derived bracket term drops out and the
covariant derivative is the ordinary one, `(∇_ρ F)^φ = ∂_ρ F^φ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivAdjoint_apply_of_map_lie {φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra}
    (hφ : ∀ x y : G.lieSubalgebra, φ ⁅x, y⁆ = 0)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivAdjoint A F ρ s φ = F (ρ ::ₘ s) φ

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.bracketFamConv_map
declarations.doc: The derived bracket family is natural in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracketFamConv_map {B' : Type} [Ring B'] [Module ℝ B'] [SMulCommClass ℝ B' B']
    [IsScalarTower ℝ B' B'] (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B') (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    bracketFamConv (fun p σ => Φ ∘ₗ A p σ) ρ (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) s =
      Φ ∘ₗ bracketFamConv A ρ F s

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.covDerivAdjoint_map
declarations.doc: The covariant derivative is natural in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivAdjoint_map {B' : Type} [Ring B'] [Module ℝ B'] [SMulCommClass ℝ B' B']
    [IsScalarTower ℝ B' B'] (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B') (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivAdjoint (fun p σ => Φ ∘ₗ A p σ) (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) ρ s =
      Φ ∘ₗ covDerivAdjoint A F ρ s

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.sum_comp_adjointDualCoeff_apply
declarations.doc:
A sum of families transported by the dual adjoint coefficients of a jet, evaluated at a
dual vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_comp_adjointDualCoeff_apply (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    ((t.antidiagonal.map fun r => F r.2 ∘ₗ G.adjointDualCoeff U r.1).sum) ψ =
      (t.antidiagonal.map fun r => F r.2 (G.adjointDualCoeff U r.1 ψ)).sum

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.sum_bracketFam_conv_eq
declarations.doc:
The derived bracket against the dual adjoint coefficients, regrouped. Bracketing the
families `A` and `F` transported by the dual adjoint coefficients of a jet, summed over all
splittings, gives the antidiagonal convolution of the derived bracket `⁅A_ρ, F⁆` against the
coefficients. This is the exchange of the four-fold splitting.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_bracketFam_conv_eq (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      bracketFam ((p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q => A q.2 ρ ∘ₗ G.adjointDualCoeff U q.1).sum)
        ((p.2.antidiagonal.map fun r => F r.2 ∘ₗ G.adjointDualCoeff U r.1).sum) φ).sum =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => bracketFamConv A ρ F p.2 (G.adjointDualCoeff U p.1 φ)).sum

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint
declarations.doc:
The iterated covariant derivative `𝒟_l F` of an adjoint family of derivative
symbols along a list of directions. Covariant derivatives do not commute (their
commutator is an `ad F` term), so the iteration is order-dependent and indexed by a
list. The result is again a family of derivative symbols, and the underived covariant
tower is its value at the empty multiset.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iteratedCovDerivAdjoint
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) →
      (Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) →
      Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_map
declarations.doc: The iterated covariant derivative is natural in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_map {B' : Type} [Ring B'] [Module ℝ B'] [SMulCommClass ℝ B' B']
    [IsScalarTower ℝ B' B'] (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B') (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra
      →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    iteratedCovDerivAdjoint (fun p σ => Φ ∘ₗ A p σ) l (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) =
      fun p => Φ ∘ₗ iteratedCovDerivAdjoint A l F p

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_neg_fam
declarations.doc: The iterated covariant derivative is odd in the family it differentiates.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_neg_fam
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    ∀ l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
      iteratedCovDerivAdjoint A l (fun t => - F t) = fun t => - iteratedCovDerivAdjoint A l F t

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_fieldStrength_map
declarations.doc:
The covariant tower of the field strength is natural in the algebra. The tower of the
image family is the image of the tower.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_fieldStrength_map {B' : Type} [Ring B'] [Module ℝ B']
    [SMulCommClass ℝ B' B'] [IsScalarTower ℝ B' B'] (Φ : B →ₗ[ℝ] B')
    (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    iteratedCovDerivAdjoint (fun p σ => Φ ∘ₗ A p σ) l
        (fieldStrength (fun p σ => Φ ∘ₗ A p σ) μ ν) 0 φ
      = Φ (iteratedCovDerivAdjoint A l (fieldStrength A μ ν) 0 φ)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_apply_of_map_lie
declarations.doc:
At a dual vector vanishing on every bracket, such as the coordinate of an abelian factor,
the iterated covariant derivative is the ordinary derivative along the multiset of its
directions. No bracket correction survives at any order.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_apply_of_map_lie {φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra}
    (hφ : ∀ x y : G.lieSubalgebra, φ ⁅x, y⁆ = 0)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    iteratedCovDerivAdjoint A l F s φ = F (↑l + s) φ

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_apply_perm_of_map_lie
declarations.doc:
Hence at such a dual vector the covariant derivatives commute. The iterated covariant
derivative depends only on the multiset of its directions.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_apply_perm_of_map_lie {φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra}
    (hφ : ∀ x y : G.lieSubalgebra, φ ⁅x, y⁆ = 0)
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    {l l' : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} (hl : l.Perm l') (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    iteratedCovDerivAdjoint A l F s φ = iteratedCovDerivAdjoint A l' F s φ

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.TransformsInAdjoint
declarations.doc:
A family of derivative symbols `F` transforms in the adjoint (is an adjoint gauge
tensor) for the gauge representation `repGauge` when each symbol `[∂_s F^φ]`
transforms by the Leibniz convolution of the dual adjoint coefficients against lower
symbols. This is the shape of `TransformsAsGaugeField` with no Maurer–Cartan shift. At
`s = 0` it is the homogeneous law `U • F^φ = F^{Ad₀^* φ}`.
declarations.statement:
def TransformsInAdjoint (repGauge : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup B)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) : Prop

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_zero
declarations.doc:
An adjoint gauge tensor transforms at the base point through the dual adjoint
coefficient of the value of the gauge jet alone. The antidiagonal of the empty multiset
has a single term.
declarations.statement:
lemma TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_zero
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B}
    (hF : TransformsInAdjoint G repGauge F) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
      (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    repGauge U (F 0 φ) = F 0 (G.adjointDualCoeff U⁻¹ 0 φ)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_cons
declarations.doc:
If `F` transforms in the adjoint, so do its `κ ::ₘ s`-derived symbols, with the
extra derivative traced through `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_cons`. The result is
the Leibniz splittings where `κ` stays a derivative, minus the convolution where `κ` hits
the adjoint, an `ad` of the derived Maurer–Cartan form.
declarations.statement:
lemma TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_cons
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B}
    (hF : TransformsInAdjoint G repGauge F)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (κ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    repGauge U (F (κ ::ₘ s) φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        F (κ ::ₘ p.2) (G.adjointDualCoeff U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum
      - (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          (p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q =>
            F p.2 (G.adjointDualCoeff U⁻¹ q.2
              (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra (G.evalLie
                (G.iteratedDerivJ q.1
                  (-G.maurerCartan U⁻¹ κ)))))).sum).sum

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_eq_of_mem_truncationKer_zero
declarations.doc:
Anything that transforms in the adjoint is invariant under the pure jets. At `s = 0`
the transformation law is the dual adjoint action of the base-point value `U₀⁻¹ = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_eq_of_mem_truncationKer_zero
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B}
    (hF : TransformsInAdjoint G repGauge F) (U : G.truncationKer 0)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) : repGauge U.1 (F 0 φ) = F 0 φ

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.fieldStrength_mem_massWeightEigenspace
declarations.doc:
The mass weight of the field strength is `4 + 2 * |s|` when each symbol `∂_p A_μ` has
weight `2 * (1 + |p|)`. Each term is two gauge-field symbols, or one with an extra
derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldStrength_mem_massWeightEigenspace
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (P : B →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial B)
    (hA : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra),
      A p μ ψ ∈ massWeightEigenspace P (2 * (1 + Multiset.card p)))
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    fieldStrength A μ ν s φ ∈ massWeightEigenspace P (4 + 2 * Multiset.card s)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_mem_massWeightEigenspace
declarations.doc:
The mass weight of an adjoint covariant tower. If the gauge-field symbols `∂_p A_μ` have
weight `2 * (1 + |p|)` and the family `G` has weight `c + 2 * |t|` at the derivative
multiset `t`, then `𝒟_l G` has weight `c + 2 * |l| + 2 * |s|` at `s`. Each covariant
derivative costs two units, whether it lands on the derivative index or brings down a
gauge-field factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_mem_massWeightEigenspace
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (P : B →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial B)
    (hA : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra),
      A p μ ψ ∈ massWeightEigenspace P (2 * (1 + Multiset.card p)))
    (c : ℕ) (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (hF : ∀ (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (χ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra),
      F t χ ∈ massWeightEigenspace P (c + 2 * Multiset.card t))
    (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    iteratedCovDerivAdjoint A l F s φ ∈
      massWeightEigenspace P (c + 2 * l.length + 2 * Multiset.card s)

modules.title: The gauge law of a gauge field and of its covariant expressions
modules.doc:
A family of gauge-field symbols transforming as a gauge field makes its field strength and the
covariant derivatives of it transform in the adjoint.

## i. Overview

A family `A` of symbols `∂_s A_μ^φ` in an algebra `B` transforms as a gauge field,
`TransformsAsGaugeField`, when a jet `U` acts on `∂_s A_μ^φ` by the Leibniz convolution of the
dual adjoint Taylor coefficients of `U⁻¹` against lower symbols, plus the base-point value of
the `s`-th derivative of the Maurer–Cartan form of `U⁻¹`. This is the law that the symbols of
the gauge-boson jet algebra satisfy (`LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.transformsAsGaugeField_gaugeField`),
and that their images under any algebra map intertwining the gauge actions inherit
(`LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.transformsAsGaugeField_mapGaugeField`). The Lorentz law of such a
family is `LorentzTransformsAsGaugeField`.

From the gauge law and the multiplicativity of the action on `B` alone, this file works out
the action on the expressions built from the symbols. The derived commutators pick up `ad`
cross terms and a constant bracket (`TransformsAsGaugeField.repGauge_commutatorFam`). In the
field strength these cancel against the inhomogeneous terms of the derivative symbols, through
the structural equation of the Maurer–Cartan form, so the field strength transforms in the
adjoint at every derivative order. The covariant derivative preserves the adjoint law
(`TransformsInAdjoint.covDerivAdjoint`), so every covariant derivative of the field strength
transforms in the adjoint. A jet acts on the symmetrized derivatives by the symmetrized
adjoint convolution plus a translation by its symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeBoson.TransformsAsGaugeField` : the gauge law of a family of gauge-field symbols.
- `GaugeBoson.LorentzTransformsAsGaugeField` : the Lorentz law of a family of gauge-field
  symbols.
- `GaugeBoson.TransformsAsGaugeField.repGauge_commutatorFam` : the gauge law of the derived
  commutators.
- `GaugeBoson.TransformsAsGaugeField.transformsInAdjoint_fieldStrength` : the field strength
  transforms in the adjoint.
- `GaugeBoson.TransformsInAdjoint.covDerivAdjoint` : the covariant derivative preserves the
  adjoint law.
- `GaugeBoson.TransformsAsGaugeField.transformsInAdjoint_iteratedCovDerivAdjoint` : every
  covariant derivative of the field strength transforms in the adjoint.
- `GaugeBoson.TransformsAsGaugeField.repGauge_symmetrizedDeriv_translation` : deep pure jets
  act on the symmetrized derivatives by translations.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The gauge and Lorentz laws of a gauge field
- B. The gauge law of the derived commutators
- C. The field strength and its covariant derivatives transform in the adjoint
- D. The gauge action on the symmetrized derivatives

## iv. References

* None.
