## B. The total derivative on the jet algebra
## C. The iterated total derivative
## D. Generation by the gauge fields and their derivatives
## E. The derivative on the complexification

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The derivative of components in the field-derivative space, in the direction `ν`, the
shift `∂_s A_μ^φ ↦ ∂_{s + {ν}} A_μ^φ` of the derivative label, i.e. right multiplication
by the degree-one symbol `∂_ν` on the `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ` factor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (FieldDerivSpace G) →ₗ[ℝ] (FieldDerivSpace G)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_tmul (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ (GaugeBoson G)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) ν (a ⊗ₜ[ℝ] φ)
      = (a * SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.basisMultiset
          ({ν} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] φ

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_comm
declarations.doc:
Total derivatives commute on the component space. The derivative labels live in a
symmetric algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ((FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) μ).comp ((FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) ν)
      = ((FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) ν).comp ((FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) μ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The formal total spacetime derivative on the gauge-boson jet algebra in the direction
`ν`, the derivation extending the shift `∂_s A_μ^φ ↦ ∂_{s + {ν}} A_μ^φ` of the component
functions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetDeriv (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₗ[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetDeriv_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_ι (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)) :
    (jetDeriv G) ν (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ x)
      = SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ ((GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) ν x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetDeriv_one
declarations.statement: lemma jetDeriv_one (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : (jetDeriv G) ν (1 : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetDeriv_algebraMap
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_algebraMap (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (r : ℝ) :
    (jetDeriv G) ν (algebraMap ℝ (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) r) = 0

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetDeriv_mul
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule, as the total derivative is a derivation.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_mul (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (jetDeriv G) ν (x * y) = (jetDeriv G) ν x * y + x * (jetDeriv G) ν y

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetDeriv_comm_apply
declarations.doc: Mixed partials agree on the jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_comm_apply (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (jetDeriv G) μ ((jetDeriv G) ν x) = (jetDeriv G) ν ((jetDeriv G) μ x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetDeriv_comm
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ((jetDeriv G) μ).comp ((jetDeriv G) ν) = ((jetDeriv G) ν).comp ((jetDeriv G) μ)

instance : RightCommutative
    (fun (D : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₗ[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) =>
      D.comp ((jetDeriv G) μ))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The iterated total derivative `∂_s` along a multiset `s` of directions, well defined
because the directional derivatives commute.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iteratedJetDeriv (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₗ[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedJetDeriv_zero :
    (iteratedJetDeriv G) (0 : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.foldl_comp_eq
declarations.doc: Any initial map factors out of the fold defining the iterated derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma foldl_comp_eq (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∀ D : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₗ[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G),
      s.foldl (fun D μ => D.comp ((jetDeriv G) μ)) D = D ∘ₗ (iteratedJetDeriv G) s

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedJetDeriv_cons (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    (iteratedJetDeriv G) (μ ::ₘ s) = (jetDeriv G) μ ∘ₗ (iteratedJetDeriv G) s

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedJetDeriv_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (iteratedJetDeriv G) ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = (jetDeriv G) μ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv_add
declarations.doc: Differentiating along `s + t` is differentiating along `t` and then along `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedJetDeriv_add (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    (iteratedJetDeriv G) (s + t) = (iteratedJetDeriv G) t ∘ₗ (iteratedJetDeriv G) s

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv_cons'
declarations.doc:
The companion of `iteratedJetDeriv_cons`, peeling the new derivative on the inside.
The derivatives commute, so the extra direction may equally be applied first.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedJetDeriv_cons' (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    (iteratedJetDeriv G) (μ ::ₘ s) = (iteratedJetDeriv G) s ∘ₗ (jetDeriv G) μ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv_ι
declarations.doc:
On a component function the iterated derivative writes the derivative symbol `∂_s`
into the derivative label.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedJetDeriv_ι (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ (GaugeBoson G)) :
    (iteratedJetDeriv G) s (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ (a ⊗ₜ[ℝ] φ))
      = SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _
          ((a * SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.basisMultiset s) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] φ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv_ofA
declarations.doc:
The derivative generator `∂_s A_μ^φ` is the iterated derivative of the gauge-field
component function.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedJetDeriv_ofA (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (iteratedJetDeriv G) s ((ofA G) μ φ)
      = SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _
          (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.basisMultiset s ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
            (GaugeBoson.componentDual G) (Lorentz.CoVector.basis.dualBasis μ) φ)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.adjoin_iteratedJetDeriv_eq_top
declarations.doc:
The jet algebra is generated by the gauge fields and their derivatives. Every
element is a polynomial in the derivative generators `∂_s A_μ^φ` — nothing else is
available to write down for the gauge sector of a Lagrangian.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoin_iteratedJetDeriv_eq_top :
    Algebra.adjoin ℝ
      (⋃ s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), ⋃ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3,
        Set.range (fun φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra => (iteratedJetDeriv G) s ((ofA G) μ φ)))
      = (⊤ : Subalgebra ℝ (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexJetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The formal total derivative on the complexified gauge-boson jet algebra, by base
change. This is the derivative the ambient Lagrangian theory uses.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def complexJetDeriv (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexJetDeriv_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma complexJetDeriv_tmul (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (z : ℂ) (x : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (complexJetDeriv G) ν (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] x) = z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (jetDeriv G) ν x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexJetDeriv_mul
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule on the complexification.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexJetDeriv_mul (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (complexJetDeriv G) ν (x * y)
      = (complexJetDeriv G) ν x * y + x * (complexJetDeriv G) ν y

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexJetDeriv_comm
declarations.doc: The complexified total derivatives commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexJetDeriv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ((complexJetDeriv G) μ).comp ((complexJetDeriv G) ν)
      = ((complexJetDeriv G) ν).comp ((complexJetDeriv G) μ)

modules.title: The Lorentz action on the gauge-boson jet algebra
modules.doc:
The action of `SL(2,ℂ)` on the gauge-boson jet algebra, for which the total derivative is a
Lorentz vector.

## i. Overview

The Lorentz group acts on the jet algebra of the gauge bosons by the symmetric-algebra
functor applied to its action on the field-derivative space. The derivative labels transform
in `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ` and the target index contragrediently through the covector action on
`GaugeBoson`. The formal total derivative is a Lorentz vector for this action. On the
complexification this is packaged as a `Lorentz.IsLorentzDeriv` instance.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup` : the Lorentz action on the component
  space.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup` : the Lorentz action on the jet algebra.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_jetDeriv` : the total derivative is a Lorentz vector.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup` : the action on the complexification.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.instIsLorentzDeriv` : the `Lorentz.IsLorentzDeriv` instance.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lorentz action on the component space
  - A.1. Covariance of the derivative shift
- B. The Lorentz action on the jet algebra
- C. Lorentz covariance of the total derivative
- D. The complexified action
- E. The Lorentz law of the gauge-field generators

## iv. References

* None.

### A.1. Covariance of the derivative shift
## B. The Lorentz action on the jet algebra
## C. Lorentz covariance of the total derivative
## D. The complexified action
## E. The Lorentz law of the gauge-field generators

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the field-derivative space of the gauge bosons. The derivative
label transforms in `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ` and the target index contragrediently.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup :
    Representation ℝ SL(2,ℂ) (FieldDerivSpace G)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.repLorentzGroup_basis_singleton
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the singleton derivative symbol. The derivative slot transforms
by the columns of the Lorentz matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.repLorentzGroup_basis_singleton
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.repLorentzGroup Λ
        (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.basisMultiset ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))) =
      ∑ a, ((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ) •
        SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.basisMultiset ({a} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The derivative shift is a Lorentz vector on the component space. Appending `∂_μ`
and then acting is acting and then appending the transformed `∂_μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_jetDeriv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (v : (FieldDerivSpace G)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup G) Λ ((FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) μ v) =
      ∑ a, ((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ) •
        (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) a ((FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup G) Λ v)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the gauge-boson jet algebra, the symmetric-algebra functor
applied to the Lorentz action on the field-derivative space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzGroup : Representation ℝ SL(2,ℂ) (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (repLorentzGroup G) Λ x =
      SymmetricAlgebra.map ((GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup G) Λ) x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_apply_one
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_one (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    (repLorentzGroup G) Λ (1 : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) = 1

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_apply_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (repLorentzGroup G) Λ (x * y) = (repLorentzGroup G) Λ x * (repLorentzGroup G) Λ y

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ι (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)) :
    (repLorentzGroup G) Λ (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ v) =
      SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ ((GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup G) Λ v)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_jetDeriv
declarations.doc: The total derivative on the gauge-boson jet algebra is a Lorentz vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_jetDeriv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (repLorentzGroup G) Λ ((jetDeriv G) μ x) =
      ∑ a, ((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ) •
        (jetDeriv G) a ((repLorentzGroup G) Λ x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup
declarations.doc: The Lorentz action on the complexified gauge-boson jet algebra, by base change.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def complexRepLorentzGroup :
    Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma complexRepLorentzGroup_tmul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (z : ℂ) (x : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (complexRepLorentzGroup G) Λ (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] x) = z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (repLorentzGroup G) Λ x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroupAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The action of a Lorentz transformation on the complexified gauge-boson jet algebra, as
an algebra endomorphism, the base change of the symmetric-algebra functor applied to the
action on the field-derivative space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def complexRepLorentzGroupAlgHom (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₐ[ℂ] ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma complexRepLorentzGroup_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (complexRepLorentzGroup G) Λ x = complexRepLorentzGroupAlgHom G Λ x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup_apply_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma complexRepLorentzGroup_apply_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (complexRepLorentzGroup G) Λ (x * y)
      = (complexRepLorentzGroup G) Λ x * (complexRepLorentzGroup G) Λ y

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup_jetDeriv
declarations.doc: The complexified total derivative is a Lorentz vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexRepLorentzGroup_jetDeriv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (complexRepLorentzGroup G) Λ ((complexJetDeriv G) μ x) =
      ∑ a, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        (complexJetDeriv G) a ((complexRepLorentzGroup G) Λ x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.instIsLorentzDeriv
declarations.doc:
The complexified total derivatives form a Lorentz derivative, a family of derivatives
transforming as a Lorentz vector.
declarations.statement:
instance instIsLorentzDeriv :
    Lorentz.IsLorentzDeriv (complexRepLorentzGroup G) (complexJetDeriv G)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.repLorentzGroup_dual_componentDual
declarations.doc:
The contragredient Lorentz action passes through a component covector to its spacetime
slot. The adjoint index is Lorentz-inert.
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.GaugeBoson.repLorentzGroup_dual_componentDual (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (ω : Module.Dual ℝ Lorentz.CoVector) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (GaugeBoson.repLorentzGroup G).dual Λ ((GaugeBoson.componentDual G) ω φ)
      = (GaugeBoson.componentDual G) (Lorentz.CoVector.sl2Rep.dual Λ ω) φ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_ofA
declarations.doc:
The gauge field is a Lorentz covector. The generator `A_μ^φ` mixes into the `A_a^φ`
by the columns of the Lorentz matrix, with the adjoint index untouched.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ofA (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (repLorentzGroup G) Λ ((ofA G) μ φ)
      = ∑ a, ((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ) • (ofA G) a φ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup_one_tmul_ofA
declarations.doc: The Lorentz law of the gauge-field generators on the complexification.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexRepLorentzGroup_one_tmul_ofA (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (complexRepLorentzGroup G) Λ ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (ofA G) μ φ)
      = ∑ a, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (ofA G) a φ)

modules.title: Mass dimension on the gauge-boson jet algebra
modules.doc:
The scaling of the gauge-boson jet algebra by mass weight.

## i. Overview

The mass dimension of the gauge bosons is tracked multiplicatively through the
*mass-weight scaling*, the algebra endomorphism multiplying each generator `∂_s A_μ^φ` by
`c ^ (2 + 2 |s|)`. The gauge field has mass dimension one, that is mass weight two, and each
derivative adds mass weight two. A monomial of total mass weight `n` is scaled by `c ^ n`,
so the scaling records the mass-weight grading of the jet algebra. This is the gauge-boson
part of the scaling `GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale` of a full local field algebra, on the
real, single-half component space of the gauge bosons.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale` : the scaling on the component space.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale` : the mass-weight scaling.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale_ofA` : the gauge field carries mass weight two.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale_jetDeriv` : a derivative adds mass weight two.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale_iteratedJetDeriv` : `∂_s` adds mass weight `2 |s|`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight scaling on the component space
- B. The mass-weight scaling on the jet algebra
- C. The mass weight of the gauge field and its derivatives

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling on the field-derivative space of the gauge bosons. The generator
`∂_s A_μ^φ` is scaled by `c ^ (2 + 2 |s|)`, through the derivative-degree scaling
`SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.gradeScale` on the derivative label.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (c : ℝ) :
    (FieldDerivSpace G) →ₗ[ℝ] (FieldDerivSpace G)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_tmul (c : ℝ) (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ (GaugeBoson G)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale G) c (a ⊗ₜ[ℝ] φ)
      = c ^ 2 • (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.gradeScale (c ^ 2) a ⊗ₜ[ℝ] φ)

declarations.name: GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_jetDeriv
declarations.doc: The derivative shift carries mass weight two on the component space.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_jetDeriv (c : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (v : (FieldDerivSpace G)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale G) c ((FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) μ v)
      = c ^ 2 • (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv G) μ ((FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale G) c v)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling on the gauge-boson jet algebra, the algebra endomorphism
scaling the generator `∂_s A_μ^φ` by `c ^ (2 + 2 |s|)`, the functorial lift of the
scaling on the field-derivative space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightScale (c : ℝ) :
    (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₐ[ℝ] (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale_ι
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_ι (c : ℝ) (x : (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)) :
    (massWeightScale G) c (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ x)
      = SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ ((GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale G) c x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale_ofA
declarations.doc: The gauge field carries mass weight two — mass dimension one.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_ofA (c : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (massWeightScale G) c ((ofA G) μ φ) = c ^ 2 • (ofA G) μ φ

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale_jetDeriv
declarations.doc: A total derivative adds mass weight two.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_jetDeriv (c : ℝ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (massWeightScale G) c ((jetDeriv G) μ x) = c ^ 2 • (jetDeriv G) μ
      ((massWeightScale G) c x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightScale_iteratedJetDeriv
declarations.doc: The iterated derivative `∂_s` adds mass weight `2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_iteratedJetDeriv (c : ℝ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (x : (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) :
    (massWeightScale G) c ((iteratedJetDeriv G) s x)
      = c ^ (2 * Multiset.card s) • (iteratedJetDeriv G) s ((massWeightScale G) c x)

modules.title: The mass-weight polynomial on the gauge-boson jet algebra
modules.doc:
The mass-weight grading of the gauge-boson jet algebra, as an algebra map into polynomials.

## i. Overview

Replacing the scalar of a mass-weight scaling by a formal variable turns the scaling into a
grading. The generator `∂_s A_μ^φ` is sent to `X ^ (2 + 2 |s|)` times itself, the gauge field
carrying mass weight two and each derivative two more.

The gauge-boson jet algebra is real, but the jet algebra of the Standard Model uses its
complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G`. So the grading is built in two steps:
the universal property of the symmetric algebra gives a real algebra map landing in
`Polynomial (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)`, a commutative target so that there is no
side condition, and the universal property of the tensor product extends it along the scalars
to `complexMassWeightPoly`, which is what the ambient theory sees.

Setting the formal variable to one recovers the element, and setting it to a real number `c`
on a component function gives the mass-weight scaling by `c`.

## ii. Key results

- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightPoly` : the mass-weight grading on the real jet algebra.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightPoly_iteratedJetDeriv_ofA` : `∂_s A_μ^φ` is a monomial
  eigenvector of weight `2 + 2 |s|`.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexMassWeightPoly` : the grading on the complexification.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexMassWeightPoly_tmul_iteratedJetDeriv_ofA` : the generator lemma
  on the complexification.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexMassWeightPoly_eval_one` : setting the variable to one recovers
  the element.
- `LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetComponentPoly_eval_algebraMap` : setting the variable to a real
  number `c` on a component function gives its mass-weight scaling by `c`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight polynomial of a component function
- B. The mass-weight polynomial on the real jet algebra
- C. The mass-weight polynomial on the complexification
- D. Evaluating the mass-weight polynomial

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The mass-weight polynomial on the real jet algebra
## C. The mass-weight polynomial on the complexification
## D. Evaluating the mass-weight polynomial

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.monomialₗ
declarations.doc:
The monomial map into polynomials over the complexified jet algebra, as a map of
`ℝ`-modules rather than of modules over the complexified jet algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def monomialₗ (n : ℕ) :
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₗ[ℝ]
      Polynomial (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.monomialₗ_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma monomialₗ_apply (n : ℕ) (x : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    (monomialₗ (G := G)) n x = Polynomial.monomial n x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.ιComplex
declarations.doc:
A component function, viewed inside the complexified jet algebra, the generator
`∂_s A_μ^φ` tensored with the scalar one.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ιComplex :
    (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) →ₗ[ℝ] ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.ιComplex_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma ιComplex_apply (x : (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)) :
    (ιComplex (G := G)) x =
      (1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetComponentPoly
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight polynomial of a component function, the linear map sending the symbol
`∂_s A^φ` to `X ^ (2 + 2 |s|)` times itself, read off from the multiset basis of the real
derivative symbols.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetComponentPoly :
    (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) →ₗ[ℝ]
      Polynomial (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetComponentPoly_basisMultiset_tmul
declarations.doc:
On the symbol `∂_s A^φ` the component map is the monomial of degree `2 + 2 |s|`. The
gauge field contributes two and each derivative two more.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetComponentPoly_basisMultiset_tmul (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ (GaugeBoson G)) :
    (jetComponentPoly (G := G)) (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.basisMultiset s ⊗ₜ[ℝ] φ) =
      Polynomial.monomial (2 + 2 * Multiset.card s)
        (ιComplex (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℝ.basisMultiset s ⊗ₜ[ℝ] φ))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightPoly
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight polynomial on the gauge-boson jet algebra, the `ℝ`-algebra map sending
a generator of mass weight `n` to `X ^ n` times its image in the complexification. It
needs no side condition because the target is commutative.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightPoly :
    LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G →ₐ[ℝ]
      Polynomial (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightPoly_ι
declarations.doc: On a component function the mass-weight polynomial is the component-function map.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_ι (x : (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)) :
    (massWeightPoly (G := G)) (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) x) =
      jetComponentPoly x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightPoly_iteratedJetDeriv_ofA
declarations.doc: The generator `∂_s A_μ^φ` is a monomial eigenvector of mass weight `2 + 2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_iteratedJetDeriv_ofA (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (massWeightPoly (G := G)) (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv G s
        (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.ofA G μ φ)) =
      Polynomial.monomial (2 + 2 * Multiset.card s) ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
        LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv G s
          (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.ofA G μ φ))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexMassWeightPoly
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight polynomial on the complexified gauge-boson jet algebra, the `ℂ`-algebra
map obtained from the real one by extending the scalars, the grading the jet algebra of
the Standard Model sees on its gauge sector.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def complexMassWeightPoly :
    (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) →ₐ[ℂ]
      Polynomial (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexMassWeightPoly_tmul
declarations.doc: On a pure tensor the complexified grading is the scalar times the real grading.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexMassWeightPoly_tmul (z : ℂ) (x : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    (complexMassWeightPoly (G := G)) (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] x) =
      Polynomial.C (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] (1 : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G)) * massWeightPoly x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexMassWeightPoly_tmul_iteratedJetDeriv_ofA
declarations.doc:
The generator `∂_s A_μ^φ` of the complexified jet algebra, with any complex coefficient,
is a monomial eigenvector of mass weight `2 + 2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexMassWeightPoly_tmul_iteratedJetDeriv_ofA (z : ℂ)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (complexMassWeightPoly (G := G)) (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv G s
        (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.ofA G μ φ)) =
      Polynomial.monomial (2 + 2 * Multiset.card s) (z ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
        LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.iteratedJetDeriv G s
          (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.ofA G μ φ))

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetComponentPoly_eval_one
declarations.doc:
Setting the formal variable to one collapses the component map back to the component
function it graded. The derivative monomials span, so it is enough to check this on the
multiset basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetComponentPoly_eval_one (x : (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)) :
    ((jetComponentPoly (G := G)) x).eval 1 = ιComplex x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.jetComponentPoly_eval_algebraMap
declarations.doc:
Setting the formal variable to a real number `c` turns the component map into the
mass-weight scaling by `c`. It is enough to check this on the multiset basis, where both
sides are `c ^ (2 + 2 |s|)` times the symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetComponentPoly_eval_algebraMap (c : ℝ) (x : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) :
    ((jetComponentPoly (G := G)) x).eval (algebraMap ℝ _ c) =
      ιComplex (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale G c x)

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.massWeightPoly_eval_one
declarations.doc:
Setting the formal variable to one recovers the original element, viewed in the
complexification.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_eval_one (x : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    ((massWeightPoly (G := G)) x).eval 1 =
      Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight (R := ℝ) (A := ℂ)
        (B := LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) x

declarations.name: LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexMassWeightPoly_eval_one
declarations.doc:
Setting the formal variable to one recovers the original element of the complexified
jet algebra. The mass-weight pieces sum back to it.
declarations.statement:
lemma complexMassWeightPoly_eval_one (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    ((complexMassWeightPoly (G := G)) y).eval 1 = y

modules.title: The field data of a gauge theory
modules.doc:
The matter content of a gauge theory, its fermionic and bosonic species over a gauge group.

## i. Overview

A gauge theory is fixed, before any Lagrangian is chosen, by a global gauge group `G` and a
matter content. The gauge group `G : GlobalGaugeGroup κ` carries its gauge jet group, its Lie
algebra and the jet operations relating them. The matter content is a finite family of
fermionic species and a finite family of bosonic species, each a matter field over `G`
(`G.MatterField`) whose declared statistic is that of its family.

`GaugeFieldData G` bundles the matter content over such a gauge group. This file is the
datum itself and the value spaces it names. Everything derived from it lives in the sibling
files of this directory.

* `FermionGenerators.lean` and `BosonGenerators.lean` give the generator spaces
  `GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators` and `GaugeFieldData.BosonGenerators`, the direct sums
  of the component spaces of the species, together with the Lorentz and jet gauge actions
  and the mass-weight scaling assembled species by species, and the identification of each
  with the component space of a single matter field.
* `FermionModule.lean` and `BosonModule.lean` give the value spaces of all the species at
  once.
* `FermionMatterField.lean` and `BosonMatterField.lean` give those modules the structure of
  one matter field, when the species share a mass weight.

The connection generator space is not among them. It is the existing
`GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G`, fixed by the gauge group alone.

The algebra built on the three generator spaces, `GaugeFieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra`, and
its mapping-out universal property are in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalFieldAlgebra.Basic`. The split is one of subject
matter, here the datum and the spaces it determines, there the algebra of local expressions
on them.

It is field and transformation data before a Lagrangian, so packaging the species'
representations separately certifies no physical compatibility between them, and no
invariance is claimed here.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData` : the matter content of a gauge theory over a gauge group, split into
  fermionic and bosonic species in agreement with their declared statistics.
- `GaugeFieldData.FermionValue`, `GaugeFieldData.BosonValue` : the value space of a
  species.
- `GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCommute`, `GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCompatible` : the
  conditions of `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField`, imposed on every species of the datum.
- `GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCommute.gaugeLorentzCompatible` : the first condition implies
  the second.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The matter content of a gauge theory
- B. The value spaces of the species
- C. Conditions on the species of a datum

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The matter content of a gauge theory

The structure below is the matter content of a gauge theory over a global gauge group `G`, that
is, a finite family of fermionic species and a finite family of bosonic species, each given as a
matter field. The gauge group is the parameter, and the gauge bosons are determined by it
alone, so they are not recorded. The structure is needed because the algebras of local
expressions are built on all the species at once, the fermionic species supplying the
generators of an exterior-algebra factor and the bosonic species those of a symmetric-algebra
factor. A single datum lets the sibling files assemble the species into one fermionic and one
bosonic matter field and keeps the statistic of each family explicit.

## B. The value spaces of the species

The datum records one matter field per species, so the value space of a species is simply
the value space of that matter field. Everything built on those value spaces is in the
sibling files. The fermionic and bosonic generator spaces, with the Lorentz action, the jet
gauge action and the mass-weight scaling on them, are in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators` and its
bosonic twin, which also identify each with the component space of a single matter field.
The value spaces themselves assemble into the `FermionModule` and `BosonModule` of the
remaining siblings.

The connection is not a species. It is fixed by the gauge group alone, and its component functions
`∂_s A_μ^φ` are the existing `GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G`, used without a new name. They are
real, a connection being a real object, which is why the third generator family of the local field
algebra is a real vector space, complexified once inside the algebra. Finite dimensionality of
`G.lieSubalgebra` is what makes `Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra` the span of the adjoint components,
so that these generators really are the `A_μ^a`.

## C. Conditions on the species of a datum

The conditions on a matter field (from
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.InfinitesimalAction`),
imposed species by species. They are stated on the datum alone so that a concrete theory can
record them next to its field data. The covariant derivative theory assumes the Lie algebra
condition where it needs it, and the descent of invariants assumes the group condition, which
implies it.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData
declarations.doc:
The field data of a gauge theory. Over a global gauge group `G`, it records a finite
family of fermionic species and a finite family of bosonic species, each given by a
`G.MatterField`. The species types are `Fintype` rather than merely `Finite`, so that a
theory may be summed over its species. This is what lets the several fermionic multiplets
be assembled into the single fermionic matter field of `GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField`.

Nothing is repeated from `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField`, whose fields already carry the
value space, the Lorentz representation, the gauge actions, the mass weight and the declared
statistic of a species. The fermionic family supplies the generators of the exterior-algebra
factor of the local field algebra `GaugeFieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra`, and the bosonic family
those of its symmetric-algebra factor. The fields `fermion_statistic` and `boson_statistic`
require every entry of each family to be declared with the corresponding statistics. The
gauge bosons are not a species, since their generator space is determined by
`G.lieSubalgebra` alone.

This is data before a Lagrangian. Collecting representations of the several species does
not assert that they are jointly consistent. Gauge-Lorentz compatibility is a separate
condition, not imposed here.
declarations.statement:
structure GaugeFieldData {κ : Type} [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] (G : GlobalGaugeGroup κ) where
  /-- The index type of the fermionic species. -/
  FermionSpecies : Type
  [decidableEqFermionSpecies : DecidableEq FermionSpecies]
  [fintypeFermionSpecies : Fintype FermionSpecies]
  /-- The matter field of each fermionic species. -/
  fermion : FermionSpecies → G.MatterField
  /-- Every fermionic species is declared fermionic. -/
  fermion_statistic : ∀ i, (fermion i).statistic = .fermionic
  /-- The index type of the bosonic species. -/
  BosonSpecies : Type
  [decidableEqBosonSpecies : DecidableEq BosonSpecies]
  [fintypeBosonSpecies : Fintype BosonSpecies]
  /-- The matter field of each bosonic species. -/
  boson : BosonSpecies → G.MatterField
  /-- Every bosonic species is declared bosonic. -/
  boson_statistic : ∀ j, (boson j).statistic = .bosonic

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.FermionValue
declarations.doc: The value space of a fermionic species.
declarations.statement: abbrev FermionValue (i : T.FermionSpecies) : Type

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.BosonValue
declarations.doc: The value space of a bosonic species.
declarations.statement: abbrev BosonValue (j : T.BosonSpecies) : Type

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCommute
declarations.doc: The gauge and Lorentz representations of every species of the datum commute.
declarations.statement: def GaugeLorentzCommute : Prop

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCompatible
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal gauge action of every species of the datum commutes with its Lorentz
representation.
declarations.statement: def GaugeLorentzCompatible : Prop

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCommute.gaugeLorentzCompatible
declarations.doc:
If the gauge and Lorentz representations of every species commute, so do the
infinitesimal gauge actions and the Lorentz representations.
declarations.statement:
lemma GaugeLorentzCommute.gaugeLorentzCompatible (h : T.GaugeLorentzCommute) :
    T.GaugeLorentzCompatible

modules.title: The bosonic generators of a gauge theory
modules.doc:
The component functions of all the bosonic species of a gauge theory, as one space.

## i. Overview

The bosonic species of a `GaugeFieldData` — its scalars — each carry a component space, the
span of the symbols `∂_s φ_α` and their conjugates for that multiplet. This file assembles them into
the bosonic generator space of the theory,

`T.BosonGenerators = ⨁ i, FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i)`,

together with the transformation data the species supply: the Lorentz action, the action of
the jets of gauge transformations, and the mass-weight scaling, each assembled species by
species. These are the bosonic generators on which
`GaugeFieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra` builds its symmetric algebra. The gauge bosons are not
among them: their generator space is fixed by the gauge algebra alone.

The direct sum, rather than a single component space on the product of the value spaces, is
what lets the species carry different mass weights: the scaling of one component space is
natural in the value space and so cannot tell the species apart.

Section C shows what happens when the species *do* share a weight, which is the case in any
theory whose scalars all have the same mass dimension. A physicist does not write each
multiplet with its own component space; they write one scalar field `φ` valued in the whole
bosonic module and take its component functions `∂_s φ_α`, a single `FieldDerivSpace`
whose target index `α` runs over everything. For the Standard Model, with its one Higgs
doublet, the two are trivially the same; for a larger scalar sector they are not.

The two descriptions agree: there is an isomorphism

`T.BosonGenerators ≃ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace T.BosonModule`,

under which the summand of a species is the pullback along the projection onto that
species, `bosonGeneratorsEquiv_inclBoson`. So the generators of one multiplet sit inside
the generators of the whole scalar field exactly as its target components sit inside the
bosonic module. The isomorphism is not merely one of vector spaces: it intertwines the
Lorentz action and the mass-weight scaling with those of the single matter field
`T.bosonMatterField w h`, the shared weight `w` being needed for the second of these and
for nothing else.

The underlying identification is `FieldDerivSpace.piEquiv`, composed with the
identification of a direct sum over a finite index with the product.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.BosonGenerators` : the bosonic generator space.
- `GaugeFieldData.inclBoson` : the inclusion of the component space of one species.
- `GaugeFieldData.assembleBoson`, `GaugeFieldData.bosonGenerators_hom_ext` : the assembly of
  a species-wise family of linear maps, and the fact that it is the only such map.
- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBoson`, `GaugeFieldData.repJetBoson` : the Lorentz and jet
  gauge actions assembled on it.
- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson` : the mass-weight scaling carrying the weight of
  each species.
- `GaugeFieldData.jetDerivBoson` : the ordinary derivative shift on the generator space.
- `GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv` : with one shared weight, the generator space is
  the component space of the bosonic matter field.
- `GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_inclBoson` : a species sits inside it as the
  pullback along the projection onto that species.
- `GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzBoson`,
  `GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repJetBoson`,
  `GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleBoson`,
  `GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivBoson` : the identification carries the
  Lorentz action, the jet gauge action, the mass-weight scaling and the derivative shift
  across.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The bosonic generator space and its species assembly
- B. The transformation data on the generator space
  - B.1. The Lorentz action
  - B.2. The jet gauge action
  - B.3. The mass weights
  - B.4. The ordinary derivative
- C. The bosonic generators as one component space
  - C.1. The species as pullbacks
  - C.2. The identification of the transformation data

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The bosonic generator space and its species assembly

## B. The transformation data on the generator space

The datum supplies, per species, a Lorentz representation and a fibrewise action of the
gauge jets. Both act on the generator space one summand at a time, so both are assembled
from the species-wise actions and the representation laws follow from
`bosonGenerators_hom_ext` alone, with no relation between the species used. Nothing here
asserts that the two actions commute, since Lorentz transformations act on nonconstant
gauge jets, and nothing extends them to the algebra `J(T)`.

### B.1. The Lorentz action
### B.2. The jet gauge action

### B.3. The mass weights

The mass weight is a property of a species, not of the theory, a fermion carrying weight
`3` and a scalar weight `2`. The generator space records one weight per species, and the
scaling acts on the summand of a species through that species' weight alone.

### B.4. The ordinary derivative

The formal total derivative shifts the derivative label of a component function,
`∂_s φ_α ↦ ∂_{s + {μ}} φ_α`. Unlike the two actions it takes no data from the species at
all, the label being blind to the value space, so on the generator space it too is
species-diagonal and the same assembly serves. It is recorded here so that the generator
space carries every operation the local field algebra is built from.
## C. The bosonic generators as one component space
### C.1. The species as pullbacks
### C.2. The identification of the transformation data

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.BosonGenerators
declarations.doc:
The bosonic generator space of the datum, holding the component functions `∂_s φ_α`
and their conjugates of every bosonic species at once, as a direct sum over the species.
A component function of the theory is a finitely supported family of component functions
of the species.

The direct sum, rather than a single component space on the product of the value spaces,
is what lets the species carry different mass weights. The scaling of one component space
is natural in the value space — `FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_massWeightScale` — and so
cannot tell the species apart. When the weights do agree the two descriptions coincide,
which is section C below.

This `def` and its explicit instances reduce instance-term expansion in the symmetric
algebra and tensor products built on it. Use the inclusion, assembly and extensionality
API in downstream proofs; unfold the direct-sum representation explicitly when necessary.
declarations.statement: def BosonGenerators : Type
instance : AddCommGroup T.BosonGenerators
instance : Module ℂ T.BosonGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.inclBoson
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the component space of one bosonic species into the bosonic generator
space.
declarations.statement:
def inclBoson (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i) →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.assembleBoson
declarations.doc:
The assembly of a species-wise family of linear maps out of the bosonic generator space
into a common target.
declarations.statement:
def assembleBoson (f : ∀ i, FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i) →ₗ[ℂ] N) :
    T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] N

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.assembleBoson_inclBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma assembleBoson_inclBoson (f : ∀ i, FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i) →ₗ[ℂ] N)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.assembleBoson f (T.inclBoson i x) = f i x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGenerators_hom_ext
declarations.doc:
Two linear maps out of the bosonic generator space agreeing on every species are
equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonGenerators_hom_ext {F F' : T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] N}
    (h : ∀ i x, F (T.inclBoson i x) = F' (T.inclBoson i x)) : F = F'

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBoson
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the bosonic generator space, acting on each species through the
Lorentz representation of its matter field.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzBoson : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.BosonGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBoson_inclBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzBoson_inclBoson (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.repLorentzBoson Λ (T.inclBoson i x)
      = T.inclBoson i (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.boson i) Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetBoson
declarations.doc:
The action of the jet gauge group on the bosonic generator space, acting on each
species through the fibrewise jet action of its matter field. Both the fibrewise
hypothesis and the finite dimensionality of the value space that
`FieldDerivSpace.repJet` needs are already fields of `MatterField`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repJetBoson : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup T.BosonGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetBoson_inclBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetBoson_inclBoson (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.repJetBoson U (T.inclBoson i x)
      = T.inclBoson i
        (FieldDerivSpace.repJet (T.boson i) U x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling on the bosonic generator space, with the weight of each species
taken from its matter field. Species of different weight scale differently, which is the
property the direct-sum generator space was chosen to have.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightScaleBoson (c : ℂ) :
    T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson
declarations.doc:
On the summand of a species the scaling is that species' own mass-weight scaling, with
the weight recorded in its matter field.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson (c : ℂ) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.massWeightScaleBoson c (T.inclBoson i x)
      = T.inclBoson i
        (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (T.boson i).massWeight c x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
A component function `∂_s φ_α` of a species scales by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, where `w` is
the mass weight of that species. There is one factor of `c` per unit of mass dimension of
the field and two per derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScaleBoson_inclBoson_basis_tmul (c : ℂ) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue i)) :
    T.massWeightScaleBoson c (T.inclBoson i
        ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0) : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i)))
      = c ^ ((T.boson i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s) • T.inclBoson i
          ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0) : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivBoson
declarations.doc:
The ordinary derivative shift on the bosonic generator space, acting on each species'
component functions by appending `∂_μ` to the derivative label.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetDerivBoson (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivBoson_inclBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivBoson_inclBoson (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.jetDerivBoson μ (T.inclBoson i x)
      = T.inclBoson i (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivBoson_comm
declarations.doc:
Mixed partials agree on the bosonic generator space, because they do on each
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivBoson_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.jetDerivBoson μ).comp (T.jetDerivBoson ν)
      = (T.jetDerivBoson ν).comp (T.jetDerivBoson μ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBoson_jetDerivBoson
declarations.doc:
The derivative shift is a Lorentz vector on the bosonic generator space. It is one
on each species, and both operations are species-diagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzBoson_jetDerivBoson (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.repLorentzBoson Λ (T.jetDerivBoson μ x)
      = ∑ a, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          T.jetDerivBoson a (T.repLorentzBoson Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv
declarations.doc:
The bosonic generator space is the component space of the bosonic matter field. The
direct sum over the species of their component spaces is, the species type being finite,
the same thing as the space of component functions of the single field
`T.bosonMatterField w h` — the presentation of the boson content used in writing a theory
down. The shared weight `w` enters only because a component space is now taken of a
matter field, and the only matter field on `T.BosonModule` is that one; the underlying
identification does not use it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bosonGeneratorsEquiv (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    T.BosonGenerators ≃ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace (T.bosonMatterField w h)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_inclBoson
declarations.doc:
A species sits inside the bosonic generators as the pullback along the projection
onto it. A component function of the multiplet `i` becomes the component function of
the whole field whose target covector is supported on that multiplet.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_inclBoson (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson i)) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.inclBoson i x)
      = FieldDerivSpace.comap
        (T.projBosonField w h i) x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzBoson
declarations.doc:
The identification is Lorentz-equivariant. The species-diagonal Lorentz action on
the generator space is the Lorentz action on the component functions of the single field.
Each species is a subrepresentation of the bosonic matter field, so pulling back along the
projection onto it commutes with the two actions.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzBoson (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (y : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.repLorentzBoson Λ y)
      = FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.bosonMatterField w h) Λ
        (T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repJetBoson
declarations.doc:
The identification is equivariant for the jet gauge action. The species-diagonal
action of the jets of gauge transformations on the generator space is the action on the
component functions of the single boson field, for the same reason as in the fermionic
case. Each species is a subrepresentation of the bosonic module. The common mass weight
enters only through the packaging of the bosonic module as a matter field; both halves
of the component space, with every derivative label, are covered.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_repJetBoson (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (y : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.repJetBoson U y)
      = FieldDerivSpace.repJet (T.bosonMatterField w h) U
        (T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleBoson
declarations.doc:
The identification carries the species-wise mass-weight scaling to a single
scaling. With one weight `w` shared by every species, the scaling that acts on each
species through its own weight is the scaling of weight `w` on the component functions of
the one field. The map `comap` is natural in the value space, so it does not see which species a
generator came from.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleBoson (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (c : ℂ) (y : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.massWeightScaleBoson c y)
      = FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale w c (T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivBoson
declarations.doc:
The identification carries the derivative shift across. The species-diagonal shift
of the derivative label on the generator space is the shift on the component functions of
the single boson field. The map `comap` is natural in the value space, and the shift touches only
the derivative label, so neither operation sees which species a generator came from. The
common mass weight enters only through the packaging of the bosonic module as a matter
field.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivBoson (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (y : T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.jetDerivBoson μ y)
      = FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ (T.bosonGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

modules.title: The bosonic matter field of a gauge theory
modules.doc:
All the bosonic species of a gauge theory with a common mass weight, as one matter field.

## i. Overview

`GaugeFieldData.BosonModule` is the value space of all the bosons of a theory at once. This file
puts on it the structure of a single `MatterField`: the Lorentz representation, the action of the
jets of gauge transformations, the infinitesimal action of the gauge algebra and the mass weight,
all acting species by species. It is the direct sum `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi` of the
family `T.boson`, and it is the object a physicist means by "the scalar field" of a theory: for the
Standard Model the Higgs doublet, for a two-Higgs-doublet model the pair of doublets read as one
field.

The bosons here are the matter bosons — the scalars. The gauge bosons are not a species of
`GaugeFieldData` at all, their generator space being fixed by the gauge algebra alone, so
they are not part of this assembly.

Beyond the datum, the assembly needs a shared mass weight. The construction packages the
family into one `MatterField`, which has one weight, so the family must be degenerate in mass
dimension, and the assembled field carries the common mass weight of its entries. That weight
`w` is taken as an argument together with the proof that every species has it. For a theory
whose scalars are all of the same mass dimension, the Standard Model included, this is no
restriction: every bosonic species has weight two. The common statistics comes from the datum
itself, whose field `boson_statistic` requires every bosonic species to be declared bosonic.

Assembling the species loses nothing, and this is the content of the lemmas below. Each
species includes into the bosonic matter field as a subrepresentation, of the Lorentz
group and of the gauge algebra alike, so the several multiplets can be read off the single
field again. What it does lose is the ability to record *different* mass weights, which is
exactly why `GaugeFieldData.BosonGenerators` is a direct sum of component spaces rather
than the component space of this one field.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField` : the matter field of all the bosons of the
  theory.
- `GaugeFieldData.repJetBosonModule` : the action of the jets of gauge transformations on
  the jets of the bosonic module, needing no common mass weight.
- `GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repLorentz_inclBosonValue`,
  `GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_inclBosonValue` : each species is a
  subrepresentation of it.
- `GaugeFieldData.finrank_bosonMatterField` : its dimension is the sum of the
  dimensions of the species.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The bosonic matter field
  - A.1. The transformation data species by species
  - A.2. The species as subrepresentations

## iv. References

* None.

### A.1. The transformation data species by species
### A.2. The species as subrepresentations

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField
declarations.doc:
The bosonic matter field of a gauge theory, the direct sum of the bosonic
species, valued in `T.BosonModule`, with the Lorentz group, the jets of gauge
transformations and the gauge algebra all acting species by species. It exists only for
a family degenerate in mass dimension, where `w` is the common mass weight of the species and
`h` the proof that they all have it, which for the Standard Model, whose only scalar is
the Higgs doublet, is weight two.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bosonMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    G.MatterField

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_massWeight
declarations.doc: The bosonic matter field carries the common mass weight of the species.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonMatterField_massWeight (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).massWeight = w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_statistic
declarations.doc: The bosonic matter field is bosonic, as every bosonic species is declared to be.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonMatterField_statistic (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).statistic = .bosonic

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBosonModule
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the bosonic module, acting species by species. This is the
Lorentz representation of the bosonic matter field, typed on `T.BosonModule` itself so
that it can be spoken of without fixing a common mass weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzBosonModule : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.BosonModule

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzBosonModule_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzBosonModule_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : T.BosonModule) (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    T.repLorentzBosonModule Λ v i = (T.boson i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetBosonModule
declarations.doc:
The action of the jets of gauge transformations on the jets of the bosonic
module, acting species by species, and typed on `T.BosonModule` itself so that it can
be spoken of without fixing a common mass weight.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repJetBosonModule :
    Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] T.BosonModule)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lTensor_projBosonValue_repJetBosonModule
declarations.doc:
A bosonic species is a subrepresentation of the jet gauge action on the bosonic
module. The projection onto its value space intertwines the two actions on the jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma lTensor_projBosonValue_repJetBosonModule (j : T.BosonSpecies) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (T.projBosonValue j)).comp (T.repJetBosonModule U)
      = ((T.boson j).repJet U).comp
        (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (T.projBosonValue j))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repJet
declarations.doc: The jet gauge action of the bosonic matter field is that of the bosonic module.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonMatterField_repJet (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repJet = T.repJetBosonModule

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repLorentz_apply
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group acts on a bosonic configuration species by species.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonMatterField_repLorentz_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : T.BosonModule)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repLorentz Λ v i = (T.boson i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_apply
declarations.doc: The gauge algebra acts on a bosonic configuration species by species.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (v : T.BosonModule)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repAlgebra c v i = (T.boson i).repAlgebra c (v i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repLorentz_inclBosonValue
declarations.doc:
A bosonic species is a Lorentz subrepresentation of the bosonic matter field.
Including a value of one species and then transforming is transforming and then
including. Assembling the species into one field therefore loses no Lorentz
information.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonMatterField_repLorentz_inclBosonValue (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : T.BosonValue i) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repLorentz Λ (T.inclBosonValue i x)
      = T.inclBosonValue i ((T.boson i).repLorentz Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_inclBosonValue
declarations.doc:
A bosonic species is a subrepresentation of the gauge algebra action on the
bosonic matter field, for the same reason. The gauge algebra does not mix the
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonMatterField_repAlgebra_inclBosonValue (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (i : T.BosonSpecies)
    (x : T.BosonValue i) :
    (T.bosonMatterField w h).repAlgebra c (T.inclBosonValue i x)
      = T.inclBosonValue i ((T.boson i).repAlgebra c x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.finrank_bosonMatterField
declarations.doc:
The dimension of the bosonic matter field is the sum of the dimensions of the
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_bosonMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w) :
    Module.finrank ℂ (T.bosonMatterField w h).V
      = ∑ i, Module.finrank ℂ (T.BosonValue i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.projBosonField
declarations.doc:
The projection of the bosonic matter field onto one species, typed as a map out of
`(T.bosonMatterField w h).V` rather than out of `T.BosonModule`. The two are the same
type by definition, but naming the first keeps unification from having to unfold the
direct sum every time the projection meets the matter field.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev projBosonField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.boson i).massWeight = w)
    (i : T.BosonSpecies) : (T.bosonMatterField w h).V →ₗ[ℂ] (T.boson i).V

modules.title: The bosonic module of a gauge theory
modules.doc:
The value space of all the bosonic species of a gauge theory at once.

## i. Overview

A `GaugeFieldData G` records its bosons species by species, each with its own value
space `(T.boson i).V`. This file assembles those into a single complex vector space, the
bosonic module

`T.BosonModule = ∀ i, (T.boson i).V`,

in which one value of the whole bosonic content of the theory lives at once. For the
Standard Model, whose only bosonic species is the Higgs doublet, this is that doublet
again. A theory with a larger scalar sector, such as a second Higgs doublet or a singlet, has
the column of all of them.

It is the *value* space, not a space of component functions, and so it is not the
`GaugeFieldData.BosonGenerators` of the sibling file. The latter is a direct sum of component
spaces `FieldDerivSpace`, one per species, and is infinite-dimensional because it
carries a derivative label of every order. The bosonic module is finite-dimensional,
with dimension the sum of the dimensions of the species, and it is the space on which
`GaugeFieldData.bosonMatterField` puts the Lorentz, gauge and mass-weight structure of a
single matter field.

The species type is finite, so the product is also a direct sum. A bosonic
configuration is the sum of its species components, `sum_inclBosonValue_proj` below, and
the two descriptions of the module agree.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.BosonModule` : the value space of all the bosons of the theory.
- `GaugeFieldData.projBosonValue`, `GaugeFieldData.inclBosonValue` : the projection
  onto and the inclusion of one species.
- `GaugeFieldData.sum_inclBosonValue_proj` : a configuration is the sum of its species
  components.
- `GaugeFieldData.finrank_bosonModule` : its dimension is the sum of the dimensions of
  the species.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The bosonic module
