declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.BosonModule
declarations.doc:
The bosonic module of a gauge theory, the product over the bosonic species of their
value spaces. One element of it is a value of the entire bosonic content of the theory, the
column of all the boson fields. This is as opposed to
`GaugeFieldData.BosonGenerators`, which is a space of component *functions* and is
infinite-dimensional. Since the species type is finite the product is also their direct
sum.
declarations.statement: abbrev BosonModule : Type

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.projBosonValue
declarations.doc: The component of a bosonic configuration in one species.
declarations.statement:
abbrev projBosonValue (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    T.BosonModule →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonValue i

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.inclBosonValue
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of one bosonic species into the bosonic module, extending a value
of that species by zero in every other.
declarations.statement:
abbrev inclBosonValue (i : T.BosonSpecies) :
    T.BosonValue i →ₗ[ℂ] T.BosonModule

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sum_inclBosonValue_proj
declarations.doc:
A bosonic configuration is the sum of its species components. The product over
the species is their direct sum, the species type being finite, so nothing is lost in
describing the bosonic content of the theory by one module.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_inclBosonValue_proj (v : T.BosonModule) :
    ∑ i, T.inclBosonValue i (v i) = v

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.finrank_bosonModule
declarations.doc:
The dimension of the bosonic module is the sum of the dimensions of the
species, each species contributing the number of complex components of its
multiplet.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_bosonModule :
    Module.finrank ℂ T.BosonModule = ∑ i, Module.finrank ℂ (T.BosonValue i)

modules.title: The fermionic generators of a gauge theory
modules.doc:
The component functions of all the fermionic species of a gauge theory, as one space.

## i. Overview

The fermionic species of a `GaugeFieldData` each carry a component space, the span of the
symbols `∂_s ψ_α` and their conjugates for that multiplet. This file assembles them into
the fermionic generator space of the theory,

`T.FermionGenerators = ⨁ i, FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)`,

together with the transformation data the species supply: the Lorentz action, the action of
the jets of gauge transformations, and the mass-weight scaling, each assembled species by
species. These are the fermionic generators on which
`GaugeFieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra` builds its exterior algebra.

The direct sum, rather than a single component space on the product of the value spaces, is
what lets the species carry different mass weights: the scaling of one component space is
natural in the value space and so cannot tell the species apart.

Section C shows what happens when the species *do* share a weight, which is the case in
every theory of Weyl fermions and in particular in the Standard Model. A physicist does not
write fifteen multiplets with their own component spaces; they write one fermion field `ψ`
valued in the whole fermionic module and take its component functions `∂_s ψ_α`, a single
`FieldDerivSpace` whose target index `α` runs over everything. The two agree: there is an
isomorphism

`T.FermionGenerators ≃ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace T.FermionModule`,

under which the summand of a species is the pullback along the projection onto that
species, `fermionGeneratorsEquiv_inclFermion`. So the generators of one multiplet sit inside
the generators of the whole fermion field exactly as its target components sit inside the
fermionic module. The isomorphism is not merely one of vector spaces: it intertwines the
Lorentz action and the mass-weight scaling with those of the single matter field
`T.fermionMatterField w h`, the shared weight `w` being needed for the second of these and
for nothing else.

The underlying identification is `FieldDerivSpace.piEquiv`, composed with the
identification of a direct sum over a finite index with the product.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators` : the fermionic generator space.
- `GaugeFieldData.inclFermion` : the inclusion of the component space of one species.
- `GaugeFieldData.assembleFermion`, `GaugeFieldData.fermionGenerators_hom_ext` : the assembly of
  a species-wise family of linear maps, and the fact that it is the only such map.
- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermion`, `GaugeFieldData.repJetFermion` : the Lorentz and jet
  gauge actions assembled on it.
- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion` : the mass-weight scaling carrying the weight of
  each species.
- `GaugeFieldData.jetDerivFermion` : the ordinary derivative shift on the generator space.
- `GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv` : with one shared weight, the generator space is
  the component space of the fermionic matter field.
- `GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_inclFermion` : a species sits inside it as the
  pullback along the projection onto that species.
- `GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzFermion`,
  `GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repJetFermion`,
  `GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleFermion`,
  `GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivFermion` : the identification carries the
  Lorentz action, the jet gauge action, the mass-weight scaling and the derivative shift
  across.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The fermionic generator space and its species assembly
- B. The transformation data on the generator space
  - B.1. The Lorentz action
  - B.2. The jet gauge action
  - B.3. The mass weights
  - B.4. The ordinary derivative
- C. The fermionic generators as one component space
  - C.1. The species as pullbacks
  - C.2. The identification of the transformation data

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The fermionic generator space and its species assembly

## B. The transformation data on the generator space

The datum supplies, per species, a Lorentz representation and a fibrewise action of the
gauge jets. Both act on the generator space one summand at a time, so both are assembled
from the species-wise actions and the representation laws follow from
`fermionGenerators_hom_ext` alone, with no relation between the species used. Nothing here
asserts that the two actions commute, since Lorentz transformations act on nonconstant
gauge jets, and nothing extends them to the algebra `J(T)`.

### B.1. The Lorentz action
### B.2. The jet gauge action

### B.3. The mass weights

The mass weight is a property of a species, not of the theory, a fermion carrying weight
`3` and a scalar weight `2`. The generator space records one weight per species, and the
scaling acts on the summand of a species through that species' weight alone.

### B.4. The ordinary derivative

The formal total derivative shifts the derivative label of a component function,
`∂_s ψ_α ↦ ∂_{s + {μ}} ψ_α`. Unlike the two actions it takes no data from the species at
all, the label being blind to the value space, so on the generator space it too is
species-diagonal and the same assembly serves. It is recorded here so that the generator
space carries every operation the local field algebra is built from.
## C. The fermionic generators as one component space
### C.1. The species as pullbacks
### C.2. The identification of the transformation data

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators
declarations.doc:
The fermionic generator space of the datum, holding the component functions `∂_s ψ_α`
and their conjugates of every fermionic species at once, as a direct sum over the species.
A component function of the theory is a finitely supported family of component functions
of the species.

The direct sum, rather than a single component space on the product of the value spaces,
is what lets the species carry different mass weights. The scaling of one component space
is natural in the value space — `FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_massWeightScale` — and so
cannot tell the species apart. When the weights do agree the two descriptions coincide,
which is section C below.

This `def` and its explicit instances reduce instance-term expansion in the exterior
algebra and tensor products built on it. Use the inclusion, assembly and extensionality
API in downstream proofs; unfold the direct-sum representation explicitly when necessary.
declarations.statement: def FermionGenerators : Type
instance : AddCommGroup T.FermionGenerators
instance : Module ℂ T.FermionGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.inclFermion
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the component space of one fermionic species into the fermionic generator
space.
declarations.statement:
def inclFermion (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i) →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.assembleFermion
declarations.doc:
The assembly of a species-wise family of linear maps out of the fermionic generator space
into a common target.
declarations.statement:
def assembleFermion (f : ∀ i, FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i) →ₗ[ℂ] N) :
    T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] N

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.assembleFermion_inclFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma assembleFermion_inclFermion (f : ∀ i, FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i) →ₗ[ℂ] N)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.assembleFermion f (T.inclFermion i x) = f i x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGenerators_hom_ext
declarations.doc:
Two linear maps out of the fermionic generator space agreeing on every species are
equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionGenerators_hom_ext {F F' : T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] N}
    (h : ∀ i x, F (T.inclFermion i x) = F' (T.inclFermion i x)) : F = F'

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermion
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the fermionic generator space, acting on each species through the
Lorentz representation of its matter field.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzFermion : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.FermionGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermion_inclFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzFermion_inclFermion (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.repLorentzFermion Λ (T.inclFermion i x)
      = T.inclFermion i (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermion i) Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetFermion
declarations.doc:
The action of the jet gauge group on the fermionic generator space, acting on each
species through the fibrewise jet action of its matter field. Both the fibrewise
hypothesis and the finite dimensionality of the value space that
`FieldDerivSpace.repJet` needs are already fields of `MatterField`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repJetFermion : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup T.FermionGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetFermion_inclFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetFermion_inclFermion (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.repJetFermion U (T.inclFermion i x)
      = T.inclFermion i
        (FieldDerivSpace.repJet (T.fermion i) U x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling on the fermionic generator space, with the weight of each species
taken from its matter field. Species of different weight scale differently, which is the
property the direct-sum generator space was chosen to have.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightScaleFermion (c : ℂ) :
    T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion
declarations.doc:
On the summand of a species the scaling is that species' own mass-weight scaling, with
the weight recorded in its matter field.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion (c : ℂ) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.massWeightScaleFermion c (T.inclFermion i x)
      = T.inclFermion i
        (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (T.fermion i).massWeight c x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
A component function `∂_s ψ_α` of a species scales by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, where `w` is
the mass weight of that species. There is one factor of `c` per unit of mass dimension of
the field and two per derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScaleFermion_inclFermion_basis_tmul (c : ℂ) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    T.massWeightScaleFermion c (T.inclFermion i
        ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0) : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)))
      = c ^ ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s) • T.inclFermion i
          ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0) : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivFermion
declarations.doc:
The ordinary derivative shift on the fermionic generator space, acting on each species'
component functions by appending `∂_μ` to the derivative label.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetDerivFermion (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivFermion_inclFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivFermion_inclFermion (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.jetDerivFermion μ (T.inclFermion i x)
      = T.inclFermion i (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.jetDerivFermion_comm
declarations.doc:
Mixed partials agree on the fermionic generator space, because they do on each
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivFermion_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.jetDerivFermion μ).comp (T.jetDerivFermion ν)
      = (T.jetDerivFermion ν).comp (T.jetDerivFermion μ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermion_jetDerivFermion
declarations.doc:
The derivative shift is a Lorentz vector on the fermionic generator space. It is
one on each species, and both operations are species-diagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzFermion_jetDerivFermion (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.repLorentzFermion Λ (T.jetDerivFermion μ x)
      = ∑ a, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          T.jetDerivFermion a (T.repLorentzFermion Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv
declarations.doc:
The fermionic generator space is the component space of the fermionic matter field. The
direct sum over the species of their component spaces is, the species type being finite,
the same thing as the space of component functions of the single field
`T.fermionMatterField w h` — the presentation of the fermion content used in writing a theory
down. The shared weight `w` enters only because a component space is now taken of a
matter field, and the only matter field on `T.FermionModule` is that one; the underlying
identification does not use it.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fermionGeneratorsEquiv (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    T.FermionGenerators ≃ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace (T.fermionMatterField w h)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_inclFermion
declarations.doc:
A species sits inside the fermionic generators as the pullback along the projection
onto it. A component function of the multiplet `i` becomes the component function of
the whole field whose target covector is supported on that multiplet.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_inclFermion (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.inclFermion i x)
      = FieldDerivSpace.comap
        (T.projFermionField w h i) x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzFermion
declarations.doc:
The identification is Lorentz-equivariant. The species-diagonal Lorentz action on
the generator space is the Lorentz action on the component functions of the single field.
Each species is a subrepresentation of the fermionic matter field, so pulling back along the
projection onto it commutes with the two actions.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repLorentzFermion (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (y : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.repLorentzFermion Λ y)
      = FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermionMatterField w h) Λ
        (T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repJetFermion
declarations.doc:
The identification is equivariant for the jet gauge action. The species-diagonal
action of the jets of gauge transformations on the generator space is the action on the
component functions of the single fermion field. Each species is a subrepresentation of
the fermionic module, so pulling back along the projection onto it commutes with the two
actions.

The common mass weight enters only through the packaging of the fermionic module as the
matter field `T.fermionMatterField w h`; the gauge action itself is `repJetFermionModule`,
which exists whatever the weights are. Both halves of the component space are covered,
the conjugate one included, and every derivative label with them. This is
`FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_repJet` at the species projection.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_repJetFermion (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (y : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.repJetFermion U y)
      = FieldDerivSpace.repJet (T.fermionMatterField w h) U
        (T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleFermion
declarations.doc:
The identification carries the species-wise mass-weight scaling to a single
scaling. With one weight `w` shared by every species, the scaling that acts on each
species through its own weight is the scaling of weight `w` on the component functions of
the one field. The map `comap` is natural in the value space, so it does not see which species a
generator came from.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_massWeightScaleFermion (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (c : ℂ) (y : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.massWeightScaleFermion c y)
      = FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale w c (T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivFermion
declarations.doc:
The identification carries the derivative shift across. The species-diagonal shift
of the derivative label on the generator space is the shift on the component functions of
the single fermion field. The map `comap` is natural in the value space, and the shift touches
only the derivative label, so neither operation sees which species a generator came from.
The common mass weight enters only through the packaging of the fermionic module as a
matter field.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionGeneratorsEquiv_jetDerivFermion (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (y : T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h (T.jetDerivFermion μ y)
      = FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ (T.fermionGeneratorsEquiv w h y)

modules.title: The fermionic matter field of a gauge theory
modules.doc:
All the fermionic species of a gauge theory with a common mass weight, as one matter field.

## i. Overview

`GaugeFieldData.FermionModule` is the value space of all the fermions of a theory at once. This file
puts on it the structure of a single `MatterField`: the Lorentz representation, the action of the
jets of gauge transformations, the infinitesimal action of the gauge algebra and the mass weight,
all acting species by species. It is the direct sum `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi` of the
family `T.fermion`, and it is the object a physicist means by "the fermion field" of a theory, as
against the fifteen separate multiplets the Standard Model is usually presented by.

Beyond the datum, the assembly needs a shared mass weight. The construction packages the
family into one `MatterField`, which has one weight, so the family must be degenerate in mass
dimension, and the assembled field carries the common mass weight of its entries. That weight
`w` is taken as an argument together with the proof that every species has it. For the
Standard Model, and for any theory whose fermions are Weyl spinors, this is no restriction:
every fermionic species has weight three. The common statistics comes from the datum itself,
whose field `fermion_statistic` requires every fermionic species to be declared fermionic.

Assembling the species loses nothing, and this is the content of the lemmas below. Each
species includes into the fermionic matter field as a subrepresentation, of the Lorentz
group and of the gauge algebra alike, so the several multiplets can be read off the single
field again. What it does lose is the ability to record *different* mass weights, which is
exactly why `GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators` is a direct sum of component spaces rather
than the component space of this one field.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField` : the matter field of all the fermions of the
  theory.
- `GaugeFieldData.repJetFermionModule` : the action of the jets of gauge transformations
  on the jets of the fermionic module, needing no common mass weight.
- `GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repLorentz_inclFermionValue`,
  `GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_inclFermionValue` : each species is a
  subrepresentation of it.
- `GaugeFieldData.finrank_fermionMatterField` : its dimension is the sum of the
  dimensions of the species.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The fermionic matter field
  - A.1. The transformation data species by species
  - A.2. The species as subrepresentations

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The fermionic matter field
### A.1. The transformation data species by species
### A.2. The species as subrepresentations

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField
declarations.doc:
The fermionic matter field of a gauge theory, the direct sum of the fermionic
species, valued in `T.FermionModule`, with the Lorentz group, the jets of gauge
transformations and the gauge algebra all acting species by species. It exists only for
a family degenerate in mass dimension, where `w` is the common mass weight of the species and
`h` the proof that they all have it, which for the Standard Model, and for any theory
whose fermions are Weyl spinors, is weight three.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fermionMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    G.MatterField

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_massWeight
declarations.doc: The fermionic matter field carries the common mass weight of the species.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMatterField_massWeight (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).massWeight = w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_statistic
declarations.doc: The fermionic matter field is fermionic, as every fermionic species is declared to be.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMatterField_statistic (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).statistic = .fermionic

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermionModule
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the fermionic module, acting species by species. This is the
Lorentz representation of the fermionic matter field, typed on `T.FermionModule` itself so
that it can be spoken of without fixing a common mass weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzFermionModule : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.FermionModule

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzFermionModule_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzFermionModule_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : T.FermionModule) (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    T.repLorentzFermionModule Λ v i = (T.fermion i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJetFermionModule
declarations.doc:
The action of the jets of gauge transformations on the jets of the fermionic
module, acting species by species. Like `repLorentzFermionModule` it is typed on
`T.FermionModule` itself, so that it can be spoken of without fixing a common mass
weight; the gauge action of a theory whose fermions carry different mass dimensions is
perfectly well defined, only its packaging as one `MatterField` is not.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repJetFermionModule :
    Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] T.FermionModule)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lTensor_projFermionValue_repJetFermionModule
declarations.doc:
A fermionic species is a subrepresentation of the jet gauge action on the fermionic
module. The projection onto its value space intertwines the two actions on the jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma lTensor_projFermionValue_repJetFermionModule (i : T.FermionSpecies) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (T.projFermionValue i)).comp (T.repJetFermionModule U)
      = ((T.fermion i).repJet U).comp
        (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (T.projFermionValue i))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repJet
declarations.doc: The jet gauge action of the fermionic matter field is that of the fermionic module.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMatterField_repJet (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repJet = T.repJetFermionModule

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repLorentz_apply
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group acts on a fermionic configuration species by species.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMatterField_repLorentz_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : T.FermionModule)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repLorentz Λ v i = (T.fermion i).repLorentz Λ (v i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_apply
declarations.doc: The gauge algebra acts on a fermionic configuration species by species.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_apply (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (v : T.FermionModule)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repAlgebra c v i = (T.fermion i).repAlgebra c (v i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repLorentz_inclFermionValue
declarations.doc:
A fermionic species is a Lorentz subrepresentation of the fermionic matter field.
Including a value of one species and then transforming is transforming and then
including. Assembling the species into one field therefore loses no Lorentz
information.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMatterField_repLorentz_inclFermionValue (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : T.FermionValue i) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repLorentz Λ (T.inclFermionValue i x)
      = T.inclFermionValue i ((T.fermion i).repLorentz Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_inclFermionValue
declarations.doc:
A fermionic species is a subrepresentation of the gauge algebra action on the
fermionic matter field, for the same reason. The gauge algebra does not mix the
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionMatterField_repAlgebra_inclFermionValue (w : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : T.FermionValue i) :
    (T.fermionMatterField w h).repAlgebra c (T.inclFermionValue i x)
      = T.inclFermionValue i ((T.fermion i).repAlgebra c x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.finrank_fermionMatterField
declarations.doc:
The dimension of the fermionic matter field is the sum of the dimensions of the
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_fermionMatterField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w) :
    Module.finrank ℂ (T.fermionMatterField w h).V
      = ∑ i, Module.finrank ℂ (T.FermionValue i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.projFermionField
declarations.doc:
The projection of the fermionic matter field onto one species, typed as a map out of
`(T.fermionMatterField w h).V` rather than out of `T.FermionModule`. The two are the same
type by definition, but naming the first keeps unification from having to unfold the
direct sum every time the projection meets the matter field.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev projFermionField (w : ℕ) (h : ∀ i, (T.fermion i).massWeight = w)
    (i : T.FermionSpecies) : (T.fermionMatterField w h).V →ₗ[ℂ] (T.fermion i).V

modules.title: The fermionic module of a gauge theory
modules.doc:
The value space of all the fermionic species of a gauge theory at once.

## i. Overview

A `GaugeFieldData G` records its fermions species by species, each with its own value
space `(T.fermion i).V`. This file assembles those into a single complex vector space, the
fermionic module

`T.FermionModule = ∀ i, (T.fermion i).V`,

in which one value of the whole fermionic content of the theory lives at once. For the
Standard Model this is the space that a physicist writes as the column of all the fermion
fields.

It is the *value* space, not a space of component functions, and so it is not the
`GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators` of the sibling file. The latter is a direct sum of component
spaces `FieldDerivSpace`, one per species, and is infinite-dimensional because it
carries a derivative label of every order. The fermionic module is finite-dimensional,
with dimension the sum of the dimensions of the species, and it is the space on which
`GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField` puts the Lorentz, gauge and mass-weight structure of a
single matter field.

The species type is finite, so the product is also a direct sum. A fermionic
configuration is the sum of its species components, `sum_inclFermionValue_proj` below, and
the two descriptions of the module agree.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.FermionModule` : the value space of all the fermions of the theory.
- `GaugeFieldData.projFermionValue`, `GaugeFieldData.inclFermionValue` : the projection
  onto and the inclusion of one species.
- `GaugeFieldData.sum_inclFermionValue_proj` : a configuration is the sum of its species
  components.
- `GaugeFieldData.finrank_fermionModule` : its dimension is the sum of the dimensions of
  the species.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The fermionic module
  - A.1. The species projections and inclusions
  - A.2. The dimension of the fermionic module

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The fermionic module
### A.1. The species projections and inclusions
### A.2. The dimension of the fermionic module

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.FermionModule
declarations.doc:
The fermionic module of a gauge theory, the product over the fermionic species of their
value spaces. One element of it is a value of the entire fermionic content of the theory, the
column of all the fermion fields. This is as opposed to
`GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators`, which is a space of component *functions* and is
infinite-dimensional. Since the species type is finite the product is also their direct
sum.
declarations.statement: abbrev FermionModule : Type

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.projFermionValue
declarations.doc: The component of a fermionic configuration in one species.
declarations.statement:
abbrev projFermionValue (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    T.FermionModule →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionValue i

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.inclFermionValue
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of one fermionic species into the fermionic module, extending a value
of that species by zero in every other.
declarations.statement:
abbrev inclFermionValue (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    T.FermionValue i →ₗ[ℂ] T.FermionModule

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sum_inclFermionValue_proj
declarations.doc:
A fermionic configuration is the sum of its species components. The product over
the species is their direct sum, the species type being finite, so nothing is lost in
describing the fermionic content of the theory by one module.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_inclFermionValue_proj (v : T.FermionModule) :
    ∑ i, T.inclFermionValue i (v i) = v

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.finrank_fermionModule
declarations.doc:
The dimension of the fermionic module is the sum of the dimensions of the
species, each species contributing the number of complex components of its
multiplet.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_fermionModule :
    Module.finrank ℂ T.FermionModule = ∑ i, Module.finrank ℂ (T.FermionValue i)

modules.title: The Taylor coefficients of the adjoint action
modules.doc:
The base-point derivatives of the adjoint action of a gauge jet on the Lie algebra.

## i. Overview

A gauge jet `U` acts on the gauge algebra of jets by the adjoint action `Ad_U`. What the
transformation law of a gauge field `A_μ ↦ Ad_U A_μ + ω_μ(U)` sees of `Ad_U`, after differentiating
`x` times and evaluating at the base point, is the physicists' `∂_x (Ad_U)^a_b|₀`, a linear map
`adjointCoeff U x : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra` on the constant gauge algebra, and its
transpose `adjointDualCoeff U x` on the dual index carried by the field symbols. This file develops
these coefficients for any global gauge group `G`, through its jet operations `G.evalLie`,
`G.iteratedDerivJ`, `G.adjointJ` and `G.ofConstantLie`.

The central result is the Taylor–Leibniz theorem `evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjointJ`. The
base-point Taylor coefficients of `Ad_U Y` for an arbitrary jet `Y` are the antidiagonal
convolution of the coefficients of `Ad_U` with those of `Y`. For a matrix group it is the Leibniz
rule for products of matrices of power series. Here it is derived from the Leibniz rule
`derivJ_adjointJ` for a single derivative, by induction on the number of derivatives. Its
corollaries are the multiplicativity `adjointCoeff_mul` of the coefficients up to convolution,
and the recursion `adjointCoeff_cons` expressing one more derivative of a coefficient through the
Maurer–Cartan form.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff` : the coefficient `∂_x (Ad_U)|₀`, with its values
  `adjointCoeff_zero` at the base point and `adjointCoeff_one` on the identity jet.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_cons` : one more derivative of a coefficient is minus the
  antidiagonal convolution of `ad` of the derived form `−ω` against lower coefficients, where
  `ω = (∂_μ U) U⁻¹` is the Maurer–Cartan form.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjointJ` : the Taylor–Leibniz theorem.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_mul` : the coefficients of a product are the convolution
  of the coefficients of the factors.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff` : the transposed coefficients, with
  `adjointDualCoeff_singleton`, `adjointDualCoeff_pair` and `adjointDualCoeff_cons`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint Taylor coefficients
- B. The recursion through the Maurer–Cartan form
- C. The Taylor–Leibniz theorem
- D. The dual coefficients

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The adjoint Taylor coefficients
## B. The recursion through the Maurer–Cartan form
## C. The Taylor–Leibniz theorem
## D. The dual coefficients

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff
declarations.doc:
The physicists' `∂_x (Ad_U)^a_b|₀`. Include a constant gauge algebra element into
jets, act by the adjoint of `U`, differentiate `x` times, and evaluate at the base
point. For `x = 0` this is the adjoint action of the value of `U`, and for `x ≠ 0` it sees
the derivatives of the gauge transformation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointCoeff (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_eq_evalLie
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_eq_evalLie (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (a : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    G.adjointCoeff U x a =
      G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ x
        (G.adjointJ U (G.ofConstantLie a)))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_zero
declarations.doc: The zeroth coefficient is the adjoint action of the value of the jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_zero (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) : G.adjointCoeff U 0 = G.adjointRep
    (G.evalGaugeJet U)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one
declarations.doc: A jet with trivial value has trivial zeroth coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one {U : G.gaugeJetGroup} (hU : G.evalGaugeJet U = 1) :
    G.adjointCoeff U 0 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_one
declarations.doc: The coefficients of the identity jet, of which only the base point survives.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_one (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.adjointCoeff (1 : G.gaugeJetGroup) p = if p = 0 then LinearMap.id else 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_lie
declarations.doc:
The coefficients are derivations of the bracket up to convolution, by the iterated
Leibniz rule for the jet bracket.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_lie (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (a b : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    G.adjointCoeff U x ⁅a, b⁆ =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p => ⁅G.adjointCoeff U p.1 a, G.adjointCoeff U p.2 b⁆).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_cons
declarations.doc:
One more derivative of a coefficient. Differentiating the adjoint once produces minus
`ad` of the Maurer–Cartan form, and the remaining derivatives distribute over the bracket
by the Leibniz rule.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_cons (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.adjointCoeff U (μ ::ₘ x) =
      -((x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra (G.evalLie
          (G.iteratedDerivJ p.1 (-G.maurerCartan U μ))) ∘ₗ
          G.adjointCoeff U p.2).sum)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.sum_antidiagonal_cons_adjointCoeff
declarations.doc:
The convolution of the adjoint coefficients with one more derivative. Splitting the
antidiagonal of `μ ::ₘ s` by where `μ` goes, the terms with `μ` on the right are the
convolution over `s` with `μ` added on the right, and those with `μ` on the left unfold by
`adjointCoeff_cons`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_antidiagonal_cons_adjointCoeff (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (y : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → G.lieSubalgebra) :
    ((μ ::ₘ s).antidiagonal.map fun p => G.adjointCoeff U p.1 (y p.2)).sum =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => G.adjointCoeff U p.1 (y (μ ::ₘ p.2))).sum
      - (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => (p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q =>
          ⁅G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ q.1 (-G.maurerCartan U μ)),
            G.adjointCoeff U q.2 (y p.2)⁆).sum).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjoint_cons
declarations.doc:
The inductive step of the Taylor–Leibniz theorem. The rule for `μ ::ₘ s` derivatives
follows from the rule for every sub-multiset of `s`. Peeling off `∂_μ` by the Leibniz
rule `derivJ_adjointJ` leaves `Ad_U (∂_μ Y)`, handled by the rule for `s`, and a bracket
with the Maurer–Cartan form, handled by the rule for the parts of `s`. On the other side
the coefficients at `μ ::ₘ p` unfold by `sum_antidiagonal_cons_adjointCoeff`, and the two
triple sums agree by coassociativity of the antidiagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjoint_cons (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (Y : G.jetLieSubalgebra)
    (ih : ∀ t ≤ s, ∀ Z : G.jetLieSubalgebra, G.evalLie
      (G.iteratedDerivJ t (G.adjointJ U Z)) =
      (t.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        G.adjointCoeff U p.1 (G.evalLie
          (G.iteratedDerivJ p.2 Z))).sum) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ (μ ::ₘ s)
      (G.adjointJ U Y)) =
      ((μ ::ₘ s).antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        G.adjointCoeff U p.1 (G.evalLie
          (G.iteratedDerivJ p.2 Y))).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjointJ
declarations.doc:
The Taylor–Leibniz theorem for the adjoint action. The base-point Taylor coefficients
of `Ad_U Y` are the antidiagonal convolution of the coefficients `adjointCoeff U` of
`Ad_U` with those of `Y`. For a matrix group this is the Leibniz rule for products of
matrices of power series. Here it follows from the single-derivative Leibniz rule
`derivJ_adjointJ` by strong induction on the number of derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjointJ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (Y : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ x (G.adjointJ U Y)) =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        G.adjointCoeff U p.1 (G.evalLie
          (G.iteratedDerivJ p.2 Y))).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjoint_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor data of `Ad_U Y` vanish up to a given order whenever those of
`Y` do.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjoint_eq_zero (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    {Y : G.jetLieSubalgebra} {s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)}
    (h : ∀ q ≤ s, G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ q Y) = 0) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s (G.adjointJ U Y))
      = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_mul
declarations.doc:
The coefficients are multiplicative up to convolution. The coefficient of a product of
jets is the antidiagonal convolution of the coefficients of the factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_mul (U V : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.adjointCoeff (U * V) x =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p => G.adjointCoeff U p.1 ∘ₗ G.adjointCoeff V p.2).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff
declarations.doc:
The physicists' `∂_x (Ad_U)^a_b|₀` acting on the dual adjoint index of a gauge-field
symbol, the transpose of `adjointCoeff U x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjointDualCoeff (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_apply (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra)
    (a : G.lieSubalgebra) : G.adjointDualCoeff U x φ a = φ (G.adjointCoeff U x a)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_zero_evalGaugeJet
declarations.doc:
The zeroth dual coefficient is the dual of the adjoint action of the value of the
jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_zero_evalGaugeJet (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    G.adjointDualCoeff U 0 = (G.adjointRep (G.evalGaugeJet U)).dualMap

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_zero_of_evalGaugeJet_eq_one
declarations.doc: A jet with trivial value has trivial zeroth dual coefficient.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_cons
declarations.doc:
The dual form of `adjointCoeff_cons`. One more derivative of a dual coefficient is
minus the antidiagonal convolution of lower dual coefficients against `ad` of the derived
Maurer–Cartan form.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_cons (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    G.adjointDualCoeff U (μ ::ₘ x) φ =
      -((x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        G.adjointDualCoeff U p.2 (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra
          (G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p.1
            (-G.maurerCartan U μ))))).sum)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_singleton
declarations.doc:
The dual coefficient at a single derivative is minus the underived coefficient
precomposed with `ad` of the base-point Maurer–Cartan form. This is what cancels the
Leibniz cross terms of the gauge law against the commutator cross terms in the field
strength.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_singleton (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    G.adjointDualCoeff U {μ} φ =
      -G.adjointDualCoeff U 0 (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra
        (G.evalLie (-G.maurerCartan U μ)))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_pair
declarations.doc:
The dual coefficient at two derivatives, the underived coefficient against `ad` of the
derived Maurer–Cartan form, and the once-derived coefficient against `ad` of the
Maurer–Cartan form itself.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointDualCoeff_pair (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (ρ μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    G.adjointDualCoeff U (ρ ::ₘ {μ}) φ =
      -G.adjointDualCoeff U 0 (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra
        (G.evalLie (G.derivJ ρ (-G.maurerCartan U μ))))
      - G.adjointDualCoeff U {ρ} (φ ∘ₗ LieAlgebra.ad ℝ G.lieSubalgebra
        (G.evalLie (-G.maurerCartan U μ)))

modules.title: Global gauge groups
modules.doc:
A global gauge group as a closed group of invertible matrices.

## i. Overview

The global gauge group of a gauge theory is presented here as a closed subgroup `G` of the
general linear group `GL(κ, ℂ)`. These are the matrix Lie groups. They include every compact
Lie group, so every gauge group of the Standard Model and its extensions, as well as
non-compact groups such as `Sp(2n, ℝ)`, `SO(p, q)`, `SL(n, ℝ)` and the Lorentz group,
disconnected groups such as `O(n)`, and finite groups. A real group sits inside `GL(κ, ℂ)` as
the real matrices it contains. Lie groups with no faithful finite-dimensional
representation, such as the metaplectic group, are not covered.

Most groups of physical interest are cut out of the matrices by closed conditions, such as
unitarity, a determinant or an invariant bilinear form. Such conditions define a closed
submonoid of matrices, and its invertible elements whose inverses also satisfy the conditions
form a global gauge group, `GlobalGaugeGroup.ofSubmonoid`. The special cases `U(1)`, `SU(n)`,
`SO(n)` and `Sp(n)` are built this way in the files `SO.lean`, `SU.lean`, `Sp.lean` and `U1.lean`.

The Lie algebra of a global gauge group is in the `LieAlgebra` directory.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup` : a closed subgroup of a general linear group.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.ofSubmonoid` : the global gauge group of the invertible elements of a
  closed submonoid of matrices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The structure
- B. Global gauge groups from closed submonoids of matrices

## iv. References

* yang-mills-group, *OpenAI-YM-20261028*, `PublicTheory.lean`, the structure `GaugeGroup`,
  https://github.com/yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028/blob/3456e5e75cf8d4cd558955a5c7638fba2d68f464/PublicTheory.lean#L22-L33

## B. Global gauge groups from closed submonoids of matrices

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup
declarations.doc: A global gauge group, a closed subgroup of the general linear group `GL(κ, ℂ)`.
declarations.statement:
structure GlobalGaugeGroup (κ : Type) [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] where
  /-- The group, as a subgroup of the general linear group. -/
  group : Subgroup (GeneralLinearGroup κ ℂ)
  /-- The group is closed in the general linear group. -/
  isClosed : IsClosed (group : Set (GeneralLinearGroup κ ℂ))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.ofSubmonoid
declarations.doc:
The global gauge group of a closed submonoid `S` of matrices. Its elements are the
invertible matrices which lie in `S` together with their inverses.
declarations.statement:
def ofSubmonoid (S : Submonoid (Matrix κ κ ℂ)) (hS : IsClosed (S : Set (Matrix κ κ ℂ))) :
    GlobalGaugeGroup κ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_ofSubmonoid_iff
GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_ofSubmonoid_iff_of_star_mem
declarations.doc:
For a submonoid of unitary matrices closed under the conjugate transpose, an invertible
matrix lies in its global gauge group exactly when it lies in the submonoid, since its
inverse is then its conjugate transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_ofSubmonoid_iff_of_star_mem {S : Submonoid (Matrix κ κ ℂ)}
    {hS : IsClosed (S : Set (Matrix κ κ ℂ))} (hU : S ≤ unitaryGroup κ ℂ)
    (hstar : ∀ A ∈ S, star A ∈ S) {g : GeneralLinearGroup κ ℂ} :
    g ∈ (ofSubmonoid S hS).group ↔ (g : Matrix κ κ ℂ) ∈ S

declarations.doc:
The group structure of a global gauge group, recorded directly so that instance search
does not pass through the units of the matrices.
declarations.statement: instance (G : GlobalGaugeGroup κ) : Group G.group

modules.title: The jet gauge group of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
The Taylor series at a point of the gauge transformations.

## i. Overview

A gauge transformation with global gauge group `G` is a smooth map from spacetime into `G`.
Its jet at the base point is an invertible matrix of jets `U` with value `U (0)` in `G`.
A map into `GL(κ, ℂ)` starting in `G` stays in `G` exactly when `(∂_μ U) U⁻¹` takes values
in the Lie algebra. The jet gauge group is therefore made of the invertible matrices of jets
with value in `G` and `(∂_μ U) U⁻¹` a Lie algebra jet. On the jet gauge group this is the
Maurer–Cartan form, of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.MaurerCartan`.

That these form a group rests on conjugation by `U` preserving the Lie algebra jets, from
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.LieAlgebra.Jet`,
together with the Leibniz rule for `(∂_μ (U V)) (U V)⁻¹` and `(∂_μ U⁻¹) U`. Evaluation at
the base point is a homomorphism onto `G`, split by the constant gauge transformations.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.gaugeJetGroup` : the jet gauge group.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.evalGaugeJet` : evaluation of a gauge jet at the base point.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.gaugeJetOfConstant` : the jet of a constant gauge transformation.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjoint_mem_jetLieAlgebra` : the jet gauge group acts by conjugation on
  the Lie algebra jets.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The jet gauge group
- B. Evaluation and constant gauge jets
- C. The adjoint action on the Lie algebra jets

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.gaugeJetGroup
declarations.doc:
The jet gauge group, the invertible matrices of jets `U` with value in the group and
`(∂_μ U) U⁻¹` a Lie algebra jet. These are the Taylor series at a point of smooth maps from
spacetime into the group, the gauge transformations seen to all orders. This is not the jet
group of diffeomorphisms of differential geometry.
declarations.statement: def gaugeJetGroup : Subgroup (GeneralLinearGroup κ SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_gaugeJetGroup
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_gaugeJetGroup {U : GeneralLinearGroup κ SpaceTimeAlgebra} :
    U ∈ G.gaugeJetGroup ↔ unitsEval U ∈ G.group ∧ ∀ μ,
      (U : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra).map (pderiv μ) * (↑U⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra)
        ∈ G.jetLieAlgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalGaugeJet
declarations.doc: The value of a gauge jet at the base point, as a homomorphism to the group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def evalGaugeJet : G.gaugeJetGroup →* G.group

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalGaugeJet_val
declarations.statement:
lemma evalGaugeJet_val (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    ((G.evalGaugeJet U).1 : Matrix κ κ ℂ) =
      (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix U.1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.unitsOfConstant_mem_gaugeJetGroup
declarations.doc: The jet of a constant gauge transformation is a gauge jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma unitsOfConstant_mem_gaugeJetGroup {g : GeneralLinearGroup κ ℂ} (hg : g ∈ G.group) :
    unitsOfConstant g ∈ G.gaugeJetGroup

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.gaugeJetOfConstant
declarations.doc: The jet of a constant gauge transformation, as a homomorphism from the group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeJetOfConstant : G.group →* G.gaugeJetGroup

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.gaugeJetOfConstant_val
declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeJetOfConstant_val (g : G.group) :
    ((G.gaugeJetOfConstant g).1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) =
      (C : ℂ →+* SpaceTimeAlgebra).mapMatrix g.1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalGaugeJet_gaugeJetOfConstant
declarations.doc: A constant gauge jet has the constant as its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalGaugeJet_gaugeJetOfConstant (g : G.group) :
    G.evalGaugeJet (G.gaugeJetOfConstant g) = g

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjoint_mem_jetLieAlgebra
declarations.doc: Conjugation `A ↦ U A U⁻¹` by a gauge jet preserves the Lie algebra jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_mem_jetLieAlgebra (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) {A : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra}
    (hA : A ∈ G.jetLieAlgebra) :
    (U.1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * A * (↑U.1⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra)
      ∈ G.jetLieAlgebra

declarations.doc:
The group structure of the gauge jets, recorded directly so that instance search does not
pass through the units of the matrices of jets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Group G.gaugeJetGroup

modules.title: The jet operations of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
The evaluation, derivatives, coordinates and adjoint actions on the jets of a global gauge group.

## i. Overview

A global gauge group `G` has gauge jets, the invertible matrices of jets with value in the
group and Maurer–Cartan form a Lie algebra jet, and Lie algebra jets, the matrices of jets with
every base-point derivative in the Lie algebra. This file gives the operations on them that the
transformation laws of gauge fields and matter fields are built from, as definitions on `G`.
Evaluation of a Lie algebra jet at the base point `G.evalLie` and the inclusion of constants
`G.ofConstantLie` are the entrywise constant coefficient and constant embedding. The derivative
`G.derivJ μ` and multiplication by a coordinate `G.mulCoordJ μ` act entrywise, `G.iteratedDerivJ`
is the iterated derivative, and the adjoint actions `G.adjointJ` of the gauge jets on the Lie
algebra jets and `G.adjointRep` of the group on its Lie algebra are conjugation `U A U⁻¹`. The
Maurer–Cartan form is `G.maurerCartan U μ = (∂_μ U) U⁻¹`. The laws these operations satisfy are
identities of matrices of jets. They include the Maurer–Cartan cocycle law and structure
equation `∂_μ ω_ν − ∂_ν ω_μ = [ω_μ, ω_ν]`, and the Leibniz rule
`∂_μ (U A U⁻¹) = U (∂_μ A) U⁻¹ + [ω_μ, U A U⁻¹]` for the adjoint action. For a compact group
inside the unitary group the hermitian generators of physics are `a = −i X`, with the bracket
`i (a b − b a)` and the Maurer–Cartan form `i (∂_μ U) U⁻¹`.

The jets of a global gauge group are determined by their Taylor data. A Lie algebra jet is
determined by its base-point derivatives, and a gauge jet with vanishing Maurer–Cartan form
is constant. Any Taylor data in `𝔤` are those of a Lie algebra jet, and any Lie algebra jet
`A` vanishing at the base point is the radial component `∑_μ x_μ ω_μ` of the Maurer–Cartan
form of the gauge jet solving `E U = −A U`, `U(0) = 1`. These facts are proved about gauge
jets and Lie algebra jets in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.LieAlgebra.Jet` and
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.MaurerCartan`, and assembled
here.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.ofConstantLie`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ`,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.mulCoordJ`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointJ`,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointRep` : the operations on the jets.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_cocycle`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_structure`,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ_adjointJ` : the laws of the Maurer–Cartan form.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.ext_of_evalLie_iteratedDerivJ`,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_eq` : a Lie algebra jet is determined by its
  base-point derivatives, and every Taylor datum is realised.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Evaluation and constants on Lie algebra jets
- B. Derivatives and coordinates
  - B.1. The iterated derivative
- C. The adjoint actions
- D. The Maurer–Cartan form
  - D.1. First consequences of the laws
- E. Determination by Taylor data

## iv. References

* None.

## E. Determination by Taylor data

A Lie algebra jet is determined by its base-point derivatives, a gauge jet with vanishing
Maurer–Cartan form is constant
(`GlobalGaugeGroup.eq_gaugeJetOfConstant_of_maurerCartan_eq_zero`), every family of Taylor data
in the Lie algebra is that of a Lie algebra jet, and every Lie algebra jet vanishing at the base
point is the radial component of the Maurer–Cartan form of a gauge jet with value one
(`GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_sum_X_smul_maurerCartan_eq`).

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie
declarations.doc: Evaluation of a Lie algebra jet at the base point, the entrywise constant coefficient.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def evalLie : G.jetLieSubalgebra →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ G.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_val
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_val (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    (G.evalLie A).1 = (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix A.1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.ofConstantLie
declarations.doc: A constant Lie algebra element as a Lie algebra jet, the entrywise constant embedding.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofConstantLie : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ G.jetLieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.ofConstantLie_val
declarations.statement:
lemma ofConstantLie_val (a : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (G.ofConstantLie a).1 = (C : ℂ →+* SpaceTimeAlgebra).mapMatrix a.1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_ofConstantLie
declarations.doc: Evaluating the constant Lie algebra jet of `a` at the base point gives back `a`.
declarations.statement: lemma evalLie_ofConstantLie (a : G.lieSubalgebra) : G.evalLie (G.ofConstantLie a) = a

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_surjective
declarations.doc: Every Lie algebra element is the value of a Lie algebra jet, namely its constant jet.
declarations.statement: lemma evalLie_surjective : Function.Surjective G.evalLie

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ
declarations.doc:
The formal derivative `∂_μ` of a Lie algebra jet in the spacetime direction `μ`, taken
entrywise.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivJ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.jetLieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.jetLieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ_val
declarations.statement:
lemma derivJ_val (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    (G.derivJ μ A).1 = A.1.map (pderiv μ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ_comm
declarations.doc: The formal derivatives commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivJ_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.derivJ μ (G.derivJ ν A) = G.derivJ ν (G.derivJ μ A)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ_bracket
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule for the bracket of Lie algebra jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivJ_bracket (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (A B : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.derivJ μ ⁅A, B⁆ = ⁅G.derivJ μ A, B⁆ + ⁅A, G.derivJ μ B⁆

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ_ofConstantLie
declarations.doc: A constant Lie algebra jet has vanishing derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivJ_ofConstantLie (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (a : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    G.derivJ μ (G.ofConstantLie a) = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mulCoordJ
declarations.doc: Multiplication of a Lie algebra jet by the spacetime coordinate `x_μ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def mulCoordJ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.jetLieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.jetLieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mulCoordJ_val
declarations.statement:
lemma mulCoordJ_val (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    (G.mulCoordJ μ A).1 = (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • A.1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ_mulCoordJ
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule for a coordinate, `∂_μ (x_ν A) = x_ν ∂_μ A + δ_{μν} A`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivJ_mulCoordJ (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.derivJ μ (G.mulCoordJ ν A) = G.mulCoordJ ν (G.derivJ μ A) + if μ = ν then A else 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_mulCoordJ
declarations.doc: A multiple of a coordinate vanishes at the base point.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_mulCoordJ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.evalLie (G.mulCoordJ μ A) = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.instRightCommutativeCompDerivJ
declarations.doc: Post-composition with `derivJ` is right-commutative.
declarations.statement:
instance instRightCommutativeCompDerivJ : RightCommutative
    (fun (D : G.jetLieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.jetLieSubalgebra) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) =>
      D.comp (G.derivJ μ))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ
declarations.doc:
The iterated formal derivative on the Lie algebra jets, the product of `derivJ` over a
multiset of directions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iteratedDerivJ (μs : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.jetLieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.jetLieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_zero :
    G.iteratedDerivJ (0 : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_cons (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (μs : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.iteratedDerivJ (μ ::ₘ μs) = (G.derivJ μ).comp (G.iteratedDerivJ μs)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_add
declarations.doc: The iterated derivative is additive in the multiset.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_add (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.iteratedDerivJ (s + t) = (G.iteratedDerivJ s).comp (G.iteratedDerivJ t)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.iteratedDerivJ ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) = G.derivJ μ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_cons_eq_comp_derivJ
declarations.doc: The first derivative in a multiset may be taken first rather than last.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_cons_eq_comp_derivJ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.iteratedDerivJ (μ ::ₘ s) = (G.iteratedDerivJ s).comp (G.derivJ μ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_bracket
declarations.doc: The iterated Leibniz rule for the bracket.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_bracket (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (a b : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.iteratedDerivJ s ⁅a, b⁆ =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => ⁅G.iteratedDerivJ p.1 a, G.iteratedDerivJ p.2 b⁆).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_val
declarations.doc: The iterated derivative is the entrywise iterated formal derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_val (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    (G.iteratedDerivJ s A).1 = A.1.map fun f => iteratedPDeriv s f

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_val
declarations.doc:
The base-point value of the iterated derivative of a Lie algebra jet is its base-point
derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_val (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    (G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s A)).1 = derivValueMatrix s A.1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_ofConstantLie_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc: Every iterated derivative of a constant Lie algebra jet vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_ofConstantLie_of_ne_zero {p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} (hp : p ≠ 0)
    (a : G.lieSubalgebra) : G.iteratedDerivJ p (G.ofConstantLie a) = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_mulCoordJ
declarations.doc: The base-point value of an iterated derivative of a multiple of a coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_mulCoordJ (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (a : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s (G.mulCoordJ μ a)) =
      s.count μ • G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ (s.erase μ) a)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointJ
declarations.doc: The adjoint action `A ↦ U A U⁻¹` of the gauge jets on the Lie algebra jets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjointJ : Representation ℝ G.gaugeJetGroup G.jetLieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointJ_val
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointJ_val (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    (G.adjointJ U A).1 = U.1.1 * A.1 * (U.1⁻¹).1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointRep
declarations.doc: The adjoint action `a ↦ g a g⁻¹` of the group on its Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjointRep : Representation ℝ G.group G.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointRep_val
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointRep_val (g : G.group) (a : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (G.adjointRep g a).1 = g.1.1 * a.1 * (g.1⁻¹).1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointJ_bracket
declarations.doc: The adjoint action of a gauge jet is by Lie algebra automorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointJ_bracket (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (A B : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.adjointJ U ⁅A, B⁆ = ⁅G.adjointJ U A, G.adjointJ U B⁆

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_adjointJ
declarations.doc: At the base point the adjoint action of a gauge jet is the adjoint action of its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_adjointJ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.evalLie (G.adjointJ U A) = G.adjointRep (G.evalGaugeJet U) (G.evalLie A)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_adjointJ_ofConstantLie
declarations.doc:
At the base point, the adjoint action of a gauge jet on a constant is the adjoint action of
its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_adjointJ_ofConstantLie (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (a : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    G.evalLie (G.adjointJ U (G.ofConstantLie a)) = G.adjointRep (G.evalGaugeJet U) a

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_cocycle
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan form is a cocycle for the adjoint action,
`ω_μ(U V) = ω_μ(U) + U ω_μ(V) U⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_cocycle (U V : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.maurerCartan (U * V) μ = G.maurerCartan U μ + G.adjointJ U (G.maurerCartan V μ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_structure
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan structure equation `∂_μ ω_ν − ∂_ν ω_μ = [ω_μ, ω_ν]` in the Lie algebra
jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_structure (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.derivJ μ (G.maurerCartan U ν) - G.derivJ ν (G.maurerCartan U μ) =
      ⁅G.maurerCartan U μ, G.maurerCartan U ν⁆

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ_adjointJ
declarations.doc:
The Leibniz rule for the adjoint action,
`∂_μ (U A U⁻¹) = U (∂_μ A) U⁻¹ + [ω_μ, U A U⁻¹]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivJ_adjointJ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    G.derivJ μ (G.adjointJ U A) =
      G.adjointJ U (G.derivJ μ A) + ⁅G.maurerCartan U μ, G.adjointJ U A⁆

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_inv_adjointJ
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan form of an inverse, `ω_μ(U⁻¹) = − Ad_{U⁻¹} ω_μ(U)`, the cocycle law
applied to `U⁻¹ U = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_inv_adjointJ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.maurerCartan U⁻¹ μ = -G.adjointJ U⁻¹ (G.maurerCartan U μ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivJ_adjointJ_ofConstantLie
declarations.doc:
One derivative of the adjoint action on a constant is the bracket with the Maurer–Cartan
form, the Leibniz rule `derivJ_adjointJ` with the constant's derivative killed.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivJ_adjointJ_ofConstantLie (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (a : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    G.derivJ μ (G.adjointJ U (G.ofConstantLie a)) =
      ⁅G.maurerCartan U μ, G.adjointJ U (G.ofConstantLie a)⁆

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_conj
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan form of a conjugate, by the cocycle law, the conjugating jet
contributes its own form and its transport by the conjugate.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_conj (g U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.maurerCartan (g * U * g⁻¹) μ =
      G.maurerCartan g μ + G.adjointJ g (G.maurerCartan U μ)
        - G.adjointJ (g * U * g⁻¹) (G.maurerCartan g μ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_bracket_congr
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor data of a bracket is determined by that of its arguments.
If the base-point values of the iterated derivatives of `a` and `b` along sub-multisets
of `w` agree with those of `a'` and `b'`, then so do those of the brackets, the iterated
Leibniz rule expands the bracket over the antidiagonal of `w`, whose parts are all
sub-multisets of `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_bracket_congr (w : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (a b a' b' : G.jetLieSubalgebra)
    (ha : ∀ p ≤ w, G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p a) = G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p a'))
    (hb : ∀ p ≤ w, G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p b) = G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p b')) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ w ⁅a, b⁆) = G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ w ⁅a', b'⁆)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.ext_of_evalLie_iteratedDerivJ
declarations.doc: A Lie algebra jet is determined by the base-point values of its iterated derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_of_evalLie_iteratedDerivJ {A B : G.jetLieSubalgebra}
    (h : ∀ s, G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s A) = G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s B)) : A = B

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_eq
declarations.doc:
Every family of Taylor data in the Lie algebra is the family of base-point values of the
iterated derivatives of a Lie algebra jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_eq (c : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → G.lieSubalgebra) :
    ∃ A : G.jetLieSubalgebra, ∀ s, G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s A) = c s

modules.title: The adjoint action of a global gauge group on its Lie algebra
modules.doc:
The action `X ↦ g X g⁻¹` of a global gauge group on its Lie algebra.

## i. Overview

A global gauge group `G` acts on its Lie algebra `𝔤` by conjugation, `X ↦ g X g⁻¹`. This is
the adjoint action, the way an infinitesimal gauge transformation changes under a global
one, and it is how the gauge fields transform under `G`. It maps the one-parameter subgroup
of `X` to the conjugate by `g` of that subgroup, since `exp (t g X g⁻¹) = g exp (t X) g⁻¹`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjoint` : the adjoint action of the group on its Lie algebra.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.oneParameterSubgroup_adjoint` : the one-parameter subgroup of `g X g⁻¹`
  is the conjugate of that of `X`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint action
- B. The adjoint action on one-parameter subgroups

## iv. References

* B. C. Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, 2nd ed., Springer (2015).

sections.text: ## A. The adjoint action
## B. The adjoint action on one-parameter subgroups

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjoint
declarations.doc: The adjoint action `X ↦ g X g⁻¹` of an element `g` of the group on its Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: def adjoint (g : G.group) (X : G.lieAlgebra) : G.lieAlgebra

modules.title: The Lie algebra of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
The generators of the one-parameter subgroups of a global gauge group.

## i. Overview

The Lie algebra `𝔤` of a global gauge group `G ⊆ GL(κ, ℂ)` is determined by the group. It
is the real subspace of matrices `X` whose one-parameter subgroup `t ↦ exp (t X)` lies in
`G`, `Matrix.lieAlgebraOfIsClosed`. That this is a subspace closed under the commutator, and
invariant under conjugation by `G`, is proved there. A finite group has zero Lie algebra. For
a compact group inside the unitary group the generators `X` are anti-hermitian, and the
hermitian generators of physics are `−i X`.

The one-parameter subgroups of the generators are in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.LieAlgebra.OneParameter`,
and the adjoint action of `G` on `𝔤` is in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.LieAlgebra.Adjoint`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.lieAlgebra` : the Lie algebra of a global gauge group.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.lieSubalgebra` : the Lie algebra as a Lie subalgebra of matrices.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lie algebra
- B. The Lie algebra as a Lie subalgebra

## iv. References

* B. C. Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, 2nd ed., Springer (2015).

modules.title: The Lie algebra jets of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
The Taylor series at a point of the infinitesimal gauge transformations.

## i. Overview

An infinitesimal gauge transformation of a global gauge group `G` with Lie algebra `𝔤` is a
smooth map from spacetime into `𝔤`. Its jet at the base point is a matrix of formal power
series in the spacetime coordinates, all of whose base-point derivatives `∂_s A (0)` lie in
`𝔤`. These Lie algebra jets form a Lie algebra under the commutator, since by the Leibniz
rule each base-point derivative of a commutator is a sum of commutators of base-point
derivatives.

Membership is checked through `mem_jetLieAlgebra_of`: a property of matrices of jets that is
preserved by every derivative, and that places the value in `𝔤`, places every base-point
derivative in `𝔤`.

This is how conjugation `A ↦ U⁻¹ A U` by an invertible matrix of jets `U` is shown to
preserve the Lie algebra jets, when the value of `U` lies in the group and `(∂_μ U) U⁻¹` is a
Lie algebra jet. At the base point it is the adjoint action of the group, and the derivative
of `U⁻¹ A U` is `U⁻¹ (∂_μ A − [(∂_μ U) U⁻¹, A]) U`, again of the same form. These are the
facts that make the jet gauge group of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.GaugeJetGroup` a group.

Being a Lie algebra jet is a condition on each Taylor coefficient separately, since the
base-point derivative along `s` is `s!` times the coefficient of `x^s`. So any Taylor data in
`𝔤` give a Lie algebra jet. A matrix of jets `W` solving the linear radial system
`E W + W = B + R W − W R`, for Lie algebra jets `B` and `R` with `R` vanishing at the base
point, is a Lie algebra jet. Here `E = ∑_ρ x_ρ ∂_ρ` is the Euler operator, which multiplies
the coefficient of degree `n` by `n`, so the coefficient of `W` of degree `n` is `1/(n + 1)`
times that of `B` plus commutators of coefficients of `R` with coefficients of `W` of lower
degree. This is how the radial transport of a Lie algebra jet is shown to be a gauge jet.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.jetLieAlgebra` : the Lie algebra jets, as a real subspace.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_jetLieAlgebra_iff` : a matrix of jets is a Lie algebra jet exactly
  when its value lies in the Lie algebra and its derivatives are Lie algebra jets.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_jetLieAlgebra_of` : the induction principle for Lie algebra jets.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.jetLieSubalgebra` : the Lie algebra jets, as a Lie subalgebra.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.inv_mul_mul_mem_jetLieAlgebra` : conjugation by an invertible matrix of
  jets with value in the group and `(∂_μ U) U⁻¹` a Lie algebra jet preserves the Lie algebra
  jets.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.taylorMatrix_mem_jetLieAlgebra` : Taylor data in the Lie algebra give a
  Lie algebra jet.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_jetLieAlgebra_of_euler` : a solution of the linear radial system
  `E W + W = B + R W − W R` with `B`, `R` Lie algebra jets is a Lie algebra jet.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lie algebra jets
- B. Closure properties
- C. Conjugation by invertible matrices of jets
- D. Taylor coefficients and the radial system

## iv. References

* None.

Conjugation `A ↦ U⁻¹ A U` preserves the Lie algebra jets, when the value of `U` lies in
the group and `(∂_μ U) U⁻¹` is a Lie algebra jet. At the base point it is the adjoint
action of the group, and the derivative of `U⁻¹ A U` is again of this form,
`U⁻¹ (∂_μ A − [(∂_μ U) U⁻¹, A]) U`.

declarations.doc:
The Taylor coefficient of `x^p` of the commutator `R W − W R` lies in the Lie algebra when

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_jetLieAlgebra_of_euler
declarations.doc:
A solution of a linear radial system built from Lie algebra jets is a Lie algebra jet. The
system is `E W + W = B + R W − W R` for a matrix of jets `W`, where `B` and `R` are Lie
algebra jets with `R` vanishing at the base point, and `E` is the Euler operator, which
multiplies the coefficient of degree `n` by `n`. The coefficient of `W` of degree `n` is
`1/(n + 1)` times that of `B` plus commutators with coefficients of `W` of lower degree, and
lies in the Lie algebra by induction on `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_jetLieAlgebra_of_euler {W B R : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra}

    (hW : ∑ ρ, (X ρ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • W.map (pderiv ρ) + W = B + (R * W - W * R)) :
    W ∈ G.jetLieAlgebra

modules.title: One-parameter subgroups of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
The one-parameter subgroup `t ↦ exp (t X)` of a generator `X` of a global gauge group.

## i. Overview

By the definition of the Lie algebra `𝔤` of a global gauge group `G`, each generator
`X ∈ 𝔤` has `exp (t X) ∈ G` for every real `t`. This gives a one-parameter subgroup
`t ↦ exp (t X)` of `G`, a continuous homomorphism from the additive group `ℝ` to `G`. In
physics it is the finite gauge transformation built from the infinitesimal one `X`. A
representation of `G` is differentiated along these subgroups in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.DerivRep`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.oneParameterSubgroup` : the one-parameter subgroup of a generator.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.oneParameterSubgroup_add` : it is a homomorphism from `ℝ`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.continuous_oneParameterSubgroup` : it is continuous.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The one-parameter subgroup of a generator
- B. Group and topological properties

## iv. References

* B. C. Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, 2nd ed., Springer (2015).
