modules.title: The Maurer–Cartan form on the jet gauge group
modules.doc:
The Lie algebra jet `(∂_μ U) U⁻¹` of a gauge jet `U`, and its transformation laws.

## i. Overview

Let `G` be a global gauge group. A gauge jet `U`, an element of the jet gauge group, is the
Taylor series at a point of a smooth map from spacetime into `G`. Its Maurer–Cartan form is
`ω_μ = (∂_μ U) U⁻¹`, the pull-back of the right-invariant Maurer–Cartan form of `G`. By the
definition of the jet gauge group it is a Lie algebra jet.

The Maurer–Cartan form vanishes on constant gauge jets. It obeys the cocycle law
`ω(U V) = ω(U) + U ω(V) U⁻¹` and the inversion law `ω(U⁻¹) = −U⁻¹ ω(U) U`. It also governs
how conjugation by `U` interacts with derivatives. For a matrix of jets `A`,
`∂_μ (U⁻¹ A U) = U⁻¹ (∂_μ A − [ω_μ, A]) U`.

A gauge jet with vanishing Maurer–Cartan form has vanishing derivatives, so it is the
constant jet of its value. Conversely every Lie algebra jet `A` vanishing at the base point
is the radial component `∑_μ x_μ ω_μ = −A` of the Maurer–Cartan form of a gauge jet. The jet
is the solution `V` of the radial system `E V = −A V` with `V(0) = 1`, where
`E = ∑_μ x_μ ∂_μ`. Its Maurer–Cartan form solves the linear radial system
`E ω_μ + ω_μ = −∂_μ A − A ω_μ + ω_μ A`, so it is a Lie algebra jet. This is the formal version
of integrating the infinitesimal gauge transformation `A` along rays from the base point.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan` : the Maurer–Cartan form of a gauge jet.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.map_pderiv_eq_maurerCartan_mul` : the derivative `∂_μ U = ω_μ U` of a gauge
  jet.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_mul` : the cocycle law.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_inv` : the inversion law.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.map_pderiv_maurerCartan_sub` : the structure equation
  `∂_μ ω_ν − ∂_ν ω_μ = [ω_μ, ω_ν]`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.map_pderiv_inv_mul_mul` : the derivative of a conjugate.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.eq_gaugeJetOfConstant_of_maurerCartan_eq_zero` : a gauge jet with vanishing
  Maurer–Cartan form is constant.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_sum_X_smul_maurerCartan_eq` : every Lie algebra jet vanishing at
  the base point is the radial component of the Maurer–Cartan form of a gauge jet.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Maurer–Cartan form
- B. Constant gauge jets
- C. The cocycle and inversion laws and the structure equation
- D. The derivative of a conjugate
- E. Gauge jets with vanishing Maurer–Cartan form
- F. Integrating a Lie algebra jet radially

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan form `(∂_μ U) U⁻¹` of a gauge jet `U` in the spacetime direction `μ`,
a Lie algebra jet.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def maurerCartan (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.jetLieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_val
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_val (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (G.maurerCartan U μ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) =
      (U.1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra).map (pderiv μ) *
        (↑U.1⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.map_pderiv_eq_maurerCartan_mul
declarations.doc: The derivative of a gauge jet in terms of its Maurer–Cartan form, `∂_ρ U = ω_ρ(U) U`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_pderiv_eq_maurerCartan_mul (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (U.1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra).map (pderiv ρ) =
      (G.maurerCartan U ρ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * U.1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_gaugeJetOfConstant
declarations.doc: A constant gauge jet has vanishing Maurer–Cartan form.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_gaugeJetOfConstant (g : G.group) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.maurerCartan (G.gaugeJetOfConstant g) μ = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_one
declarations.statement: lemma maurerCartan_one (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : G.maurerCartan 1 μ = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_mul
declarations.doc:
The cocycle law `ω(U V) = ω(U) + U ω(V) U⁻¹` of the Maurer–Cartan form `ω` on the
product of two gauge jets `U` and `V`.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_mul (U V : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (G.maurerCartan (U * V) μ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) =
      G.maurerCartan U μ + (U.1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) *
        G.maurerCartan V μ * (↑U.1⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_inv
declarations.doc:
The inversion law `ω(U⁻¹) = −U⁻¹ ω(U) U` of the Maurer–Cartan form `ω` on the inverse
of a gauge jet `U`.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_inv (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (G.maurerCartan U⁻¹ μ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) =
      -((↑U.1⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * G.maurerCartan U μ * U.1)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.map_pderiv_maurerCartan_sub
declarations.doc:
The Maurer–Cartan structure equation `∂_μ ω_ν − ∂_ν ω_μ = [ω_μ, ω_ν]` for the
Maurer–Cartan form `ω` of a gauge jet. The curl of `ω` is its commutator.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_pderiv_maurerCartan_sub (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (G.maurerCartan U ν : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra).map (pderiv μ) -
        (G.maurerCartan U μ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra).map (pderiv ν) =
      (G.maurerCartan U μ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * G.maurerCartan U ν -
        (G.maurerCartan U ν : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * G.maurerCartan U μ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.map_pderiv_inv_mul_mul
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the conjugate `U⁻¹ A U` of a matrix of jets by a gauge jet, in terms of
the Maurer–Cartan form `ω_μ` of `U`, `∂_μ (U⁻¹ A U) = U⁻¹ (∂_μ A − [ω_μ, A]) U`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_pderiv_inv_mul_mul (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (A : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ((↑U.1⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * A * U.1).map (pderiv μ) =
      (↑U.1⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * (A.map (pderiv μ) -
        ((G.maurerCartan U μ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * A -
          A * G.maurerCartan U μ)) * U.1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.eq_gaugeJetOfConstant_of_maurerCartan_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A gauge jet with vanishing Maurer–Cartan form is the constant gauge jet of its value, since
its derivatives `∂_μ U = ω_μ U` vanish.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_gaugeJetOfConstant_of_maurerCartan_eq_zero {U : G.gaugeJetGroup}
    (h : ∀ μ, G.maurerCartan U μ = 0) : U = G.gaugeJetOfConstant (G.evalGaugeJet U)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_gaugeJetGroup_of_eulerTransport
declarations.doc:
Radially integrating a Lie algebra jet gives a gauge jet. An invertible matrix of jets with
value one at the base point which solves the radial system `E V = −A V`, for a Lie algebra
jet `A` vanishing at the base point, is a gauge jet. Here `E` is the Euler operator, which
multiplies the part of each degree by that degree.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_gaugeJetGroup_of_eulerTransport {A : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra}
    (hA : A ∈ G.jetLieAlgebra) (hA0 : (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix A = 0)
    {V : GeneralLinearGroup κ SpaceTimeAlgebra}
    (hV0 : (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix (V : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) = 1)
    (hEV : ∑ μ, (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • (V : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra).map (pderiv μ) =
      -A * V) :
    V ∈ G.gaugeJetGroup

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_sum_X_smul_maurerCartan_eq
declarations.doc:
Every Lie algebra jet vanishing at the base point is, up to sign, the radial component of
the Maurer–Cartan form of a gauge jet with value one. In symbols, `∑_μ x_μ (∂_μ U) U⁻¹ = −A`
for the Lie algebra jet `A`. The gauge jet is the solution `U` of the radial system
`E U = −A U` with `U(0) = 1`, where `E` is the Euler operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_sum_X_smul_maurerCartan_eq {A : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra}
    (hA : A ∈ G.jetLieAlgebra) (hA0 : (constantCoeff : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* ℂ).mapMatrix A = 0) :
    ∃ U : G.gaugeJetGroup, G.evalGaugeJet U = 1 ∧
      ∑ μ, (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • (G.maurerCartan U μ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) = -A

modules.title: The product of global gauge groups
modules.doc:
The product `G₁ × G₂` of two global gauge groups, acting block-diagonally.

## i. Overview

The gauge group of a theory with several independent gauge interactions is a product of
groups, such as `SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)` for the Standard Model. For global gauge groups
`G₁ ⊆ GL(κ₁, ℂ)` and `G₂ ⊆ GL(κ₂, ℂ)` the product sits inside `GL(κ₁ ⊕ κ₂, ℂ)` as the
block-diagonal matrices `diag(g₁, g₂)` with `g₁ ∈ G₁` and `g₂ ∈ G₂`. Taking the two diagonal
blocks is a continuous left inverse of `(A₁, A₂) ↦ diag(A₁, A₂)`, so this embedding is
closed, and so is the induced embedding of pairs of invertible matrices. The product group is
the image of the closed set `G₁ × G₂` under it, and so it is closed.

The Lie algebra of the product is the direct sum of the Lie algebras. A block-diagonal
matrix `diag(X₁, X₂)` of generators is a generator of the product, since the exponential of
a block-diagonal matrix is taken blockwise. Conversely, the one-parameter subgroup of a
generator of the product lies in the closed subspace of block-diagonal matrices, so the
generator, its derivative at `t = 0`, does too, and its diagonal blocks are generators.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.prod` : the product of two global gauge groups.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_prod_iff` : the elements of the product are the block-diagonal
  matrices `diag(g₁, g₂)` with `g₁ ∈ G₁` and `g₂ ∈ G₂`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.prodGroupEquiv` : the elements of the product are the pairs of elements of
  the factors.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.exp_smul_eq_fromBlocks_of_mem_lieAlgebra_prod` : the exponential of a
  generator of the product is taken blockwise.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_lieAlgebra_prod_iff` : the generators of the product are the
  block-diagonal matrices of generators.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The product of global gauge groups
  - A.1. Pairs of elements
- B. The Lie algebra of the product
  - B.1. The generators of the product

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The global gauge group SO(n)
modules.doc:
The special orthogonal group, as a global gauge group.

## i. Overview

The special orthogonal group `SO(n)` is the group of real orthogonal `n × n` matrices of
determinant one, the rotations of `ℝⁿ`. It appears as a gauge group in grand unified
theories, such as `SO(10)`. A global gauge group sits inside `GL(n, ℂ)`, and there `SO(n)`
is the group of real matrices in `SU(n)`. A real matrix `B` is unitary exactly when
`Bᵀ B = 1`, and has determinant one as a complex matrix exactly when it does as a real one.

The real matrices are the image of the entrywise embedding `ℝ → ℂ`. This embedding has the
entrywise real part as a continuous left inverse, so its image is closed, and the real
matrices in `SU(n)` form a closed submonoid. The conjugate transpose of a real matrix is its
transpose, again real, so the submonoid is closed under the conjugate transpose.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.realSpecialOrthogonalGroup` : the real special orthogonal matrices, as
  complex matrices.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.ofReal_mem_realSpecialOrthogonalGroup_iff` : a real matrix lies in it
  exactly when it is orthogonal of determinant one.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.SO` : the global gauge group `SO(n)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_SO_iff` : an invertible matrix lies in `SO(n)` exactly when it is a
  real orthogonal matrix of determinant one.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The real special orthogonal matrices
- B. Real matrices
- C. Membership in the real special orthogonal matrices
- D. The group SO(n)

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The global gauge group Sp(n)
modules.doc:
The compact symplectic group, as a global gauge group.

## i. Overview

The compact symplectic group `Sp(n)`, also written `USp(2n)`, is the group of unitary
`2n × 2n` complex matrices `A` which preserve the standard symplectic form `J`,
`A J Aᵀ = J`. It is the compact real form of the complex symplectic group, and it appears as
a gauge group in grand unified and supersymmetric theories. Here `Sp(1)` is `SU(2)`.

Unitarity and the symplectic condition are both closed, so the compact symplectic matrices
form a closed submonoid of matrices. The conjugate transpose of a unitary matrix is its
inverse, and the inverse of a symplectic matrix is symplectic, so the submonoid is closed
under the conjugate transpose. An invertible matrix therefore lies in the global gauge
group `Sp(n)` exactly when it is unitary and symplectic.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.compactSymplecticGroup` : the unitary symplectic matrices.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.Sp` : the global gauge group `Sp(n)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_Sp_iff` : an invertible matrix lies in `Sp(n)` exactly when it is
  unitary and symplectic.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The group Sp(n)
- B. Membership

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The global gauge group SU(n)
modules.doc:
The special unitary group, as a global gauge group.

## i. Overview

The gauge groups of the strong and weak interactions are `SU(3)` and `SU(2)`, and `SU(n)`
is the gauge group of Yang–Mills theory with `n` colours. It is the group of unitary
`n × n` complex matrices of determinant one. Both conditions are closed, so `SU(n)` is a
closed submonoid of matrices. It is closed under the conjugate transpose, which is the
inverse of a unitary matrix, so an invertible matrix lies in the global gauge group `SU(n)`
exactly when it is special unitary.

Every traceless anti-hermitian matrix `X` is a generator of `SU(n)`. The exponential
`exp (t X)` is unitary, its conjugate transpose being `exp (−t X)`, and has determinant
`exp (t tr X) = 1`. The hermitian generators of physics, such as the Gell-Mann matrices for
`SU(3)`, are `−i X`.

The scalar matrices in `SU(n)` are the multiples of the identity by an `n`-th root of unity.
They form the centre `ℤ_n` of `SU(n)`, generated by the multiple of the identity by the primitive
root of unity `exp (2 π i / n)`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.SU` : the global gauge group `SU(n)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_SU_iff` : an invertible matrix lies in `SU(n)` exactly when it is
  unitary of determinant one.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_lieAlgebra_SU` : traceless anti-hermitian matrices are generators of
  `SU(n)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.trace_eq_zero_of_mem_lieAlgebra_SU` : generators of `SU(n)` are traceless.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.centreGenerator` : the generator of the centre `ℤ_n` of `SU(n)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The group SU(n)
- B. The Lie algebra of SU(n)
- C. The centre of SU(n)

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The adjoint representation of `SU(N)`
modules.doc:
The action of `SU(N)` on its complexified Lie algebra, and its matrix in the Gell-Mann basis.

## i. Overview

The adjoint representation of `SU(N)` acts on the complexified Lie algebra
`SUAlgebraComplexified N = ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(N)` as the complexification of the conjugation action
`X ↦ g X g⁻¹` on `su(N)` (A). The generalized Gell-Mann matrices, a real basis of `su(N)`, give the
basis `adjBasis N` of the complexified Lie algebra. Sending `z ⊗ X` to the matrix `z X` identifies
the complexified Lie algebra with the traceless complex matrices (`adjMat`), injectively
(`adjMat_injective`) and onto (`adjMat_ofTraceless`), and on matrices the adjoint action is
conjugation (`adjMat_adjRep`). The coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis are the trace pairings
`tr (λ_a A) / 2`.

In the Gell-Mann basis the adjoint action of `g` has the matrix `adjMatrix g`, with entries
`tr (λ_a g λ_b g⁻¹) / 2`: real, the Gell-Mann matrices being hermitian, and orthogonal, the matrix
of `g⁻¹` being the transpose (B).

The trace form `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)` is symmetric and nondegenerate, the trace pairing with a Gell-Mann
matrix being twice the coordinate, and it is invariant under the adjoint action, so it is the
contraction `adjContr` of two adjoint indices (C).

For two distinct coordinates `p` and `q`, an element `U` of `SU(2)` acts on the plane they span
and fixes the other coordinates. This is `SU.planeEmbed p q`, a group homomorphism from `SU(2)`
to `SU(N)` (D), built from the plane matrices of
`PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.ForMathlib.DataStructures.Matrix.PlaneMatrix`. A diagonal phase
`diag (u, ū)` and the rotation by a quarter turn, embedded in every plane, force a matrix commuting
with all of `SU(N)` to be scalar (E). The matrix `adjMat A` of an invariant of the adjoint
representation commutes with every element of `SU(N)`, so it is a scalar, and it is traceless, so
the adjoint representation has no invariants but zero (F).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.adjRep` : the adjoint representation on the complexified Lie algebra.
- `suTensor.adjMat` : the complexified Lie algebra as traceless complex matrices.
- `suTensor.adjMatrix` : the matrix of the adjoint action in the Gell-Mann basis.
- `suTensor.adjMatrix_inv` : the matrix of `g⁻¹` is the transpose of that of `g`.
- `suTensor.traceForm_nondegenerate` : the trace form is nondegenerate.
- `suTensor.adjContr` : the contraction of two adjoint indices.
- `SU.planeEmbed` : `SU(2)` acting on the plane of two coordinates, as a subgroup of `SU(N)`.
- `SU.eq_smul_one_of_commute` : a matrix commuting with `SU(N)` is scalar.
- `suTensor.invariants_adjRep_eq_bot` : the adjoint representation has no invariants but zero.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The adjoint representation on the complexified Lie algebra
- B. The matrix of the adjoint action
- C. The trace form and the contraction
- D. The plane embedding of `SU(2)`
- E. Matrices commuting with `SU(N)`
- F. One adjoint index has no invariants

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The adjoint representation on the complexified Lie algebra
## B. The matrix of the adjoint action
## C. The trace form and the contraction
## D. The plane embedding of `SU(2)`

## E. Matrices commuting with `SU(N)`

The diagonal phase `diag (i, -i)` in the plane of `p` and `q` negates the entries at `(p, q)`
and `(q, p)` of a matrix it commutes with, and the quarter turn exchanges the diagonal entries
at `p` and `q`.

## F. One adjoint index has no invariants

An invariant of the adjoint representation is a traceless matrix commuting with every element of
`SU(N)`, so it is a scalar by E, and its trace vanishes.

declarations.name: SU
declarations.doc: The gauge group `SU(n)`, the special unitary matrices.
declarations.statement: abbrev SU (n : ℕ) : Type

declarations.name: SUAlgebra
declarations.doc: The Lie algebra `su(n)`, the traceless hermitian matrices.
declarations.statement: abbrev SUAlgebra (n : ℕ) : Type

declarations.name: SUAlgebra.adjointValue
declarations.doc: The adjoint action `a ↦ U a U†` of `SU(n)` on `su(n)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def SUAlgebra.adjointValue {n : ℕ} : Representation ℝ (SU n) (SUAlgebra n)

declarations.name: SUAlgebra.adjointValue_val
declarations.statement:
lemma SUAlgebra.adjointValue_val {n : ℕ} (U : SU n) (a : SUAlgebra n) :
    (SUAlgebra.adjointValue U a).1 = U.1 * a.1 * star U.1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjBasis
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann basis `1 ⊗ λ_a` of the complexified Lie algebra `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjBasis : Basis (GellMann.Index N) ℂ (SUAlgebraComplexified N)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjBasis_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma adjBasis_apply (a : GellMann.Index N) :
    adjBasis N a = (1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] GellMann.realBasis a

declarations.name: suTensor.val_inv_mul_val
declarations.statement: lemma val_inv_mul_val (g : SU N) : (g⁻¹).1 * g.1 = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.val_inv
declarations.statement: lemma val_inv (g : SU N) : (g⁻¹).1 = star g.1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjRep
declarations.doc:
The adjoint representation on the complexified Lie algebra, the complexification of the
adjoint action `X ↦ g X g⁻¹` on `su(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjRep : Representation ℂ (SU N) (SUAlgebraComplexified N)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat
declarations.doc:
The matrix of an element of the complexified Lie algebra, `z ⊗ X ↦ z X`, a traceless complex
matrix.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjMat : SUAlgebraComplexified N →ₗ[ℂ] Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_tmul
declarations.statement: lemma adjMat_tmul (z : ℂ) (X : SUAlgebra N) : adjMat N (z ⊗ₜ X) = z • X.1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_adjBasis
declarations.statement: lemma adjMat_adjBasis (a : GellMann.Index N) : adjMat N (adjBasis N a) = GellMann.matrix a

declarations.name: suTensor.trace_adjMat
declarations.doc: The matrix of an element of the complexified Lie algebra is traceless.
declarations.statement: lemma trace_adjMat (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) : (adjMat N A).trace = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_adjRep
declarations.doc: The adjoint representation moves the matrix by conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMat_adjRep (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    adjMat N (adjRep N g A) = g.1 * adjMat N A * (g⁻¹).1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjBasis_repr_apply
declarations.doc:
The coordinates in the Gell-Mann basis are read off by the trace form,
`A = ∑ (tr (λ_a A) / 2) λ_a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjBasis_repr_apply (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (a : GellMann.Index N) :
    (adjBasis N).repr A a = (GellMann.matrix a * adjMat N A).trace / 2

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_injective
declarations.doc: An element of the complexified Lie algebra is determined by its matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma adjMat_injective : Function.Injective (adjMat N)

declarations.name: suTensor.ofTraceless
declarations.doc: The element of the complexified Lie algebra with a given traceless matrix.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofTraceless (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) : SUAlgebraComplexified N

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_ofTraceless
declarations.doc: Every traceless matrix is the matrix of an element of the complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMat_ofTraceless {M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ} (hM : M.trace = 0) :
    adjMat N (ofTraceless M) = M

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMatrix
declarations.doc: The matrix, in the Gell-Mann basis, of the adjoint action of an element of `SU(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev adjMatrix (g : SU N) : Matrix (GellMann.Index N) (GellMann.Index N) ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMatrix_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of the matrix of the adjoint action, `tr (λ_a g λ_b g⁻¹) / 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMatrix_apply (g : SU N) (a b : GellMann.Index N) :
    adjMatrix g a b = (GellMann.matrix a * (g.1 * GellMann.matrix b * (g⁻¹).1)).trace / 2

declarations.name: suTensor.star_adjMatrix_apply
declarations.doc: The matrix of the adjoint action is real, the Gell-Mann matrices being hermitian.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_adjMatrix_apply (g : SU N) (a b : GellMann.Index N) :
    star (adjMatrix g a b) = adjMatrix g a b

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMatrix_inv
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of the inverse of an element of `SU(N)` is the transpose of
that of the element, by the cyclicity of the trace.
declarations.statement: lemma adjMatrix_inv (g : SU N) : adjMatrix g⁻¹ = (adjMatrix g)ᵀ

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMatrix_inv_mul
declarations.doc:
The matrix of the adjoint action of the inverse of an element of `SU(N)` times that of the
element is the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma adjMatrix_inv_mul (g : SU N) : adjMatrix g⁻¹ * adjMatrix g = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm
declarations.doc: The trace form `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)` on the complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def traceForm : LinearMap.BilinForm ℂ (SUAlgebraComplexified N)

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma traceForm_apply (A B : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    traceForm N A B = (adjMat N A * adjMat N B).trace

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_isSymm
declarations.doc: The trace form is symmetric.
declarations.statement: lemma traceForm_isSymm : (traceForm N).IsSymm

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_adjBasis
declarations.doc: The trace form against a Gell-Mann basis vector is twice the coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceForm_adjBasis (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (a : GellMann.Index N) :
    traceForm N A (adjBasis N a) = 2 * (adjBasis N).repr A a

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_separatingLeft
declarations.doc:
An element orthogonal to every element under the trace form vanishes. Its coordinates are its
trace pairings with the Gell-Mann basis.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceForm_separatingLeft (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (hA : ∀ B, traceForm N A B = 0) :
    A = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_nondegenerate
declarations.doc: The trace form is nondegenerate on the complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: lemma traceForm_nondegenerate : (traceForm N).Nondegenerate

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContr
declarations.doc: The contraction of two adjoint indices, the trace form `A ⊗ B ↦ tr (A B)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjContr : ((adjRep N).tprod (adjRep N)).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℂ (SU N) ℂ)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContr_flip_injective
declarations.doc: The trace form separates the complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjContr_flip_injective :
    Function.Injective (TensorProduct.curry (adjContr N).toLinearMap).flip

declarations.name: SU.planeEmbed
declarations.doc:
`SU(2)` acting on the plane of two distinct coordinates `p` and `q` and trivially on the
others, a homomorphism from `SU(2)` to `SU(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def planeEmbed (p q : Fin N) (hpq : p ≠ q) : SU 2 →* SU N

declarations.name: SU.planeEmbed_val
declarations.statement: lemma planeEmbed_val (hpq : p ≠ q) (U : SU 2) : (planeEmbed p q hpq U).1 = planeMatrix p q U.1

declarations.name: SU.diagPhase
declarations.doc: The diagonal element `diag (u, ū)` of `SU(2)`, for any complex number `u` of modulus one.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagPhase (u : ℂ) (hu : u * star u = 1) : SU 2

declarations.name: SU.diagPhase_val
declarations.statement:
lemma diagPhase_val (u : ℂ) (hu : u * star u = 1) :
    (diagPhase u hu).1 = diagonal ![u, star u]

declarations.name: SU.rotation
declarations.doc:
The real rotation of `SU(2)` with matrix `!![c, -s; s, c]`, for any real cosine `c` and sine
`s` with `c² + s² = 1`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rotation (c s : ℝ) (h : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) : SU 2

declarations.name: SU.rotation_val
declarations.statement:
lemma rotation_val (c s : ℝ) (h : c ^ 2 + s ^ 2 = 1) :
    (rotation c s h).1 = !![(c : ℂ), -s; s, c]

declarations.name: SU.conj_eq_of_commute
declarations.doc: A matrix commuting with every element of `SU(N)` is fixed by conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_eq_of_commute {C : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ} (hC : ∀ g : SU N, g.1 * C = C * g.1)
    (g : SU N) : g.1 * C * g.1ᴴ = C

declarations.name: SU.apply_eq_of_commute
declarations.doc:
A matrix commuting with every element of `SU(N)` is diagonal, with equal diagonal
entries.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_eq_of_commute {C : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ} (hC : ∀ g : SU N, g.1 * C = C * g.1)
    (hpq : p ≠ q) : C p q = 0 ∧ C p p = C q q

declarations.name: SU.eq_smul_one_of_commute
declarations.doc: A matrix commuting with every element of `SU(N)` is scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_smul_one_of_commute {C : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ}
    (hC : ∀ g : SU N, g.1 * C = C * g.1) : ∃ z : ℂ, C = z • 1

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_adjRep_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
The adjoint representation has no invariants but zero. The matrix of an invariant commutes
with every element of `SU(N)`, so it is a scalar, and its trace vanishes.
declarations.statement: lemma invariants_adjRep_eq_bot : (adjRep N).invariants = ⊥

modules.title: The Lie algebra `su(n)` over a `*`-algebra
modules.doc:
The traceless hermitian matrices over a `*`-algebra, with the bracket `i (a b − b a)`.

## i. Overview

The Lie algebra of `SU(n)` is the real Lie algebra of traceless hermitian `n × n` matrices,
with bracket `⁅a, b⁆ = i (a b − b a)`. The factor of `i` keeps the bracket of two hermitian
matrices hermitian. Nothing in this description depends on the entries being complex
numbers, and it makes sense over any commutative `*`-algebra `R` over `ℂ`, and the two cases the
theory of jets needs are `R = ℂ` (the Lie algebra itself) and `R` the ring of formal power
series in the spacetime coordinates (its jets). `SUAlgebraOver R n` is this Lie algebra,
together with the conjugation action `a ↦ U a U†` of the unitary group of `R`.

Over `R = ℂ` the Lie algebra is real, since `i` times a hermitian matrix is anti-hermitian. Its
complexification `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(n)` is `SUAlgebraComplexified n`, the complex vector space on which
the adjoint representation of `SU(n)` acts in the complex tensors of `SU(n)`.

## ii. Key results

- `SUAlgebraOver` : the traceless hermitian matrices as a real Lie algebra.
- `SUAlgebraOver.conj` : the conjugation representation of the unitary group.
- `SUAlgebraComplexified` : the complexification of `su(n)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Traceless hermitian matrices
- B. The conjugation representation
- C. The bracket
- D. The complexification

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.submodule
declarations.doc: The submodule of traceless hermitian matrices.

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra `su(n)` over `R`, the traceless hermitian `n × n` matrices with entries in
`R`, a real Lie algebra with bracket `i (a b − b a)`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev SUAlgebraOver (R : Type) [CommRing R] [StarRing R] [Algebra ℝ R] [StarModule ℝ R]
    (n : ℕ) : Type

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.mem_iff
declarations.doc: A matrix lies in the real Lie algebra `su(n)` exactly when it is hermitian and traceless.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_iff (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) :
    A ∈ submodule R n ↔ star A = A ∧ A.trace = 0

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.ofMatrix
declarations.doc: An element from a traceless hermitian matrix.
declarations.statement:
def ofMatrix (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) (hA : star A = A) (hT : A.trace = 0) :
    SUAlgebraOver R n

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.ofMatrix_val
declarations.statement:
lemma ofMatrix_val (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R) (hA : star A = A) (hT : A.trace = 0) :
    (ofMatrix A hA hT).1 = A

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.star_val
declarations.doc: Every element of `su(n)`, viewed as a matrix, is hermitian.
declarations.statement: lemma star_val (a : SUAlgebraOver R n) : star a.1 = a.1

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.trace_val
declarations.doc: Every element of `su(n)`, viewed as a matrix, is traceless.
declarations.statement: lemma trace_val (a : SUAlgebraOver R n) : a.1.trace = 0

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.ext
declarations.doc: Two elements of `su(n)` are equal when their underlying matrices are equal.
declarations.statement: lemma ext {a b : SUAlgebraOver R n} (h : a.1 = b.1) : a = b

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.conj
declarations.doc: The conjugation representation of the unitary group on `su(n)`, `a ↦ U a U†`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def conj : Representation ℝ (unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (SUAlgebraOver R n)

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.conj_apply_val
declarations.statement:
lemma conj_apply_val (U : unitaryGroup (Fin n) R) (a : SUAlgebraOver R n) :
    (conj U a).1 = U.1 * a.1 * star U.1

declarations.doc: The bracket `i (a b − b a)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Bracket (SUAlgebraOver R n) (SUAlgebraOver R n)

declarations.name: SUAlgebraOver.bracket_val
declarations.doc: The matrix of the bracket of two elements of `su(n)` is `i` times their commutator.
declarations.statement:
lemma bracket_val (a b : SUAlgebraOver R n) :
    ⁅a, b⁆.1 = Complex.I • (a.1 * b.1 - b.1 * a.1)
noncomputable instance : LieRing (SUAlgebraOver R n)
noncomputable instance : LieAlgebra ℝ (SUAlgebraOver R n)

modules.title: The eigenspaces of the centre of `SU(N)`
modules.doc:
The subspaces on which the central element `ω 1` of `SU(N)` acts by a scalar, and the tensors of
`SU(N)` with no invariants for that reason.

## i. Overview

The centre of `SU(N)` is generated by `ω 1`, for `ω` a primitive `N`-th root of unity
(`GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.centreGenerator`). `centreEigenspace` names the subspace on which it acts by
a scalar `ε` (A). For a representation on an algebra by algebra maps the scalar of a product is the
product of the scalars (B), and a vector that the group fixes and that lies in an eigenspace with
`ε ≠ 1` is zero, also modulo a stable submodule `S` (C).

The element `ω 1` acts on a fundamental index by `ω`, on an anti-fundamental index by `ω̄ = ω⁻¹`
and on an adjoint index by `1`, so on the tensors with colours `c` by `ω` to the number of
fundamental minus anti-fundamental colours of `c` (D). When this power is not one there are no
invariant tensors but zero. For `N ≥ 3` this is the case for two fundamental, or two
anti-fundamental, indices, `ω² ≠ 1` (E).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.centreEigenspace` : the subspace on which the centre acts by `ε`.
- `suTensor.mul_le_centreEigenspace` : the scalar of a product is the product of the scalars.
- `suTensor.mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace` : a subspace on which the centre acts by
  `ε ≠ 1` carries no invariant beyond a stable submodule `S`.
- `suTensor.tensorRep_centreGenerator` : the centre acts on the tensors by `ω` to the number of
  fundamental minus anti-fundamental colours.
- `suTensor.invariants_eq_bot_of_zpow_ne_one` : the tensors on which the centre does not act
  trivially have no invariants but zero.
- `suTensor.invariants_fund_pow_two_eq_bot` : for `N ≥ 3` there are no invariant tensors with two
  fundamental indices but zero, and its anti-fundamental twin.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The eigenspaces of the centre
- B. Scalars multiply
- C. The classification modulo a stable submodule
- D. The centre on the tensors
- E. Tensors with no invariants

## iv. References

The same pattern for `SL(2,ℂ)` is
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Invariants.CentreEigenspace`.

declarations.name: suTensor.centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: The subspace on which the central element `ω 1` of `SU(N)` acts by the scalar `ε`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def centreEigenspace (hN : N ≠ 0) (ρ : Representation ℂ (SU N) V) (ε : ℂ) :
    Submodule ℂ V

declarations.name: suTensor.mem_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc: Membership of `centreEigenspace` unfolded: the centre scales the vector by `ε`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_centreEigenspace {hN : N ≠ 0} {ρ : Representation ℂ (SU N) V} {ε : ℂ} {x : V} :
    x ∈ centreEigenspace hN ρ ε ↔ ρ (centreGenerator N hN) x = ε • x

declarations.name: suTensor.dual_centreGenerator_eq_smul_id
declarations.doc: Dualising a representation inverts the scalar by which the centre acts.

declarations.name: suTensor.mul_le_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc:
For a representation by multiplicative maps, the scalar of a product is the product of the
scalars.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_le_centreEigenspace {hN : N ≠ 0} {ρ : Representation ℂ (SU N) A}
    (hmul : ∀ (g : SU N) (x y : A), ρ g (x * y) = ρ g x * ρ g y)
    {W₁ W₂ : Submodule ℂ A} {ε₁ ε₂ : ℂ} (h₁ : W₁ ≤ centreEigenspace hN ρ ε₁)
    (h₂ : W₂ ≤ centreEigenspace hN ρ ε₂) :
    W₁ * W₂ ≤ centreEigenspace hN ρ (ε₁ * ε₂)

declarations.name: suTensor.mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace
declarations.doc:
A subspace on which the centre acts by `ε ≠ 1` carries no invariant beyond a stable submodule
`S`: an invariant of the join with `S` already lies in `S`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace {hN : N ≠ 0} {ρ : Representation ℂ (SU N) V}
    {ε : ℂ} (hε : ε ≠ 1) {W : Submodule ℂ V} (hW : W ≤ centreEigenspace hN ρ ε)
    (S : Submodule ℂ V) (hS : ∀ g : SU N, ∀ y ∈ S, ρ g y ∈ S) {x : V} (hx : x ∈ W ⊔ S)
    (hinv : ∀ g : SU N, ρ g x = x) : x ∈ S

declarations.name: suTensor.centreScalar
declarations.doc:
The scalar by which the centre acts on a colour: `ω` on the fundamental colour, `ω̄` on the
anti-fundamental colour and `1` on the adjoint colour.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def centreScalar (N : ℕ) : Color → ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.rep_centreGenerator
declarations.doc: The centre acts on the representation of each colour by its scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma rep_centreGenerator (hN : N ≠ 0) (k : Color) (v : modules N k) :
    rep N k (centreGenerator N hN) v = centreScalar N k • v

declarations.name: suTensor.tensorRep_centreGenerator
declarations.doc:
The centre acts on the tensors with colours `c` by `ω` to the number of fundamental minus
anti-fundamental colours of `c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorRep_centreGenerator (hN : N ≠ 0) {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → Color) :
    (suTensor N).tensorRep c (centreGenerator N hN) =
      rootOfUnity N ^ (((Finset.univ.filter fun i => c i = .fund).card : ℤ) -
        (Finset.univ.filter fun i => c i = .antiFund).card) • LinearMap.id

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_eq_bot_of_zpow_ne_one
declarations.doc:
When the centre does not act trivially on the tensors with colours `c`, there are no invariant
tensors but zero: an invariant tensor is fixed by the centre and scaled by a scalar `≠ 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_eq_bot_of_zpow_ne_one (hN : N ≠ 0) {n : ℕ} {c : Fin n → Color}
    (h : rootOfUnity N ^ (((Finset.univ.filter fun i => c i = .fund).card : ℤ) -
      (Finset.univ.filter fun i => c i = .antiFund).card) ≠ 1) :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep c).invariants = ⊥

declarations.name: suTensor.rootOfUnity_sq_ne_one
declarations.statement: lemma rootOfUnity_sq_ne_one (hN : 3 ≤ N) : rootOfUnity N ^ 2 ≠ 1

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_fund_pow_two_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
For `N ≥ 3` there are no invariant tensors with two fundamental indices but zero. The centre
scales them by `ω² ≠ 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_fund_pow_two_eq_bot (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep fun _ : Fin 2 => .fund).invariants = ⊥

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_antiFund_pow_two_eq_bot
declarations.doc:
For `N ≥ 3` there are no invariant tensors with two anti-fundamental indices but zero. The
centre scales them by `ω⁻² ≠ 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_antiFund_pow_two_eq_bot (hN : 3 ≤ N) :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep fun _ : Fin 2 => .antiFund).invariants = ⊥

declarations.name: suTensor.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_span_fund
declarations.doc:
For `N ≥ 3` and a family with two fundamental labels whose map is equivariant, the
invariants of the span reduce to `⊥`.

declarations.name: suTensor.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_span_antiFund
declarations.doc:
For `N ≥ 3` and a family with two anti-fundamental labels whose map is equivariant, the
invariants of the span reduce to `⊥`.

modules.title: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices
modules.doc:
A basis of the traceless complex matrices generalizing the Pauli and the Gell-Mann matrices.

## i. Overview

The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are the standard basis of the traceless complex `N × N`
matrices, the complexified Lie algebra of `SU(N)`, generalizing the Pauli matrices (`N = 2`) and
the Gell-Mann matrices (`N = 3`). There are `N² - 1` of them, of three kinds:

- for `j < k` the symmetric matrix `E_jk + E_kj`,
- for `j < k` the antisymmetric matrix `-i E_jk + i E_kj`,
- for `1 ≤ n ≤ N - 1` the diagonal matrix `√(2 / (n (n + 1))) (E_00 + ⋯ + E_(n-1)(n-1) - n E_nn)`.

They are hermitian and traceless, and orthogonal under the trace form, `tr (λ_a λ_b) = 2 δ_ab`.
Orthogonality makes them linearly independent, and there are as many as the dimension of the
traceless matrices, so they form a basis, `GellMann.basis`, whose coordinates are read off by the
trace form, `GellMann.basis_repr_apply`. Being hermitian they lie in the real Lie algebra `su(N)`
of traceless hermitian matrices, and there they form a real basis, `GellMann.realBasis`: the
coordinates `tr (λ_a H) / 2` of a traceless hermitian matrix `H` are real (E).

## ii. Key results

- `GellMann.Index` : the labels of the generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
- `GellMann.matrix` : the generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
- `GellMann.trace_matrix_mul_matrix` : `tr (λ_a λ_b) = 2 δ_ab`.
- `GellMann.basis` : the basis of the traceless matrices they form.
- `GellMann.realBasis` : the basis of the real Lie algebra `su(N)` they form.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The matrices
- B. The diagonal profiles
- C. Orthogonality
- D. The basis
- E. The real basis of `su(N)`

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The diagonal profiles

declarations.name: GellMann.Index
declarations.doc:
The labels of the generalized Gell-Mann matrices, a pair `j < k` for each symmetric and each
antisymmetric matrix, and `l : Fin (N - 1)` for the diagonal matrix of size `n = l + 1`.
declarations.statement: abbrev Index (N : ℕ) : Type

declarations.name: GellMann.diagProfile
declarations.doc:
The diagonal profile of size `n = l + 1`, `1` on the first `n` entries, `-n` on the next, and
`0` beyond.
declarations.statement: def diagProfile (l : Fin (N - 1)) (m : Fin N) : ℂ

declarations.name: GellMann.diagNorm
declarations.doc: The normalization `√(2 / (n (n + 1)))` of the diagonal matrix of size `n = l + 1`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagNorm (l : Fin (N - 1)) : ℂ

declarations.name: GellMann.matrix
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def matrix : Index N → Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ

declarations.name: GellMann.sum_diagProfile
declarations.statement: lemma sum_diagProfile (l : Fin (N - 1)) : ∑ m, diagProfile l m = 0

declarations.name: GellMann.sum_diagProfile_mul
declarations.doc: The diagonal profiles are orthogonal, with `∑ d_l (m)² = n (n + 1)` for `n = l + 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_diagProfile_mul (l l' : Fin (N - 1)) :
    ∑ m, diagProfile l m * diagProfile l' m
      = if l = l' then ((l.val + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ) * ((l.val + 2 : ℕ) : ℂ) else 0

declarations.name: GellMann.diagNorm_mul_self
declarations.doc:
The square of the normalization of the diagonal matrix of size `n = l + 1` is
`2 / (n (n + 1))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma diagNorm_mul_self (l : Fin (N - 1)) :
    diagNorm l * diagNorm l * (((l.val + 1 : ℕ) : ℂ) * ((l.val + 2 : ℕ) : ℂ)) = 2

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_matrix_inl_mul
declarations.doc:
The trace of the product of a symmetric Gell-Mann matrix with any complex matrix is the sum
of the two entries of that matrix at the positions of the Gell-Mann matrix's units.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_matrix_inl_mul (p : {p : Fin N × Fin N // p.1 < p.2}) (X : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    (matrix (.inl p) * X).trace = X p.1.2 p.1.1 + X p.1.1 p.1.2

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_matrix_inr_inl_mul
declarations.doc:
The trace of the product of an antisymmetric Gell-Mann matrix with any complex matrix is the
difference of the two entries of that matrix at the positions of the Gell-Mann matrix's
units, weighted by `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_matrix_inr_inl_mul (p : {p : Fin N × Fin N // p.1 < p.2})
    (X : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    (matrix (.inr (.inl p)) * X).trace
      = -Complex.I * X p.1.2 p.1.1 + Complex.I * X p.1.1 p.1.2

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_matrix_inr_inr_mul
declarations.doc:
The trace of the product of a diagonal Gell-Mann matrix with any complex matrix is its
normalization times the sum of the diagonal entries of that matrix weighted by the diagonal
profile.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_matrix_inr_inr_mul (l : Fin (N - 1)) (X : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) :
    (matrix (.inr (.inr l)) * X).trace = diagNorm l * ∑ m, diagProfile l m * X m m

declarations.name: GellMann.matrix_inl_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of a symmetric Gell-Mann matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma matrix_inl_apply (p : {p : Fin N × Fin N // p.1 < p.2}) (m n : Fin N) :
    matrix (.inl p) m n
      = (if p.1.1 = m ∧ p.1.2 = n then 1 else 0) + (if p.1.2 = m ∧ p.1.1 = n then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: GellMann.matrix_inr_inl_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of an antisymmetric Gell-Mann matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma matrix_inr_inl_apply (p : {p : Fin N × Fin N // p.1 < p.2}) (m n : Fin N) :
    matrix (.inr (.inl p)) m n = (if p.1.1 = m ∧ p.1.2 = n then -Complex.I else 0)
      + (if p.1.2 = m ∧ p.1.1 = n then Complex.I else 0)

declarations.name: GellMann.matrix_inr_inr_apply
declarations.doc: The entries of a diagonal Gell-Mann matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma matrix_inr_inr_apply (l : Fin (N - 1)) (m n : Fin N) :
    matrix (.inr (.inr l)) m n = if m = n then diagNorm l * diagProfile l m else 0

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_matrix_inl_mul_matrix
declarations.doc: The symmetric Gell-Mann matrices are orthogonal to all others and have norm `2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_matrix_inl_mul_matrix (p : {p : Fin N × Fin N // p.1 < p.2}) (b : Index N) :
    (matrix (.inl p) * matrix b).trace = if .inl p = b then 2 else 0

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_matrix_inr_inl_mul_matrix
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric Gell-Mann matrices are orthogonal to all others and have norm `2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_matrix_inr_inl_mul_matrix (p : {p : Fin N × Fin N // p.1 < p.2}) (b : Index N) :
    (matrix (.inr (.inl p)) * matrix b).trace = if .inr (.inl p) = b then 2 else 0

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_matrix_inr_inr_mul_matrix
declarations.doc: The diagonal Gell-Mann matrices are orthogonal to all others and have norm `2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_matrix_inr_inr_mul_matrix (l : Fin (N - 1)) (b : Index N) :
    (matrix (.inr (.inr l)) * matrix b).trace = if .inr (.inr l) = b then 2 else 0

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_matrix_mul_matrix
declarations.doc:
The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are orthogonal under the trace form,
`tr (λ_a λ_b) = 2 δ_ab`.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_matrix_mul_matrix (a b : Index N) :
    (matrix a * matrix b).trace = if a = b then 2 else 0

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_matrix
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are traceless.
declarations.statement: lemma trace_matrix (a : Index N) : (matrix a).trace = 0

declarations.name: GellMann.conjTranspose_matrix
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are hermitian.
declarations.statement: lemma conjTranspose_matrix (a : Index N) : (matrix a)ᴴ = matrix a

declarations.name: GellMann.traceless
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices as traceless matrices.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def traceless (a : Index N) :
    ↥(LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin N) ℂ ℂ))

declarations.name: GellMann.linearIndependent_traceless
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are linearly independent, by orthogonality.
declarations.statement: lemma linearIndependent_traceless : LinearIndependent ℂ (traceless (N := N))

declarations.name: GellMann.two_mul_card_lt_add
declarations.doc:
There are `N² - 1` ordered pairs with `j < k`, counted twice, and `N - 1` diagonal labels,
`2 #{j < k} + N = N²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma two_mul_card_lt_add :
    2 * Fintype.card {p : Fin N × Fin N // p.1 < p.2} + N = N * N

declarations.name: GellMann.finrank_traceless
declarations.doc: The traceless `N × N` matrices have dimension `N² - 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_traceless :
    finrank ℂ ↥(LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin N) ℂ ℂ)) = N * N - 1

declarations.name: GellMann.card_index
declarations.statement:
lemma card_index : Fintype.card (Index N)
    = finrank ℂ ↥(LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin N) ℂ ℂ))

declarations.name: GellMann.basis
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann basis of the traceless complex `N × N` matrices.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def basis : Basis (Index N) ℂ ↥(LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin N) ℂ ℂ))

declarations.name: GellMann.basis_apply_val
declarations.statement: lemma basis_apply_val (a : Index N) : (basis a).1 = matrix a

declarations.name: GellMann.basis_repr_apply
declarations.doc:
The coordinates of a traceless matrix in the Gell-Mann basis are read off by the trace form,
`x = ∑ (tr (λ_a x) / 2) λ_a`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_apply (x : ↥(LinearMap.ker (Matrix.traceLinearMap (Fin N) ℂ ℂ))) (a : Index N) :
    basis.repr x a = (matrix a * x.1).trace / 2

declarations.name: GellMann.hermitian
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices as elements of the real Lie algebra `su(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hermitian (a : Index N) : SUAlgebraOver ℂ N

declarations.name: GellMann.linearIndependent_hermitian
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann matrices are linearly independent over the reals.
declarations.statement: lemma linearIndependent_hermitian : LinearIndependent ℝ (hermitian (N := N))

declarations.name: GellMann.trace_mul_ofReal_re
declarations.doc: The trace pairing of two hermitian matrices is real.
declarations.statement:
lemma trace_mul_ofReal_re {A H : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ} (hA : Aᴴ = A) (hH : Hᴴ = H) :
    (((A * H).trace.re : ℝ) : ℂ) = (A * H).trace

declarations.name: GellMann.eq_sum_re_trace_smul_hermitian
declarations.doc:
A traceless hermitian matrix is the real combination `∑ (tr (λ_a H) / 2) λ_a` of the
generalized Gell-Mann matrices.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_sum_re_trace_smul_hermitian (H : SUAlgebraOver ℂ N) :
    ∑ a, ((matrix a * H.1).trace.re / 2) • hermitian a = H

declarations.name: GellMann.realBasis
declarations.doc: The generalized Gell-Mann basis of the real Lie algebra `su(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def realBasis : Basis (Index N) ℝ (SUAlgebraOver ℂ N)

declarations.name: GellMann.realBasis_apply_val
declarations.statement: lemma realBasis_apply_val (a : Index N) : (realBasis a).1 = matrix a

modules.title: The unit tensor of the adjoint colour of `SU(N)`
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the unit tensor is the only invariant with two adjoint indices.

## i. Overview

A tensor with one adjoint index has no invariants but zero (`suTensor.invariants_adj_eq_bot`, with
the adjoint colour). A tensor with two adjoint indices has a matrix of components `C` in the
Gell-Mann basis, moved by `g` to `M C Mᵀ`, where `M` is the matrix of the adjoint action of `g`.
That matrix is real and `Mᵀ` is the matrix of `g⁻¹`, so the components of an invariant tensor are
the matrix of an endomorphism of the complexified Lie algebra commuting with the adjoint action. By
`suTensor.eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjRep` that endomorphism is scalar, and the invariant tensors are
the line through the unit tensor of the adjoint color, `∑ λ_a ⊗ λ_a / 2` (A).

For equivariant maps out of these tensors the invariants of the range reduce to `⊥` for one
adjoint index and to the image of the unit tensor for two (B). A family indexed by the Gell-Mann
labels is the map `liftComponents (T ∘ adjIdx)` or `liftComponents (T ∘ adjPairIdx)`, and for two
indices the image of twice the unit tensor is the trace contraction `∑ a, T ![a, a]` (C). The
invariants of the tensor square of the adjoint representation are the line through the unit
`∑ λ_a ⊗ λ_a / 2` (D).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.invariants_adj_adj_eq_span_adjUnitTensor` : the invariant tensors with two adjoint
  indices are the line through the unit tensor.
- `suTensor.invariantReductionToTrace` : the reduction of the invariants of the span of a family
  with two adjoint indices to the trace contraction.
- `suTensor.invariants_tprod_eq_span_adjUnitVal` : the invariants of the tensor square of the
  adjoint representation are the line through the unit.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Two adjoint indices
- B. The invariants of equivariant maps
- C. Maps from components
- D. The invariants of the tensor square of the adjoint representation

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The invariants of equivariant maps
## C. Maps from components
## D. The invariants of the tensor square of the adjoint representation

declarations.name: suTensor.adjPairIdx
declarations.doc:
The component indices of a tensor with two adjoint indices, as the pair of their Gell-Mann
labels.
declarations.statement: def adjPairIdx : ComponentIdx (S := suTensor N) ![.adj, .adj] ≃ (Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N)

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_smul_adjPair
declarations.doc:
The components of `g • t` for a tensor with two adjoint indices. The matrix of components
`C` is moved to `M C Mᵀ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_smul_adjPair (g : SU N) (t : SuT[N, .adj, .adj])
    (n : Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (g • t) (adjPairIdx.symm n)
      = ∑ x, ∑ y, adjMatrix g (n 0) x * adjMatrix g (n 1) y
        * (Tensor.basis _).repr t (adjPairIdx.symm ![x, y])

declarations.name: suTensor.adjUnitTensor
declarations.doc: The unit tensor of the adjoint color, `∑ λ_a ⊗ λ_a / 2`, with two adjoint indices.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjUnitTensor : SuT[N, .adj, .adj]

declarations.name: suTensor.adjUnitTensor_invariant
declarations.doc: The unit tensor of the adjoint color is invariant.
declarations.statement: lemma adjUnitTensor_invariant (g : SU N) : g • adjUnitTensor N = adjUnitTensor N

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_adjUnitTensor
declarations.doc:
The components of the unit tensor of the adjoint color, `δ / 2`, the Gell-Mann matrices
being orthogonal with `tr (λ_a λ_b) = 2 δ_ab`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_adjUnitTensor (n : Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (adjUnitTensor N) (adjPairIdx.symm n)
      = if n 0 = n 1 then 1 / 2 else 0

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_adj_adj_eq_span_adjUnitTensor
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with two adjoint indices are the line through the unit tensor of the
adjoint color. The matrix of components of an invariant tensor commutes with the matrices of the
adjoint action, so it is the matrix of an endomorphism commuting with the adjoint action, which
is scalar.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_adj_adj_eq_span_adjUnitTensor :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep ![.adj, .adj]).invariants = ℂ ∙ adjUnitTensor N

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_adj_adj_eq_span_two_smul_adjUnitTensor
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with two adjoint indices are the line through twice the unit tensor,
the tensor whose image under a map of a family is the trace contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_adj_adj_eq_span_two_smul_adjUnitTensor :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep ![.adj, .adj]).invariants = ℂ ∙ ((2 : ℂ) • adjUnitTensor N)

declarations.name: suTensor.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_of_isEquivariant_adj
declarations.doc:
For an equivariant map out of the tensors with one adjoint index, the invariants of the range
reduce to `⊥`.

declarations.name: suTensor.adjIdx
declarations.doc: The component indices of a tensor with one adjoint index, as its Gell-Mann label.
declarations.statement: def adjIdx : ComponentIdx (S := suTensor N) ![.adj] ≃ GellMann.Index N

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_adj_smul_of_law
declarations.doc:
A linear map moving a family indexed by one adjoint label by the matrix of the adjoint action
of `g` intertwines the map of the family with the action of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_adj_smul_of_law (T : GellMann.Index N → B) {σ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B} (g : SU N)
    (hσ : ∀ a : GellMann.Index N, σ (T a) = ∑ b, adjMatrix g b a • T b) (t : SuT[N, .adj]) :
    σ (liftComponents (T ∘ adjIdx) t) = liftComponents (T ∘ adjIdx) (g • t)

declarations.name: suTensor.isEquivariant_liftComponents_adj
declarations.doc:
The map of a family indexed by one adjoint label is equivariant when the family moves by the
matrix of the adjoint action, the summed label first.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_adj (T : GellMann.Index N → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SU N) (a : GellMann.Index N), ρ g (T a) = ∑ b, adjMatrix g b a • T b) :
    (suTensor N).IsEquivariant ![.adj] ρ (liftComponents (T ∘ adjIdx))

declarations.name: suTensor.reducesInvariantsTo_bot_span_adj
declarations.doc:
For a family indexed by one adjoint label whose map is equivariant, the invariants of the
span of the family reduce to `⊥`.

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_two_smul_adjUnitTensor
declarations.doc:
The map of a family relabelled by `adjPairIdx` sends twice the unit tensor to the trace
contraction `∑ a, T ![a, a]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_two_smul_adjUnitTensor (T : (Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N) → B) :
    liftComponents (T ∘ adjPairIdx) ((2 : ℂ) • adjUnitTensor N) = ∑ a, T ![a, a]

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_adjPair_smul_of_law
declarations.doc:
A linear map moving a family indexed by two adjoint labels by the matrix of the adjoint
action of `g` on each label intertwines the map of the family with the action of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_adjPair_smul_of_law (T : (Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N) → B) {σ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (g : SU N) (hσ : ∀ l : Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N, σ (T l)
      = ∑ a : Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N, (adjMatrix g (a 0) (l 0) * adjMatrix g (a 1) (l 1)) • T a)
    (t : SuT[N, .adj, .adj]) :
    σ (liftComponents (T ∘ adjPairIdx) t) = liftComponents (T ∘ adjPairIdx) (g • t)

declarations.name: suTensor.isEquivariant_liftComponents_adjPair
declarations.doc:
The map of a family indexed by two adjoint labels is equivariant when the family moves by the
matrix of the adjoint action on each label, the summed label first.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_adjPair (T : (Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N) → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SU N) (l : Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N), ρ g (T l)
      = ∑ a : Fin 2 → GellMann.Index N, (adjMatrix g (a 0) (l 0) * adjMatrix g (a 1) (l 1)) • T a) :
    (suTensor N).IsEquivariant ![.adj, .adj] ρ (liftComponents (T ∘ adjPairIdx))

declarations.name: suTensor.invariantReductionToTrace
declarations.doc:
For a family indexed by two adjoint labels whose map is equivariant, the invariants of the
span of the family reduce to the span of the trace contraction `∑ a, T ![a, a]`.

declarations.name: suTensor.adjUnitTensor_eq_fromPairT
declarations.doc: The unit tensor of the adjoint color is the tensor of `∑ b_a ⊗ bᵃ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjUnitTensor_eq_fromPairT :
    adjUnitTensor N = fromPairT (S := suTensor N) (c1 := .adj) (c2 := .adj) (adjUnitVal N)

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_tprod_eq_span_adjUnitVal
declarations.doc:
The invariants of the tensor square of the adjoint representation are the line through the
unit `∑ b_a ⊗ bᵃ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tprod_eq_span_adjUnitVal :
    ((adjRep N).tprod (adjRep N)).invariants = ℂ ∙ adjUnitVal N

modules.title: What commutes with the adjoint action of `SU(N)`, and the Reynolds element of its tensors
modules.doc:
Schur's lemma for the adjoint representation, and the Haar average over the tensors.

## i. Overview

The elements `SU.planeEmbed p q U` of `SU(N)`, an element `U` of `SU(2)` acting on the plane of two
coordinates (`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.Adjoint`), do all
the work. A diagonal phase `diag (u, ū)`, the rotation by a quarter turn, and the rotation by an
eighth of a turn, embedded in every plane, force a linear endomorphism of the complexified Lie
algebra `ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(N)` commuting with the adjoint action to be scalar (A); this is computed on the
matrices `adjMat A`, which identify the complexified Lie algebra with the traceless complex
matrices. With Schur's lemma for the fundamental representation, `SU.eq_smul_one_of_commute`,
these are the facts behind the classification of the invariant tensors of `SU(N)` with a
fundamental and an anti-fundamental index, and with one or two adjoint indices.

The tensors of `SU(N)` have a Reynolds element, the Haar average over the compact group, so the
invariants in the range of an equivariant map out of them come from invariant tensors (B).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjRep` : an endomorphism of the complexified Lie algebra
  commuting with the adjoint action is scalar.
- `suTensor.hasReynolds` : the tensors of `SU(N)` have a Reynolds element.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Endomorphisms of the complexified Lie algebra commuting with `SU(N)`
- B. Reynolds elements for the tensors

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Endomorphisms of the complexified Lie algebra commuting with `SU(N)`

## B. Reynolds elements for the tensors

`SU(N)` is identified with the global gauge group `GlobalGaugeGroup.SU N`, a compact topological
group, by `GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.groupEquiv`. On it the matrix entries of every color are continuous,
being those of `g`, of `g⁻¹ = g†` and the traces `tr (λ_a g λ_b g⁻¹) / 2` of the adjoint action, so
the Haar average gives a Reynolds element, which is pushed forward to `SU(N)`.

declarations.name: suTensor.offDiag
declarations.doc:
The matrix unit at `(x, y)` off the diagonal, as an element of the complexified Lie algebra,
and zero on the diagonal.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def offDiag (x y : Fin N) : SUAlgebraComplexified N

declarations.name: suTensor.diagDiff
declarations.doc:
The difference of the diagonal matrix units at `x` and at `y`, as an element of the
complexified Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def diagDiff (x y : Fin N) : SUAlgebraComplexified N

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_offDiag
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMat_offDiag (x y : Fin N) :
    adjMat N (offDiag x y) = if x = y then 0 else single x y 1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_offDiag_of_ne
declarations.statement: lemma adjMat_offDiag_of_ne {x y : Fin N} (h : x ≠ y) : adjMat N (offDiag x y) = single x y 1

declarations.name: suTensor.offDiag_self
declarations.statement: lemma offDiag_self (x : Fin N) : offDiag x x = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_diagDiff
declarations.statement: lemma adjMat_diagDiff (x y : Fin N) : adjMat N (diagDiff x y) = single x x 1 - single y y 1

declarations.name: suTensor.diagDiff_self
declarations.statement: lemma diagDiff_self (x : Fin N) : diagDiff x x = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_adjRep_planeEmbed
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action of an element of `SU(2)` embedded in a plane of two coordinates on a
matrix supported on that plane is the conjugation of the matrix on the plane.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMat_adjRep_planeEmbed {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) (U : SU 2)
    (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (M : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)
    (hA : adjMat N A = planeInclusion p q * M * (planeInclusion p q)ᵀ) :
    adjMat N (adjRep N (planeEmbed p q hpq U) A)
      = planeInclusion p q * (U.1 * M * U.1ᴴ) * (planeInclusion p q)ᵀ

declarations.name: suTensor.sqrtI
declarations.doc: The phase `(1 + i) / √2`, a square root of `i` of modulus one.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sqrtI : ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.star_sqrtI
declarations.statement: lemma star_sqrtI : star sqrtI = (1 - Complex.I) / (Real.sqrt 2 : ℂ)

declarations.name: suTensor.sqrtI_mul_star
declarations.statement: lemma sqrtI_mul_star : sqrtI * star sqrtI = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.sqrtI_mul_self
declarations.statement: lemma sqrtI_mul_self : sqrtI * sqrtI = Complex.I

declarations.name: suTensor.star_sqrtI_mul_self
declarations.statement: lemma star_sqrtI_mul_self : star sqrtI * star sqrtI = -Complex.I

declarations.name: suTensor.sqrtI_ne_I
declarations.statement: lemma sqrtI_ne_I : sqrtI ≠ Complex.I

declarations.name: suTensor.star_sqrtI_ne_I
declarations.statement: lemma star_sqrtI_ne_I : star sqrtI ≠ Complex.I

declarations.name: suTensor.adjMat_adjRep_apply_of_diagonal
declarations.doc:
The adjoint action of a diagonal matrix of `SU(N)` scales the entry at `(x, y)` by
`d x * star (d y)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjMat_adjRep_apply_of_diagonal {g : SU N} {d : Fin N → ℂ} (hg : g.1 = diagonal d)
    (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (x y : Fin N) :
    adjMat N (adjRep N g A) x y = d x * adjMat N A x y * star (d y)

declarations.name: suTensor.map_offDiag_eq_smul
declarations.doc:
For two distinct coordinates `p` and `q`, an endomorphism commuting with the adjoint action
sends the matrix unit at `(p, q)` to a multiple of itself. The phase `diag (ω, ω̄)` in the
plane of `p` and `q`, with `ω² = i`, multiplies that matrix unit by `i` and no other entry
by `i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_offDiag_eq_smul (hL : ∀ (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N),
    L (adjRep N g A) = adjRep N g (L A)) {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    L (offDiag p q) = adjMat N (L (offDiag p q)) p q • offDiag p q

declarations.name: suTensor.adjRep_quarterTurn_offDiag
declarations.doc:
The quarter turn in the plane of `p` and `q` sends the matrix unit at `(p, q)` to minus the
one at `(q, p)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjRep_quarterTurn_offDiag {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    adjRep N (planeEmbed p q hpq (rotation 0 1 (by norm_num))) (offDiag p q) = -offDiag q p

declarations.name: suTensor.coeff_offDiag_swap
declarations.doc: The coefficients of the matrix units at `(p, q)` and at `(q, p)` agree.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_offDiag_swap (hL : ∀ (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N),
    L (adjRep N g A) = adjRep N g (L A)) {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    adjMat N (L (offDiag q p)) q p = adjMat N (L (offDiag p q)) p q

declarations.name: suTensor.invSqrtTwo
declarations.doc: The cosine and sine of an eighth of a turn, the real number `1 / √2`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def invSqrtTwo : ℝ

declarations.name: suTensor.invSqrtTwo_sq_add
declarations.statement: lemma invSqrtTwo_sq_add : invSqrtTwo ^ 2 + invSqrtTwo ^ 2 = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.invSqrtTwo_mul_self
declarations.statement: lemma invSqrtTwo_mul_self : (invSqrtTwo : ℂ) * invSqrtTwo = 1 / 2

declarations.name: suTensor.adjRep_eighthTurn_offDiag
declarations.doc:
The eighth turn in the plane of `p` and `q` sends the sum of the matrix units at `(p, q)`
and at `(q, p)` to minus the difference of the diagonal matrix units at `p` and at `q`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjRep_eighthTurn_offDiag {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    adjRep N (planeEmbed p q hpq (rotation invSqrtTwo invSqrtTwo invSqrtTwo_sq_add))
      (offDiag p q + offDiag q p) = -diagDiff p q

declarations.name: suTensor.map_diagDiff_eq_smul
declarations.doc:
For two distinct coordinates `p` and `q`, an endomorphism commuting with the adjoint action
scales the difference of the diagonal matrix units at `p` and at `q` by the coefficient of the
matrix unit at `(p, q)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_diagDiff_eq_smul (hL : ∀ (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N),
    L (adjRep N g A) = adjRep N g (L A)) {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) :
    L (diagDiff p q) = adjMat N (L (offDiag p q)) p q • diagDiff p q

declarations.name: suTensor.coeff_offDiag_eq
declarations.doc:
For three distinct coordinates `p`, `q` and `r`, the coefficients of the matrix units at
`(p, q)` and at `(p, r)` agree. The difference of the diagonal units at `p` and `r` is the sum
of those at `p` and `q` and at `q` and `r`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_offDiag_eq (hL : ∀ (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N),
    L (adjRep N g A) = adjRep N g (L A)) {p q r : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) (hpr : p ≠ r)
    (hqr : q ≠ r) : adjMat N (L (offDiag p r)) p r = adjMat N (L (offDiag p q)) p q

declarations.name: suTensor.exists_coeff_offDiag_eq
declarations.doc:
All the matrix units off the diagonal have the same coefficient under an endomorphism
commuting with the adjoint action.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_coeff_offDiag_eq (hL : ∀ (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N),
    L (adjRep N g A) = adjRep N g (L A)) :
    ∃ μ : ℂ, ∀ x y : Fin N, x ≠ y → adjMat N (L (offDiag x y)) x y = μ

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_sum_offDiag_add_sum_diagDiff
declarations.doc:
An element of the complexified Lie algebra is the combination of the entries of its matrix off
the diagonal against the matrix units, and of its diagonal entries against the differences of
the diagonal matrix units at a fixed coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_sum_offDiag_add_sum_diagDiff (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (x₀ : Fin N) :
    A = ∑ x, ∑ y, adjMat N A x y • offDiag x y + ∑ x, adjMat N A x x • diagDiff x x₀

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjRep
declarations.doc:
An endomorphism of the complexified Lie algebra commuting with the adjoint action of every
element of `SU(N)` is scalar, a form of Schur's lemma for the adjoint representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_smul_id_of_commute_adjRep (hL : ∀ (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N),
    L (adjRep N g A) = adjRep N g (L A)) :
    ∃ z : ℂ, L = z • LinearMap.id

declarations.name: suTensor.continuous_toMatrix_rep
declarations.doc:
The matrix entries of every color depend continuously on the element of the global gauge group
`SU(N)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_toMatrix_rep (k : Color) (x y : basisIdx N k) :
    Continuous fun h : (GlobalGaugeGroup.SU N).group => LinearMap.toMatrix (basis N k)
      (basis N k) (rep N k ((GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.groupEquiv N).symm h)) x y

declarations.name: suTensor.hasReynolds
declarations.doc:
The tensors of `SU(N)` with any list of colors have a Reynolds element, the Haar average over
the compact group `SU(N)`.
declarations.statement: lemma hasReynolds {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → Color) : (suTensor N).HasReynolds c

modules.title: The Kronecker delta of `SU(N)`
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the Kronecker delta is the only invariant tensor with a fundamental and an
anti-fundamental index.

## i. Overview

The invariant tensors of `SuT[N, .fund, .antiFund]` are the line through the Kronecker delta
`δᵃ_b`, the unit tensor `delta N` of the anti-fundamental color (A, B). The components of a
tensor with these indices form a matrix `C`, which `g` moves to `g C g⁻¹`, so the components of
an invariant tensor commute with every element of `SU(N)` and are scalar
(`SU.eq_smul_one_of_commute`).

A family `T` of vectors indexed by `Fin 2 → Fin N`, a fundamental index first, is the map
`liftComponents (T ∘ fundAntiFundIdx)`, equivariant exactly when `T` obeys the transformation law of
the components, and `f (delta N)` is then the contraction `∑ a, T ![a, a]`. The invariants of the
span of such a
family, modulo a stable submodule, reduce to the line through that contraction (C).

The invariants of `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ` under the fundamental and the anti-fundamental representation are the
line through `∑ eᵢ ⊗ eᵢ` (D).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.delta` : the Kronecker delta.
- `suTensor.invariants_fund_antiFund_eq_span_delta` : the invariant tensors are the line through it.
- `suTensor.invariantReductionToDelta` : the reduction of the invariants of the span of a family
  to the delta contraction.
- `suTensor.invariants_tprod_eq_span_pairUnitVal` : the invariants of the fundamental times the
  anti-fundamental representation are the line through `∑ eᵢ ⊗ eᵢ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Kronecker delta
- B. The invariant tensors
- C. Maps from components
- D. The invariants of the tensor product

## iv. References

* None.

## C. Maps from components

declarations.name: suTensor.fundAntiFundIdx
declarations.doc:
The component indices of a tensor with a fundamental and an anti-fundamental index, as the
pair of their labels.
declarations.statement: def fundAntiFundIdx : ComponentIdx (S := suTensor N) ![.fund, .antiFund] ≃ (Fin 2 → Fin N)

declarations.name: suTensor.delta
declarations.doc:
The Kronecker delta `δᵃ_b`, the unit tensor of the anti-fundamental color, with a
fundamental and an anti-fundamental index.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def delta : SuT[N, .fund, .antiFund]

declarations.name: suTensor.delta_invariant
declarations.doc: The Kronecker delta is invariant.
declarations.statement: lemma delta_invariant (g : SU N) : g • delta N = delta N

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_delta
declarations.doc: The components of the Kronecker delta.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_delta (n : Fin 2 → Fin N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (delta N) (fundAntiFundIdx.symm n) = if n 0 = n 1 then 1 else 0

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_smul_fundAntiFund
declarations.doc:
The components of `g • t` for a tensor with a fundamental and an anti-fundamental index.
The matrix of components `C` is moved to `g C g⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_smul_fundAntiFund (g : SU N) (t : SuT[N, .fund, .antiFund])
    (n : Fin 2 → Fin N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (g • t) (fundAntiFundIdx.symm n)
      = ∑ x, ∑ y, g.1 (n 0) x * (g⁻¹).1 y (n 1)
        * (Tensor.basis _).repr t (fundAntiFundIdx.symm ![x, y])

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_fund_antiFund_eq_span_delta
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with a fundamental and an anti-fundamental index are the line through
the Kronecker delta. The matrix of components of an invariant tensor commutes with every element
of `SU(N)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_fund_antiFund_eq_span_delta :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep ![.fund, .antiFund]).invariants = ℂ ∙ delta N

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_delta
declarations.doc:
The map of a family relabelled by `fundAntiFundIdx` sends the Kronecker delta to the
contraction `∑ a, T ![a, a]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_delta (T : (Fin 2 → Fin N) → B) :
    liftComponents (T ∘ fundAntiFundIdx) (delta N) = ∑ a, T ![a, a]

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_fundAntiFund_smul_of_law
declarations.doc:
A linear map moving a family as a group element moves the components of a tensor with a
fundamental and an anti-fundamental index intertwines the map of the family with the action of
that element. The element acts by one factor of itself on the first index and of its complex
conjugate on the second, the summed index first.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_fundAntiFund_smul_of_law (T : (Fin 2 → Fin N) → B) {σ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (g : SU N) (hσ : ∀ l : Fin 2 → Fin N, σ (T l)
      = ∑ a : Fin 2 → Fin N, (g.1 (a 0) (l 0) * starRingEnd ℂ (g.1 (a 1) (l 1))) • T a)
    (t : SuT[N, .fund, .antiFund]) :
    σ (liftComponents (T ∘ fundAntiFundIdx) t) = liftComponents (T ∘ fundAntiFundIdx) (g • t)

declarations.name: suTensor.isEquivariant_liftComponents_fundAntiFund
declarations.doc:
The map of a family is equivariant when the family moves as the components of a tensor
with a fundamental and an anti-fundamental index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_fundAntiFund (T : (Fin 2 → Fin N) → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SU N) (l : Fin 2 → Fin N), ρ g (T l)
      = ∑ a : Fin 2 → Fin N, (g.1 (a 0) (l 0) * starRingEnd ℂ (g.1 (a 1) (l 1))) • T a) :
    (suTensor N).IsEquivariant ![.fund, .antiFund] ρ (liftComponents (T ∘ fundAntiFundIdx))

declarations.name: suTensor.invariantReductionToDelta
declarations.doc:
For a family whose map is equivariant, the invariants of the span of the family reduce to
the span of the delta contraction `∑ a, T ![a, a]`.

declarations.name: suTensor.delta_eq_fromPairT
declarations.doc: The Kronecker delta is the tensor of `∑ eᵢ ⊗ eᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma delta_eq_fromPairT :
    delta N = fromPairT (S := suTensor N) (c1 := .fund) (c2 := .antiFund) (pairUnitVal N)

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_tprod_eq_span_pairUnitVal
declarations.doc:
The invariants of `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ` under the fundamental and the anti-fundamental representation are
the line through `∑ eᵢ ⊗ eᵢ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tprod_eq_span_pairUnitVal :
    ((fundRep N).tprod (antiFundRep N)).invariants = ℂ ∙ pairUnitVal N

modules.title: The generator tensor of `SU(N)`
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the generators `(Tᵃ)_i^j = (λ_a)_{ij} / 2` form the only invariant tensor with an
adjoint, a fundamental and an anti-fundamental index.

## i. Overview

An element of `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ`, with the fundamental and the anti-fundamental representation, is a
matrix of components moved by `g` to `g X g⁻¹` (`pairMatrix`). Writing the matrix of an element
of the complexified Lie algebra in this way is an equivariant map `adjToPair` from the adjoint
representation (A).

An element `x` of `adj ⊗ U`, for any representation `U`, is a linear map `adj → U` once its first
index is contracted against the argument with the trace form (`adjContract`). This identifies
`adj ⊗ U` with the linear maps, and an invariant `x` gives an equivariant map (B).

An equivariant linear map `Φ` from the adjoint representation to the matrices is a multiple of
the matrix of the argument (C). Its trace is an invariant linear form, which by the trace form
is an invariant of the adjoint representation and so vanishes. Then `Φ` lands in the traceless
matrices, that is in the complexified Lie algebra, and commutes with the adjoint action, so it is
scalar.

The generator tensor `generatorVal N` is the unit `∑ b_a ⊗ bᵃ` of the adjoint color with its
second factor written as a matrix, in `adj ⊗ (ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ)`, and it is invariant (D). As a linear map
`adj → ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ` it is `adjToPair`. So an invariant `x` gives a map which, written as matrices, is
equivariant and hence a multiple of the matrix of the argument, and `x` is that multiple of the
generator tensor (E). The tensor `generator N`, with an adjoint, a fundamental and an
anti-fundamental index, has the components `(λ_a)_{ij} / 2` (F).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.pairMatrix` : the components of an element of `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ` as a matrix.
- `suTensor.exists_eq_smul_adjMat_of_equivariant` : an equivariant map from the adjoint
  representation to the matrices is a multiple of the matrix of the argument.
- `suTensor.generatorVal` : the generator tensor.
- `suTensor.invariants_tprod_eq_span_generatorVal` : the invariants of
  `adj ⊗ (ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ)` are the line through the generator tensor.
- `suTensor.generator` : the generator tensor with an adjoint, a fundamental and an
  anti-fundamental index.
- `suTensor.invariants_adj_fund_antiFund_eq_span_generator` : the invariant tensors with these
  indices are the line through it.
- `suTensor.basis_repr_generator` : its components are the entries of `λ_a / 2`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. A fundamental and an anti-fundamental index as a matrix
- B. Contracting an adjoint index
- C. Equivariant maps from the adjoint representation to the matrices
- D. The generator tensor
- E. The generator tensor is the unique invariant
- F. The generator tensor with three indices

## iv. References

* None.
