declarations.name: suTensor.pairMatrix
declarations.doc: The components of an element of `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ` as a matrix, `v ⊗ w ↦ v wᵀ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pairMatrix : (Fin N → ℂ) ⊗[ℂ] (Fin N → ℂ) ≃ₗ[ℂ] Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.pairMatrix_tmul
declarations.statement: lemma pairMatrix_tmul (v w : Fin N → ℂ) : pairMatrix N (v ⊗ₜ w) = vecMulVec v w

declarations.name: suTensor.pairMatrix_map
declarations.doc:
The fundamental and the anti-fundamental representation move the matrix of components by
conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairMatrix_map (g : SU N) (x : (Fin N → ℂ) ⊗[ℂ] (Fin N → ℂ)) :
    pairMatrix N (TensorProduct.map (fundRep N g) (antiFundRep N g) x)
      = g.1 * pairMatrix N x * (g⁻¹).1

declarations.name: suTensor.adjToPair
declarations.doc: The matrix of an element of the complexified Lie algebra, as an element of `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def adjToPair : SUAlgebraComplexified N →ₗ[ℂ] (Fin N → ℂ) ⊗[ℂ] (Fin N → ℂ)

declarations.name: suTensor.pairMatrix_adjToPair
declarations.statement:
lemma pairMatrix_adjToPair (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    pairMatrix N (adjToPair N A) = adjMat N A

declarations.name: suTensor.adjToPair_adjRep
declarations.doc:
Writing the matrix of an element of the complexified Lie algebra in `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ` is
equivariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjToPair_adjRep (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    adjToPair N (adjRep N g A)
      = TensorProduct.map (fundRep N g) (antiFundRep N g) (adjToPair N A)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContract
declarations.doc:
An element of `adj ⊗ U` as the linear map `adj → U` contracting its first index against the
argument with the trace form, `A₀ ⊗ u ↦ (A ↦ tr (A₀ A) u)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def adjContract :
    SUAlgebraComplexified N ⊗[ℂ] U ≃ₗ[ℂ] (SUAlgebraComplexified N →ₗ[ℂ] U)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContract_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma adjContract_tmul (A₀ : SUAlgebraComplexified N) (u : U) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    adjContract N U (A₀ ⊗ₜ u) A = traceForm N A₀ A • u

declarations.name: suTensor.traceForm_adjRep
declarations.doc: The trace form is invariant under the adjoint action.
declarations.statement:
lemma traceForm_adjRep (g : SU N) (A B : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    traceForm N (adjRep N g A) (adjRep N g B) = traceForm N A B

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContract_map
declarations.doc: Transforming both factors of `x` conjugates the map `adjContract x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjContract_map (σ : Representation ℂ (SU N) U) (g : SU N)
    (x : SUAlgebraComplexified N ⊗[ℂ] U) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    adjContract N U (TensorProduct.map (adjRep N g) (σ g) x) (adjRep N g A)
      = σ g (adjContract N U x A)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContract_lTensor
declarations.doc: Applying a linear map to the second factor of `x` composes `adjContract x` with it.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjContract_lTensor {U' : Type*} [AddCommGroup U'] [Module ℂ U'] (ι : U →ₗ[ℂ] U')
    (x : SUAlgebraComplexified N ⊗[ℂ] U) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    adjContract N U' (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id ι x) A = ι (adjContract N U x A)

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContract_adjUnitVal
declarations.doc: The unit of the adjoint color, as a linear map, is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjContract_adjUnitVal (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    adjContract N _ (adjUnitVal N) A = A

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_zero_of_adjRep_invariant
declarations.doc:
An invariant linear form on the complexified Lie algebra vanishes. By the trace form it is
the pairing with an invariant element, which is zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_adjRep_invariant {ℓ : Module.Dual ℂ (SUAlgebraComplexified N)}
    (hℓ : ∀ (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N), ℓ (adjRep N g A) = ℓ A) : ℓ = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.exists_eq_smul_adjMat_of_equivariant
declarations.doc:
An equivariant linear map from the complexified Lie algebra to the matrices, moved by
conjugation, is a multiple of the matrix of the argument.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_smul_adjMat_of_equivariant
    {Φ : SUAlgebraComplexified N →ₗ[ℂ] Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ}
    (hΦ : ∀ (g : SU N) (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N), Φ (adjRep N g A) = g.1 * Φ A * (g⁻¹).1) :
    ∃ μ : ℂ, Φ = μ • adjMat N

declarations.name: suTensor.generatorVal
declarations.doc:
The generator tensor, the unit `∑ b_a ⊗ bᵃ` of the adjoint color with its second factor
written as a matrix, in `adj ⊗ (ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ)`. Its components are the entries of `λ_a / 2`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def generatorVal :
    SUAlgebraComplexified N ⊗[ℂ] ((Fin N → ℂ) ⊗[ℂ] (Fin N → ℂ))

declarations.name: suTensor.adjContract_generatorVal
declarations.doc:
As a linear map from the complexified Lie algebra, the generator tensor writes the matrix of
the argument in `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjContract_generatorVal (A : SUAlgebraComplexified N) :
    adjContract N _ (generatorVal N) A = adjToPair N A

declarations.name: suTensor.generatorVal_mem_invariants
declarations.doc: The generator tensor is invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma generatorVal_mem_invariants :
    generatorVal N ∈ ((adjRep N).tprod ((fundRep N).tprod (antiFundRep N))).invariants

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_tprod_eq_span_generatorVal
declarations.doc:
The invariants of `adj ⊗ (ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ)`, with the adjoint, the fundamental and the
anti-fundamental representation, are the line through the generator tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_tprod_eq_span_generatorVal :
    ((adjRep N).tprod ((fundRep N).tprod (antiFundRep N))).invariants = ℂ ∙ generatorVal N

declarations.name: suTensor.generator
declarations.doc:
The generator tensor `(Tᵃ)_i^j` with an adjoint, a fundamental and an anti-fundamental
index.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def generator : SuT[N, .adj, .fund, .antiFund]

declarations.name: suTensor.generator_invariant
declarations.doc: The generator tensor is invariant.
declarations.statement: lemma generator_invariant (g : SU N) : g • generator N = generator N

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_adj_fund_antiFund_eq_span_generator
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with an adjoint, a fundamental and an anti-fundamental index are the
line through the generator tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_adj_fund_antiFund_eq_span_generator :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep ![.adj, .fund, .antiFund]).invariants = ℂ ∙ generator N

declarations.name: suTensor.dualBasis_adjBasis
declarations.doc: The dual basis of the Gell-Mann basis under the trace form is half of it.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualBasis_adjBasis (a : GellMann.Index N) :
    (traceForm N).dualBasis (traceForm_nondegenerate N) (adjBasis N) a
      = (1 / 2 : ℂ) • adjBasis N a

declarations.name: suTensor.generatorVal_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
The generator tensor as a sum over the Gell-Mann basis, with the matrices `λ_a / 2` in its
second factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma generatorVal_eq_sum : generatorVal N
    = ∑ a, adjBasis N a ⊗ₜ adjToPair N ((1 / 2 : ℂ) • adjBasis N a)

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_generator
declarations.doc: The components of the generator tensor are the entries of the generators `λ_a / 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_generator (a : GellMann.Index N) (i j : Fin N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (generator N) (fun | 0 => a | 1 => i | 2 => j)
      = GellMann.matrix a i j / 2

modules.title: The Levi-Civita tensors of `SU(N)`
modules.doc:
Up to scale, the Levi-Civita symbol is the only invariant with `N` fundamental indices of
`SU(N)`, and the only one with `N` anti-fundamental indices.

## i. Overview

The tensors with `n` fundamental indices, or with `n` anti-fundamental indices, have the tuples
`Fin n → Fin N` as component indices, and `g` moves the components by one factor of `g`, or of
its complex conjugate, per index (A).

The Levi-Civita symbol `ε_a`, for `a : Fin N → Fin N`, is the sign of `a` when `a` is a
permutation and zero when a label repeats (B). Contracting its indices with the rows `a` of a
matrix `M` gives `ε_a det M`. So the tensors with these components, `leviCivitaFund N` with `N`
fundamental indices and `leviCivitaAntiFund N` with `N` anti-fundamental indices, are invariant,
because `det g = 1` (C).

Conversely, let the components `c` of a tensor with `N` fundamental indices be fixed by `SU(N)`
(D). If a label of `a` repeats, some label `q` is missed by `a`. Take a label `p` that `a` hits
`m` times, and the diagonal element of `SU(N)` with a primitive `(N + 1)`-th root of unity `ω`
at `p`, its conjugate at `q` and one elsewhere. It scales `c a` by `ω ^ m` with `0 < m ≤ N`, so
`c a = 0`. The quarter turn in the plane of two labels `p` and `q` is a signed transposition, and
it gives `c (swap p q ∘ σ) = -c σ` for every permutation `σ`. By induction over transpositions
`c σ = sign σ * c id`, and so `c = c id • ε`. On anti-fundamental indices `g` acts through its
complex conjugate, itself an element of `SU(N)`, and the same holds (E).

The invariant tensors are therefore the line through the Levi-Civita tensor. For `N = 2` the
Levi-Civita tensors are the antisymmetric symbols `epsilonFund` and `epsilonAntiFund`, so the
invariant tensors with two fundamental, or two anti-fundamental, indices of `SU(2)` are the line
through `ε` (F). For `N ≥ 3` there are none with two such indices, which is a centre argument
(`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.CentreEigenspace`).

A family indexed by `Fin n → Fin N` is the map `liftComponents T` out of these tensors, and for
`SU(2)` the invariants of the span of such a family with two indices reduce to the epsilon
contraction `T ![0, 1] - T ![1, 0]` (G).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.leviCivitaCoeff` : the Levi-Civita symbol.
- `suTensor.sum_prod_mul_leviCivitaCoeff` : contracting it with the rows of a matrix gives the
  determinant.
- `suTensor.leviCivitaFund`, `suTensor.leviCivitaAntiFund` : the Levi-Civita tensors.
- `suTensor.invariants_fund_pow_eq_span_leviCivitaFund` : the invariant tensors with `N`
  fundamental indices are the line through it, and its anti-fundamental twin.
- `suTensor.epsilonFund`, `suTensor.epsilonAntiFund` : the antisymmetric symbols of `SU(2)`.
- `suTensor.leviCivitaFund_two` : for `SU(2)` the Levi-Civita tensor is the antisymmetric symbol.
- `suTensor.invariants_fund_pow_two_eq_span_epsilonFund` : the invariant tensors with two
  fundamental indices of `SU(2)` are the line through `ε`, and its anti-fundamental twin.
- `suTensor.invariantReductionToEpsilonFund` : the reduction of the invariants of the span of a
  family to the epsilon contraction, and its anti-fundamental twin.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Tensors with fundamental or with anti-fundamental indices
- B. The Levi-Civita symbol
- C. The Levi-Civita tensors are invariant
- D. Components fixed by `SU(N)`
- E. The invariant tensors
- F. Two indices of `SU(2)`: the antisymmetric symbol
- G. Maps from components

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_smul_fund
declarations.doc:
The components of `g • t` for a tensor with `n` fundamental indices, with one factor of `g` per
index.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_smul_fund {n : ℕ} (g : SU N) (t : (suTensor N).Tensor fun _ : Fin n => .fund)
    (φ : Fin n → Fin N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (g • t) φ
      = ∑ ψ : Fin n → Fin N, (∏ i, g.1 (φ i) (ψ i)) * (Tensor.basis _).repr t ψ

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_smul_antiFund
declarations.doc:
The components of `g • t` for a tensor with `n` anti-fundamental indices, with one factor of the
complex conjugate of `g` per index.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_smul_antiFund {n : ℕ} (g : SU N)
    (t : (suTensor N).Tensor fun _ : Fin n => .antiFund) (φ : Fin n → Fin N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (g • t) φ = ∑ ψ : Fin n → Fin N,
      (∏ i, starRingEnd ℂ (g.1 (φ i) (ψ i))) * (Tensor.basis _).repr t ψ

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaCoeff
declarations.doc:
The Levi-Civita symbol `ε_a` of `N` labels. It is the sign of `a` when `a` is a permutation of
`Fin N`, and zero when a label repeats.
declarations.statement: def leviCivitaCoeff (a : Fin N → Fin N) : ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.sum_mul_leviCivitaCoeff
declarations.doc: A sum against the Levi-Civita symbol is a signed sum over the permutations.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_mul_leviCivitaCoeff (F : (Fin N → Fin N) → ℂ) :
    ∑ a, F a * leviCivitaCoeff a = ∑ σ : Perm (Fin N), (Perm.sign σ : ℂ) * F σ

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaCoeff_perm
declarations.doc: The Levi-Civita symbol at a permutation is its sign.
declarations.statement: lemma leviCivitaCoeff_perm (σ : Perm (Fin N)) : leviCivitaCoeff ⇑σ = (Perm.sign σ : ℂ)

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaCoeff_of_not_injective
declarations.doc: The Levi-Civita symbol vanishes when a label repeats.
declarations.statement:
lemma leviCivitaCoeff_of_not_injective {a : Fin N → Fin N} (ha : ¬ Function.Injective a) :
    leviCivitaCoeff a = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaCoeff_id
declarations.doc: The Levi-Civita symbol at the identity is one.
declarations.statement: lemma leviCivitaCoeff_id : leviCivitaCoeff (id : Fin N → Fin N) = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.sum_prod_mul_leviCivitaCoeff
declarations.doc:
Contracting the indices of the Levi-Civita symbol with the rows `a` of a matrix `M` gives
`ε_a det M`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_prod_mul_leviCivitaCoeff (M : Matrix (Fin N) (Fin N) ℂ) (a : Fin N → Fin N) :
    ∑ b, (∏ i, M (a i) (b i)) * leviCivitaCoeff b = leviCivitaCoeff a * M.det

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaFund
declarations.doc: The Levi-Civita tensor `ε^{a₁ … a_N}` with `N` fundamental indices.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def leviCivitaFund : (suTensor N).Tensor fun _ : Fin N => .fund

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaAntiFund
declarations.doc: The Levi-Civita tensor `ε_{a₁ … a_N}` with `N` anti-fundamental indices.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def leviCivitaAntiFund : (suTensor N).Tensor fun _ : Fin N => .antiFund

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_leviCivitaFund
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_leviCivitaFund (a : Fin N → Fin N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (leviCivitaFund N) a = leviCivitaCoeff a

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_leviCivitaAntiFund
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_leviCivitaAntiFund (a : Fin N → Fin N) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (leviCivitaAntiFund N) a = leviCivitaCoeff a

declarations.name: suTensor.det_val
declarations.statement: lemma det_val (g : SU N) : g.1.det = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.det_map_star_val
declarations.doc: The complex conjugate of an element of `SU(N)` has determinant one.
declarations.statement: lemma det_map_star_val (g : SU N) : (g.1.map star).det = 1

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaFund_invariant
declarations.doc:
The Levi-Civita tensor with `N` fundamental indices is invariant, since `g^{⊗N}` scales it by
`det g = 1`.
declarations.statement: lemma leviCivitaFund_invariant (g : SU N) : g • leviCivitaFund N = leviCivitaFund N

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaAntiFund_invariant
declarations.doc:
The Levi-Civita tensor with `N` anti-fundamental indices is invariant, since `ḡ^{⊗N}` scales it
by the conjugate of `det g = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma leviCivitaAntiFund_invariant (g : SU N) :
    g • leviCivitaAntiFund N = leviCivitaAntiFund N

declarations.name: suTensor.quarterTurn_val_apply
declarations.doc:
The quarter turn in the plane of `p` and `q` is the signed transposition sending `e_p` to
`e_q` and `e_q` to `-e_p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma quarterTurn_val_apply {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) (x y : Fin N) :
    (planeEmbed p q hpq (rotation 0 1 (by norm_num))).1 x y
      = (if x = p then -1 else 1) * (if swap p q x = y then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_prod_mul_of_diagonal
declarations.doc:
A diagonal element of `SU(N)` scales each component by the product of its diagonal entries at
the labels.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_prod_mul_of_diagonal {g : SU N} {d : Fin N → ℂ} (hg : g.1 = diagonal d)
    (a : Fin N → Fin N) : c a = (∏ i, d (a i)) * c a

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_zero_of_not_injective
declarations.doc:
A component with a repeated label vanishes. Some label `q` is then missed, and the diagonal
element with `ω` at `p = a q`, `ω̄` at `q` and one elsewhere, for `ω` a primitive `(N + 1)`-th
root of unity, scales the component by `ω ^ m`, with `m` the number of labels equal to `p`.
declarations.statement: lemma eq_zero_of_not_injective {a : Fin N → Fin N} (ha : ¬ Function.Injective a) : c a = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.prod_quarterTurn_val
declarations.doc:
The product of the quarter turn's entries along a permutation `σ` and labels `b` is `-1` when
`b` is `swap p q ∘ σ` and zero otherwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma prod_quarterTurn_val {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) (σ : Perm (Fin N)) (b : Fin N → Fin N) :
    ∏ i, (planeEmbed p q hpq (rotation 0 1 (by norm_num))).1 (σ i) (b i)
      = if b = ⇑(swap p q * σ) then -1 else 0

declarations.name: suTensor.swap_mul_eq_neg
declarations.doc: The quarter turn in the plane of `p` and `q` gives `c (swap p q ∘ σ) = -c σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma swap_mul_eq_neg {p q : Fin N} (hpq : p ≠ q) (σ : Perm (Fin N)) :
    c ⇑(swap p q * σ) = -c σ

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_sign_mul
declarations.doc: The component at a permutation is its sign times the component at the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma eq_sign_mul (σ : Perm (Fin N)) : c σ = (Perm.sign σ : ℂ) * c id

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_mul_leviCivitaCoeff
declarations.doc: Components fixed by `SU(N)` are those of a multiple of the Levi-Civita symbol.
declarations.statement: lemma eq_mul_leviCivitaCoeff (a : Fin N → Fin N) : c a = c id * leviCivitaCoeff a

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_fund_pow_eq_span_leviCivitaFund
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with `N` fundamental indices of `SU(N)` are the line through the
Levi-Civita tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_fund_pow_eq_span_leviCivitaFund :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep fun _ : Fin N => .fund).invariants = ℂ ∙ leviCivitaFund N

declarations.name: suTensor.starElem
declarations.doc: The complex conjugate of an element of `SU(N)`, itself an element of `SU(N)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def starElem (g : SU N) : SU N

declarations.name: suTensor.starElem_val
declarations.statement: lemma starElem_val (g : SU N) : (starElem g).1 = g.1.map star

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_antiFund_pow_eq_span_leviCivitaAntiFund
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with `N` anti-fundamental indices of `SU(N)` are the line through the
Levi-Civita tensor. Here `g` acts through its complex conjugate, which runs over `SU(N)` with
`g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_antiFund_pow_eq_span_leviCivitaAntiFund :
    ((suTensor N).tensorRep fun _ : Fin N => .antiFund).invariants
      = ℂ ∙ leviCivitaAntiFund N

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilonFund
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric symbol `ε^{ab}` with two fundamental indices of `SU(2)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def epsilonFund : (suTensor 2).Tensor fun _ : Fin 2 => .fund

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilonAntiFund
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric symbol `ε_{ab}` with two anti-fundamental indices of `SU(2)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def epsilonAntiFund : (suTensor 2).Tensor fun _ : Fin 2 => .antiFund

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_epsilonFund
declarations.doc: The components of the antisymmetric symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_epsilonFund (φ : Fin 2 → Fin 2) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr epsilonFund φ
      = (if φ = ![0, 1] then 1 else 0) - (if φ = ![1, 0] then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_epsilonAntiFund
declarations.doc: The components of the antisymmetric symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_epsilonAntiFund (φ : Fin 2 → Fin 2) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr epsilonAntiFund φ
      = (if φ = ![0, 1] then 1 else 0) - (if φ = ![1, 0] then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaCoeff_two
declarations.doc: On two labels the Levi-Civita symbol is `1` at `01`, `-1` at `10` and `0` otherwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma leviCivitaCoeff_two (a : Fin 2 → Fin 2) :
    leviCivitaCoeff a = (if a = ![0, 1] then 1 else 0) - (if a = ![1, 0] then 1 else 0)

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaFund_two
declarations.doc:
For `SU(2)` the Levi-Civita tensor with two fundamental indices is the antisymmetric
symbol.
declarations.statement: lemma leviCivitaFund_two : leviCivitaFund 2 = epsilonFund

declarations.name: suTensor.leviCivitaAntiFund_two
declarations.doc:
For `SU(2)` the Levi-Civita tensor with two anti-fundamental indices is the antisymmetric
symbol.
declarations.statement: lemma leviCivitaAntiFund_two : leviCivitaAntiFund 2 = epsilonAntiFund

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilonFund_invariant
declarations.doc:
The antisymmetric symbol with two fundamental indices is invariant, being the Levi-Civita
tensor of `SU(2)`.
declarations.statement: lemma epsilonFund_invariant (g : SU 2) : g • epsilonFund = epsilonFund

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilonAntiFund_invariant
declarations.doc:
The antisymmetric symbol with two anti-fundamental indices is invariant, being the Levi-Civita
tensor of `SU(2)`.
declarations.statement: lemma epsilonAntiFund_invariant (g : SU 2) : g • epsilonAntiFund = epsilonAntiFund

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_fund_pow_two_eq_span_epsilonFund
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with two fundamental indices of `SU(2)` are the line through the
antisymmetric symbol, the Levi-Civita tensor of `SU(2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_fund_pow_two_eq_span_epsilonFund :
    ((suTensor 2).tensorRep fun _ : Fin 2 => .fund).invariants = ℂ ∙ epsilonFund

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_antiFund_pow_two_eq_span_epsilonAntiFund
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with two anti-fundamental indices of `SU(2)` are the line through the
antisymmetric symbol, the Levi-Civita tensor of `SU(2)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariants_antiFund_pow_two_eq_span_epsilonAntiFund :
    ((suTensor 2).tensorRep fun _ : Fin 2 => .antiFund).invariants = ℂ ∙ epsilonAntiFund

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_fund_smul_of_law
declarations.doc:
A linear map moving a family with `n` fundamental labels by one factor of `g` per label
intertwines the map of the family with the action of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_fund_smul_of_law {n : ℕ} (T : (Fin n → Fin N) → B) {σ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B} (g : SU N)
    (hσ : ∀ l : Fin n → Fin N, σ (T l) = ∑ a : Fin n → Fin N, (∏ i, g.1 (a i) (l i)) • T a)
    (t : (suTensor N).Tensor fun _ : Fin n => .fund) :
    σ (liftComponents (S := suTensor N) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .fund) T t)
      = liftComponents (S := suTensor N) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .fund) T (g • t)

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_antiFund_smul_of_law
declarations.doc:
A linear map moving a family with `n` anti-fundamental labels by one factor of the complex
conjugate of `g` per label intertwines the map of the family with the action of `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_antiFund_smul_of_law {n : ℕ} (T : (Fin n → Fin N) → B) {σ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (g : SU N) (hσ : ∀ l : Fin n → Fin N, σ (T l)
      = ∑ a : Fin n → Fin N, (∏ i, starRingEnd ℂ (g.1 (a i) (l i))) • T a)
    (t : (suTensor N).Tensor fun _ : Fin n => .antiFund) :
    σ (liftComponents (S := suTensor N) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .antiFund) T t)
      = liftComponents (S := suTensor N) (c := fun _ : Fin n => .antiFund) T (g • t)

declarations.name: suTensor.isEquivariant_liftComponents_fund
declarations.doc:
The map of a family with `n` fundamental labels is equivariant when the family moves by one
factor of `g` per label, the summed label first.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_fund {n : ℕ} (T : (Fin n → Fin N) → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SU N) (l : Fin n → Fin N), ρ g (T l)
      = ∑ a : Fin n → Fin N, (∏ i, g.1 (a i) (l i)) • T a) :
    (suTensor N).IsEquivariant (fun _ => .fund) ρ (liftComponents T)

declarations.name: suTensor.isEquivariant_liftComponents_antiFund
declarations.doc:
The map of a family with `n` anti-fundamental labels is equivariant when the family moves by
one factor of the complex conjugate of `g` per label, the summed label first.
declarations.statement:
lemma isEquivariant_liftComponents_antiFund {n : ℕ} (T : (Fin n → Fin N) → B)
    (hT : ∀ (g : SU N) (l : Fin n → Fin N), ρ g (T l)
      = ∑ a : Fin n → Fin N, (∏ i, starRingEnd ℂ (g.1 (a i) (l i))) • T a) :
    (suTensor N).IsEquivariant (fun _ => .antiFund) ρ (liftComponents T)

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_epsilonFund
declarations.doc:
The map of a family with two fundamental labels sends the antisymmetric symbol to the
epsilon contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_epsilonFund (T : (Fin 2 → Fin 2) → B) :
    liftComponents (S := suTensor 2) (c := fun _ : Fin 2 => .fund) T epsilonFund
      = T ![0, 1] - T ![1, 0]

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_epsilonAntiFund
declarations.doc:
The map of a family with two anti-fundamental labels sends the antisymmetric symbol to the
epsilon contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_epsilonAntiFund (T : (Fin 2 → Fin 2) → B) :
    liftComponents (S := suTensor 2) (c := fun _ : Fin 2 => .antiFund) T epsilonAntiFund
      = T ![0, 1] - T ![1, 0]

declarations.name: suTensor.invariantReductionToEpsilonFund
declarations.doc:
For a family with two fundamental labels of `SU(2)` whose map is equivariant, the invariants
of the span reduce to the span of the epsilon contraction `T ![0, 1] - T ![1, 0]`.

declarations.name: suTensor.invariantReductionToEpsilonAntiFund
declarations.doc:
For a family with two anti-fundamental labels of `SU(2)` whose map is equivariant, the
invariants of the span reduce to the span of the epsilon contraction
`T ![0, 1] - T ![1, 0]`.

modules.title: The pairings of four fundamental indices of `SU(2)` by the Levi-Civita symbol
modules.doc:
The invariant tensors with four fundamental indices of `SU(2)` are spanned by two pairings of
antisymmetric symbols.

## i. Overview

Four fundamental indices of `SU(2)` can be paired off by the antisymmetric symbol in three
ways, and the Schouten identity is one linear relation between them. The invariant tensors are
the combinations of the pairings `ε^{ab} ε^{cd}` and `ε^{ac} ε^{bd}`, `epsilonPair₁₂` and
`epsilonPair₁₃` (A, B).

Three elements of `SU(2)` pin the components `c` of an invariant tensor down (B). The phase
`diag (ω, ω̄)`, for `ω` a primitive eighth root of unity, scales `c l` by `ω` to the power of the
number of zeros of `l` plus seven times the number of ones, so only the six balanced components,
with two labels of each kind, survive. The quarter turn equates each balanced component with its
complement, leaving three unknowns. The eighth turn carries `c ![0, 0, 0, 0]` to a quarter of the
sum of the balanced components, which therefore vanishes. Two unknowns remain, and they are the
coefficients of the two pairings.

For an equivariant map out of these tensors, and for the map `liftComponents T` of a family, the
invariants reduce to the span of the images of the two pairings (C).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.epsilonPair₁₂`, `suTensor.epsilonPair₁₃` : the two pairings.
- `suTensor.invariants_fund_pow_four_eq_span_epsilonPairs` : the invariant tensors are the span
  of the two pairings.
- `suTensor.reducesInvariantsTo_span_epsilonContractions` : the reduction of the invariants of
  the span of a family.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The two pairings
- B. The invariant tensors
- C. The invariants of the span of a family

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilon
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric symbol of `SU(2)` as a function of two labels.
declarations.statement: def epsilon (a b : Fin 2) : ℂ

declarations.name: suTensor.sum_mul_epsilon
declarations.doc: The antisymmetric symbol is invariant, `∑ g a x g b y ε x y = det g ε a b`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_mul_epsilon (g : SU 2) (a b : Fin 2) :
    ∑ x, ∑ y, g.1 a x * g.1 b y * epsilon x y = epsilon a b

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilonPair₁₂
declarations.doc:
The pairing `ε^{ab} ε^{cd}` of the first index with the second and the third with the
fourth.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def epsilonPair₁₂ : (suTensor 2).Tensor fun _ : Fin 4 => .fund

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilonPair₁₃
declarations.doc:
The pairing `ε^{ac} ε^{bd}` of the first index with the third and the second with the
fourth.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def epsilonPair₁₃ : (suTensor 2).Tensor fun _ : Fin 4 => .fund

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_epsilonPair₁₂
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_epsilonPair₁₂ (l : Fin 4 → Fin 2) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr epsilonPair₁₂ l = epsilon (l 0) (l 1) * epsilon (l 2) (l 3)

declarations.name: suTensor.basis_repr_epsilonPair₁₃
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_repr_epsilonPair₁₃ (l : Fin 4 → Fin 2) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr epsilonPair₁₃ l = epsilon (l 0) (l 2) * epsilon (l 1) (l 3)

declarations.name: suTensor.sum_fin_four_arrow
declarations.doc: A sum over four labels is a fourfold sum.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_fin_four_arrow {M : Type*} [AddCommMonoid M] (F : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → M) :
    ∑ ψ : Fin 4 → Fin 2, F ψ = ∑ x, ∑ y, ∑ z, ∑ w, F ![x, y, z, w]

declarations.name: suTensor.sum_mul_epsilon_mul_epsilon
declarations.doc: A product of two invariant pairings of labels is invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_mul_epsilon_mul_epsilon (g : SU 2) (l : Fin 4 → Fin 2) (i j k m : Fin 4)
    (hijkm : ∀ ψ : Fin 4 → Fin 2, (∏ r, g.1 (l r) (ψ r))
      = g.1 (l i) (ψ i) * g.1 (l j) (ψ j) * (g.1 (l k) (ψ k) * g.1 (l m) (ψ m)))
    (F : Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Fin 2 → Fin 4 → Fin 2) (hF : ∀ x y z w, F x y z w i = x ∧
      F x y z w j = y ∧ F x y z w k = z ∧ F x y z w m = w)
    (hsum : ∀ G : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → ℂ, ∑ ψ, G ψ = ∑ x, ∑ y, ∑ z, ∑ w, G (F x y z w)) :
    ∑ ψ : Fin 4 → Fin 2, (∏ r, g.1 (l r) (ψ r)) * (epsilon (ψ i) (ψ j) * epsilon (ψ k) (ψ m))
      = epsilon (l i) (l j) * epsilon (l k) (l m)

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilonPair₁₂_invariant
declarations.doc: The pairing `ε^{ab} ε^{cd}` is invariant.
declarations.statement: lemma epsilonPair₁₂_invariant (g : SU 2) : g • epsilonPair₁₂ = epsilonPair₁₂

declarations.name: suTensor.epsilonPair₁₃_invariant
declarations.doc: The pairing `ε^{ac} ε^{bd}` is invariant.
declarations.statement: lemma epsilonPair₁₃_invariant (g : SU 2) : g • epsilonPair₁₃ = epsilonPair₁₃

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_zero_of_not_dvd
declarations.doc:
The phase `diag (ω, ω̄)`, with `ω` a primitive eighth root of unity, scales the component at
`l` by `ω` to the power of the number of zeros of `l` plus seven times the number of ones, so
the component vanishes unless that power is a multiple of eight.
declarations.statement: lemma eq_zero_of_not_dvd (l : Fin 4 → Fin 2) (hl : ¬ 8 ∣ ∑ i, ![1, 7] (l i)) : c l = 0

declarations.name: suTensor.quarterTurn_relations
declarations.doc: The quarter turn equates each balanced component with its complement.

declarations.name: suTensor.unbalanced_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The ten unbalanced components vanish.

declarations.name: suTensor.sum_balanced_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The eighth turn carries the component at `![0, 0, 0, 0]` to a quarter of the sum of the
balanced components, so that sum vanishes.

declarations.name: suTensor.eq_add_of_pairings
declarations.doc:
An invariant function of four labels is a combination of the two pairings, with the
components at `![0, 1, 0, 1]` and `![0, 0, 1, 1]` as coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_add_of_pairings (l : Fin 4 → Fin 2) :
    c l = c ![0, 1, 0, 1] * (epsilon (l 0) (l 1) * epsilon (l 2) (l 3))
      + c ![0, 0, 1, 1] * (epsilon (l 0) (l 2) * epsilon (l 1) (l 3))

declarations.name: suTensor.invariants_fund_pow_four_eq_span_epsilonPairs
declarations.doc:
The invariant tensors with four fundamental indices of `SU(2)` are the span of the two
pairings of their indices by the antisymmetric symbol.

declarations.name: suTensor.reducesInvariantsTo_span_map_epsilonPairs
declarations.doc:
For any equivariant linear map out of the tensors with four fundamental indices of `SU(2)`,
the invariants of its range reduce to the span of the images of the two pairings.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_span_map_epsilonPairs
    {f : (suTensor 2).Tensor (fun _ : Fin 4 => .fund) →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hf : (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant (fun _ => .fund) ρ f) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SU 2 => ρ g) (LinearMap.range f)
      (Submodule.span ℂ {f epsilonPair₁₂, f epsilonPair₁₃})

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_epsilonPair₁₂
declarations.doc:
The map of a family sends the first pairing to the contraction pairing the first label with
the second and the third with the fourth.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_epsilonPair₁₂ (T : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → B) :
    liftComponents (S := suTensor 2) (c := fun _ : Fin 4 => .fund) T epsilonPair₁₂
      = T ![0, 1, 0, 1] - T ![0, 1, 1, 0] - T ![1, 0, 0, 1] + T ![1, 0, 1, 0]

declarations.name: suTensor.liftComponents_epsilonPair₁₃
declarations.doc:
The map of a family sends the second pairing to the contraction pairing the first label with
the third and the second with the fourth.
declarations.statement:
lemma liftComponents_epsilonPair₁₃ (T : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → B) :
    liftComponents (S := suTensor 2) (c := fun _ : Fin 4 => .fund) T epsilonPair₁₃
      = T ![0, 0, 1, 1] - T ![0, 1, 1, 0] - T ![1, 0, 0, 1] + T ![1, 1, 0, 0]

declarations.name: suTensor.reducesInvariantsTo_span_epsilonContractions
declarations.doc:
For a family with four fundamental labels of `SU(2)` whose map is equivariant, the invariants
of the span of the family reduce to the span of its two epsilon contractions.
declarations.statement:
lemma reducesInvariantsTo_span_epsilonContractions {T : (Fin 4 → Fin 2) → B}
    (hT : (suTensor 2).IsEquivariant (fun _ => .fund) ρ (liftComponents T)) :
    ReducesInvariantsTo (fun g : SU 2 => ρ g) (Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range T))
      (Submodule.span ℂ
        {T ![0, 1, 0, 1] - T ![0, 1, 1, 0] - T ![1, 0, 0, 1] + T ![1, 0, 1, 0],
          T ![0, 0, 1, 1] - T ![0, 1, 1, 0] - T ![1, 0, 0, 1] + T ![1, 1, 0, 0]})

modules.title: The complex tensor species of `SU(N)`
modules.doc:
The tensors of `SU(N)` with fundamental, anti-fundamental and adjoint indices.

## i. Overview

The complex tensors of `SU(N)` carry three kinds of index, in analogy with the complex Lorentz
tensors `complexLorentzTensor`: a fundamental index, an anti-fundamental index and an adjoint index.
`suTensor N` is the tensor species with these three colors. The fundamental color is `Fin N → ℂ`
moved by `g`, the anti-fundamental color is `Fin N → ℂ` moved by `(g⁻¹)ᵀ` (for a unitary `g` the
complex conjugate), and the adjoint color is the complexification
`SUAlgebraComplexified N = ℂ ⊗[ℝ] su(N)` of the Lie algebra `SUAlgebra N` of traceless hermitian
matrices, moved by the adjoint representation `adjRep` with the generalized Gell-Mann matrices as
basis, as set up in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.Adjoint`. The type of tensors
with colors `c₁, …, cₙ` is written `SuT[N, c₁, …, cₙ]`.

The fundamental and anti-fundamental colors are dual to each other and contract by the dot
product, with unit `∑ eᵢ ⊗ eᵢ`. The adjoint color is dual to itself and contracts by the trace
form `tr (A B)` (`adjContr`), with unit `∑ λ_a ⊗ λᵃ` for the Gell-Mann matrices `λ_a` and their
trace-dual basis `λᵃ = λ_a / 2`. In the standard basis the matrix of `g` is `g` on the
fundamental color and `(g⁻¹)ᵀ` on the anti-fundamental color (F). The species has no metric
(`TensorSpecies.WithMetric`). For `N ≥ 3` the fundamental of `SU(N)` is not self-dual, so there is
no invariant in `ℂᴺ ⊗ ℂᴺ` to raise and lower its indices with. A tensor with one adjoint index
is an element of the adjoint representation, which has no invariants but zero, so neither has the
tensor (G).

## ii. Key results

- `suTensor.Color` : the fundamental, anti-fundamental and adjoint colors.
- `suTensor.fundRep`, `suTensor.antiFundRep` : the fundamental and anti-fundamental
  representations.
- `suTensor` : the complex tensor species of `SU(N)`, with the notation `SuT[N, c₁, …, cₙ]`.
- `suTensor.toMatrix_fundRep`, `suTensor.toMatrix_antiFundRep` : the matrices of the fundamental
  and anti-fundamental colors.
- `suTensor.invariants_adj_eq_bot` : there are no invariant tensors with one adjoint index but
  zero.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The colors and the carriers
- B. The representations
- C. The contractions
- D. The units
- E. The tensor species
- F. The matrices of the fundamental and anti-fundamental colors
- G. One adjoint index

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The colors and the carriers
## B. The representations
## C. The contractions

## D. The units

The unit of a color is determined by its contraction. For a contraction `V ⊗ W → ℂ`, an element
`U ∈ W ⊗ V` is sent to the endomorphism `x ↦ ∑ contr (x ⊗ wᵢ) vᵢ` of `V` (`coevalMap`), and `U` is
a unit exactly when this is the identity. When the contraction separates `W` the map is
injective, so a unit is unique, and it is invariant, its transform being sent to
`g ∘ id ∘ g⁻¹ = id`.
## E. The tensor species
## F. The matrices of the fundamental and anti-fundamental colors
## G. One adjoint index

declarations.doc:
The contraction of a fundamental against an anti-fundamental index, the dot product
`v ⊗ w ↦ ∑ vᵢ wᵢ`.
declarations.statement:

    (Representation.trivial ℂ (SU N) ℂ)

The contraction of an anti-fundamental against a fundamental index, the dot product
`w ⊗ v ↦ ∑ wᵢ vᵢ`.

declarations.name: suTensor.coevalMap
declarations.doc: The endomorphism `x ↦ ∑ contr (x ⊗ wᵢ) vᵢ` of `V` attached to `∑ wᵢ ⊗ vᵢ ∈ W ⊗ V`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def coevalMap (contr : (ρ.tprod σ).IntertwiningMap
    (Representation.trivial ℂ (SU N) ℂ)) : W ⊗[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V

declarations.name: suTensor.coevalMap_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma coevalMap_tmul (w : W) (v x : V) :
    coevalMap contr (w ⊗ₜ v) x = contr (x ⊗ₜ w) • v

declarations.name: suTensor.lid_rTensor_assoc_symm_eq_coevalMap
declarations.doc: The contraction of `x` against the first factor of `U` is `coevalMap contr U x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lid_rTensor_assoc_symm_eq_coevalMap (x : V) (U : W ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    TensorProduct.lid ℂ V (contr.toLinearMap.rTensor V
      ((TensorProduct.assoc ℂ V W V).symm (x ⊗ₜ[ℂ] U))) = coevalMap contr U x

declarations.name: suTensor.coevalMap_injective
declarations.doc: `coevalMap` is injective when the contraction separates `W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coevalMap_injective [FiniteDimensional ℂ V]
    (h : Function.Injective (TensorProduct.curry contr.toLinearMap).flip) :
    Function.Injective (coevalMap contr)

declarations.name: suTensor.coevalMap_map
declarations.doc:
Transforming both factors of `U` conjugates `coevalMap contr U`, by the invariance of the
contraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma coevalMap_map (g : SU N) (U : W ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    coevalMap contr (TensorProduct.map (σ g) (ρ g) U)
      = ρ g ∘ₗ coevalMap contr U ∘ₗ ρ g⁻¹

declarations.name: suTensor.map_eq_self_of_coevalMap_eq_id
declarations.doc:
An element whose `coevalMap` is the identity is invariant, when the contraction separates
`W`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_eq_self_of_coevalMap_eq_id [FiniteDimensional ℂ V]
    (h : Function.Injective (TensorProduct.curry contr.toLinearMap).flip) {U : W ⊗[ℂ] V}
    (hU : coevalMap contr U = LinearMap.id) (g : SU N) :
    TensorProduct.map (σ g) (ρ g) U = U

declarations.doc: The unit intertwining map `a ↦ a • U` of an invariant element `U ∈ W ⊗ V`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def unitOf {U : W ⊗[ℂ] V} (hU : ∀ g : SU N, TensorProduct.map (σ g) (ρ g) U = U) :
    (Representation.trivial ℂ (SU N) ℂ).IntertwiningMap (σ.tprod ρ)

declarations.name: suTensor.unitOf_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma unitOf_apply {U : W ⊗[ℂ] V} (hU : ∀ g : SU N, TensorProduct.map (σ g) (ρ g) U = U)
    (a : ℂ) : unitOf hU a = a • U

noncomputable def antiFundUnit : (Representation.trivial ℂ (SU N) ℂ).IntertwiningMap

The element `∑ b_a ⊗ bᵃ` of `su(N)_ℂ ⊗ su(N)_ℂ`, for the Gell-Mann basis `b` and its dual basis

declarations.doc: The unit of the adjoint color, `∑ b_a ⊗ bᵃ`.
declarations.statement:

declarations.doc:
The complex tensor species of `SU(N)`, with fundamental, anti-fundamental and adjoint
indices. The fundamental and anti-fundamental colors are dual to each other, the adjoint
color dual to itself.

    (modules N) (basisIdx N) (rep N) (basis N)

declarations.name: suTensor.toMatrix_fundRep
declarations.doc: The matrix of `g` on the fundamental color is `g`.
declarations.statement:

    LinearMap.toMatrix (Pi.basisFun ℂ (Fin N)) (Pi.basisFun ℂ (Fin N)) (fundRep N g) = g.1

declarations.doc: The matrix of `g` on the anti-fundamental color is `(g⁻¹)ᵀ`.

    LinearMap.toMatrix (Pi.basisFun ℂ (Fin N)) (Pi.basisFun ℂ (Fin N)) (antiFundRep N g)
      = (g⁻¹).1ᵀ

There are no invariant tensors with one adjoint index but zero. A tensor with one adjoint
index is `fromSingleT` of an element of the adjoint representation, which has none.
declarations.statement: lemma invariants_adj_eq_bot : ((suTensor N).tensorRep ![.adj]).invariants = ⊥

modules.title: The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
The average of the derivatives of the Maurer–Cartan form over its directions.

## i. Overview

The Maurer–Cartan form `ω_μ(U) = (∂_μ U) U⁻¹` of a gauge jet `U` of a global gauge group `G` is
`G.maurerCartan`, subject to the cocycle law `maurerCartan_cocycle`, its value
`maurerCartan_gaugeJetOfConstant` on constants, and the flatness (structure) equation
`maurerCartan_structure`. This file develops what follows from those laws alone, for any global
gauge group. The statements are about the form `−ω_μ(U) = −(∂_μ U) U⁻¹`, the sign in which the
transformation laws of gauge fields use it.

The main construction is the *symmetrized* Maurer–Cartan form

  `ω̄_r(U) = (1 / |r|) ∑_{μ ∈ r} ∂_{r − {μ}} ω_μ(U)`,

the average over which direction of the multiset `r` is carried by the form itself rather than by a
derivative. Its point is `iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add`: an iterated
derivative `∂_s ω_μ(U)` is the symmetrized form at `μ ::ₘ s` plus an average of iterated derivatives
of *brackets* of Maurer–Cartan forms in strictly fewer directions. This is the structural
equation used to trade an antisymmetric part for lower-order data. It gives the inductive step
`evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq`, and iterating it,
`evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all`, the base-point Taylor
data of `ω` are determined by the base-point symmetrized data. How this determines a pure jet, and
the truncation filtration it defines, is the subject of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.Truncation`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_structure` : the structural
  equation at the base point, to all orders.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm` : the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form, with
  `symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_singleton` and the recursion
  `symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_cons`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add` : the
  symmetrization defect is an average of brackets in fewer directions.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all` :
  the base-point symmetrized data determine the base-point Taylor data of `ω`, with the inductive
  step `evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_zero_of_symmetrized_eq_zero` : the
  base-point half of Maurer–Cartan triangularity.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_eq_zero_iff` : the Maurer–Cartan form vanishes
  exactly on the constant jets.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The structural equation at the base point
- B. The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form
- C. Determination of the Maurer–Cartan form by its symmetrized coefficients
- D. Vanishing of the Maurer–Cartan form

## iv. References

* None.

## B. The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form
## C. Determination of the Maurer–Cartan form by its symmetrized coefficients
## D. Vanishing of the Maurer–Cartan form

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_structure
declarations.doc:
The all-orders structural equation of the Maurer–Cartan form `−ω`, at the base point.
It is the `s`-th derivative of `∂_μ (−ω_ν) − ∂_ν (−ω_μ) + ⁅−ω_μ, −ω_ν⁆ = 0`, with the bracket
expanded by the iterated Leibniz rule.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_structure
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ (μ ::ₘ s) (-G.maurerCartan U ν)) =
      G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ (ν ::ₘ s) (-G.maurerCartan U μ))
      - (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          ⁅G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p.1 (-G.maurerCartan U μ)),
            G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p.2 (-G.maurerCartan U ν))⁆).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form `ω̄_r(U) = (1/|r|) ∑_{μ ∈ r} ∂_{r − {μ}} ω_μ(U)`,
the average, over the directions of `r`, of the Maurer–Cartan form in one direction
differentiated along the remaining ones.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    G.jetLieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_zero (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U 0 = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_singleton (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U {μ} = (-G.maurerCartan U μ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_cons
declarations.doc:
The recursion for the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form, peeling one direction off the
multiset.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm_cons (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U (μ ::ₘ r) =
    (1/(r.card + 1 : ℝ) : ℝ) • (G.iteratedDerivJ r (-G.maurerCartan U μ))
    + ((r.card : ℝ)/(r.card + 1 : ℝ)) •
      G.derivJ μ (G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U r)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add
declarations.doc:
The symmetrization defect of the Maurer–Cartan form. An iterated derivative of
`ω` is the corresponding symmetrized form plus an average of iterated derivatives
of brackets of `ω` in strictly fewer directions. This is the structural equation
`maurerCartan_structure` used to trade the antisymmetric part for lower-order data.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.iteratedDerivJ s (-G.maurerCartan U μ) =
      G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U (μ ::ₘ s) +
      (1/(s.card + 1 : ℝ)) • (s.map fun ν =>
        G.iteratedDerivJ (s.erase ν)
          ⁅-G.maurerCartan U μ, -G.maurerCartan U ν⁆).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_zero_of_symmetrized_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Maurer–Cartan triangularity, base-point half. If the base-point symmetrized
Maurer–Cartan data of `U` vanish in every nonempty multiset of at most `n` directions,
then so do all its base-point Maurer–Cartan Taylor coefficients below order `n`. The
induction is on the order. The symmetrization defect
`iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_symmetrized_add` expresses `∂_s ω_μ` through the
symmetrized form, which vanishes by hypothesis, and brackets of `ω`s differentiated
strictly fewer times, which vanish by the inductive hypothesis through
`evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_bracket_congr`.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_zero_of_symmetrized_eq_zero
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) {n : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), r ≠ 0 → r.card ≤ n →
      G.evalLie (G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U r) = 0)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (hs : s.card < n) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s (-G.maurerCartan U μ))
      = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq
declarations.doc:
The determination step. If the base-point symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of `U` and
`V` agree, and their Maurer–Cartan Taylor data agree in fewer than `n` directions,
then they agree in `n` directions.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq
    (U V : G.gaugeJetGroup) (n : ℕ)
    (hsym : ∀ r, G.evalLie (G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U r) =
      G.evalLie (G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm V r))
    (ih : ∀ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), s.card < n →
      G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s (-G.maurerCartan U μ)) =
        G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s
          (-G.maurerCartan V μ)))
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (hs : s.card = n) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s (-G.maurerCartan U μ)) =
      G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s
        (-G.maurerCartan V μ))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized data determine the Maurer–Cartan Taylor data. If the base-point
symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of `U` and `V` agree, so do all base-point Taylor
coefficients of their Maurer–Cartan forms. Strong induction on the order, with
`evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq` as the step.
declarations.statement:
lemma evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all
    (U V : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (hsym : ∀ r, G.evalLie (G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U r) =
      G.evalLie (G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm V r))
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s (-G.maurerCartan U μ)) =
      G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ s
        (-G.maurerCartan V μ))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_eq_zero_iff
declarations.doc: The Maurer–Cartan form of a gauge jet vanishes exactly when the jet is constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_eq_zero_iff (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    G.maurerCartan U = 0 ↔ U = G.gaugeJetOfConstant (G.evalGaugeJet U)

modules.title: The truncation filtration of the jet gauge group
modules.doc:
The normal subgroups of gauge jets that are trivial up to a given order.

## i. Overview

A jet of gauge transformations is *trivial to order `n`* when it agrees with the identity up to and
including its `n`-th derivatives. For a matrix group this is a statement about Taylor coefficients
of matrix entries. It is phrased here through two things given at the base point, the value
`G.evalGaugeJet U` and the Maurer–Cartan form: `U` is trivial to order `n` when
`G.evalGaugeJet U = 1` and the base-point Taylor coefficients of `ω_μ(U)` vanish below order
`n`. The Taylor–Leibniz theorem makes these jets a subgroup `truncationKer n`, normal in
`G.gaugeJetGroup`, and the subgroups decrease with `n`.

The zeroth member, the *pure jets* with `G.evalGaugeJet U = 1`, is the complement of the constant
jets. Every jet factors uniquely as a pure jet times the constant jet of its value,
`truncationProjZero` and `eq_truncationProjZero_mul_ofConstant`. A pure jet is determined by its
Maurer–Cartan form, and hence by the base-point values of the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan form,
`symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff`. Membership in `truncationKer n` is exactly the vanishing of those
symmetrized data up to order `n`.

What a jet trivial to order `n` does to the fields is the point of the filtration: all its
adjoint Taylor coefficients of order between `1` and `n` vanish,
`adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer`, so it acts on the gauge-field symbols with at
most `n` derivatives by a pure translation.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.truncationKer` : the jets trivial to order `n`, as a subgroup.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_truncationKer_zero_iff_evalGaugeJet` : the pure jets.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer` : deep jets kill the positive
  adjoint coefficients.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.truncationKer_normal` : the filtration is by normal subgroups.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.truncationProjZero` : the projection of a jet onto the pure jets.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero` : a pure jet is determined by its
  Maurer–Cartan form.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_injective` : and by its symmetrized
  Maurer–Cartan data.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_truncationKer_iff_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero` : the
  filtration through the symmetrized data.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.radial` : the radial component `−∑_μ x_μ ω_μ` of the Maurer–Cartan form,
  whose Taylor data are the symmetrized data.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_radial_eq` : radial integrability, which with the realisation of
  Taylor data makes the symmetrized data free coordinates on the pure jets,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_bijective`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.truncation` : the `n`-th truncation of a gauge jet, a matrix of
  polynomials.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.truncation_eq_one_of_mem_truncationKer` : jets trivial to order `n`
  truncate to the identity.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The truncation filtration
- B. The adjoint coefficients of a deep jet
- C. Normality
- D. The projection onto the pure jets
- E. Pure jets and their Maurer–Cartan data
- F. The radial component of the Maurer–Cartan form
- G. Radial integrability
- H. Truncation of a gauge jet

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The truncation filtration
## B. The adjoint coefficients of a deep jet
## C. Normality
## D. The projection onto the pure jets
## E. Pure jets and their Maurer–Cartan data

## F. The radial component of the Maurer–Cartan form

The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of a pure jet are, up to the normalization by the
order, the base-point Taylor data of a single element of `G.jetLieSubalgebra`, the radial
component `ρ(U) = −∑_μ x_μ ω_μ(U)` of the Maurer–Cartan form. This is the Euler identity applied
to each summand.

## G. Radial integrability

Every Lie algebra jet vanishing at the base point is the radial component of the
Maurer–Cartan form of a pure jet, the jet `U` solving `E U = −A U` with `U(0) = 1`, from
`GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_sum_X_smul_maurerCartan_eq`. With the realisation of Taylor data,
`GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_eq`, this makes the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan
data free coordinates on the pure jets.

## H. Truncation of a gauge jet

Truncating a gauge jet at order `n` sets to zero, in every matrix entry, the Taylor
coefficients of total degree above `n`. This is a plain function into matrices, not a
homomorphism, since deleting the coefficients above order `n` breaks multiplicativity
between orders `n + 1` and `2n`. A jet trivial to order `n` in the sense of `truncationKer`
truncates to the identity, by the Euler vanishing principle applied to
`∂_ρ U = ω_ρ(U) U`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.truncationKer
declarations.doc:
The jets trivial to order `n`, with value the identity and with the base-point Taylor
coefficients of the Maurer–Cartan form vanishing below order `n`. Closure under products and
inverses is the cocycle law together with the Taylor–Leibniz theorem for the adjoint action.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def truncationKer (n : ℕ) : Subgroup G.gaugeJetGroup

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_truncationKer_zero_iff_evalGaugeJet
declarations.doc: The zeroth truncation kernel is the group of pure jets, those with identity value.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_truncationKer_zero_iff_evalGaugeJet {U : G.gaugeJetGroup} : U ∈ G.truncationKer 0 ↔
    G.evalGaugeJet U = 1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
Deep jets kill the positive adjoint coefficients. For a jet trivial to order `n`, the
adjoint coefficients of order between `1` and `n` vanish. One derivative of the adjoint
is `ad` of the Maurer–Cartan form, whose base-point data vanish below order `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer {n : ℕ} {U : G.gaugeJetGroup}
    (hU : U ∈ G.truncationKer n)
    {x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)} (hx : x ≠ 0) (hxn : x.card ≤ n) :
    G.adjointCoeff U x = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc: The dual form of `adjointCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_mul_of_mem_truncationKer_right
declarations.doc: Up to order `n`, a jet trivial to order `n` is invisible on the right of a product.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_conj_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
Up to order `n`, a conjugate of a jet trivial to order `n` has the adjoint
coefficients of the identity.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_adjoint_conj_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
Up to order `n`, a conjugate of a jet trivial to order `n` acts trivially on the
base-point Taylor data of the jet Lie algebra.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.truncationKer_normal
declarations.doc:
The truncation kernels are normal subgroups, since conjugating a jet trivial to order `n`
gives a jet trivial to order `n`.
declarations.statement: instance truncationKer_normal (n : ℕ) : (G.truncationKer n).Normal

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.truncationProjZero
declarations.doc:
The projection `U ↦ U · (U₀)⁻¹` of a jet onto the pure jets, stripping its value.
This is not a group homomorphism. It is the cocycle of the splitting of `G.gaugeJetGroup` by
the constant jets.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def truncationProjZero (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) : G.truncationKer 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.coe_truncationProjZero
declarations.statement:
lemma coe_truncationProjZero (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    (G.truncationProjZero U : G.gaugeJetGroup) = U *
      (G.gaugeJetOfConstant (G.evalGaugeJet U))⁻¹

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.eq_truncationProjZero_mul_ofConstant
declarations.doc: Every jet is its pure part times the constant jet of its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_truncationProjZero_mul_ofConstant (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    U = G.truncationProjZero U * G.gaugeJetOfConstant (G.evalGaugeJet U)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of a pure jet, the base-point values of its
symmetrized Maurer–Cartan forms, indexed by nonempty multisets of directions. Total
symmetry is automatic from the multiset indexing.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff (U : G.truncationKer 0)
    (r : {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0}) : G.lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_apply (U : G.truncationKer 0)
    (r : {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0}) :
    G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U r =
      G.evalLie (G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanForm U.1 r.1)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_truncationKer_of_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Maurer–Cartan triangularity. A pure jet whose symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data vanish
up to order `n` is trivial to order `n`. The symmetrized data control the Taylor data of
the Maurer–Cartan form through the symmetrization defect.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_truncationKer_of_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero (U : G.truncationKer 0)
    (n : ℕ) (h : ∀ (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (hr : r ≠ 0), r.card ≤ n →
      G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U ⟨r, hr⟩ = 0) :
    U.1 ∈ G.truncationKer n

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
Conversely, the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data of a jet trivial to order `n` vanish
up to order `n`, since each term of the symmetrized form carries fewer than `n`
derivatives.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_truncationKer_iff_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
The truncation filtration through the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data. A pure jet is
trivial to order `n` exactly when its symmetrized data vanish up to order `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_truncationKer_iff_symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_zero (U : G.truncationKer 0)
    (n : ℕ) : U.1 ∈ G.truncationKer n ↔
      ∀ (r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (hr : r ≠ 0), r.card ≤ n →
        G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U ⟨r, hr⟩ = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero
declarations.doc:
A pure jet is determined by its Maurer–Cartan form. By the
cocycle and inverse laws `ω(V⁻¹ U) = Ad_{V⁻¹}(ω(U) − ω(V)) = 0`, so `V⁻¹ U` is the
constant jet of its value, which is the identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero {U V : G.gaugeJetGroup} (hU : U ∈ G.truncationKer 0)
    (hV : V ∈ G.truncationKer 0) (h : G.maurerCartan U = G.maurerCartan V) :
    U = V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_injective
declarations.doc:
A pure jet is determined by its symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data. The symmetrized data determine
all base-point Taylor data of the Maurer–Cartan form
(`evalLie_iteratedDerivJ_maurerCartan_eq_of_symmetrized_eq_all`), hence the form
itself by Taylor determinacy, hence the jet by `maurerCartan_injOn_truncationKer_zero`.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_injective :
    Function.Injective G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.radial
declarations.doc:
The radial component `−∑_μ x_μ ω_μ(U)` of the Maurer–Cartan form of a jet. It collects the
Maurer–Cartan forms in all directions into a single Lie algebra jet, whose base-point Taylor
data are the symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data. A pure jet is reconstructed from its
Maurer–Cartan form by solving the radial system for this jet, and `exists_radial_eq` shows
that every Lie algebra jet vanishing at the base point arises this way.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def radial (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) : G.jetLieSubalgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_evalLie_iteratedDeriv_radial
declarations.doc:
The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data are the Taylor data of the radial component,
`sym(ω(U))_r|₀ = (1/|r|) (∂_r ρ(U))|₀`.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_eq_evalLie_iteratedDeriv_radial (U : G.truncationKer 0)
    (r : {r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) // r ≠ 0}) :
    G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff U r =
      (1 / (r.1.card : ℝ)) • G.evalLie
        (G.iteratedDerivJ r.1 (G.radial U.1))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.radial_val
declarations.doc:
The radial component `−∑_μ x_μ ω_μ` of the Maurer–Cartan form of a gauge jet, as a matrix,
`−∑_μ x_μ (∂_μ U) U⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma radial_val (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    (G.radial U).1 =
      ∑ μ, (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) • -((U.1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra).map (pderiv μ) *
        (U.1⁻¹).1)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_radial_eq
declarations.doc:
Every Lie algebra jet vanishing at the base point is the radial component of the
Maurer–Cartan form of a pure jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_radial_eq {A : G.jetLieSubalgebra} (hA : G.evalLie A = 0) :
    ∃ U : G.truncationKer 0, G.radial U.1 = A

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_surjective
declarations.doc:
Every family of symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data is realized by a pure jet. Realize the
data, rescaled by the order, as the Taylor data of an element `ρ` vanishing at the base
point, and integrate `ρ` to a pure jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_surjective :
    Function.Surjective G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_bijective
declarations.doc: The symmetrized Maurer–Cartan data are free coordinates on the pure jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff_bijective :
    Function.Bijective G.symmetrizedMaurerCartanCoeff

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.truncation
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th truncation of a gauge jet, entrywise, all Taylor coefficients of total degree
greater than `n` are set to zero.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def truncation (n : ℕ) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.truncation_one
declarations.doc: Truncation of the identity jet is the identity matrix.
declarations.statement: lemma truncation_one (n : ℕ) : G.truncation n 1 = 1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.coeff_maurerCartan_eq_zero_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the Maurer–Cartan form of a jet trivial to order
`n` vanish below degree `n`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.truncation_eq_one_of_mem_truncationKer
declarations.doc:
A jet trivial to order `n` in the sense of the truncation filtration truncates to the
identity at order `n`. The radial relation `∂_ρ U = ω_ρ(U) U` and the Euler vanishing
principle propagate the vanishing of the Maurer–Cartan coefficients below degree `n` to
the vanishing of the coefficients of `U` in nonzero degree up to `n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma truncation_eq_one_of_mem_truncationKer {n : ℕ} {U : G.gaugeJetGroup}
    (hU : U ∈ G.truncationKer n) : G.truncation n U = 1

modules.title: The global gauge group U(1)
modules.doc:
The group of phases, as a global gauge group.

## i. Overview

The gauge group of electromagnetism, and of weak hypercharge in the Standard Model, is
`U(1)`. It is the group of complex numbers of modulus one, the phases `e^{iθ}`, acting on a
charged field by multiplication. As a global gauge group it is the group of unitary `1 × 1`
complex matrices, and an invertible `1 × 1` matrix lies in it exactly when its entry has
modulus one.

Its generators are the anti-hermitian `1 × 1` matrices, the imaginary numbers `i θ`, whose
exponentials `e^{i t θ}` are phases. The hermitian generator of physics is the real charge
`θ`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.U1` : the global gauge group `U(1)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_U1_iff` : an invertible `1 × 1` matrix lies in `U(1)` exactly when
  its entry has modulus one.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_lieAlgebra_U1` : anti-hermitian `1 × 1` matrices are generators of
  `U(1)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.exists_eq_I_smul_scalar_of_mem_lieAlgebra_U1` : generators of `U(1)` are
  imaginary scalars.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The group U(1)
- B. Elements as phases
- C. The Lie algebra of U(1)

## iv. References

* None.

modules.title: The eigenspaces of the elements of `U(1)`
modules.doc:
The subspaces on which an element of `U(1)` acts by a scalar, and the families of a given charge.

## i. Overview

The group `U(1)`, the unit complex numbers `unitary ℂ`, is abelian, so it is its own centre and
every element `z` plays the part that `-1` plays for `SL(2,ℂ)` and `ω 1` for `SU(N)`.
`centreEigenspace ρ z ε` names the subspace on which `z` acts by the scalar `ε` (A). A family of
charge `q`, moved by `u` to `u ^ q` times itself, spans a subspace of the eigenspace of `z` at
`z ^ q` (B). For a representation on an algebra by algebra maps the scalar of a product is the
product of the scalars (C), and a vector that the group fixes and that lies in an eigenspace with
`ε ≠ 1` is zero, also modulo a stable submodule `S` (D).

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.U1.centreEigenspace` : the subspace on which `z` acts by `ε`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.U1.span_le_centreEigenspace_of_charge` : a family of charge `q` lies in the
  eigenspace of `z` at `z ^ q`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.U1.eq_zero_of_invariant_of_mem_centreEigenspace` : an invariant in an
  eigenspace with `ε ≠ 1` is zero.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.U1.mem_of_invariant_of_mem_sup_centreEigenspace` : the same modulo a stable
  submodule.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The eigenspaces
- B. Families of a given charge
- C. Scalars multiply
- D. Invariants in an eigenspace

## iv. References

The same pattern for `SL(2,ℂ)` is
`PhyslibAlpha.Relativity.LorentzGroup.Invariants.CentreEigenspace`, and for `SU(N)`
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.CentreEigenspace`.

modules.title: The gauge jets of unitary gauge groups
modules.doc:
The gauge jets of `SU(n)` and `U(1)` are unitary at every order.

## i. Overview

When every element of a global gauge group is unitary, its generators are anti-hermitian, the
derivative at `t = 0` of `exp (t X)† exp (t X) = 1`. The Maurer–Cartan form `ω_μ = (∂_μ U) U⁻¹`
of a gauge jet is a Lie algebra jet, so each of its base-point derivatives is anti-hermitian,
and so `ω_μ† = −ω_μ` as a matrix of jets. Then `U† U` has vanishing derivatives,
`∂_μ (U† U) = (ω_μ U)† U + U† ω_μ U = 0`, so it is the constant `1` of its value. Thus
every gauge jet of `SU(n)` or `U(1)` is a unitary matrix of jets, with `U⁻¹ = U†`.

For `U(1)` this makes every gauge jet the scalar matrix of a unitary jet.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.star_eq_neg_of_mem_lieAlgebra` : the generators of a unitary global gauge
  group are anti-hermitian.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.star_mul_self_gaugeJet` : a gauge jet of a unitary global gauge group is
  unitary.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.star_mul_self`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.SU.mul_star_self` : the gauge jets of
  `SU(n)` are unitary matrices of jets.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.U1.unitaryJet` : the unitary jet of a gauge jet of `U(1)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.U1.gaugeJet_eq_scalar` : every gauge jet of `U(1)` is a scalar matrix.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Generators of unitary groups are anti-hermitian
- B. Lie algebra jets of unitary groups are anti-hermitian
- C. Gauge jets of unitary groups are unitary
- D. The gauge jets of SU(n)
- E. The gauge jets of U(1)

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.star_eq_neg_of_mem_lieAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The generators of a global gauge group all of whose elements are unitary are
anti-hermitian. The conjugate transpose of `exp (t X)` is `exp (t X†)` and is the inverse
`exp (−t X)`, so the two one-parameter families have the same derivative at `t = 0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_eq_neg_of_mem_lieAlgebra (hG : ∀ g ∈ G.group, star (g : Matrix κ κ ℂ) * g = 1)
    {X : Matrix κ κ ℂ} (hX : X ∈ G.lieAlgebra) : star X = -X

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivValueMatrix_star
declarations.doc:
The base-point derivatives of the conjugate transpose of a matrix of jets are the
conjugate transposes of its base-point derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivValueMatrix_star (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (M : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    derivValueMatrix s (star M) = star (derivValueMatrix s M)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.star_eq_neg_of_mem_jetLieAlgebra

A Lie algebra jet of a global gauge group all of whose elements are unitary is

lemma star_eq_neg_of_mem_jetLieAlgebra (hG : ∀ g ∈ G.group, star (g : Matrix κ κ ℂ) * g = 1)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.star_mul_self_gaugeJet
declarations.doc:
A gauge jet of a global gauge group all of whose elements are unitary is a unitary
matrix of jets, `U† U = 1`. The product `U† U` has vanishing derivatives, since the
Maurer–Cartan form is anti-hermitian, so it is the constant of its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma star_mul_self_gaugeJet (hG : ∀ g ∈ G.group, star (g : Matrix κ κ ℂ) * g = 1)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    star (U.1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) * (U.1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) = 1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.star_eq_inv_gaugeJet
declarations.doc:

declarations.statement:
lemma star_eq_inv_gaugeJet (hG : ∀ g ∈ G.group, star (g : Matrix κ κ ℂ) * g = 1)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    star (U.1 : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra) = (↑U.1⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ SpaceTimeAlgebra)

modules.title: The local field algebra of a gauge theory and its universal property
modules.doc:
The algebra generated by the derivative symbols of the matter and gauge fields, and its
mapping-out property.

## i. Overview

The local field algebra of a field theory is the algebra in which its local expressions,
such as Lagrangian terms, currents and field strengths, live. A `GaugeFieldData G`
already determines its three generator spaces, the fermionic and bosonic species
generators `T.FermionGenerators` and `T.BosonGenerators` and the connection generators
`GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G`, and this file builds the algebra on them. Writing `Λ` for
the exterior algebra and `Sym` for the symmetric algebra, it is

`T.LocalFieldAlgebra =
  (Λ_ℂ E_f(T) ⊗[ℂ] Sym_ℂ E_b(T)) ⊗[ℂ] (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] Sym_ℝ E_A(T))`,

the shape of the Standard Model's algebra `StandardModel.fieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra`, with
the Standard Model's species replaced by those of the datum. All fermionic generators of all
species enter a single exterior algebra, so that symbols of different species anticommute
with each other and not merely with themselves; separate exterior algebras joined by an
ordinary tensor product would make them commute. The connection generators are real and
are complexified once, a connection being a real object whose algebra of polynomials is
then extended to complex coefficients. Nothing here is finite-dimensional, the generator
spaces being spaces of ordinary derivative symbols of arbitrary order however few species
the datum has.

The file proves the algebra's mapping-out universal property. A compatible `T.Assignment`
of the generators in an associative unital complex algebra `B`, not assumed commutative,
extends to a unique complex algebra homomorphism `T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] B`. That is
the realization arrow `T → J(T) → B`, and it is what makes the carrier canonical rather
than merely a convenient tensor product.

An assignment is given species by species, and its Fermi statistics is two conditions, not
one. `fermion_mul_self` within a species does not imply `fermion_mul_swap` across species:
by `DirectSum.mul_self_iff_lof` the square-zero condition on the assembled fermionic map is
exactly the conjunction of the two, and the cross terms of `(x + y) * (x + y)` for `x` and
`y` in different species are what the second condition kills.

The construction has one subtlety. Mathlib's `SymmetricAlgebra.lift` requires a commutative
target, while `B` need not be commutative. The bosonic and connection generators are
therefore lifted into `Assignment.evenSubalgebra`, the subalgebra of `B` generated by their
images, which the hypotheses make commutative, and the result is composed with its
inclusion. The connection factor is then extended from `ℝ` to `ℂ` by `AlgHom.liftEquiv`,
which, unlike the symmetric lift, does accept a noncommutative target. Uniqueness likewise
cannot use `SymmetricAlgebra.algHom_ext`, whose target is commutative; it uses generation
instead, through `adjoin_generators_eq_top`.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.LocalFieldAlgebra` : the local field algebra `J(T)` of a field datum,
  with the generator maps `ιFermion`, `ιBoson`, `ιConnection` and the relations they
  satisfy.
- `GaugeFieldData.ιFermion_mul_swap` : the generators of two different fermionic species
  anticommute, which is polarization of the square-zero relation and not an extra
  relation.
- `GaugeFieldData.adjoin_generators_eq_top` : the algebra is generated by the three
  families.
- `GaugeFieldData.commute_ιBosonTotal`, `GaugeFieldData.commute_includeBoson` : the bosonic
  generators, and with them the whole bosonic factor, are central.
- `GaugeFieldData.Assignment` : a compatible species-wise assignment of the generators in
  an arbitrary complex algebra.
- `GaugeFieldData.Assignment.lift` : the induced algebra homomorphism, with the
  computation lemmas `lift_ιFermion`, `lift_ιBoson` and `lift_ιConnection`.
- `GaugeFieldData.algHom_ext` : two algebra maps agreeing on the generators are equal.
- `GaugeFieldData.Assignment.existsUnique_algHom` : the mapping-out universal property.
- `GaugeFieldData.liftEquiv` : compatible assignments in `B` are the same thing as algebra
  maps into `B`.
- `GaugeFieldData.Assignment.range_lift` : the range is the subalgebra generated by the
  assignment images.
- `GaugeFieldData.includeConnection_injective` : the complexified connection algebra embeds
  in the local field algebra, by a retraction that forgets the matter symbols.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The local field algebra of a field datum
  - A.1. The factor inclusions and the generators
  - A.2. The relations satisfied by the generators
  - A.3. Generation by the three families
- B. Compatible generator assignments
  - B.1. The assembled generator maps
  - B.2. The commutative subalgebra of even images
  - B.3. The three factor maps
  - B.4. Commutation of the factor images
- C. The mapping-out universal property
  - C.1. The induced algebra homomorphism
  - C.2. Uniqueness
  - C.3. Assignments are the same thing as algebra maps
  - C.4. The range of the induced map
- D. The connection inclusion is injective

## iv. References

* None.
