declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.FieldKind
declarations.doc: The kinds of covariant generators of a gauge field theory.
declarations.statement:
inductive FieldKind
  /-- The field strength `F_μν` and its covariant derivatives. -/
  | gauge
  /-- A bosonic matter field or its conjugate, and their covariant derivatives. -/
  | scalar
  /-- A fermionic matter field or its conjugate, and their covariant derivatives. -/
  | fermion
  deriving DecidableEq

declarations.doc:
The three kinds exhaust `FieldKind`. The instance is written out rather than derived, as
for the earlier Standard Model class of generators, where the deriving handler produced a
membership that did not typecheck.
declarations.statement: instance : Fintype FieldKind

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.kindGenerators
declarations.doc:
The covariant generators of a given kind, as elements of the covariant field algebra. These
are the field-strength tower for `gauge`, the bosonic towers and their conjugates for `scalar`,
and the fermionic towers and their conjugates for `fermion`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def kindGenerators : FieldKind → Set T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.covFieldStrength_mem_kindGenerators
declarations.statement:
lemma covFieldStrength_mem_kindGenerators (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    covFieldStrength T l μ ν φ ∈ T.kindGenerators .gauge

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.covBoson_mem_kindGenerators
declarations.statement:
lemma covBoson_mem_kindGenerators (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) : covBoson T j l φ ∈ T.kindGenerators .scalar

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.covConjBoson_mem_kindGenerators
GaugeFieldData.covFermion_mem_kindGenerators
GaugeFieldData.covConjFermion_mem_kindGenerators
GaugeFieldData.weightedGenerators
declarations.doc:
The covariant generators of kind `k` and mass weight `w`. The field-strength tower
`∇_l F_μν` has weight `4 + 2 |l|`, and the tower of `n` covariant derivatives of a species of
mass weight `c`, or of its conjugate, has weight `c + 2 n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def weightedGenerators : FieldKind → ℕ → Set T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.covFieldStrength_mem_weightedGenerators
declarations.statement:
lemma covFieldStrength_mem_weightedGenerators (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    covFieldStrength T l μ ν φ ∈ T.weightedGenerators .gauge (4 + 2 * l.length)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.covBoson_mem_weightedGenerators
GaugeFieldData.covConjBoson_mem_weightedGenerators
GaugeFieldData.covFermion_mem_weightedGenerators
GaugeFieldData.covConjFermion_mem_weightedGenerators
GaugeFieldData.weightedGenerators_cases
declarations.doc: Case analysis on the covariant generators of a given kind and mass weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma weightedGenerators_cases {P : FieldKind → ℕ → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra → Prop}
    {k : FieldKind} {w : ℕ} {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w)
    (hF : ∀ (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra),
      P .gauge (4 + 2 * l.length) (covFieldStrength T l μ ν φ))
    (hψ : ∀ (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)),
      P .fermion ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * n) (covFermion T i l φ))
    (hψc : ∀ (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))),
      P .fermion ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * n) (covConjFermion T i l φ))
    (hφ : ∀ (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)),
      P .scalar ((T.boson j).massWeight + 2 * n) (covBoson T j l φ))
    (hφc : ∀ (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))),
      P .scalar ((T.boson j).massWeight + 2 * n) (covConjBoson T j l φ)) :
    P k w b

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_kindGenerators_of_mem_weightedGenerators
declarations.doc: A generator of kind `k` and some mass weight is a generator of kind `k`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_kindGenerators_of_mem_weightedGenerators {k : FieldKind} {w : ℕ}
    {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w) : b ∈ T.kindGenerators k

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_mem_weightedGenerators
declarations.doc: Every generator of kind `k` has a mass weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_mem_weightedGenerators {k : FieldKind} {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ T.kindGenerators k) : ∃ w, b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.four_le_of_mem_weightedGenerators_gauge
declarations.doc: A gauge generator has mass weight at least four.
declarations.statement:
lemma four_le_of_mem_weightedGenerators_gauge {w : ℕ} {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators .gauge w) : 4 ≤ w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.le_of_mem_weightedGenerators_scalar
declarations.doc:
A scalar generator has mass weight at least any lower bound on the mass weights of the
bosonic species.
declarations.statement:
lemma le_of_mem_weightedGenerators_scalar {m w : ℕ} {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hm : ∀ j, m ≤ (T.boson j).massWeight) (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators .scalar w) : m ≤ w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.le_of_mem_weightedGenerators_fermion
declarations.doc:
A fermionic generator has mass weight at least any lower bound on the mass weights of the
fermionic species.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.HasPositiveMassWeights
declarations.doc: Every species has positive mass weight.
declarations.statement: def HasPositiveMassWeights : Prop

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.pos_of_mem_weightedGenerators
declarations.doc: When every species has positive mass weight, so does every generator.
declarations.statement:
lemma pos_of_mem_weightedGenerators (hpos : T.HasPositiveMassWeights) {k : FieldKind} {w : ℕ}
    {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w) : 0 < w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_mem_weightedGenerators
declarations.doc: A jet carries a covariant generator to a generator of the same kind and mass weight.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_mem_span_weightedGenerators
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz transformation carries a covariant generator to a combination of generators of
the same kind and mass weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_mem_span_weightedGenerators (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    {k : FieldKind} {w : ℕ} {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hGL Λ b
      ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedGenerators k w)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
The products of covariant generators with set of kinds `A` and total mass weight `w`. A
product `b₁ ⋯ bₘ` is recorded as the list of its factors, each with its kind `kᵢ` and mass
weight `wᵢ`, with `{k₁, …, kₘ} = A` and `w₁ + ⋯ + wₘ = w`. The empty product `1` is the only
one with `A = ∅`.
declarations.statement: def weightedMonomials (A : Finset FieldKind) (w : ℕ) : Set T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.one_mem_weightedMonomials
declarations.statement: lemma one_mem_weightedMonomials : (1 : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ∈ T.weightedMonomials ∅ 0

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_weightedMonomials_singleton
declarations.doc: A generator of kind `k` and mass weight `w` is a product with kinds `{k}` and weight `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_weightedMonomials_singleton {k : FieldKind} {w : ℕ} {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w) : b ∈ T.weightedMonomials {k} w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_mem_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
The product of two products of generators has the union of their sets of kinds and the
sum of their mass weights.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.eq_one_of_mem_weightedMonomials_empty
declarations.doc: The only product of generators with no kinds is the empty product, of weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_one_of_mem_weightedMonomials_empty {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ T.weightedMonomials ∅ w) : w = 0 ∧ x = 1

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.eq_one_of_mem_weightedMonomials_zero
declarations.doc:
A product of generators all of whose weights are positive has weight zero only when it is
the empty product.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_one_of_mem_weightedMonomials_zero (hpos : T.HasPositiveMassWeights)
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.weightedMonomials A 0) :
    x = 1

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_span_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
Every element of the covariant field algebra is a combination of products of generators.
This is the generation principle in the form used for the mass weights and the sectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_span_weightedMonomials (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (⋃ A, ⋃ w, T.weightedMonomials A w)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.map_list_prod_mem_span_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
A unital multiplicative linear map carrying every generator into the span of the generators
of the same kind and mass weight carries a product of generators into the span of the products
with the same kinds and weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_list_prod_mem_span_weightedMonomials
    {f : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (h1 : f 1 = 1)
    (hmul : ∀ x y, f (x * y) = f x * f y)
    (hgen : ∀ k w, ∀ b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w,
      f b ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedGenerators k w))
    (L : List (FieldKind × ℕ × T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra))
    (hL : ∀ p ∈ L, p.2.2 ∈ T.weightedGenerators p.1 p.2.1) :
    f (L.map fun p => p.2.2).prod ∈ Submodule.span ℂ
      (T.weightedMonomials (L.map Prod.fst).toFinset (L.map fun p => p.2.1).sum)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.map_mem_span_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
A unital multiplicative linear map carrying every generator into the span of the generators
of the same kind and mass weight preserves the span of the products of any given kinds and
weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_mem_span_weightedMonomials {f : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (h1 : f 1 = 1) (hmul : ∀ x y, f (x * y) = f x * f y)
    (hgen : ∀ k w, ∀ b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w,
      f b ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedGenerators k w))
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedMonomials A w)) :
    f x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedMonomials A w)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_mem_span_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc: The jet gauge group preserves the span of the products of any given kinds and weight.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repValue_mem_span_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
The ordinary gauge group preserves the span of the products of any given kinds and
weight.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_mem_span_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group preserves the span of the products of any given kinds and weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_mem_span_weightedMonomials (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible)
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) {A : Finset FieldKind} {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedMonomials A w)) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hGL Λ x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedMonomials A w)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.commute_of_mem_kindGenerators
declarations.doc: A gauge or scalar generator is central in the covariant field algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_of_mem_kindGenerators {k : FieldKind} (hk : k ≠ .fermion)
    {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hb : b ∈ T.kindGenerators k) (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    Commute b x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.anticomm_of_mem_kindGenerators_fermion
declarations.doc: Two fermionic generators anticommute.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.anticomm_of_mem_span_kindGenerators_fermion
declarations.doc: Any two combinations of fermionic generators anticommute.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.HasMassWeightParity
declarations.doc:
The mass weights of the species have the parity of their statistics, odd for the fermionic
species and even for the bosonic ones.
declarations.statement: def HasMassWeightParity : Prop

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.even_of_mem_weightedGenerators
declarations.doc: Under `HasMassWeightParity`, a gauge or scalar generator has even mass weight.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.odd_of_mem_weightedGenerators_fermion
declarations.doc: Under `HasMassWeightParity`, a fermionic generator has odd mass weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma odd_of_mem_weightedGenerators_fermion (hpar : T.HasMassWeightParity) {w : ℕ}
    {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators .fermion w) : Odd w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_weightedGenerators
declarations.doc:
Under `HasMassWeightParity`, two generators of mass weights `v` and `w` exchange up to the
sign `(-1) ^ (v * w)`, which is `-1` exactly when both are fermionic.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_weightedGenerators (hpar : T.HasMassWeightParity)
    {k k' : FieldKind} {v w : ℕ} {b b' : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k v) (hb' : b' ∈ T.weightedGenerators k' w) :
    b * b' = ((-1 : ℂ) ^ (v * w)) • (b' * b)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_list_prod_eq_smul
declarations.doc:
Under `HasMassWeightParity`, a generator of mass weight `v` moves past a product of
generators of weight `w` up to the sign `(-1) ^ (v * w)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_list_prod_eq_smul (hpar : T.HasMassWeightParity) {k : FieldKind} {v : ℕ}
    {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hb : b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k v)
    (L : List (FieldKind × ℕ × T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra))
    (hL : ∀ p ∈ L, p.2.2 ∈ T.weightedGenerators p.1 p.2.1) :
    b * (L.map fun p => p.2.2).prod
      = ((-1 : ℂ) ^ (v * (L.map fun p => p.2.1).sum)) • ((L.map fun p => p.2.2).prod * b)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
Under `HasMassWeightParity`, two products of generators of mass weights `v` and `w`
exchange up to the sign `(-1) ^ (v * w)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_weightedMonomials (hpar : T.HasMassWeightParity)
    {A B : Finset FieldKind} {v w : ℕ} {x y : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ T.weightedMonomials A v) (hy : y ∈ T.weightedMonomials B w) :
    x * y = ((-1 : ℂ) ^ (v * w)) • (y * x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_span_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
Under `HasMassWeightParity`, combinations of products of generators of mass weights `v`
and `w` exchange up to the sign `(-1) ^ (v * w)`. The fermion parity is the parity of the
mass weight.

modules.title: The mass-weight grading of the covariant field algebra
modules.doc:
The grading of the covariant field algebra by mass weight, its components and its filtration.

## i. Overview

The mass weight of a covariant expression is twice its mass dimension. It is recorded by an
algebra map `P` from the covariant field algebra to the polynomials over it, the element `b`
of weight `w` going to `b X ^ w`. The statement `IsMassWeightPoly P` says that `P` gives every
covariant generator its mass weight: `4 + 2 |l|` for the field-strength tower `∇_l F_μν`, and
`c + 2 n` for the tower of `n` covariant derivatives of a species of mass weight `c`.

The weight-`n` piece `massWeightSubmodule P n` is the set of elements `x` with `P x = x X ^ n`.
Products add weights. Under `IsMassWeightPoly P` the weight-`n` piece is spanned by the products
of generators of total weight `n`. The weight-`k` component `massWeightComponent P k x` of an
element is the coefficient of `X ^ k` in `P x`. It lies in the weight-`k` piece, and every element
is the sum of its components.

The gauge and Lorentz groups carry each generator into a combination of generators of the same
weight, so they preserve every weight piece and commute with taking components. The components
of an invariant element are therefore invariant. The filtration `massWeightSubmoduleLE P w` is the
join of the pieces of weight at most `w`, and an element of it is the sum of its components of
weight at most `w`.

When every species has positive mass weight, the weight-zero piece is the constants. When the
fermionic species have odd mass weight and the bosonic species even mass weight, elements of
weights `v` and `w` exchange up to the sign `(-1) ^ (v * w)`.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly` : `P` gives every generator its mass
  weight, with the constructor `isMassWeightPoly_of` from the towers.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule`,
  `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE` : the weight pieces and the
  filtration.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent` : the projection onto a weight.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule_eq_span` : the weight-`n` piece is
  spanned by the products of generators of weight `n`.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_mem_invariants_repValue` and its
  Lorentz companion : the components of an invariant are invariant.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sum_massWeightComponent_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE` :
  an element of the filtration is the sum of its low-weight components.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule_zero` : the weight-zero piece is the
  constants.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule` : elements of
  given weights supercommute.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Mass-weight polynomials
- B. The weight pieces
  - B.1. Products of generators are homogeneous
- C. The weight components
  - C.1. The weight pieces as spans of products
- D. Stability under the gauge and Lorentz groups
  - D.1. The components of invariants
- E. The mass-weight filtration
- F. The weight-zero piece
- G. Supercommutativity of homogeneous elements

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly
declarations.doc:
An algebra map `P` from the covariant field algebra to the polynomials over it is a
mass-weight polynomial when every covariant generator of mass weight `w` is homogeneous of
weight `w`, `P b = b X ^ w`.
declarations.statement: def IsMassWeightPoly : Prop

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.isMassWeightPoly_of
declarations.doc:
`P` is a mass-weight polynomial when the field-strength tower `∇_l F_μν` has weight
`4 + 2 |l|` and the towers of `n` covariant derivatives of a species of mass weight `c`, and of
its conjugate, have weight `c + 2 n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isMassWeightPoly_of
    (hF : ∀ (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra),
      P (covFieldStrength T l μ ν φ)
        = Polynomial.monomial (4 + 2 * l.length) (covFieldStrength T l μ ν φ))
    (hψ : ∀ (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)),
      P (covFermion T i l φ)
        = Polynomial.monomial ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * n) (covFermion T i l φ))
    (hψc : ∀ (i : T.FermionSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))),
      P (covConjFermion T i l φ)
        = Polynomial.monomial ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * n) (covConjFermion T i l φ))
    (hφ : ∀ (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)),
      P (covBoson T j l φ)
        = Polynomial.monomial ((T.boson j).massWeight + 2 * n) (covBoson T j l φ))
    (hφc : ∀ (j : T.BosonSpecies) {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))),
      P (covConjBoson T j l φ)
        = Polynomial.monomial ((T.boson j).massWeight + 2 * n) (covConjBoson T j l φ)) :
    IsMassWeightPoly P

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The weight-`n` piece of the covariant field algebra, the elements `x` with
`P x = x X ^ n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff {n : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ massWeightSubmodule P n ↔ P x = Polynomial.monomial n x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The weight pieces are multiplicative, since weights add under multiplication.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.one_mem_massWeightSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc: The unit has weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma one_mem_massWeightSubmodule_zero :
    (1 : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ∈ massWeightSubmodule P 0

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule_of_mem_weightedGenerators
declarations.doc: Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, a generator of mass weight `w` lies in the weight-`w` piece.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmodule_of_mem_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, a product of generators of total mass weight `w` lies in the
weight-`w` piece.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.span_weightedMonomials_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the combinations of products of generators of weight `w` lie in
the weight-`w` piece.
declarations.statement:
lemma span_weightedMonomials_le_massWeightSubmodule (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P) (w : ℕ) :
    Submodule.span ℂ (⋃ A, T.weightedMonomials A w) ≤ massWeightSubmodule P w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent
declarations.doc:
The weight-`k` component of an element of the covariant field algebra, the coefficient of
`X ^ k` in its image under `P`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightComponent (k : ℕ) :
    T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_apply (k : ℕ) (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    massWeightComponent P k x = (P x).coeff k

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_of_mem
declarations.doc:
The weight-`k` component of an element of the weight-`w` piece is the element itself when
`w = k`, and zero otherwise.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_self
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_self {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule P w) : massWeightComponent P w x = x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_mem_span
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight-`k` component of any element is a combination of
products of generators of weight `k`. On a product of generators the component is the product
or zero, and both sides are linear.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_mem_span (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P) (k : ℕ)
    (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    massWeightComponent P k x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (⋃ A, T.weightedMonomials A k)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight-`k` component lies in the weight-`k` piece.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_mem_massWeightSubmodule (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P) (k : ℕ)
    (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) : massWeightComponent P k x ∈ massWeightSubmodule P k

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.eq_sum_coeff
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, every element of the covariant field algebra is the sum of its
weight components, the coefficients of its image under `P`. It holds on the products of
generators, which are homogeneous, and both sides are linear.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_sum_coeff (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P) (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    x = (P x).sum fun _ a => a

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule_eq_span
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight-`w` piece is exactly the span of the products of
generators of total weight `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_span (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P) (w : ℕ) :
    massWeightSubmodule P w = Submodule.span ℂ (⋃ A, T.weightedMonomials A w)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.map_massWeightComponent
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, a linear map preserving every weight piece commutes with taking
weight components.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_massWeightComponent (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P)
    {f : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hf : ∀ w y, y ∈ massWeightSubmodule P w → f y ∈ massWeightSubmodule P w) (k : ℕ)
    (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    f (massWeightComponent P k x) = massWeightComponent P k (f x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.map_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
A map preserving the span of the products of every given kinds and weight preserves every
weight piece.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_mem_massWeightSubmodule (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P)
    {f : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hf : ∀ (A : Finset FieldKind) (w : ℕ) (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra),
      x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedMonomials A w) →
        f x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedMonomials A w))
    {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule P w) :
    f x ∈ massWeightSubmodule P w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repJet_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The jet gauge group preserves every weight piece.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repValue_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The ordinary gauge group preserves every weight piece.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group preserves every weight piece.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_repValue
declarations.doc: Taking a weight component commutes with the ordinary gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_repValue (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P) (g : G.group) (k : ℕ)
    (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    massWeightComponent P k (repValue T g x) = repValue T g (massWeightComponent P k x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc: Taking a weight component commutes with the Lorentz group.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_repLorentzGroup (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (k : ℕ) (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    massWeightComponent P k (repLorentzGroup T hGL Λ x)
      = repLorentzGroup T hGL Λ (massWeightComponent P k x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_mem_invariants_repValue
declarations.doc: The weight components of a gauge invariant are gauge invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_mem_invariants_repValue (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P) (k : ℕ)
    {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ Representation.invariants (repValue T)) :
    massWeightComponent P k x ∈ Representation.invariants (repValue T)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_mem_invariants_repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc: The weight components of a Lorentz invariant are Lorentz invariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_mem_invariants_repLorentzGroup (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible) (k : ℕ) {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ Representation.invariants (repLorentzGroup T hGL)) :
    massWeightComponent P k x ∈ Representation.invariants (repLorentzGroup T hGL)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight filtration, the join of the weight pieces of weight at most `w`. A
Lagrangian of mass dimension at most `w / 2` lies in it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc: Each weight piece of weight at most `w` sits inside the filtration at `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE {k w : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ w) :
    massWeightSubmodule P k ≤ massWeightSubmoduleLE P w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE {k w : ℕ} (hk : k ≤ w) {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule P k) : x ∈ massWeightSubmoduleLE P w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE_le
declarations.doc:
A submodule containing every weight piece of weight at most `w` contains the filtration
at `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_le {w : ℕ} {V : Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hV : ∀ k ≤ w, massWeightSubmodule P k ≤ V) : massWeightSubmoduleLE P w ≤ V

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE_eq_iSup
declarations.doc: The filtration as a join over a finite index type.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_eq_iSup (w : ℕ) :
    massWeightSubmoduleLE P w = ⨆ k : Fin (w + 1), massWeightSubmodule P (k : ℕ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent_mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight-`k` component of any element lies in the filtration
at every `w ≥ k`.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE_le_eqLocus
declarations.doc: The filtration at `w` is fixed by the sum of the weight components of weight at most `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_le_eqLocus (w : ℕ) :
    massWeightSubmoduleLE P w ≤ LinearMap.eqLocus
      (∑ k ∈ Finset.range (w + 1), massWeightComponent P k) LinearMap.id

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.sum_massWeightComponent_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
An element of the filtration at `w` is the sum of its weight components of weight at
most `w`. No hypothesis on `P` is needed, since each weight piece has a single component.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.map_mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc: A map preserving every weight piece preserves the filtration.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repValue_mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc: The ordinary gauge group preserves the filtration.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup_mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group preserves the filtration.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule_zero
declarations.doc:
When every species has positive mass weight, the weight-zero piece is the constants. The
only product of generators of weight zero is the empty one, whose value is the unit. This is
the constant term of a Lagrangian, the cosmological term.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_zero (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P) (hpos : T.HasPositiveMassWeights) :
    massWeightSubmodule P 0 = 1

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
When the fermionic species have odd mass weight and the bosonic species even mass weight,
elements of weights `v` and `w` exchange up to the sign `(-1) ^ (v * w)`, since the fermion
parity is the parity of the mass weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_eq_smul_mul_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule (hP : IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (hpar : T.HasMassWeightParity) {v w : ℕ} {x y : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ massWeightSubmodule P v) (hy : y ∈ massWeightSubmodule P w) :
    x * y = ((-1 : ℂ) ^ (v * w)) • (y * x)

modules.title: Realizations of the covariant field algebra
modules.doc:
Equivariant algebra maps out of the covariant field algebra of a gauge theory.

## i. Overview

A complex algebra `B` carries the covariant expressions of a gauge-field datum when the
covariant field algebra maps into it by a complex algebra map equivariant for the ordinary
gauge group `G.group` and for the Lorentz group, both acting on `B` by algebra endomorphisms.
Such a map is a `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization`. The gauge compatibility is
with `G.group` alone because the source action of the ordinary gauge group is the jet action at
the constant jets. The Lorentz action of the source exists only under
`GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCompatible`, which is therefore a parameter.

A realization of the local field algebra restricts to one of the covariant field algebra
(`GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrict`), with `G.group` acting on the target through the
constant jets. The converse extension is not claimed.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization` : an algebra carrying the covariant
  field algebra, with the equivariance laws `map_repValue` and `map_repLorentz`.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrict` : restriction to the covariant field algebra.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Realizations
- B. Restriction from the local field algebra

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Realizations
## B. Restriction from the local field algebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization
declarations.doc:
A complex algebra `B` carrying the covariant expressions of the datum `T`, through a complex
algebra map out of the covariant field algebra, equivariant for the ordinary gauge group
and the Lorentz group, both acting on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms. The
Lorentz action of the source needs `GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCompatible`, which is a
parameter. No other species condition is used. It is built from the fields `toAlgHom`,
`map_fst`, `map_snd`, `fst_mul`, `snd_mul` of `Representation.EquivariantAlgHom`, which
the lemmas `map_repValue`, `map_repLorentz`, `repGauge_mul` and `repLorentz_mul` name.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Realization (T : GaugeFieldData G) (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible) (B : Type)
    [Semiring B] [Algebra ℂ B] (repGauge : Representation ℂ G.group B)
    (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization.map_repValue
declarations.doc: The map is equivariant for the ordinary gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_repValue (g : G.group) (x : ↥T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    k.toAlgHom (repValue T g x) = repGauge g (k.toAlgHom x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization.map_repLorentz
declarations.doc: The map is equivariant for the Lorentz group.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_repLorentz (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : ↥T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    k.toAlgHom (repLorentzGroup T hGL Λ x) = repLorentz Λ (k.toAlgHom x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization.repGauge_mul
declarations.doc: The ordinary gauge group acts on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_mul (g : G.group) (b₁ b₂ : B) :
    repGauge g (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge g b₁ * repGauge g b₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization.repLorentz_mul
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group acts on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B) :
    repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrict
declarations.doc:
The restriction of a realization of the local field algebra to the covariant field
algebra, along the inclusion; the ordinary gauge group acts on the target through the
constant jets. No species condition beyond `hGL` is used.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def restrict :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization T hGL B (repJet.comp G.gaugeJetOfConstant) repLorentz

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.restrict_toAlgHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma restrict_toAlgHom_apply (x : ↥T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    (h.restrict hGL).toAlgHom x = h.toAlgHom x

modules.title: The sectors of a gauge field theory
modules.doc:
The covariant field algebra is spanned by sectors labelled by the kinds of field they contain.

## i. Overview

The covariant field algebra `T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra` of a field datum `T` is generated by three
kinds of covariant expressions, `GaugeFieldData.FieldKind`.

- Gauge. The field strength `F_μν` and its covariant derivatives `∇_l F_μν`.
- Scalar. The bosonic matter fields `φ`, their conjugates `φ†`, and their covariant
  derivatives `∇_l φ` and `∇_l φ†`.
- Fermion. The fermionic matter fields `ψ`, their conjugates `ψ̄`, and their covariant
  derivatives `∇_l ψ` and `∇_l ψ̄`.

A product of generators contains a set of kinds. For a set `A` of kinds, the sector `T.sector A`
is the span of the products whose set of kinds is exactly `A`. Two such products multiply to a
third, so each sector is a non-unital subalgebra. The empty set gives the constants `ℂ • 1`.
The seven nonempty sets give the seven named sectors, from the pure gauge sector, which
contains `tr F_μν F^μν`, to the mixed sector, which contains the dipole operators
`ψ̄ σ^μν φ F_μν ψ`. The gauge field enters minimal couplings only through covariant derivatives,
so the kinetic terms `ψ̄ γ^μ ∇_μ ψ` and `(∇_μ φ)† ∇^μ φ` lie in the fermion and scalar sectors.

The gauge and Lorentz groups preserve every sector. A jet carries each generator to a generator
of the same kind, and a Lorentz transformation carries it to a combination of generators of the
same kind. Both act by algebra maps, so a product of generators goes to a combination of
products with the same set of kinds.

Refining by mass weight, `T.sectorMassWeight A w` is the span of the products of kinds `A` and
total weight `w`. For a mass-weight polynomial `P` it is the intersection of the sector with the
weight-`w` piece, and the weight-`w` component of an element of a sector lies in this
intersection. Each weight piece is the join of the weight pieces of the sectors. A lower bound on
the weights of the generators of each kind gives a lower bound on the weights at which a sector
can be nonzero, and a sector of two kinds splits into products of the pieces of the two kinds.

Every element of the covariant field algebra is a constant plus a sum of one element from each
of the seven nonempty sectors. Under the conditions of the descent theorem, an element invariant
under the gauge and Lorentz groups has such a decomposition with every component invariant. The
proof applies a Reynolds element for the joint action to a decomposition. The Reynolds element
fixes the invariant element, and it is a combination of group elements, so it keeps every
component in its sector. Projecting the components onto weights keeps them in their sectors and
invariant, so an invariant of weight `w`, or of weight at most `w`, decomposes into invariant
components of the same weights.

The decomposition is not unique. The covariant field algebra is not free on its generators. The
Ricci identity `[∇_μ, ∇_ν] ψ = F_μν ψ` and the Bianchi identity relate products of different
kinds, so the sectors span the covariant field algebra but their sum is not direct.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.sector` : the sector of a set of kinds, with `GaugeFieldData.mem_sector_iff`.
- `GaugeFieldData.gaugeSector` and the six other named sectors.
- `GaugeFieldData.repValue_mem_sector`, `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_mem_sector` : the
  sectors are stable under the gauge and Lorentz groups.
- `GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector` : every element is a constant plus a sum
  of elements of the seven nonempty sectors.
- `GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight` : the weight piece of a sector, with
  `GaugeFieldData.massWeightComponent_mem_sectorMassWeight`,
  `GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_eq_inf` and
  `GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_sectorMassWeight`.
- `GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_eq_bot_of_lt` and `GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_pair_le` :
  the vanishing of a sector at low weight, and the two-kind sectors as products.
- `GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants` : every invariant is a
  constant plus a sum of invariant elements of the seven nonempty sectors.
- `GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeightLE` and
  `GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeight` : the same with
  every component of weight at most `w`, or of weight `w`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The sectors
  - A.1. Products of generators with a given set of kinds
  - A.2. The sector of a set of kinds
  - A.3. The seven named sectors
- B. Stability under the gauge and Lorentz groups
- C. The sectors span the covariant field algebra
- D. The sectors at a fixed mass weight
  - D.1. The weight components of the sectors
  - D.2. Vanishing at low weight
  - D.3. Sectors of two kinds
  - D.4. Algebras generated by one kind
- E. The decomposition of invariants
  - E.1. Stable subspaces containing a finite family
  - E.2. Invariant sector components
  - E.3. Invariant sector components of given mass weight

## iv. References

* None.

The components of the decomposition of section E.2 are projected onto weights. Taking a weight

filtration at `w` is the sum of its components of weight at most `w`. The argument uses only

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMonomials
declarations.doc:
The products of covariant generators whose set of kinds is exactly `A`, of any mass
weight. The empty product `1` is the only one for `A = ∅`.
declarations.statement: abbrev sectorMonomials (A : Finset FieldKind) : Set T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.one_mem_sectorMonomials_empty
declarations.statement: lemma one_mem_sectorMonomials_empty : (1 : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ∈ T.sectorMonomials ∅

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_sectorMonomials_singleton
declarations.doc: A generator of kind `k` is a product of generators with set of kinds `{k}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMonomials_singleton {k : FieldKind} {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ T.kindGenerators k) : b ∈ T.sectorMonomials {k}

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_mem_sectorMonomials
declarations.doc: The product of two products of generators has the union of their sets of kinds.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMonomials_empty
declarations.doc: The only product of generators with no kinds is the empty product.
declarations.statement: lemma sectorMonomials_empty : T.sectorMonomials ∅ = {1}

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_mem_span_sectorMonomials
declarations.doc:
Multiplication carries the spans of the products with sets of kinds `A` and `B` into the
span of the products with set of kinds `A ∪ B`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_mem_span_sectorMonomials {A B : Finset FieldKind} {x y : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.sectorMonomials A))
    (hy : y ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.sectorMonomials B)) :
    x * y ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.sectorMonomials (A ∪ B))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sector
declarations.doc:
The sector of a set `A` of kinds, the span of the products of covariant generators whose set
of kinds is exactly `A`. It is a non-unital subalgebra since `A ∪ A = A`. For nonempty `A` it
is spanned by nonempty products, and `T.sector ∅` is the constants `ℂ • 1`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def sector (A : Finset FieldKind) : NonUnitalSubalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_sector_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sector_iff {A : Finset FieldKind} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.sector A ↔ x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.sectorMonomials A)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_sector_of_mem_kindGenerators
declarations.doc: A generator of kind `k` lies in the sector of `{k}`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sector_of_mem_kindGenerators {k : FieldKind} {b : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hb : b ∈ T.kindGenerators k) : b ∈ T.sector {k}

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_mem_sector
declarations.doc: Multiplication carries the sectors of `A` and `B` into the sector of `A ∪ B`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_mem_sector {A B : Finset FieldKind} {x y : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ T.sector A) (hy : y ∈ T.sector B) : x * y ∈ T.sector (A ∪ B)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_sector_empty_iff
declarations.doc: The sector of the empty set of kinds is the constants.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sector_empty_iff {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.sector ∅ ↔ ∃ c : ℂ, c • 1 = x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeSector
declarations.doc:
The pure gauge sector, of the polynomials in the field strength `F_μν` and its covariant
derivatives alone. It contains the Yang-Mills term `tr F_μν F^μν`, the theta term
`tr F_μν F̃^μν` and higher-derivative terms such as `tr ∇_ρ F_μν ∇^ρ F^μν`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev gaugeSector : NonUnitalSubalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.scalarSector
declarations.doc:
The pure scalar sector, of the polynomials in the bosonic matter fields, their conjugates
and their covariant derivatives alone. It contains the kinetic term `(∇_μ φ)† ∇^μ φ` and the
potential terms `φ† φ` and `(φ† φ)²`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev scalarSector : NonUnitalSubalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionSector
declarations.doc:
The pure fermion sector, of the polynomials in the fermionic matter fields, their
conjugates and their covariant derivatives alone. It contains the kinetic term
`ψ̄ γ^μ ∇_μ ψ`, the Majorana mass terms `ψ ψ` and the four-fermion terms `(ψ̄ γ^μ ψ)²`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev fermionSector : NonUnitalSubalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.yukawaSector
declarations.doc:
The Yukawa sector, of the products containing fermions and scalars but no field strength.
It contains the Yukawa couplings `ψ̄ φ ψ`, the Weinberg operator `L L φ φ` and the current
terms `(φ† ∇_μ φ) (ψ̄ γ^μ ψ)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev yukawaSector : NonUnitalSubalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeHiggsSector
declarations.doc:
The gauge-Higgs sector, of the products containing field strengths and scalars but no
fermions. It contains the terms `(φ† φ) tr F_μν F^μν` and `φ† F_μν F̃^μν φ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev gaugeHiggsSector : NonUnitalSubalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionGaugeSector
declarations.doc:
The fermion-gauge sector, of the products containing fermions and field strengths but no
scalars. It contains the dipole terms `ψ̄ σ^μν F_μν ψ` and the terms `ψ̄ γ^μ ∇^ν F_μν ψ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev fermionGaugeSector : NonUnitalSubalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mixedSector
declarations.doc:
The mixed sector, of the products containing fermions, field strengths and scalars. It
contains the dipole terms `ψ̄ σ^μν φ F_μν ψ`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable abbrev mixedSector : NonUnitalSubalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.map_mem_sector
declarations.doc:
A unital multiplicative linear map carrying every generator into the span of the generators
of the same kind and mass weight preserves every sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_mem_sector {f : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (h1 : f 1 = 1)
    (hmul : ∀ x y, f (x * y) = f x * f y)
    (hgen : ∀ k w, ∀ b ∈ T.weightedGenerators k w,
      f b ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (T.weightedGenerators k w))
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.sector A) :
    f x ∈ T.sector A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_mem_sector
declarations.doc: The jet gauge group preserves every sector.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repValue_mem_sector
declarations.doc: The ordinary gauge group preserves every sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma repValue_mem_sector (g : G.group) {A : Finset FieldKind} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ T.sector A) : repValue T g x ∈ T.sector A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_mem_sector
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group preserves every sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_mem_sector (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.sector A) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hGL Λ x ∈ T.sector A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repGaugeLorentz_mem_sector
declarations.doc: The joint action of the gauge and Lorentz groups preserves every sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGaugeLorentz_mem_sector (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute) (q : G.group × SL(2,ℂ))
    {A : Finset FieldKind}
    {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.sector A) :
    repGaugeLorentz T hC q x ∈ T.sector A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.asAlgebraHom_repGaugeLorentz_mem_sector
declarations.doc: Every element of the monoid algebra of `G × SL(2,ℂ)` preserves every sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma asAlgebraHom_repGaugeLorentz_mem_sector (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute)
    (r : MonoidAlgebra ℂ (G.group × SL(2,ℂ)))
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.sector A) :
    (repGaugeLorentz T hC).asAlgebraHom r x ∈ T.sector A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_span_iUnion_sectorMonomials
declarations.doc: Every element of the covariant field algebra is a combination of products of generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_span_iUnion_sectorMonomials (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    x ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (⋃ A, T.sectorMonomials A)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_sum_sector
declarations.doc:
Every element of the covariant field algebra is a sum of one element from the sector of
each set of kinds, the sector of `∅` supplying the constants. The decomposition is not
unique, since the covariant field algebra is not free on its generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_sum_sector (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    ∃ y : Finset FieldKind → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra, (∀ A, y A ∈ T.sector A) ∧ x = ∑ A, y A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector
declarations.doc:
Every element of the covariant field algebra is a constant plus a sum of one element from
each of the seven nonempty sectors, `x = c • 1 + ∑_{A ≠ ∅} x_A`.

The decomposition is not unique. The covariant field algebra is not free on its generators.
The Ricci identity `[∇_μ, ∇_ν] ψ = F_μν ψ` and the Bianchi identity relate products of
different kinds, so the sectors span the covariant field algebra but their sum is not
direct.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector (x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    ∃ (c : ℂ) (y : Finset FieldKind → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra), (∀ A, y A ∈ T.sector A) ∧
      x = c • 1 + ∑ A ∈ Finset.univ.erase ∅, y A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc:
The weight-`w` piece of the sector of `A`, the span of the products of covariant generators
with set of kinds `A` and total mass weight `w`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def sectorMassWeight (A : Finset FieldKind) (w : ℕ) :
    Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_sectorMassWeight_of_mem_weightedMonomials
declarations.doc: A product of generators lies in the weight piece of its sector given by its weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sectorMassWeight_of_mem_weightedMonomials {A : Finset FieldKind} {w : ℕ}
    {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.weightedMonomials A w) : x ∈ T.sectorMassWeight A w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_sector_of_mem_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc: The weight pieces of a sector lie in the sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_sector_of_mem_sectorMassWeight {A : Finset FieldKind} {w : ℕ}
    {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.sectorMassWeight A w) : x ∈ T.sector A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mul_mem_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc:
Multiplication carries the weight-`v` piece of the sector of `A` and the weight-`w` piece of
the sector of `B` into the weight-`v + w` piece of the sector of `A ∪ B`.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repValue_mem_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc: The gauge group preserves the weight pieces of every sector.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_mem_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group preserves the weight pieces of every sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_mem_sectorMassWeight (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hx : x ∈ T.sectorMassWeight A w) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hGL Λ x ∈ T.sectorMassWeight A w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_le_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight pieces of a sector lie in the weight pieces of the
covariant field algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_le_massWeightSubmodule (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (A : Finset FieldKind) (w : ℕ) :
    T.sectorMassWeight A w ≤ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule P w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightComponent_mem_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight-`k` component of an element of the sector of `A`
lies in the weight-`k` piece of that sector. On a product of generators the component is the
product or zero, and both sides are linear.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_mem_sectorMassWeight (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.sector A) (k : ℕ) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent P k x ∈ T.sectorMassWeight A k

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightComponent_mem_sector
declarations.doc: Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, taking a weight component preserves every sector.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightComponent_mem_sector (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.sector A) (k : ℕ) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightComponent P k x ∈ T.sector A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_eq_inf
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight-`w` piece of the sector of `A` is the intersection of
the sector with the weight-`w` piece of the covariant field algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_eq_inf (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (A : Finset FieldKind) (w : ℕ) :
    T.sectorMassWeight A w
      = (T.sector A).toSubmodule ⊓ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule P w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight-`w` piece of the covariant field algebra is the join
over the sets of kinds of the weight-`w` pieces of the sectors, every product of generators
having exactly one set of kinds. The join is not direct.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_eq_iSup_sectorMassWeight (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (w : ℕ) :
    LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule P w = ⨆ A, T.sectorMassWeight A w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_empty_of_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
At a non-zero weight the sector of `∅` has no weight piece, since its only product is the empty
one, of weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_empty_of_ne_zero {w : ℕ} (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    T.sectorMassWeight ∅ w = ⊥

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sum_le_sum_of_forall_le
declarations.doc:
If every factor of a product of generators of kind `k` has weight at least `m k`, the
product has weight at least the sum of `m` over its set of kinds.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_le_sum_of_forall_le (m : FieldKind → ℕ)
    (L : List (FieldKind × ℕ × T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)) (h : ∀ p ∈ L, m p.1 ≤ p.2.1) :
    ∑ k ∈ (L.map Prod.fst).toFinset, m k ≤ (L.map fun p => p.2.1).sum

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_eq_bot_of_lt
declarations.doc:
If the generators of each kind `k ∈ A` have mass weight at least `m k`, the sector of `A`
vanishes at every weight below `∑ k ∈ A, m k`.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.kindWeight
declarations.doc: The total mass weight of the factors of kind `c` in a product of generators.
declarations.statement: def kindWeight (c : FieldKind) (L : List (FieldKind × ℕ × T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)) : ℕ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.kindWeight_nil
declarations.statement:
lemma kindWeight_nil (c : FieldKind) :
    kindWeight c ([] : List (FieldKind × ℕ × T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)) = 0

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.kindWeight_cons_of_eq
GaugeFieldData.kindWeight_cons_of_ne
GaugeFieldData.kindWeight_ne_zero
declarations.doc:
When every species has positive mass weight, a kind present in a product carries a
non-zero part of its weight.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.kindWeight_add
declarations.doc:
Over a product realising only two kinds, the two kind weights add up to the total
weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma kindWeight_add {c₁ c₂ : FieldKind} (hne : c₁ ≠ c₂)
    {L : List (FieldKind × ℕ × T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)}
    (hL : ∀ p ∈ L, p.1 = c₁ ∨ p.1 = c₂) :
    kindWeight c₁ L + kindWeight c₂ L = (L.map fun p => p.2.1).sum

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.list_prod_mem_mul_of_forall_kind
declarations.doc:
A product of generators of two kinds is a product of an element of weight `kindWeight c₁`
from a family of submodules dominating the first kind's sector and an element of weight
`kindWeight c₂` from one dominating the second. The second family is assumed to commute
past the first.
declarations.statement:
lemma list_prod_mem_mul_of_forall_kind {c₁ c₂ : FieldKind} (hne : c₁ ≠ c₂)
    {M₁ M₂ : ℕ → Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hM₁ : ∀ w, T.sectorMassWeight {c₁} w ≤ M₁ w) (hM₂ : ∀ w, T.sectorMassWeight {c₂} w ≤ M₂ w)
    (hone₁ : (1 : Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ≤ M₁ 0)
    (hone₂ : (1 : Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ≤ M₂ 0)
    (hmul₁ : ∀ a b, M₁ a * M₁ b ≤ M₁ (a + b)) (hmul₂ : ∀ a b, M₂ a * M₂ b ≤ M₂ (a + b))
    (hcomm : ∀ a b, M₂ a * M₁ b ≤ M₁ b * M₂ a)
    (L : List (FieldKind × ℕ × T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra))
    (hL : ∀ p ∈ L, p.2.2 ∈ T.weightedGenerators p.1 p.2.1)
    (hgl : ∀ p ∈ L, p.1 = c₁ ∨ p.1 = c₂) :
    (L.map fun p => p.2.2).prod ∈ M₁ (kindWeight c₁ L) * M₂ (kindWeight c₂ L)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_pair_le
declarations.doc:
The weight-`w` piece of the sector of two kinds is contained in the join, over the
splittings of `w` into two non-zero parts, of the products of submodule families dominating
the two one-kind sectors, the second family commuting past the first. This needs every
species to have positive mass weight, so that each kind present carries non-zero weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_pair_le (hpos : T.HasPositiveMassWeights) {c₁ c₂ : FieldKind}
    (hne : c₁ ≠ c₂) {M₁ M₂ : ℕ → Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hM₁ : ∀ w, T.sectorMassWeight {c₁} w ≤ M₁ w) (hM₂ : ∀ w, T.sectorMassWeight {c₂} w ≤ M₂ w)
    (hone₁ : (1 : Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ≤ M₁ 0)
    (hone₂ : (1 : Submodule ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) ≤ M₂ 0)
    (hmul₁ : ∀ a b, M₁ a * M₁ b ≤ M₁ (a + b)) (hmul₂ : ∀ a b, M₂ a * M₂ b ≤ M₂ (a + b))
    (hcomm : ∀ a b, M₂ a * M₁ b ≤ M₁ b * M₂ a) (w : ℕ) :
    T.sectorMassWeight {c₁, c₂} w
      ≤ ⨆ (p : ℕ × ℕ) (_ : p.1 + p.2 = w) (_ : p.1 ≠ 0) (_ : p.2 ≠ 0), M₁ p.1 * M₂ p.2

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.adjoin_le_sector_sup_sector_empty
declarations.doc:
The algebra generated by generators of one kind `k` lies in the sector of `{k}` plus the
constants.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoin_le_sector_sup_sector_empty {k : FieldKind} {s : Set T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hs : s ⊆ T.kindGenerators k) :
    Subalgebra.toSubmodule (Algebra.adjoin ℂ s)
      ≤ (T.sector {k}).toSubmodule ⊔ (T.sector ∅).toSubmodule

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.sectorMassWeight_le_inf
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, the weight-`w` piece of the sector of `A` lies in every
subalgebra containing the generators of the kinds in `A`, intersected with the weight-`w`
piece.
declarations.statement:
lemma sectorMassWeight_le_inf (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    {A : Finset FieldKind} {S : Subalgebra ℂ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra}
    (hS : ∀ k ∈ A, T.kindGenerators k ⊆ S) (w : ℕ) :
    T.sectorMassWeight A w
      ≤ Subalgebra.toSubmodule S ⊓ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule P w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.inf_massWeightSubmodule_le_sectorMassWeight
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, at a non-zero weight `w` the weight-`w` piece of the algebra
generated by generators of one kind `k` lies in the weight-`w` piece of the sector of `{k}`,
since the constants have weight zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma inf_massWeightSubmodule_le_sectorMassWeight (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    {k : FieldKind} {s : Set T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hs : s ⊆ T.kindGenerators k) {w : ℕ}
    (hw : w ≠ 0) :
    Subalgebra.toSubmodule (Algebra.adjoin ℂ s) ⊓ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule P w
      ≤ T.sectorMassWeight {k} w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_isContinuousFamily_forall_mem_span
declarations.doc:
The elements `a i`, for `i ∈ s`, lie in the span of one finite family on which the gauge and
Lorentz groups act with continuous coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_isContinuousFamily_forall_mem_span (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible)
    (hL : T.LorentzContinuous) {ι : Type*} (a : ι → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) (s : Finset ι) :
    ∃ (ι' : Type) (_ : Fintype ι') (v : ι' → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra),
      (∀ i ∈ s, a i ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range v)) ∧
      Representation.IsContinuousFamily (repValue T) v ∧
      Representation.IsContinuousFamily (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hGL) v

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_subrepresentation_forall_mem
declarations.doc:
A finite family of elements of the covariant field algebra lies in one finite-dimensional
subrepresentation of the joint action of the gauge and Lorentz groups, on which both groups
act with continuous matrix coefficients. This is the version of
`LocalCovFieldAlgebra.exists_subrepresentation` for a finite family.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_subrepresentation_forall_mem (hL : T.LorentzContinuous) (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute)
    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (a : ι → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    ∃ W : Subrepresentation (repGaugeLorentz T hC), (∀ i, a i ∈ W.toSubmodule) ∧
      FiniteDimensional ℂ W.toSubmodule ∧
      Representation.ContinuousMatrixCoeff (W.comp (MonoidHom.inl G.group SL(2,ℂ))) ∧
      Representation.ContinuousMatrixCoeff (W.comp (MonoidHom.inr G.group SL(2,ℂ)))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_isReynolds_repGaugeLorentz
declarations.doc:
For a compact gauge group, the joint action of the gauge and Lorentz groups has a Reynolds
element on every finite-dimensional subrepresentation with continuous matrix coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_isReynolds_repGaugeLorentz [CompactSpace G.group]
    (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute)
    (W : Subrepresentation (repGaugeLorentz T hC)) [FiniteDimensional ℂ W.toSubmodule]
    (h₁ : Representation.ContinuousMatrixCoeff (W.comp (MonoidHom.inl G.group SL(2,ℂ))))
    (h₂ : Representation.ContinuousMatrixCoeff (W.comp (MonoidHom.inr G.group SL(2,ℂ)))) :
    ∃ r, (repGaugeLorentz T hC).IsReynolds W.toSubmodule r

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants
declarations.doc:
An element of the covariant field algebra invariant under the gauge and Lorentz groups is a
sum of one element from the sector of each set of kinds, every one of them invariant under
both groups. This needs a compact gauge group, continuous Lorentz representations, and
commuting gauge and Lorentz representations of every species. The decomposition is not
unique, since the covariant field algebra is not free on its generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants [CompactSpace G.group]
    (hL : T.LorentzContinuous) (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute)
    {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (h₁ : x ∈ (repValue T).invariants)
    (h₂ : x ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants) :
    ∃ y : Finset FieldKind → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra, (∀ A, y A ∈ T.sector A ∧
      y A ∈ (repValue T).invariants ∧
      y A ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants) ∧
      x = ∑ A, y A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants
declarations.doc:
An element of the covariant field algebra invariant under the gauge and Lorentz groups is a
constant plus a sum of one element from each of the seven nonempty sectors,
`x = c • 1 + ∑_{A ≠ ∅} x_A`, every `x_A` invariant under both groups. This needs a compact
gauge group, continuous Lorentz representations, and commuting gauge and Lorentz
representations of every species.

The decomposition is not unique. The covariant field algebra is not free on its generators.
The Ricci identity `[∇_μ, ∇_ν] ψ = F_μν ψ` and the Bianchi identity relate products of
different kinds, so the sectors span the covariant field algebra but their sum is not
direct.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants [CompactSpace G.group]
    (hL : T.LorentzContinuous) (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute)
    {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (h₁ : x ∈ (repValue T).invariants)
    (h₂ : x ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants) :
    ∃ (c : ℂ) (y : Finset FieldKind → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra), (∀ A, y A ∈ T.sector A ∧
      y A ∈ (repValue T).invariants ∧
      y A ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants) ∧
      x = c • 1 + ∑ A ∈ Finset.univ.erase ∅, y A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeightLE
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, an invariant element of mass weight at most `w` is a sum of one
element from the sector of each set of kinds, every one of them of mass weight at most `w` and
invariant under the gauge and Lorentz groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeightLE [CompactSpace G.group]
    (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (hL : T.LorentzContinuous) (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute)
    {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE P w)
    (h₁ : x ∈ (repValue T).invariants)
    (h₂ : x ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants) :
    ∃ y : Finset FieldKind → T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra, (∀ A, y A ∈ T.sector A ∧
      y A ∈ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE P w ∧ y A ∈ (repValue T).invariants ∧
      y A ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants) ∧
      x = ∑ A, y A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeightLE
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, an invariant element of mass weight at most `w` is a constant
plus a sum of one element from each of the seven nonempty sectors,
`x = c • 1 + ∑_{A ≠ ∅} x_A`, every `x_A` of mass weight at most `w` and invariant under the
gauge and Lorentz groups. This needs a compact gauge group, continuous Lorentz

declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeightLE
    [CompactSpace G.group] (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (hL : T.LorentzContinuous) (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute)
    {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE P w)
    (h₁ : x ∈ (repValue T).invariants)
    (h₂ : x ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants) :

      y A ∈ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmoduleLE P w ∧ y A ∈ (repValue T).invariants ∧
      y A ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants) ∧
      x = c • 1 + ∑ A ∈ Finset.univ.erase ∅, y A

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeight
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, an invariant element of mass weight `w` is a sum of one element

declarations.statement:
lemma exists_eq_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeight [CompactSpace G.group]

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeight
declarations.doc:
Under `IsMassWeightPoly P`, an invariant element of mass weight `w` is a constant plus a sum

`x_A` of mass weight `w` and invariant under the gauge and Lorentz groups. The decomposition is

lemma exists_eq_smul_one_add_sum_sector_of_mem_invariants_massWeight
    [CompactSpace G.group] (hP : LocalCovFieldAlgebra.IsMassWeightPoly P)
    (hL : T.LorentzContinuous) (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute)

      y A ∈ LocalCovFieldAlgebra.massWeightSubmodule P w ∧ y A ∈ (repValue T).invariants ∧

modules.title: The Lorentz action on the local field algebra
modules.doc:
The action of `SL(2,ℂ)` on the local field algebra by algebra endomorphisms.

## i. Overview

The Lorentz group `SL(2,ℂ)` acts on the local field algebra `J(T)` of a field datum by
algebra endomorphisms. It acts on the generators of a matter species by the action
`FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup` of that species, mixing the derivative label and the
target index, and on the connection generators by the gauge-only action
`LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup`. The construction is that of the jet gauge action
in `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalFieldAlgebra.GaugeAction`, the lift of a
compatible assignment, with the representation laws from uniqueness.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom`, `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup` : the action of a
  Lorentz transformation, as an algebra endomorphism and as a representation, with
  `repLorentzGroup_ιFermion`, `repLorentzGroup_ιBoson`, `repLorentzGroup_ιConnection` on the
  generators.
- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_includeConnection` : on the connection factor the action
  is the complexified gauge-only action.
- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιConnection_eq` : the law of the connection generators.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lorentz assignment of a transformation
- B. The action of a transformation
- C. The action on the connection factor
- D. The representation

## iv. References

* None.
