declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lorentzConnection
declarations.doc:
The connection generators after a Lorentz transformation, the gauge-only action on the
degree-one element, included into the local field algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def lorentzConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G →ₗ[ℝ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lorentzAssignment
declarations.doc:
The assignment of the generators defining the action of a Lorentz transformation. Each
matter species acts on its own component functions, the connection generators through
the gauge-only action.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lorentzAssignment (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) : T.Assignment T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The action of a Lorentz transformation on the local field algebra, as an algebra
endomorphism, the lift of its Lorentz assignment.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repLorentzAlgHom (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_ιFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_ιFermion (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.ιFermion i x)
      = T.ιFermion i (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermion i) Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_ιBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_ιBoson (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.ιBoson j y)
      = T.ιBoson j (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.boson j) Λ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_ιConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_ιConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.ιConnection v)
      = T.includeConnection ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
          LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup G Λ (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ v))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_comp_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
The action of a Lorentz transformation restricts to the complexified gauge-only action
on the connection factor, as an equation of algebra maps out of the complexified
gauge-only algebra, compared on the real generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_comp_includeConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    (T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ).comp T.includeConnection
      = T.includeConnection.comp (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroupAlgHom G Λ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
The action of a Lorentz transformation restricts to the complexified gauge-only action
on the connection factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_includeConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.includeConnection y)
      = T.includeConnection (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup G Λ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_includeConnection_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
On the real gauge-only algebra, included, a Lorentz transformation acts through the
gauge-only action.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_includeConnection_one_tmul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ (T.includeConnection ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] x))
      = T.includeConnection ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup G Λ
        x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_one
declarations.doc: The identity transformation acts as the identity.
declarations.statement: lemma repLorentzAlgHom_one : T.repLorentzAlgHom 1 = AlgHom.id ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzAlgHom_mul
declarations.doc: The action of a product of transformations is the composite of the actions.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzAlgHom_mul (Λ₁ Λ₂ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    T.repLorentzAlgHom (Λ₁ * Λ₂) = (T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ₁).comp (T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ₂)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc: The action of the Lorentz group on the local field algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentzGroup : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ x = T.repLorentzAlgHom Λ x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_apply_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x y : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (x * y) = T.repLorentzGroup Λ x * T.repLorentzGroup Λ y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_apply_one
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_apply_one (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (1 : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) = 1

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ιFermion (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.ιFermion i x)
      = T.ιFermion i (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.fermion i) Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ιBoson (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.ιBoson j y)
      = T.ιBoson j (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (T.boson j) Λ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ιConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.ιConnection v)
      = T.includeConnection ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
          LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup G Λ (SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ _ v))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action restricts to the complexified gauge-only action on the connection
factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_includeConnection (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.includeConnection y)
      = T.includeConnection (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexRepLorentzGroup G Λ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιConnection_eq
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of the connection generators. A transformation carries a connection
generator to the generator of the transformed component, with no shift. This is the
generator-level form of `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_ιConnection`, with no reference
to the connection factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_ιConnection_eq (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.ιConnection v)
      = T.ιConnection (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup G Λ v)

modules.title: The mass-weight filtration and the invariants of a local field algebra
modules.doc:
The grading of the local field algebra by mass weight, and its gauge and Lorentz invariants of
bounded mass weight.

## i. Overview

The local field algebra of a field datum is graded by mass weight: a generator `∂_s φ_α`
of a field of mass weight `w` has weight `w + 2 |s|`, a connection generator `∂_s A_μ` has
weight `2 + 2 |s|`. The grading is recorded by the algebra endomorphisms scaling each
generator by `c` to its weight, for real `c`.

The same grading is also recorded with the scalar replaced by a formal variable. The
mass-weight polynomial is the algebra map into the polynomials over the local field algebra
sending a generator of weight `n` to `X ^ n` times itself. It is built from the universal
property of the local field algebra. The polynomials over a noncommutative algebra are
noncommutative, so the statistics of the images have to be checked, and they follow from
those of the coefficients. The weight-`n` piece is the eigenspace on which the mass-weight
polynomial is `X ^ n`, and the filtration is the join of the pieces of weight at most `w`.
Setting the formal variable to a real number `c` gives back the scaling by `c`, so the
weight-`n` piece is also the set of elements scaled by `c ^ n` for every `c`.

Together with the actions of the jet gauge group and of the Lorentz group this gives the
submodule of gauge and Lorentz invariants of mass weight at most `w`, which is what a
Lagrangian classification describes. Everything here is generic: a model contributes only
its datum.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale` : the scaling of the local field algebra by `c` to the
  mass weight of each generator.
- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly` : the mass-weight polynomial, sending a generator of
  weight `n` to `X ^ n` times itself.
- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_fermionSymbol`, `massWeightPoly_bosonSymbol` and their
  conjugates : the symbols `∂_s ψ` of a species of mass weight `w` have weight `w + 2 |s|`.
- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_gaugeField` : the gauge-field symbols `∂_s A_μ`
  have weight `2 (1 + |s|)`.
- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_eq_polyEval_comp_massWeightPoly` : the scaling by `c` is
  the mass-weight polynomial evaluated at `c`.
- `GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule`, `massWeightSubmoduleLE` : the graded pieces and
  the filtration.
- `GaugeFieldData.mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff_massWeightScale` : the weight-`n` piece is the
  set of elements scaled by `c ^ n` under the scaling by every real `c`.
- `GaugeFieldData.gaugeInvariants`, `lorentzInvariants`, `invariantsLE` : the invariants,
  and the invariants of mass weight at most `w`.
- `GaugeFieldData.bosonNormSq` : the contraction `φ† φ` of a bosonic species with its
  conjugate through a basis of its value space, the simplest invariant.
- `GaugeFieldData.invariantsLE_map` : an isomorphism of local field algebras respecting the
  actions and the mass-weight polynomial carries the invariants of one datum onto those of the
  other.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The mass-weight scaling
- B. The mass-weight polynomial
  - B.1. The grading of a component function
  - B.2. The images of the generators
  - B.3. The mass-weight polynomial and its generators
  - B.4. Evaluation at a real number
- C. The graded pieces and the filtration
- D. The invariants
- E. The contraction of a boson with its conjugate
- F. Transport along an isomorphism

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The mass-weight scaling

## B. The mass-weight polynomial

Replacing the scalar `c` of the scaling by a formal variable `X` turns the scaling into a
grading. The image of a generator is a polynomial over the local field algebra whose
coefficients are generators of the same species, so the relations among the generators hold
for their images coefficient by coefficient. That is what makes the images a compatible
assignment, and the grading the algebra map it induces.
### B.1. The grading of a component function

### B.2. The images of the generators

The image of a matter generator is the sum of the two half gradings of its component
space, at the mass weight of its species, with the symbol maps of the species as the maps
`k`. The image of a connection generator is the grading of the complexified gauge-boson
algebra, pushed into the local field algebra coefficient by coefficient.
### B.3. The mass-weight polynomial and its generators

### B.4. Evaluation at a real number

Setting the formal variable of the mass-weight polynomial to a real number `c` gives back the
mass-weight scaling by `c`. The scalar `c` is central, so evaluation at it is an algebra map,
and it is enough to compare the two algebra maps on the generators.
## C. The graded pieces and the filtration
## D. The invariants
## E. The contraction of a boson with its conjugate

## F. Transport along an isomorphism

An isomorphism of local field algebras intertwining the jet gauge action, the Lorentz
action and the mass-weight polynomial carries the graded pieces, the filtration and the
invariants of one datum onto those of the other. This is what relates two presentations
of the same field content, such as a model's table and a hand-built datum.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightAssignment
declarations.doc:
The assignment scaling each generator by `c` to its mass weight. A component function
`∂_s φ_α` of a species of mass weight `w` by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, a connection generator
`∂_s A_μ` by `c ^ (2 + 2 |s|)`. The relations hold because the images are generators of
the same kind.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightAssignment (c : ℝ) : T.Assignment T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling of the local field algebra, the algebra endomorphism
scaling each generator by `c` to its mass weight.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightScale (c : ℝ) : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_ιFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_ιFermion (c : ℝ) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.massWeightScale c (T.ιFermion i x)
      = T.ιFermion i (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (T.fermion i).massWeight (c : ℂ) x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_ιBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_ιBoson (c : ℝ) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.massWeightScale c (T.ιBoson j y)
      = T.ιBoson j (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (T.boson j).massWeight (c : ℂ) y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_ιConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_ιConnection (c : ℝ) (v : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) :
    T.massWeightScale c (T.ιConnection v)
      = T.ιConnection (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale G c v)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.instRingPolynomialLocalFieldAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The polynomials over the local field algebra form a ring. The instance is recorded here
so that it is found directly, without searching through the tensor-product structure of
the local field algebra once more.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instRingPolynomialLocalFieldAlgebra :
    Ring (Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.monomialₗ
declarations.doc:
The monomial of degree `n` over the local field algebra, as a map of complex vector
spaces rather than of modules over the local field algebra.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def monomialₗ (n : ℕ) :
    T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.halfPoly
declarations.doc:
One half of the grading of a component space, for a species of mass weight `w`. It
sends the symbol `∂_s φ` to `X ^ (w + 2 |s|)` times its image under `k`, and is defined on
the multiset basis of the derivative labels.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def halfPoly {W : Type} [AddCommGroup W] [Module ℂ W] (w : ℕ)
    (k : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] W →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] W →ₗ[ℂ] Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.monomialₗ_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma monomialₗ_apply (n : ℕ) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.monomialₗ n x = Polynomial.monomial n x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.halfPoly_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
On the symbol `∂_s φ` the half grading is the monomial of degree `w + 2 |s|`, since the
field contributes `w` and each derivative two.
declarations.statement:
lemma halfPoly_basis_tmul {W : Type} [AddCommGroup W] [Module ℂ W] (w : ℕ)
    (k : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] W →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (x : W) :
    T.halfPoly w k (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] x) =
      Polynomial.monomial (w + 2 * Multiset.card s)
        (k (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] x))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.halfPoly_coeff_mem
declarations.doc:
Every coefficient of the half grading lies in the range of `k`. The derivative monomials
span the derivative labels, and on each of them the half grading is a single monomial
whose coefficient is in the range.
declarations.statement:
lemma halfPoly_coeff_mem {W : Type} [AddCommGroup W] [Module ℂ W] (w : ℕ)
    (k : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] W →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] W) (n : ℕ) :
    (T.halfPoly w k z).coeff n ∈ LinearMap.range k

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionPoly
declarations.doc:
The grading of the component space of a fermionic species, the half gradings of the
symbols and of the conjugate symbols, at the mass weight of the species.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fermionPoly (i : T.FermionSpecies) :
    FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i) →ₗ[ℂ] Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonPoly
declarations.doc:
The grading of the component space of a bosonic species, the half gradings of the
symbols and of the conjugate symbols, at the mass weight of the species.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bosonPoly (j : T.BosonSpecies) :
    FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j) →ₗ[ℂ] Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.connectionOfAlgHom
declarations.doc:
An algebra map out of the complexified connection factor, read on the connection
generators, `v ↦ h (1 ⊗ v)`. It is stated for an arbitrary complex algebra `C`, so that
the real structure of `C` is the one the generator assignments use.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def connectionOfAlgHom {C : Type*} [Ring C] [Algebra ℂ C]
    (h : (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] SymmetricAlgebra ℝ (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)) →ₐ[ℂ] C) :
    GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G →ₗ[ℝ] C

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.connectionPoly
declarations.doc:
The grading of the connection generators, a real-linear map from
`GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G` to `Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra`, the grading of the
complexified gauge-boson algebra, pushed into the local field algebra coefficient by
coefficient. Its type is left to be inferred, so that the real structure on the
polynomials is the one `connectionOfAlgHom` and the generator assignments use.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def connectionPoly

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionPoly_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionPoly_apply (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.fermionPoly i x = T.halfPoly (T.fermion i).massWeight (T.fermionSymbolMap i) x.1
      + T.halfPoly (T.fermion i).massWeight (T.conjFermionSymbolMap i) x.2

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonPoly_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonPoly_apply (j : T.BosonSpecies) (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.bosonPoly j y = T.halfPoly (T.boson j).massWeight (T.bosonSymbolMap j) y.1
      + T.halfPoly (T.boson j).massWeight (T.conjBosonSymbolMap j) y.2

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.connectionPoly_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma connectionPoly_apply (v : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) :
    T.connectionPoly v = Polynomial.mapAlgHom T.includeConnection
      (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexMassWeightPoly (G := G)
        ((1 : ℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℝ (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) v))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionPoly_inl
declarations.doc:
On an unconjugated symbol `∂_s ψ^φ` of a fermionic species of mass weight `w` the
grading is the monomial of degree `w + 2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionPoly_inl (i : T.FermionSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    T.fermionPoly i (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0)
      = Polynomial.monomial ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s)
          (T.fermionSymbol i s φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionPoly_inr
declarations.doc: On a conjugate symbol `∂_s ψ̄^φ` the grading is the monomial of the same degree.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionPoly_inr (i : T.FermionSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    T.fermionPoly i (0, SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)
      = Polynomial.monomial ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s)
          (T.conjFermionSymbol i s φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonPoly_inl
declarations.doc:
On an unconjugated symbol `∂_s φ^χ` of a bosonic species of mass weight `w` the
grading is the monomial of degree `w + 2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonPoly_inl (j : T.BosonSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) :
    T.bosonPoly j (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, 0)
      = Polynomial.monomial ((T.boson j).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s)
          (T.bosonSymbol j s φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonPoly_inr
declarations.doc: On a conjugate symbol `∂_s φ̄^χ` the grading is the monomial of the same degree.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonPoly_inr (j : T.BosonSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))) :
    T.bosonPoly j (0, SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)
      = Polynomial.monomial ((T.boson j).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s)
          (T.conjBosonSymbol j s φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionPoly_coeff_mem
declarations.doc:
Every coefficient of the image of a fermionic generator is a generator of the same
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionPoly_coeff_mem (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i))
    (n : ℕ) : (T.fermionPoly i x).coeff n ∈ LinearMap.range (T.ιFermion i)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonPoly_coeff_mem
declarations.doc:
Every coefficient of the image of a bosonic generator is a generator of the same
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma bosonPoly_coeff_mem (j : T.BosonSpecies) (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j))
    (n : ℕ) : (T.bosonPoly j y).coeff n ∈ LinearMap.range (T.ιBoson j)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.fermionPoly_mul_swap
declarations.doc:
The images of two fermionic generators anticommute, because their coefficients are
fermionic generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma fermionPoly_mul_swap (i j : T.FermionSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i))
    (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion j)) :
    T.fermionPoly i x * T.fermionPoly j y = -(T.fermionPoly j y * T.fermionPoly i x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.commute_bosonPoly
declarations.doc: The image of a bosonic generator is central, because its coefficients are.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_bosonPoly (j : T.BosonSpecies) (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j))
    (q : Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra) : Commute (T.bosonPoly j y) q

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.commute_mapAlgHom_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
A polynomial with coefficients in the connection factor is central, because the
connection factor is.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_mapAlgHom_includeConnection
    (p : Polynomial (ℂ ⊗[ℝ] SymmetricAlgebra ℝ (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)))
    (q : Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    Commute (Polynomial.mapAlgHom T.includeConnection p) q

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.commute_connectionPoly
declarations.doc: The image of a connection generator is central.
declarations.statement:
lemma commute_connectionPoly (v : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G)
    (q : Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra) : Commute (T.connectionPoly v) q

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPolyAssignment
declarations.doc:
The grading of the generators as a compatible assignment in the polynomials over the
local field algebra. The fermionic images anticommute and the bosonic and connection
images are central, because their coefficients do and are.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def massWeightPolyAssignment :
    T.Assignment (Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight polynomial of the local field algebra, the algebra map sending a
generator of mass weight `n` to `X ^ n` times itself, so that the coefficient of `X ^ n`
in the image of an element is its part of mass weight `n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightPoly : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_ιFermion
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_ιFermion (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.massWeightPoly (T.ιFermion i x) = T.fermionPoly i x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_ιBoson
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_ιBoson (j : T.BosonSpecies) (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.massWeightPoly (T.ιBoson j y) = T.bosonPoly j y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_ιConnection
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_ιConnection (v : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) :
    T.massWeightPoly (T.ιConnection v) = T.connectionPoly v

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_fermionSymbol
declarations.doc:
The symbol `∂_s ψ^φ` of a fermionic species of mass weight `w` has weight
`w + 2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_fermionSymbol (i : T.FermionSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    T.massWeightPoly (T.fermionSymbol i s φ)
      = Polynomial.monomial ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s)
          (T.fermionSymbol i s φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_conjFermionSymbol
declarations.doc: The conjugate symbol `∂_s ψ̄^φ` has the same weight `w + 2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_conjFermionSymbol (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    T.massWeightPoly (T.conjFermionSymbol i s φ)
      = Polynomial.monomial ((T.fermion i).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s)
          (T.conjFermionSymbol i s φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_bosonSymbol
declarations.doc: The symbol `∂_s φ^χ` of a bosonic species of mass weight `w` has weight `w + 2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_bosonSymbol (j : T.BosonSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) :
    T.massWeightPoly (T.bosonSymbol j s φ)
      = Polynomial.monomial ((T.boson j).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s)
          (T.bosonSymbol j s φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_conjBosonSymbol
declarations.doc: The conjugate symbol `∂_s φ̄^χ` has the same weight `w + 2 |s|`.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_conjBosonSymbol (j : T.BosonSpecies) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))) :
    T.massWeightPoly (T.conjBosonSymbol j s φ)
      = Polynomial.monomial ((T.boson j).massWeight + 2 * Multiset.card s)
          (T.conjBosonSymbol j s φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightPoly_gaugeField
declarations.doc:
The gauge-field symbol `∂_s A_μ^φ` has mass weight `2 (1 + |s|)`, since the gauge field has
mass dimension one and each derivative adds one more. This is the form of the hypothesis
that the mass weights of the covariant towers take.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightPoly_gaugeField (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    T.massWeightPoly (T.gaugeField s μ φ)
      = Polynomial.monomial (2 * (1 + Multiset.card s)) (T.gaugeField s μ φ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.polyEval
declarations.doc:
Evaluation of a polynomial over the local field algebra at a real number `c`. It is an
algebra map because `c` is central.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def polyEval (c : ℝ) :
    Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₐ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.polyEval_monomial
declarations.doc: Evaluating the monomial `x X ^ n` at `c` gives `c ^ n x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyEval_monomial (c : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.polyEval c (Polynomial.monomial n x) = ((c : ℂ) ^ n) • x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.polyEval_eq_sum
declarations.doc: Evaluation at `c` as a sum over the coefficients.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyEval_eq_sum (c : ℝ) (q : Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.polyEval c q = ∑ m ∈ Finset.range (q.natDegree + 1), ((c : ℂ) ^ m) • q.coeff m

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.eq_zero_of_forall_polyEval_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
A polynomial over the local field algebra vanishing at every real number is zero, its
coefficients being those of an identically vanishing polynomial function.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_zero_of_forall_polyEval_eq_zero {q : Polynomial T.LocalFieldAlgebra}
    (h : ∀ c : ℝ, T.polyEval c q = 0) : q = 0

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.polyEval_halfPoly
declarations.doc:
The half grading evaluated at `c` is the mass-weight scaling of the half component space,
`c ^ w` times the derivative-degree scaling by `c ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyEval_halfPoly (c : ℝ) {W : Type} [AddCommGroup W] [Module ℂ W] (w : ℕ)
    (k : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] W →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] W) :
    T.polyEval c (T.halfPoly w k z) = ((c : ℂ) ^ w) • k (TensorProduct.map
      (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.gradeScale ((c : ℂ) ^ 2)).toLinearMap LinearMap.id z)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.polyEval_fermionPoly
declarations.doc: The image of a fermionic generator evaluated at `c` is its mass-weight scaling by `c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyEval_fermionPoly (c : ℝ) (i : T.FermionSpecies) (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.polyEval c (T.fermionPoly i x)
      = T.ιFermion i (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (T.fermion i).massWeight (c : ℂ) x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.polyEval_bosonPoly
declarations.doc: The image of a bosonic generator evaluated at `c` is its mass-weight scaling by `c`.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyEval_bosonPoly (c : ℝ) (j : T.BosonSpecies) (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.polyEval c (T.bosonPoly j y)
      = T.ιBoson j (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (T.boson j).massWeight (c : ℂ) y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.polyEval_connectionPoly
declarations.doc:
The image of a connection generator evaluated at `c` is its mass-weight scaling by `c`.
The evaluation is pushed through the inclusion of the connection factor, where it is the
evaluation of the gauge-boson grading.
declarations.statement:
lemma polyEval_connectionPoly (c : ℝ) (v : GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace G) :
    T.polyEval c (T.connectionPoly v)
      = T.ιConnection (GaugeBoson.FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale G c v)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_eq_polyEval_comp_massWeightPoly
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling by `c` is the mass-weight polynomial evaluated at `c`, since both are
algebra maps, and they agree on the generators.
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_eq_polyEval_comp_massWeightPoly (c : ℝ) :
    T.massWeightScale c = (T.polyEval c).comp T.massWeightPoly

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightScale_apply (c : ℝ) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.massWeightScale c x = T.polyEval c (T.massWeightPoly x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc:
The weight-`n` piece of the local field algebra, the eigenspace on which the
mass-weight polynomial is the monomial `X ^ n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmodule (n : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: Membership of the weight-`n` piece is the eigenvalue equation.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule {n : ℕ} {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.massWeightSubmodule n ↔ T.massWeightPoly x = Polynomial.monomial n x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightScale_of_mem_massWeightSubmodule
declarations.doc: The mass-weight scaling by `c` multiplies the weight-`n` piece by `c ^ n`.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff_massWeightScale
declarations.doc:
The weight-`n` piece is the set of elements scaled by `c ^ n` under the mass-weight
scaling by every real `c`. Conversely to the eigenvalue equation, the difference of the two
sides of it is a polynomial vanishing at every real number.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_iff_massWeightScale {n : ℕ} {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.massWeightSubmodule n ↔ ∀ c : ℝ, T.massWeightScale c x = ((c : ℂ) ^ n) • x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight filtration, the join of the pieces of weight at most `w`. An element
lies in it exactly when it is a sum of eigenvectors of the mass-weight polynomial of weight at
most `w`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def massWeightSubmoduleLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_le_massWeightSubmoduleLE {k w : ℕ} (h : k ≤ w) :
    T.massWeightSubmodule k ≤ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.coeff_massWeightPoly_eq_zero_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE
declarations.doc:
An element of the filtration up to weight `w` has no component above `w`, so the
coefficient of `X ^ n` in its image under the mass-weight polynomial vanishes for `n > w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_massWeightPoly_eq_zero_of_mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE {w n : ℕ} (hn : w < n)
    {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} (hx : x ∈ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w) :
    (T.massWeightPoly x).coeff n = 0

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeInvariants
declarations.doc: The gauge invariants, the elements fixed by every jet of gauge transformations.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeInvariants : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_gaugeInvariants_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_gaugeInvariants_iff {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.gaugeInvariants ↔ ∀ U : G.gaugeJetGroup, T.repJet U x = x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.lorentzInvariants
declarations.doc: The Lorentz invariants, the elements fixed by every Lorentz transformation.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lorentzInvariants : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_lorentzInvariants_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_lorentzInvariants_iff {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.lorentzInvariants ↔ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), T.repLorentzGroup Λ x = x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.invariantsLE
declarations.doc:
The invariants of mass weight at most `w`, the gauge and Lorentz invariants in the
filtration. A Lagrangian of mass dimension at most `w / 2` is an element of it.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def invariantsLE (w : ℕ) : Submodule ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_invariantsLE_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_invariantsLE_iff {w : ℕ} {x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra} :
    x ∈ T.invariantsLE w ↔ x ∈ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w
      ∧ (∀ U : G.gaugeJetGroup, T.repJet U x = x) ∧ ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), T.repLorentzGroup Λ x = x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.bosonNormSq
declarations.doc:
The contraction `φ† φ` of a bosonic species with its conjugate, through a basis of
its value space, the sum over the basis of the conjugate coordinate times the coordinate.
For a scalar in a unitary representation it is the mass term.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def bosonNormSq (j : T.BosonSpecies) {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    (b : Module.Basis ι ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) : T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_massWeightSubmodule_apply_iff
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight polynomial is respected, so the weight-`n` piece is carried onto the
weight-`n` piece.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmodule_apply_iff
    (hpoly : ∀ x, (T.massWeightPoly x).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →+* T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightPoly (e x))
    (n : ℕ) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    e x ∈ T'.massWeightSubmodule n ↔ x ∈ T.massWeightSubmodule n

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmodule_map
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmodule_map
    (hpoly : ∀ x, (T.massWeightPoly x).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →+* T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightPoly (e x)) (n : ℕ) :
    (T.massWeightSubmodule n).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightSubmodule n

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.massWeightSubmoduleLE_map
declarations.statement:
lemma massWeightSubmoduleLE_map
    (hpoly : ∀ x, (T.massWeightPoly x).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →+* T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightPoly (e x)) (w : ℕ) :
    (T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_apply_iff
declarations.doc: The filtration is respected, element by element.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_massWeightSubmoduleLE_apply_iff
    (hpoly : ∀ x, (T.massWeightPoly x).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →+* T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightPoly (e x)) (w : ℕ)
    (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    e x ∈ T'.massWeightSubmoduleLE w ↔ x ∈ T.massWeightSubmoduleLE w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.mem_invariantsLE_apply_iff
declarations.doc: The invariants of mass weight at most `w` are respected, element by element.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_invariantsLE_apply_iff
    (hjet : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) x, e (T.repJet U x) = T'.repJet U (e x))
    (hlor : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) x, e (T.repLorentzGroup Λ x) = T'.repLorentzGroup Λ (e x))
    (hpoly : ∀ x, (T.massWeightPoly x).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →+* T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightPoly (e x)) (w : ℕ)
    (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    e x ∈ T'.invariantsLE w ↔ x ∈ T.invariantsLE w

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.invariantsLE_map
declarations.doc:
The invariants of mass weight at most `w` are carried onto the invariants of mass
weight at most `w` by an isomorphism respecting the two actions and the mass-weight
polynomial.
declarations.statement:
lemma invariantsLE_map (hjet : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) x, e (T.repJet U x) = T'.repJet U (e x))
    (hlor : ∀ (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) x, e (T.repLorentzGroup Λ x) = T'.repLorentzGroup Λ (e x))
    (hpoly : ∀ x, (T.massWeightPoly x).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →+* T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.massWeightPoly (e x)) (w : ℕ) :
    (T.invariantsLE w).map (e : T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T'.LocalFieldAlgebra)
      = T'.invariantsLE w

modules.title: Realizations of the local field algebra
modules.doc:
Equivariant algebra maps out of the local field algebra of a gauge theory.

## i. Overview

A complex algebra `B` carries the fields of a gauge-field datum when the local field
algebra `J(T)` maps into it by a complex algebra map equivariant for the jet gauge group
and the Lorentz group, both acting on `B` by algebra endomorphisms. Such a map is a
`GaugeFieldData.Realization`. The gauge-field symbols of a realization are those of the
gauge-boson jet algebra carried along the composite of the inclusion of the connection factor
with the map, `mapGaugeField (h.toAlgHom.comp T.includeConnection)`. They transform as a gauge
field, so the gauge-boson symbol theory applies to them, and the realized field-strength tower
is identified with their covariant tower.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.Realization` : an algebra carrying the fields of a datum.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.id` : the local field algebra realized in itself.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.transformsAsGaugeField_mapGaugeField` : the gauge-field symbols
  of a realization transform as a gauge field.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_covDerivFieldStrength` : the realized field-strength
  tower is the covariant tower of the realized symbols.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Realizations
- B. The gauge bosons of a realization

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization
declarations.doc:
A complex algebra `B` carrying the fields of the datum `T`, through a complex algebra map out
of the local field algebra, equivariant for the jet gauge group and the Lorentz group,
both acting on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms. No commutativity, injectivity
or surjectivity is assumed, and no derivative operator on `B` is involved. It is built
from the fields `toAlgHom`, `map_fst`, `map_snd`, `fst_mul`, `snd_mul` of
`Representation.EquivariantAlgHom`, which the lemmas `map_repJet`, `map_repLorentz`,
`repJet_mul` and `repLorentz_mul` name.
declarations.statement:
abbrev Realization (T : GaugeFieldData G) (B : Type) [Ring B] [Algebra ℂ B]
    (repJet : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup B) (repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) B)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.id
declarations.doc: The local field algebra realized in itself, by the identity.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def id : Realization T T.LocalFieldAlgebra T.repJet T.repLorentzGroup

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.map_repJet
declarations.doc: The map is equivariant for the jet gauge group.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_repJet (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.repJet U x) = repJet U (h.toAlgHom x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.map_repLorentz
declarations.doc: The map is equivariant for the Lorentz group.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_repLorentz (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.repLorentzGroup Λ x) = repLorentz Λ (h.toAlgHom x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.repJet_mul
declarations.doc: The jet gauge group acts on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_mul (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (b₁ b₂ : B) :
    repJet U (b₁ * b₂) = repJet U b₁ * repJet U b₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.repLorentz_mul
declarations.doc: The Lorentz group acts on the whole of `B` by algebra endomorphisms.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_mul (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (b₁ b₂ : B) :
    repLorentz Λ (b₁ * b₂) = repLorentz Λ b₁ * repLorentz Λ b₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.transformsAsGaugeField_mapGaugeField
declarations.doc:
The gauge-field symbols of a realization, those of `J(T)` carried along the map, transform
as a gauge field.
declarations.statement:
lemma transformsAsGaugeField_mapGaugeField :
    GaugeBoson.TransformsAsGaugeField G repJet
      (mapGaugeField (h.toAlgHom.comp T.includeConnection))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_covDerivFieldStrength
declarations.doc:
The map of a realization carries the included field-strength tower to the covariant
tower of the realized gauge-field symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma toAlgHom_covDerivFieldStrength (l : List (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    h.toAlgHom (T.covDerivFieldStrength l μ ν φ)
      = iteratedCovDerivAdjoint (mapGaugeField (h.toAlgHom.comp T.includeConnection)) l
        (fieldStrength (mapGaugeField (h.toAlgHom.comp T.includeConnection)) μ ν) 0 φ

modules.title: Invariants descend along realizations
modules.doc:
An invariant in the image of a realization of the covariant or the local field algebra is the
image of an invariant of the covariant field algebra.

## i. Overview

Let `k` be a realization of the covariant field algebra of a field datum `T` in an algebra `B`.
It is an algebra map, equivariant for the ordinary gauge group and for the Lorentz group. Suppose
`k a` is invariant under both groups. We show that `k a = k a'` for some `a'` invariant under both
groups in the covariant field algebra. So every gauge and Lorentz invariant expression of a
realization is written by an invariant covariant expression.

The proof averages `a` over both groups. By
`GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.finiteSubrep`, the element `a` lies in a finite-dimensional
subspace `W`, stable under both groups, on which both act continuously. For a compact gauge group
the Haar average gives a Reynolds element `r₁` of the gauge group on `W`, and the Casimir
projection gives a Reynolds element `r₂` of `SL(2,ℂ)` on `W`. Their product `r` is a Reynolds
element for the joint action, so `a' = r • a` is invariant under both groups. The map `k`
intertwines the actions of `r₁` and `r₂`. On the invariant vector `k a` they act as the sums of
their coefficients, which are one, so `k a' = k a`.

The theorem needs three conditions. The gauge group must be compact, the Lorentz representation
of every species continuous, and the gauge and Lorentz representations of every species must
commute (see `GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCommute`).

The same holds for a realization `k` of the whole local field algebra, now with the jet gauge
group acting on the target. The image `k x` is invariant under the jet gauge group and the
Lorentz group exactly when `k x = k a'` for some `a'` of the covariant field algebra invariant
under the ordinary gauge group and the Lorentz group. The reverse direction holds because the
jet action on the covariant field algebra factors through evaluation. The forward direction has
three steps.

* The local field algebra is generated by the gauge-field symbols `∂_s A_μ` and the covariant
  field algebra. The matter symbols `∂_s ψ` are polynomials in the covariant towers `∇_l ψ` and
  the gauge-field symbols, by the span lemma
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjoin_symbols_eq_adjoin_covDerivIter`.
* So `k x` lies in the subalgebra generated by the realized gauge-field symbols and the image
  `S` of the covariant field algebra. The elements of `S` are fixed by the pure jets and commute
  with the gauge-field symbols, which come from the central connection factor. The
  classification `GaugeBoson.invariant_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength` then places the
  jet-invariant `k x` in the subalgebra generated by the realized field-strength tower and `S`,
  which is the image of the covariant field algebra. So `k x = k c` for a covariant `c`.
* `exists_mem_invariants_map_eq`, applied to the restriction of `k` to the covariant field
  algebra and to `c`, gives the invariant `a'`.

## ii. Key results

- `Representation.IsReynolds.exists_mem_invariants_map_eq_prod` : descent along an intertwining
  map for Reynolds elements of the two factors of a product group.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.exists_isReynolds_finiteSubrep` : the joint action of the
  gauge and Lorentz groups has a Reynolds element on `finiteSubrep`.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization.exists_mem_invariants_map_eq` : invariants of
  a realization descend to invariants of the covariant field algebra.
- `GaugeFieldData.adjoin_symbols_union_localCovFieldAlgebra_eq_top` : the local field algebra
  is generated by the gauge-field symbols and the covariant field algebra.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.exists_mem_localCovFieldAlgebra_map_eq` : a jet-invariant image of
  a realization of the local field algebra is the image of a covariant expression.
- `GaugeFieldData.Realization.mem_invariants_iff_exists_mem_invariants` : the invariants of a
  realization of the local field algebra are the images of the invariants of the covariant
  field algebra.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Descent for products of groups
- B. Reynolds elements for the joint action
- C. Invariants descend along realizations
- D. Generation by the gauge-field symbols and the covariant field algebra
- E. Invariants of realizations of the local field algebra

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Representation.IsReynolds.exists_mem_invariants_map_eq_prod
declarations.doc:
The descent property for a representation of `H₁ × H₂` with Reynolds elements for both
factors on the same subspace. If `f` intertwines each factor with a representation on `B`, the
vector `a` lies in the subspace, and `f a` is invariant under both representations on `B`, then
`f a` is the image of an invariant vector. The representations on `B` need not commute.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.exists_isReynolds_finiteSubrep
declarations.doc:
For a compact gauge group, the joint action of the gauge and Lorentz groups has a Reynolds
element on `finiteSubrep`, the product of the Reynolds elements of the two groups.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_isReynolds_finiteSubrep [CompactSpace G.group] (hL : T.LorentzContinuous)
    (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute) (a : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) :
    ∃ (r₁ : MonoidAlgebra ℂ G.group) (r₂ : MonoidAlgebra ℂ SL(2,ℂ)),
      Representation.IsReynolds ((repGaugeLorentz T hC).comp (MonoidHom.inl _ _))
        (finiteSubrep hL hC a).toSubmodule r₁ ∧
      Representation.IsReynolds ((repGaugeLorentz T hC).comp (MonoidHom.inr _ _))
        (finiteSubrep hL hC a).toSubmodule r₂

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.Realization.exists_mem_invariants_map_eq
declarations.doc:
Invariants descend along realizations. If the image `k a` of a covariant expression under a
realization is invariant under the gauge and Lorentz groups, it is the image of a covariant
expression invariant under both groups. This needs a compact gauge group, continuous Lorentz
representations, and commuting gauge and Lorentz representations of every species.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_mem_invariants_map_eq [CompactSpace G.group] (hL : T.LorentzContinuous)
    (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute) (k : Realization T hGL B repGauge repLorentz)
    (a : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra) (h₁ : k.toAlgHom a ∈ repGauge.invariants)
    (h₂ : k.toAlgHom a ∈ repLorentz.invariants) :
    ∃ a' : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra, a' ∈ (repValue T).invariants ∧
      a' ∈ (repLorentzGroup T hGL).invariants ∧ k.toAlgHom a' = k.toAlgHom a

declarations.name: TensorProduct.apply_mem_of_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
A linear map out of a tensor product lands in a submodule as soon as it does on the pure
tensors of the basis vectors of the left factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma TensorProduct.apply_mem_of_basis_tmul {R M N P ι : Type*} [CommSemiring R]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] [AddCommMonoid P]

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.symbolMap_mem_of_covDerivIter_mem
declarations.doc:
Let `f` be a linear map out of one half of the component space of a matter species, with
symbol family `∂_s ↦ f (∂_s ⊗ ·)`. If a subalgebra contains the gauge-field symbols and the
covariant tower of that family, it contains the whole image of `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbolMap_mem_of_covDerivIter_mem {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
    [FiniteDimensional ℂ V] (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (f : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
    {P : Subalgebra ℂ T.LocalFieldAlgebra} (hA : ∀ s μ ψ, T.gaugeField s μ ψ ∈ P)
    (hF : ∀ n (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) φ, GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter
      T.gaugeField act (fun s => f ∘ₗ TensorProduct.mk ℂ _ _

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.ιFermion_mem_adjoin_symbols_union
declarations.doc:
A fermionic generator is a polynomial in the gauge-field symbols and the covariant
field algebra, since its symbols are polynomials in the gauge-field symbols and its covariant
towers.
declarations.statement:
lemma ιFermion_mem_adjoin_symbols_union (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.ιFermion i x ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      (symbols T.gaugeField ∪ (T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra : Set T.LocalFieldAlgebra))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.ιBoson_mem_adjoin_symbols_union
declarations.doc:
A bosonic generator is a polynomial in the gauge-field symbols and the covariant field
algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma ιBoson_mem_adjoin_symbols_union (j : T.BosonSpecies) (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.ιBoson j y ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.adjoin_symbols_union_localCovFieldAlgebra_eq_top
declarations.doc:
The local field algebra is generated by the gauge-field symbols `∂_s A_μ^φ` together with
the covariant field algebra. The matter symbols `∂_s ψ` are polynomials in the covariant
towers `∇_l ψ` and the gauge-field symbols, by induction on the number of derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoin_symbols_union_localCovFieldAlgebra_eq_top :
    Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      (symbols T.gaugeField ∪ (T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra : Set T.LocalFieldAlgebra)) = ⊤

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.toAlgHom_mem_adjoin_symbols_union
declarations.doc:
The image of a realization is generated by the realized gauge-field symbols together with
the image of the covariant field algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma toAlgHom_mem_adjoin_symbols_union (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    k.toAlgHom x ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ (symbols (mapGaugeField (k.toAlgHom.comp T.includeConnection)) ∪
      k.toAlgHom '' (T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra : Set T.LocalFieldAlgebra))

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.exists_mem_localCovFieldAlgebra_map_eq
declarations.doc:
A jet-invariant element of the image of a realization is the image of a covariant
expression. The gauge-field symbols are classified by
`GaugeBoson.invariant_mem_adjoin_fieldStrength`, with the image of the covariant
field algebra as the further generators. They are fixed by the pure jets and commute with the
gauge-field symbols, which come from the central connection factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_mem_localCovFieldAlgebra_map_eq (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra)
    (hx : k.toAlgHom x ∈ repJet.invariants) :
    ∃ c ∈ T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra, k.toAlgHom c = k.toAlgHom x

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.Realization.mem_invariants_iff_exists_mem_invariants
declarations.doc:
The gauge and Lorentz invariants of a realization of the local field algebra. The image
`k x` is invariant under the jet gauge group and the Lorentz group exactly when it is the image
of a covariant expression invariant under the ordinary gauge group and the Lorentz group. This
needs a compact gauge group, continuous Lorentz representations, and commuting gauge and
Lorentz representations of every species.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_invariants_iff_exists_mem_invariants [CompactSpace G.group]
    (hL : T.LorentzContinuous) (hC : T.GaugeLorentzCommute) (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    k.toAlgHom x ∈ repJet.invariants ∧ k.toAlgHom x ∈ repLorentz.invariants ↔
      ∃ a' : T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra, a' ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repValue T).invariants ∧
        a' ∈ (LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repLorentzGroup T hC.gaugeLorentzCompatible).invariants ∧
        k.toAlgHom (a' : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) = k.toAlgHom x

modules.title: Conditions for the reduction of invariants
modules.doc:
Compactness of the gauge group, continuity of the Lorentz representations and commutation of the
gauge and Lorentz actions.

## i. Overview

Invariants of a realization of the covariant field algebra descend to invariants of the
covariant field algebra itself when both symmetry groups can be averaged over. This needs three
conditions on a gauge theory.

The gauge group must be compact, so that it has a normalized Haar measure. This is
`CompactSpace G.group`, for the topology of `G.group` as a subspace of `GL(κ, ℂ)`. A global
gauge group made of unitary matrices is compact, being closed in the compact unitary group, and
this covers `SU(n)`, `U(1)`, `SO(n)` and `Sp(n)`. The product of two compact global gauge groups
is compact, being the continuous image of the product of the two groups. So the gauge group of
the Standard Model is compact by these instances.

The Lorentz representation of every species must be continuous, in the sense that its matrix
coefficients `Λ ↦ φ (ρ(Λ) v)` are continuous on `SL(2,ℂ)`. The gauge representation of a matter
field is continuous by definition, and its matrix coefficients are continuous too.

The gauge and Lorentz representations of every species must commute,
`GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCommute`. This implies the infinitesimal condition
`GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCompatible` used by the covariant derivative, but not conversely,
since the infinitesimal action does not determine the action of a disconnected gauge group. For
a matter field built as a tensor product of a gauge multiplet and a Lorentz multiplet the two
actions commute.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.compactSpace_ofSubmonoid` : a global gauge group of unitary matrices is
  compact.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.compactSpace_prod` : the product of compact global gauge groups is compact.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.LorentzContinuous` : continuity of the Lorentz representation of
  a matter field.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.continuous_rep_apply` : continuity of the matrix coefficients of
  the gauge representation of a matter field.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.ofMatrixRep_lorentzContinuous`,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.ofMatrixRep_gaugeLorentzCommute` : both conditions hold for the
  matter field of a matrix representation, given continuity of the Lorentz representation on the
  Lorentz factor.
- `Fermion.LeftHandedWeyl.continuous_rep_apply`, `Fermion.RightHandedWeyl.continuous_rep_apply` :
  continuity of the Weyl representations.
- `GaugeFieldData.LorentzContinuous` : the continuity condition on every species of a field
  datum.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Compact global gauge groups
  - A.1. Global gauge groups of unitary matrices
  - A.2. The groups SU(n), U(1), SO(n) and Sp(n)
  - A.3. Products
- B. Conditions on matter fields
  - B.1. Continuity of the gauge representation
  - B.2. Continuity of the Lorentz representation
  - B.3. Matter fields of matrix representations
  - B.4. Continuity of the Weyl representations
- C. Conditions on a field datum

## iv. References

- The compact classical groups, see for example
  T. Bröcker and T. tom Dieck, *Representations of Compact Lie Groups*.

modules.title: Finite-dimensional stable subspaces of the covariant field algebra
modules.doc:
Every covariant expression lies in a finite-dimensional subspace stable under the gauge and
Lorentz groups, on which both act continuously.

## i. Overview

The Haar average over the gauge group and the Casimir projection for the Lorentz group act on
finite-dimensional spaces with continuous actions. To use them on the covariant field algebra,
every covariant expression must lie in such a space. This file constructs one, stable under the
joint action of the ordinary gauge group and the Lorentz group.

Two conditions are needed. The Lorentz representation of every species must be continuous,
`GaugeFieldData.LorentzContinuous`, and the gauge and Lorentz representations of every species
must commute, `GaugeFieldData.GaugeLorentzCommute`. The second makes the two actions on the
covariant field algebra commute, so that together they form one representation
`repGaugeLorentz` of `G × SL(2,ℂ)`.

The construction is by generation, through the continuous families of
`PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.RepresentationTheory.Reynolds.ContinuousFamily`. A finite family of
vectors is a continuous family when each group element maps every vector of the family to a
combination of the family with coefficients depending continuously on the group element. The
span of a continuous family for both groups is a finite-dimensional subrepresentation on which
both groups act continuously. Each covariant generator lies in such a span.

- The field strength `∇_l F_μν^φ` with `l` of fixed length, over a basis of the adjoint index
  `φ`. The gauge group acts on `φ` through the adjoint representation, and the Lorentz group
  mixes the directions and the two indices by the Lorentz matrix.
- The covariant tower `∇_l ψ^φ` of a species with `l` of fixed length, over a basis of the value
  index `φ`. The gauge group acts on `φ` through the gauge representation, and the Lorentz group
  mixes the directions by the Lorentz matrix and acts on `φ` through the Lorentz representation.
  The same holds for the conjugate towers.

The scalars span a continuous family, sums of elements lie in the span of the union of their
families, and products in the span of the products of their families, since both groups act by
algebra maps. So every element of the covariant field algebra lies in the span of a continuous
family.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.commute_repValue_repLorentzGroup` : the gauge and Lorentz
  actions on the covariant field algebra commute.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.repGaugeLorentz` : the joint action of `G × SL(2,ℂ)`.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.exists_subrepresentation` : every covariant expression
  lies in a finite-dimensional subrepresentation of the joint action on which both groups act
  with continuous matrix coefficients.
- `GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.finiteSubrep` : a chosen such subrepresentation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The actions on the value space of a matter field
  - A.1. Continuity
  - A.2. Commutation
- B. The joint action of the gauge and Lorentz groups
- C. Continuity on the covariant towers
  - C.1. The Lorentz matrix
  - C.2. The field-strength tower
  - C.3. The matter towers
- D. Finite-dimensional stable subspaces

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.hasContinuousSpan_tower
declarations.doc:
A tower `t p x`, linear in `x`, on which the gauge group acts through an operator family with
continuous coefficients on `x`, and the Lorentz group through the Lorentz matrix on the
directions `p` and an operator family with continuous coefficients on `x`, has a continuous
span.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasContinuousSpan_tower (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible) {D : Type} [AddCommGroup D]
    [Module ℂ D] [FiniteDimensional ℂ D] {n : ℕ}
    (t : (Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → D →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalCovFieldAlgebra)
    {σ₁ : G.group → Module.End ℂ D} (hσ₁ : ContinuousCoeff σ₁)
    (h₁ : ∀ g p x, repValue T g (t p x) = t p (σ₁ g x))
    {σ₂ : SL(2,ℂ) → Module.End ℂ D} (hσ₂ : ContinuousCoeff σ₂)
    (h₂ : ∀ Λ p x, repLorentzGroup T hGL Λ (t p x) =
      ∑ p', (∏ k, L[Λ] (p' k) (p k)) • t p' (σ₂ Λ x))
    (l : Fin n → Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : D) :
    HasContinuousSpan (repValue T) (repLorentzGroup T hGL) (t l x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.hasContinuousSpan

Every element of the covariant field algebra lies in the span of a finite family on which

lemma hasContinuousSpan (hGL : T.GaugeLorentzCompatible) (hL : T.LorentzContinuous)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.LocalCovFieldAlgebra.exists_subrepresentation
declarations.doc:
Every element of the covariant field algebra lies in a finite-dimensional subrepresentation
for the joint action of the gauge and Lorentz groups, on which both groups act with continuous

      Representation.ContinuousMatrixCoeff (W.comp (MonoidHom.inr G.group SL(2,ℂ)))

modules.title: Reynolds elements for SL(2, ℂ)
modules.doc:
A continuous finite-dimensional representation of `SL(2, ℂ)` has a Reynolds element.

## i. Overview

Let `ρ` be a representation of `SL(2, ℂ)`, the double cover of the proper orthochronous Lorentz
group, and `W` a finite-dimensional subrepresentation on which `ρ` is continuous. We show that
`ρ` has a Reynolds element on `W`. This is an element of the group algebra whose coefficients sum
to one and which projects `W` onto its invariant vectors. Unlike for a compact group, there is no
Haar average, and the projection is built from Casimir operators instead.

The group `SL(2, ℂ)` is realized as the global gauge group `GlobalGaugeGroup.SL 2`, the closed
subgroup of `GL(2, ℂ)` of matrices of determinant one. The continuous representation on `W`
differentiates to a real Lie algebra representation `dρ`. We extend it to all `2 × 2` matrices
through their traceless part. Its holomorphic and antiholomorphic parts
`X_L = (dρ X - i dρ (i X)) / 2` and `X_R = (dρ X + i dρ (i X)) / 2` are two commuting complex
representations of `sl₂`, with `dρ X = X_L + X_R`.

Let `C_L` and `C_R` be the Casimirs of the two `sl₂` actions, and `q_L`, `q_R` polynomials with
constant term one such that `q_L(C_L)` and `q_R(C_R)` project onto the generalized kernels of the
Casimirs. Then `P = q_L(C_L) q_R(C_R)` maps `W` into the joint generalized kernel. There both
`sl₂` actions vanish, so `dρ` vanishes, and `P w` is fixed by every exponential `exp X`. These
generate `SL(2, ℂ)`, since every matrix of determinant one is a product of transvections and a
diagonal matrix of determinant one, each of which is an exponential of a traceless matrix.

The general mathematics used here lives in `PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.RepresentationTheory.Sl2`.
The generation by exponentials is in `Sl2.Exponential`, the holomorphic and antiholomorphic parts
in `Sl2.HolomorphicPart`, and the standard triple with its Casimir in `Sl2.Triple` and
`Sl2.Casimir`.

Finally `P` lies in `1 + span {ρ g - 1}`. The span of the operators `ρ g - 1` is closed under
products and, being finite-dimensional, closed. It therefore contains each `dρ X`, as the limit of
`(ρ (exp (t X)) - 1) / t`, and every polynomial in the `dρ X` without constant term. So `P` comes
from a Reynolds element.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.SL` : the global gauge group `SL(n, ℂ)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.SL.exists_sub_one_mem_span` : an operator in `1 + span {ρ g - 1}` with image
  in the invariants, for a continuous finite-dimensional representation of `SL(2, ℂ)`.
- `Representation.exists_isReynolds_of_specialLinearGroup` : a representation of `SL(2, ℂ)`
  continuous on a finite-dimensional subrepresentation has a Reynolds element on it.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The global gauge group SL(n, ℂ)
- B. The span of the operators ρ g - 1
  - B.1. Products and polynomials
  - B.2. Derivatives
- C. Representations of SL(2, ℂ)
  - C.1. The derivative on all matrices
  - C.2. Generation by exponentials
  - C.3. The projection onto the invariants
- D. Reynolds elements for SL(2, ℂ)

## iv. References

- B. C. Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, 2nd ed., Springer (2015).
- J. E. Humphreys, *Introduction to Lie Algebras and Representation Theory*.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.SL
declarations.doc: The global gauge group `SL(n, ℂ)`, the complex `n × n` matrices of determinant one.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_SL_iff
declarations.doc: An invertible matrix lies in `SL(n, ℂ)` exactly when it has determinant one.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_SL_iff {n : ℕ} {g : GL (Fin n) ℂ} :
    g ∈ (SL n).group ↔ (g : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ).det = 1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.mem_lieAlgebra_SL
declarations.doc: A traceless matrix is a generator of `SL(n, ℂ)`, since `det (exp (t X)) = exp (t tr X) = 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_lieAlgebra_SL {n : ℕ} {X : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ} (htr : X.trace = 0) :
    X ∈ (SL n).lieAlgebra

declarations.statement:

    X ∈ (SL n).lieSubalgebra

declarations.name: Submodule.mul_mem_span_sub_one
declarations.doc:
The span of `σ h - 1`, for a monoid homomorphism `σ` into an algebra, is closed under
multiplication, since `(σ g - 1) (σ h - 1) = (σ (g h) - 1) - (σ g - 1) - (σ h - 1)`.

In a subspace closed under multiplication, a polynomial in an element `x` of it differs from
its constant term by an element of it.

A closed subspace containing every difference `f t - f 0` contains the derivative of `f`

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep_mem_span

The derivative of a representation along a generator lies in the span of the operators

lemma derivRep_mem_span (X : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    derivRep ρ X ∈
      Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun g => ((ρ g : (W →L[ℂ] W)ˣ) : W →L[ℂ] W) - 1)

declarations.doc:

declarations.doc: The representation maps `exp X`, for a traceless `X`, to `exp (dρ X)`.

declarations.doc:
An induction principle for `SL(2, ℂ)`. A property of group elements which holds for every
exponential of a traceless matrix and is stable under products holds for every element.
declarations.statement:
lemma SL.induction {p : (SL 2).group → Prop}
    (hexp : ∀ (g : (SL 2).group) (X : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ), X.trace = 0 →
      ((g : GL (Fin 2) ℂ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ) = exp X → p g)
    (hmul : ∀ g h, p g → p h → p (g * h)) (g : (SL 2).group) : p g

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.SL.apply_eq_self_of_sl2
declarations.doc:
A vector killed by the holomorphic and antiholomorphic images of the standard `sl₂` triple is
invariant under the representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma SL.apply_eq_self_of_sl2 {w : E}
    (hL : ∀ X ∈ ({sl2E, sl2F, sl2H} : Set (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)),
      (SL.derivRepMatrix ρ).holPart X w = 0)
    (hR : ∀ X ∈ ({sl2E, sl2F, sl2H} : Set (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)),
      (SL.derivRepMatrix ρ).antiholPart X w = 0) (g : (SL 2).group) :
    ((ρ g : (E →L[ℂ] E)ˣ) : E →L[ℂ] E) w = w

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.SL.apply_eq_zero_of_mem_maxGenEigenspace
declarations.doc:
A vector in the generalized kernel of the Casimir of a map preserving brackets and real
multiples is killed by the images of the standard `sl₂` triple.
declarations.statement:
lemma SL.apply_eq_zero_of_mem_maxGenEigenspace {φ : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ → E →L[ℂ] E}
    (hlie : ∀ X Y, ⁅φ X, φ Y⁆ = φ ⁅X, Y⁆) (hsmul : ∀ (r : ℝ) X, φ ((r : ℂ) • X) = (r : ℂ) • φ X)
    {w : E} (hw : w ∈ Module.End.maxGenEigenspace (ψ (sl2Casimir φ)) 0) :
    ∀ X ∈ ({sl2E, sl2F, sl2H} : Set (Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℂ)), φ X w = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.SL.exists_sub_one_mem_span
declarations.doc:
A continuous finite-dimensional representation of `SL(2, ℂ)` has an operator in
`1 + span {ρ g - 1}` with image in the invariants, the product `q_L(C_L) q_R(C_R)` of the
projections onto the generalized kernels of the two Casimirs.
declarations.statement:
lemma SL.exists_sub_one_mem_span :
    ∃ P : E →L[ℂ] E,
      P - 1 ∈ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun g => ((ρ g : (E →L[ℂ] E)ˣ) : E →L[ℂ] E) - 1) ∧
      ∀ g v, ((ρ g : (E →L[ℂ] E)ˣ) : E →L[ℂ] E) (P v) = P v

modules.title: The field symbols of the local field algebra and their transformation laws
modules.doc:
The derivative symbols of the matter species as families in the local field algebra, with their
gauge and Lorentz laws.

## i. Overview

The generators of the local field algebra `J(T)` of a field datum are the derivative
symbols of its species. These are `∂_s ψ^φ`, indexed by a derivative multiset `s` and a covector `φ`
of the value space, the conjugate symbols `∂_s ψ̄^φ`, indexed by a covector of the
conjugate value space, and the gauge-field symbols `∂_s A_μ^φ` of the connection factor.
This file packages the matter symbols of each species as families over `s` and proves
their two transformation laws, the Leibniz convolution law for the jet gauge action and
`IsLorentzDerivTransforms` for the Lorentz action. The gauge-field symbols of `J(T)` are those
of the gauge-boson jet algebra carried in by the inclusion of the connection factor,
`GaugeFieldData.gaugeField`. The inclusion intertwines both actions, so they transform
as a gauge field under both, and the covariant derivative theory of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.CovariantDeriv`
applies inside `J(T)`.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.gaugeField` : the gauge-field symbols of `J(T)`.
- `GaugeFieldData.transformsAsGaugeField_gaugeField`,
  `GaugeFieldData.lorentzTransformsAsGaugeField_gaugeField` : their gauge and Lorentz laws.
- `GaugeFieldData.fermionSymbol`, `GaugeFieldData.conjFermionSymbol`,
  `GaugeFieldData.bosonSymbol`, `GaugeFieldData.conjBosonSymbol` : the matter symbols.
- `GaugeFieldData.repJet_fermionSymbol`,
  `GaugeFieldData.isLorentzDerivTransforms_fermionSymbol` and companions : their gauge
  and Lorentz laws.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The gauge-field symbols of the connection factor
- B. The matter symbol families
- C. The jet gauge transformation of the matter symbols
- D. The Lorentz transformation of the matter symbols

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The gauge-field symbols of the connection factor
## B. The matter symbol families

## C. The jet gauge transformation of the matter symbols

Each symbol map intertwines the jet gauge action on `J(T)` with `FieldDerivSpace.repDual`
on its half of the component space, and the law of the symbols is
`FieldDerivSpace.repDual_basis_tmul` pushed through the symbol map.

## D. The Lorentz transformation of the matter symbols

Each symbol map intertwines the Lorentz action on `J(T)` with the tensor product of the
action on derivative labels and the contragredient action on the value index, and the law
of the symbols is that of the derivative monomials,
`SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.repLorentzGroup_basis_ofFn`.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.gaugeField
declarations.doc:
The gauge-field symbols `∂_s A_μ^φ` of `J(T)`, the symbols of the gauge-boson jet algebra
carried in by the inclusion of the connection factor. The real structure on `J(T)` is the
one restricted from its complex structure, as for every family of symbols in a complex
algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gaugeField

declarations.statement:
lemma gaugeField_apply (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    T.gaugeField s μ φ = T.includeConnection (LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.gaugeField G s μ φ)

since the inclusion of the connection factor intertwines the two actions.
declarations.statement:
lemma transformsAsGaugeField_gaugeField :
    GaugeBoson.TransformsAsGaugeField G T.repJet T.gaugeField

declarations.statement:

The conjugate symbols of a fermionic species, as a linear map on the conjugate half of

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_fermionSymbolMap
declarations.doc: The unconjugated fermionic symbol map intertwines the jet gauge actions.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_fermionSymbolMap (i : T.FermionSpecies) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (x : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    T.repJet U (T.fermionSymbolMap i x)
      = T.fermionSymbolMap i
        (FieldDerivSpace.repDual (T.fermion i).repJet (T.fermion i).repJet_smul U x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_conjFermionSymbolMap
declarations.doc: The conjugate fermionic symbol map intertwines the jet gauge actions.
declarations.statement:

    T.repJet U (T.conjFermionSymbolMap i x)
      = T.conjFermionSymbolMap i
        (FieldDerivSpace.repDual (FieldDerivSpace.repConj (T.fermion i).repJet)
          (FieldDerivSpace.repConj_smul_comm (T.fermion i).repJet_smul) U x)

declarations.doc: The unconjugated bosonic symbol map intertwines the jet gauge actions.
declarations.statement:

    T.repJet U (T.bosonSymbolMap j x)
      = T.bosonSymbolMap j
        (FieldDerivSpace.repDual (T.boson j).repJet (T.boson j).repJet_smul U x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_conjBosonSymbolMap
declarations.doc: The conjugate bosonic symbol map intertwines the jet gauge actions.
declarations.statement:

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_fermionSymbol
declarations.doc:
The symbols of a fermionic species transform in the jet gauge representation of the
species, each derivative symbol by the Leibniz convolution of the dual base-point
coefficients against the lower symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_fermionSymbol (i : T.FermionSpecies) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    T.repJet U (T.fermionSymbol i s φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        T.fermionSymbol i p.2 (repDualCoeff (T.fermion i).repJet U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_conjFermionSymbol
declarations.doc:
The conjugate symbols of a fermionic species transform in the conjugate of the jet
gauge representation of the species.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_conjFermionSymbol (i : T.FermionSpecies) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    T.repJet U (T.conjFermionSymbol i s φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        T.conjFermionSymbol i p.2
          (repDualCoeff (FieldDerivSpace.repConj (T.fermion i).repJet) U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_bosonSymbol
declarations.doc:
The symbols of a bosonic species transform in the jet gauge representation of the
species.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_bosonSymbol (j : T.BosonSpecies) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)

    T.repJet U (T.bosonSymbol j s φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        T.bosonSymbol j p.2 (repDualCoeff (T.boson j).repJet U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repJet_conjBosonSymbol
declarations.doc:
The conjugate symbols of a bosonic species transform in the conjugate of the jet gauge

declarations.statement:

    T.repJet U (T.conjBosonSymbol j s φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        T.conjBosonSymbol j p.2
          (repDualCoeff (FieldDerivSpace.repConj (T.boson j).repJet) U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_fermionSymbolMap
declarations.doc: The unconjugated fermionic symbol map intertwines the Lorentz actions.
declarations.statement:
