modules.title: The total derivative on the local field algebra
modules.doc:
The formal total derivative `∂_μ` on the local field algebra of a field datum, its Leibniz
rule, its action on the symbols and its Lorentz covariance.

## i. Overview

The formal total derivative on the local field algebra of a field datum `T` is the sum of
the total derivatives of its three factors, each acting on its own tensor factor. On the two
matter factors it is the free-algebra derivation extending the derivative shift
`∂_s ψ_α ↦ ∂_{s + {μ}} ψ_α` of the generator space of the datum, an even derivation of the
exterior algebra on the fermionic side and an ordinary derivation of the symmetric algebra on
the bosonic side. On the connection factor it is the derivative of the complexified
gauge-boson algebra. It obeys the Leibniz rule, its components commute, and on each factor
it is that factor's own derivative.

On a matter symbol the total derivative appends the direction `μ` to the derivative label,
`∂_μ (∂_s ψ^φ) = ∂_{s + {μ}} ψ^φ`, so the symbol `∂_s ψ^φ` is the iterated total derivative
along `s` of the undifferentiated symbol. On the connection factor the iterated total
derivative is the iterated derivative of the gauge-boson algebra.

The total derivative is a Lorentz vector. The Lorentz action of the datum intertwines `∂_μ`
with `∑_a Λ_{a μ} ∂_a`. This is proved for the action written factor by factor, through the
covariance of the derivation extending a linear endomorphism on each free-algebra factor,
and transported to `T.repLorentzGroup`, which agrees with it.

The Leibniz rule, the commutation and the covariance are assembled from the factor facts
through abstract lemmas proved at small types and instantiated, which keeps the proofs
outside the full tensor product. The name `totalDeriv` distinguishes the derivative from the
`jetDeriv` on `V`-valued jets.

## ii. Key results

- `GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv` : the formal total derivative.
- `GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_mul` : the Leibniz rule.
- `GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_comm` : the total derivatives commute.
- `GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_includeFermionFactor`, `totalDeriv_includeBosonFactor`,
  `totalDeriv_includeConnection` : the restrictions to the three factors.
- `GaugeFieldData.iteratedD_includeConnection` : the iterated derivative on the connection
  factor.
- `GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_fermionSymbol`, `totalDeriv_bosonSymbol` and their conjugates :
  the total derivative appends a direction to the derivative label.
- `GaugeFieldData.iteratedD_fermionSymbol`, `iteratedD_bosonSymbol` and their conjugates :
  the iterated total derivative appends a multiset of directions.
- `GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_totalDeriv` : the total derivative is a Lorentz vector.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The formal total derivative
  - A.1. The action on the three factors
- B. The Leibniz rule
- C. Commutativity
- D. The iterated derivative on the connection factor
- E. The derivative shift on a component space
- F. The total derivative of the matter generators
- G. The total derivative of the matter symbols
- H. The iterated total derivative of the matter symbols
- I. Lorentz covariance
  - I.1. The factorwise action
  - I.2. Multiplicativity
  - I.3. The action on the three factors
  - I.4. The total derivative is a Lorentz vector for the factorwise action
  - I.5. Agreement with the generic action

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDerivFermionFactor
declarations.doc:
The total derivative on the fermionic factor, the even derivation of the exterior
algebra extending the derivative shift on the fermionic generator space of the datum.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev totalDerivFermionFactor (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ExteriorAlgebra ℂ T.FermionGenerators →ₗ[ℂ]
      ExteriorAlgebra ℂ T.FermionGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDerivBosonFactor
declarations.doc:
The total derivative on the bosonic factor, the derivation of the symmetric algebra
extending the derivative shift on the bosonic generator space of the datum.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable abbrev totalDerivBosonFactor (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    SymmetricAlgebra ℂ T.BosonGenerators →ₗ[ℂ]
      SymmetricAlgebra ℂ T.BosonGenerators

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv
declarations.doc:
The formal total derivative on the local field algebra, the sum of the total
derivatives of the three factors, each acting on its own factor.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def totalDeriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    T.LocalFieldAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] T.LocalFieldAlgebra

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_includeFermionFactor
declarations.doc:
The derivative acts on the fermionic factor through that factor's own derivation. The
factor inclusions are unfolded through the generic `GaugeFieldData` rules rather than by
`rfl`, since at a concrete datum the definitional unfolding of the units has to see
through the unexposed ring congruence of the symmetric algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_includeFermionFactor (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (f : ExteriorAlgebra ℂ T.FermionGenerators) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.includeFermion f)
      = T.includeFermion (T.totalDerivFermionFactor μ f)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_includeBosonFactor
declarations.doc: The derivative acts on the bosonic factor through that factor's own derivation.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_includeBosonFactor (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (h : SymmetricAlgebra ℂ T.BosonGenerators) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.includeBoson h)
      = T.includeBoson (T.totalDerivBosonFactor μ h)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
The derivative acts on the connection factor through the generic gauge-boson
derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_includeConnection (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] _root_.LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.includeConnection y)
      = T.includeConnection
          (_root_.LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexJetDeriv G μ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_mul
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule for the total derivative on the local field algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_mul (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x y : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (x * y) = T.totalDeriv μ x * y + x * T.totalDeriv μ y

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDerivFermionFactor_comm
declarations.doc: The total derivatives on the fermionic factor commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDerivFermionFactor_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.totalDerivFermionFactor μ).comp (T.totalDerivFermionFactor ν)
      = (T.totalDerivFermionFactor ν).comp (T.totalDerivFermionFactor μ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDerivBosonFactor_comm
declarations.doc: The total derivatives on the bosonic factor commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDerivBosonFactor_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.totalDerivBosonFactor μ).comp (T.totalDerivBosonFactor ν)
      = (T.totalDerivBosonFactor ν).comp (T.totalDerivBosonFactor μ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_comm
declarations.doc: The total derivatives on the local field algebra commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (T.totalDeriv μ).comp (T.totalDeriv ν) = (T.totalDeriv ν).comp (T.totalDeriv μ)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.iteratedD_includeConnection
declarations.doc:
The iterated total derivative acts on the connection factor through the gauge sector's
own iterated derivative. It instantiates the abstract `iteratedD_map` rather than running
the induction inside the local field algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_includeConnection (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (y : ℂ ⊗[ℝ] _root_.LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra G) :
    Lorentz.iteratedD T.totalDeriv T.totalDeriv_comm s (T.includeConnection y)
      = T.includeConnection (Lorentz.iteratedD
          (_root_.LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexJetDeriv G)
          _root_.LocalGaugeFieldAlgebra.complexJetDeriv_comm s y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_ιFermion
declarations.doc:
The total derivative of a fermionic generator is the generator of the shifted
component.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_ιFermion (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (x : FieldDerivSpace (T.fermion i)) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.ιFermion i x)
      = T.ιFermion i (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_ιBoson
declarations.doc:
The total derivative of a bosonic generator is the generator of the shifted
component.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_ιBoson (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (y : FieldDerivSpace (T.boson j)) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.ιBoson j y)
      = T.ιBoson j (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ y)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_fermionSymbol
declarations.doc:
The total derivative appends the direction `μ` to the derivative label of a fermionic
symbol, `∂_μ (∂_s ψ^φ) = ∂_{s + {μ}} ψ^φ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_fermionSymbol (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.fermionSymbol i s φ) = T.fermionSymbol i (μ ::ₘ s) φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_conjFermionSymbol
declarations.doc:
The total derivative appends the direction `μ` to the derivative label of a conjugate
fermionic symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_conjFermionSymbol (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.conjFermionSymbol i s φ)
      = T.conjFermionSymbol i (μ ::ₘ s) φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_bosonSymbol
declarations.doc:
The total derivative appends the direction `μ` to the derivative label of a bosonic
symbol, `∂_μ (∂_s φ) = ∂_{s + {μ}} φ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_bosonSymbol (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.bosonSymbol j s φ) = T.bosonSymbol j (μ ::ₘ s) φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.totalDeriv_conjBosonSymbol
declarations.doc:
The total derivative appends the direction `μ` to the derivative label of a conjugate
bosonic symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalDeriv_conjBosonSymbol (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (j : T.BosonSpecies)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))) :
    T.totalDeriv μ (T.conjBosonSymbol j s φ)
      = T.conjBosonSymbol j (μ ::ₘ s) φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.iteratedD_fermionSymbol
declarations.doc:
The iterated total derivative along `s` appends `s` to the derivative label of a
fermionic symbol. For `r = 0` it says that `∂_s ψ^φ` is the iterated total derivative of
the undifferentiated symbol `ψ^φ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_fermionSymbol (i : T.FermionSpecies) (s r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.FermionValue i)) :
    Lorentz.iteratedD T.totalDeriv T.totalDeriv_comm s (T.fermionSymbol i r φ)
      = T.fermionSymbol i (s + r) φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.iteratedD_conjFermionSymbol
declarations.doc:
The iterated total derivative along `s` appends `s` to the derivative label of a
conjugate fermionic symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_conjFermionSymbol (i : T.FermionSpecies)
    (s r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.FermionValue i))) :
    Lorentz.iteratedD T.totalDeriv T.totalDeriv_comm s (T.conjFermionSymbol i r φ)
      = T.conjFermionSymbol i (s + r) φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.iteratedD_bosonSymbol
declarations.doc:
The iterated total derivative along `s` appends `s` to the derivative label of a bosonic
symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_bosonSymbol (j : T.BosonSpecies) (s r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (T.BosonValue j)) :
    Lorentz.iteratedD T.totalDeriv T.totalDeriv_comm s (T.bosonSymbol j r φ)
      = T.bosonSymbol j (s + r) φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.iteratedD_conjBosonSymbol
declarations.doc:
The iterated total derivative along `s` appends `s` to the derivative label of a
conjugate bosonic symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedD_conjBosonSymbol (j : T.BosonSpecies) (s r : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (T.BosonValue j))) :
    Lorentz.iteratedD T.totalDeriv T.totalDeriv_comm s (T.conjBosonSymbol j r φ)
      = T.conjBosonSymbol j (s + r) φ

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.repLorentzGroup_totalDeriv
declarations.doc:
The total derivative is a Lorentz vector. The Lorentz action intertwines the total
derivative through the columns of the Lorentz matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentzGroup_totalDeriv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : T.LocalFieldAlgebra) :
    T.repLorentzGroup Λ (T.totalDeriv μ x) =
      ∑ a, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        T.totalDeriv a (T.repLorentzGroup Λ x)

declarations.name: GaugeFieldData.instIsLorentzDerivTotalDeriv
declarations.doc:
The total derivatives on the local field algebra form a Lorentz derivative for the
Lorentz action of the field datum.
declarations.statement: instance instIsLorentzDerivTotalDeriv : Lorentz.IsLorentzDeriv T.repLorentzGroup T.totalDeriv

modules.title: Matter fields of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
A matter field transforming under a continuous finite-dimensional representation of a global
gauge group.

## i. Overview

A matter field of a gauge theory with global gauge group `G` takes values in a
finite-dimensional complex vector space `V`, on which `G` acts through a continuous
representation `ρ : G → GL(V)` by invertible linear maps. Here `V` is a normed space, which
fixes its topology, the unique one of a finite-dimensional complex vector space, and makes the
linear maps `V →L[ℂ] V` a Banach algebra. Continuity is what lets `ρ` be differentiated to the
Lie algebra, in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.DerivRep`,
and extended to the jets of gauge transformations, in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.JetRep`.
As for any matter field, `V` also carries a representation of the Lorentz group, and the
field has a mass weight and a declared statistics.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField` : a matter field transforming under a continuous
  representation of a global gauge group.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Matter fields

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Matter fields

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField
declarations.doc:
A matter field transforming under a continuous representation of the global gauge group
`G`. It has a finite-dimensional complex normed target space `V`, the continuous
representation `rep : G → GL(V)` by invertible linear maps, the Lorentz representation on
`V`, the mass weight of the field (in the units in which a derivative has weight `2`), and
its declared statistics.
declarations.statement:
structure MatterField (G : GlobalGaugeGroup κ) where
  /-- The target space of the field. -/
  V : Type
  [instNormedAddCommGroup : NormedAddCommGroup V]
  [instNormedSpace : NormedSpace ℂ V]
  [instFiniteDimensional : FiniteDimensional ℂ V]
  /-- The continuous representation of the global gauge group on the target space. -/
  rep : G.group →ₜ* (V →L[ℂ] V)ˣ
  /-- The representation of the Lorentz group on the target space. -/
  repLorentz : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V
  /-- The mass weight of the field. -/
  massWeight : ℕ
  /-- The statistics the field is declared to obey, bosonic or fermionic. -/
  statistic : FieldStatistic

declarations.doc: The target space of a matter field is complete, being finite-dimensional.
declarations.statement: instance (G : GlobalGaugeGroup κ) (M : G.MatterField) : CompleteSpace M.V

modules.title: The covariant derivative of a matter family
modules.doc:
The covariant derivative tower of a family of matter symbols in an algebra of symbols.

## i. Overview

A matter field valued in a complex vector space `V` has derivative symbols `[∂_s ψ]`,
indexed by a multiset `s` of directions and contracted against the dual of `V`. This file
works with such families `F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B` in an
algebra of symbols `B`, together with a family `A` of gauge-field symbols `[∂_s A_μ]`.

Under a jet gauge transformation the value of `rep U` at a constant vector depends on the
spacetime point, so the derivative symbols see its Taylor coefficients at the base point.
These are `repCoeff rep U x`, and their transposes to the dual of `V` are
`repDualCoeff rep U x`, the analogue of `adjointDualCoeff` for a general representation.

The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = ∂_ρ F + A_ρ · F` needs the infinitesimal action
`act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V` of the gauge algebra on `V`, the physicists'
`i dρ(T^a)`. Here it is an argument. For a matter field it is the derivative of the group
representation, `MatterField.repAlgebra`. The derived action `A_ρ · F` is the Leibniz
convolution of the action of the gauge-field symbols on the matter symbols, and
`covDerivIter` iterates `∇` along an ordered tuple of directions.

The covariant tower and the plain derivative symbols generate the same algebra together with
the gauge-field symbols (the span lemma). The tower is natural under multiplicative linear maps
of the algebra and inherits mass weights and anticommutation from the bare family. That the
covariant derivative preserves the transformation law is proved in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.InfinitesimalAction`.

## ii. Key results

- `repDualCoeff` : the physicists' `∂_x (rep U)^i_j|₀` acting on the complex dual index of a
  matter-field symbol, the transpose of `repCoeff`
- `covDerivIter` : the iterated covariant derivative of a matter family
- `adjoin_symbols_eq_adjoin_covDerivIter` : the span lemma, and its membership form
  `apply_mem_of_covDerivIter_mem`
- `covDerivIter_map` : the covariant tower is natural in the algebra
- `covDerivIter_mem_massWeightEigenspace` : the covariant tower of a family of weight
  `c + 2 * |t|` has weight `c + 2 * n + 2 * |s|`
- `covDerivIter_mem_anticommuteSubmodule` : anything commuting with the gauge-field symbols and
  anticommuting with the bare family anticommutes with its covariant tower

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The dual representation coefficients and gauge tensors in a representation
- B. The covariant derivative through an infinitesimal action
- C. The span lemma
- D. Naturality in the algebra
- E. Mass weights and statistics of the tower

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The dual representation coefficients and gauge tensors in a representation

## B. The covariant derivative through an infinitesimal action

The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + A_ρ · F` requires the infinitesimal
action of the gauge algebra on the value space, the physicists' `i dρ(T^a)`. Here it is an
argument `act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V`, real-linear in the algebra slot (the
gauge algebra is a real Lie algebra) and complex-linear in the value slot, matching
the complex duals indexing the matter families. For a matter field it is
`MatterField.repAlgebra`, the derivative of the group representation.

## C. The span lemma

Replacing derivatives of a matter family by covariant derivatives does not change
the generated algebra of symbols: the correction terms are products of gauge-field
components with matter components. Note the statement is about generated
*subalgebras*, not linear spans — `∇_ρ F − ∂_ρ F` is a sum of products `A · F`,
which lies in the algebra generated by the symbols but not in their linear span.

## D. Naturality in the algebra

The matter analogue of `bracketFam_map` and `iteratedCovDerivAdjoint_map`: a
multiplicative linear map into another algebra carries the derived action, and hence
the whole covariant matter tower, to the tower of the image families. The derived
action is a finite sum of products of components, so only multiplicativity is needed;
no derivative operator on the target is involved.

## E. Mass weights and statistics of the tower

Each term of a covariant tower is a product of gauge-field symbols with a single bare symbol
of the family, so a property of the bare family that is a submodule and is stable under
multiplication by the gauge-field symbols passes to the tower. Two such properties matter:
the mass weight, and anticommutation with a fixed element.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficient of the representation. It includes the constant
vector into `V`-valued jets, acts by `rep U`, differentiates `x` times and evaluates at
the base point. The composite is the physicists' `∂_x (rep U)^i_j|₀` as a ℂ-linear map on
the value space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repCoeff (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : V →ₗ[ℂ] V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repDualCoeff
declarations.doc:
The physicists' `∂_x (rep U)^i_j|₀` acting on the complex dual index of a
matter-field symbol, the transpose of `repCoeff`. This is the analogue of
`adjointDualCoeff` for a general representation of the jet gauge group; for `x = 0`
it is the dual (contragredient) action of the value of `U`, and for `x ≠ 0` it sees
the derivatives of the gauge transformation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repDualCoeff (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.jetEval_rep_of_smul
declarations.doc:
For a fibrewise representation, evaluating the transform of a jet at the base point
is the zeroth Taylor coefficient of the transform of its base-point value. The jet
ring factor passes through the action and is then evaluated.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_rep_of_smul (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V), rep U
        (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    jetEval (rep U z) = repCoeff rep U 0 (jetEval z)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff_zero_mul
declarations.doc:
The zeroth Taylor coefficients of a fibrewise representation are multiplicative, so they
form a representation of the jet gauge group on the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_zero_mul (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V), rep U
        (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U W : G.gaugeJetGroup) : repCoeff rep (U * W) 0 = repCoeff rep U 0 ∘ₗ repCoeff rep W 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.tensorAction
declarations.doc:
The action of an adjoint-valued field on a matter field at the tensor level. It is
multiplication in `B` on the first factors and the ℂ-linear infinitesimal action `act`
of the gauge algebra on `V` on the second factors, so that on pure tensors
`(b₁ ⊗ c) · (b₂ ⊗ v) = (b₁ b₂) ⊗ act c v`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def tensorAction (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) :
    (B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) →ₗ[ℝ] (B ⊗[ℂ] V) →ₗ[ℂ] B ⊗[ℂ] V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.tensorAction_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorAction_tmul (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (b₁ b₂ : B)
    (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (v : V) :
    tensorAction act (b₁ ⊗ₜ[ℝ] c) (b₂ ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = (b₁ * b₂) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] act c v

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.tensorAction_map_left
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorAction_map_left (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (Φ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hΦ : ∀ b₁ b₂, Φ (b₁ * b₂) = Φ b₁ * Φ b₂) (s : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra)
    (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    tensorAction act ((TensorProduct.map (Φ.restrictScalars ℝ) LinearMap.id) s)
        ((TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) t) =
      (TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) (tensorAction act s t)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.tensorAction_one_left
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorAction_one_left (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (c : G.lieSubalgebra)
    (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    tensorAction act ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] c) t =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (act c)) t

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.tensorAction_map_right_antidiagonal
declarations.doc:
`tensorAction` under an antidiagonal pair of transport families. If the
`V`-transports intertwine `act` with the `G.lieSubalgebra`-transports as an
antidiagonal convolution, so do `id ⊗ ·` over `tensorAction`.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorAction_map_right_antidiagonal (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (Tg : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra)
    (Tv : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (hT : ∀ (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (w : V), Tv x (act c w) =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p => act (Tg p.1 c) (Tv p.2 w)).sum)
    (s : B ⊗[ℝ] G.lieSubalgebra) (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    (x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      tensorAction act ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Tg p.1)) s)
        ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Tv p.2)) t)).sum =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Tv x)) (tensorAction act s t)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.dualPairEquivC
declarations.doc:
The canonical equivalence between matter fields `B ⊗[ℂ] V` and their component
families `φ ↦ F^φ` over the complex dual — `dualPairEquiv` for a general
finite-dimensional complex value space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def dualPairEquivC : (B ⊗[ℂ] V) ≃ₗ[ℂ] (Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.dualPairEquivC_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquivC_tmul (b : B) (v : V) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    dualPairEquivC (b ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) φ = φ v • b

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.dualPairEquivC_map_left
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquivC_map_left (Φ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B) (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    dualPairEquivC ((TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) t) φ =
      Φ (dualPairEquivC t φ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.dualPairEquivC_map_right
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquivC_map_right (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (t : B ⊗[ℂ] V)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    dualPairEquivC ((TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id T) t) φ =
      dualPairEquivC t (T.dualMap φ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symm_comp_left_C
declarations.statement:
lemma symm_comp_left_C (Φ : B →ₗ[ℂ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    dualPairEquivC.symm (Φ ∘ₗ g) =
      (TensorProduct.map Φ LinearMap.id) (dualPairEquivC.symm g)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.symm_comp_right_C
declarations.statement:
lemma symm_comp_right_C (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    dualPairEquivC.symm (g ∘ₗ T.dualMap) =
      (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id T) (dualPairEquivC.symm g)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam
declarations.doc:
The action of an adjoint-indexed component family on a matter one, through the
infinitesimal action `act`. Both are assembled into fields, acted on by `tensorAction`
and read back out as components. This is the physicists' `f^a (T_a)^i_j g^j` with `T = act`,
basis-free.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionFam (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_add_left
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_add_left (f₁ f₂ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act (f₁ + f₂) g = actionFam act f₁ g + actionFam act f₂ g

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_add_right
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_add_right (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (g₁ g₂ : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act f (g₁ + g₂) = actionFam act f g₁ + actionFam act f g₂

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_zero_left
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_zero_left (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act 0 g = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_zero_right
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_zero_right (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    actionFam act f 0 = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_sum_left
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_sum_left (S : Multiset (Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B))
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act S.sum g = (S.map fun f => actionFam act f g).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_sum_right
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_sum_right (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (S : Multiset (Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)) :
    actionFam act f S.sum = (S.map fun g => actionFam act f g).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repGauge_actionFam
declarations.doc:
The gauge transformation of the action of an affinely-transforming
adjoint-indexed family on a linearly-transforming matter family. It is the action of the
transformed families plus one `act`-type cross term. This is `GaugeBoson.repGauge_bracketFam`
with a homogeneous second slot and the bracket replaced by a general action. Only the
multiplicativity of the action of `U` is used.
declarations.statement:
lemma repGauge_actionFam
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (hmul : ∀ b₁ b₂ : B, repGauge U (b₁ * b₂) = repGauge U b₁ * repGauge U b₂)
    {f f' : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B}
    {g g' : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B} {cf : G.lieSubalgebra}
    (hf : ∀ ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra,
      repGauge U (f ψ) = f' ψ + algebraMap ℂ B (ψ cf))
    (hg : ∀ ψ : Module.Dual ℂ V, repGauge U (g ψ) = g' ψ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U (actionFam act f g φ) =
      actionFam act f' g' φ + g' (φ ∘ₗ act cf)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFamConv
declarations.doc:
The derived action family `A_ρ · F`, the `s`-derivative of the action of the
gauge field on a matter family, given by the Leibniz convolution of the derivative
symbols over the multiset antidiagonal — the matter analogue of `GaugeBoson.bracketFamConv`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionFamConv
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivAction
declarations.doc:
The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + A_ρ · F` of a matter family of
derivative symbols, in the single direction `ρ`, the extra derivative on the symbol
plus the derived action of the gauge field on the value index. With the physicists'
factor of `i` absorbed into `act` (as it is in the gauge-algebra bracket), this is
`∂_ρ F + i A_ρ^a T_a F` in the `D = ∂ + i A` convention.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def covDerivAction
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivAction_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivAction_apply
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    covDerivAction A act F ρ s φ = F (ρ ::ₘ s) φ + actionFamConv A act ρ F s φ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
The iterated covariant derivative `∇_{l 0} ⋯ ∇_{l (n-1)} F` of a matter family
along an ordered tuple of directions. Covariant derivatives do not commute (their
commutator is the action of the field strength), so the iteration is order-dependent
and indexed by `(n : ℕ)` and `l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)`. The result is again a
family of derivative symbols; the physical iterated covariant derivative is its
value at the empty multiset.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def covDerivIter
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    (n : ℕ) → (Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) →
      Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_zero (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (l : Fin 0 → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivIter A act F 0 l = F

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_succ (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n + 1) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivIter A act F (n + 1) l =
      covDerivAction A act (covDerivIter A act F n fun i => l i.succ) (l 0)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.dualPairEquiv_symm_eq_sum
declarations.doc:
Decomposition of an assembled adjoint-indexed family along a basis of the gauge
algebra, as the components against the dual basis, tensored with the basis vectors.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquiv_symm_eq_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (bW : Module.Basis ι ℝ G.lieSubalgebra)
    (g : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) :
    dualPairEquiv.symm g = ∑ i, g (bW.coord i) ⊗ₜ[ℝ] bW i

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.dualPairEquivC_symm_eq_sum
declarations.doc: Decomposition of an assembled matter family along a basis of the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma dualPairEquivC_symm_eq_sum {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (bW : Module.Basis ι ℂ V)
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    dualPairEquivC.symm g = ∑ i, g (bW.coord i) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] bW i

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_apply_mem
declarations.doc:
The value of an action of families lies in any subalgebra containing the values
of both families, since the action is a finite sum of products of components.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter_succ_sub
declarations.doc:
One step of the unitriangular expansion. The difference between a covariant symbol with
`n + 1` directions and the plain symbol of the same total order is the difference one step
lower plus the derived action of the gauge field on the lower tower.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_succ_sub (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    {n : ℕ} (l : Fin (n + 1) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    covDerivIter A act F (n + 1) l s φ - F (List.ofFn l + s) φ =
      (covDerivIter A act F n (fun i => l i.succ) (l 0 ::ₘ s) φ -
          F (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => l i.succ) + (l 0 ::ₘ s)) φ) +
        actionFamConv A act (l 0) (covDerivIter A act F n fun i => l i.succ) s φ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter_sub_mem
declarations.doc:
Unitriangularity of the covariant matter tower. The covariant and plain
derivative symbols of a matter family differ by an element of the subalgebra
generated by the gauge-field symbols and the strictly lower-order matter symbols.
Stated at every derivative multiset `s`, as needed for the induction.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_sub_mem (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    covDerivIter A act F n l s φ - F (List.ofFn l + s) φ ∈
      Algebra.adjoin ℂ
        ({b : B | ∃ (u : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
            (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), b = A u μ ψ} ∪
          {b : B | ∃ (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (χ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
            t.card < n + s.card ∧ b = F t χ})

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter_mem_adjoin_symbols
declarations.doc:
Every derivative symbol of the covariant tower is a polynomial in the gauge-field
symbols and the matter symbols.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_mem_adjoin_symbols (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    covDerivIter A act F n l s φ ∈ Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      ({b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
          (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), b = A s μ ψ} ∪
        {b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
          b = F s φ})

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.adjoin_symbols_eq_adjoin_covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
The span lemma. The algebra of symbols generated by the gauge field together
with a matter family's derivative symbols equals the one generated by the gauge
field together with the matter family's covariant derivative tower. The
correction `∇_ρ − ∂_ρ` is the derived action of the gauge field — a sum of products
of symbols, absorbed by the algebra structure.
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoin_symbols_eq_adjoin_covDerivIter (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      ({b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
          (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), b = A s μ ψ} ∪
        {b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
          b = F s φ}) =
    Algebra.adjoin ℂ
      ({b : B | ∃ (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
          (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), b = A s μ ψ} ∪
        {b : B | ∃ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
          b = covDerivIter A act F n l 0 φ})

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.apply_mem_of_covDerivIter_mem
declarations.doc:
A derivative symbol of a matter family lies in every subalgebra containing the gauge-field
symbols and the covariant tower of the family. This is the span lemma
`adjoin_symbols_eq_adjoin_covDerivIter` read as a membership statement.
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_mem_of_covDerivIter_mem (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) {P : Subalgebra ℂ B}
    (hA : ∀ s μ ψ, A s μ ψ ∈ P)
    (hF : ∀ n (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) φ, covDerivIter A act F n l 0 φ ∈ P)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) : F s φ ∈ P

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_map
declarations.doc:
The action of an adjoint-indexed family on a matter family is natural in the
algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_map (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) :
    actionFam act (Φ.restrictScalars ℝ ∘ₗ f) (Φ ∘ₗ g) = Φ ∘ₗ actionFam act f g

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFamConv_map
declarations.doc: The derived action family is natural in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFamConv_map
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    actionFamConv (fun p σ => Φ.restrictScalars ℝ ∘ₗ A p σ) act ρ (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) s
      = Φ ∘ₗ actionFamConv A act ρ F s

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivAction_map
declarations.doc: The covariant derivative of a matter family is natural in the algebra.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivAction_map
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivAction (fun p σ => Φ.restrictScalars ℝ ∘ₗ A p σ) act (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) ρ s
      = Φ ∘ₗ covDerivAction A act F ρ s

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter_map
declarations.doc:
The iterated covariant derivative of a matter family is natural in the algebra. The
image of the tower is the tower of the image families, at every ordered tuple of
directions and every derivative multiset.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_map
    (A : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    covDerivIter (fun p σ => Φ.restrictScalars ℝ ∘ₗ A p σ) act (fun p => Φ ∘ₗ F p) n l
      = fun s => Φ ∘ₗ covDerivIter A act F n l s

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_apply_mem_submodule
declarations.doc:
The action pairing of two families lands in any submodule containing the products of
their components, since expanded in bases it is a finite sum of scalar multiples of them.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter_mem_massWeightEigenspace
declarations.doc:
The mass weight of a matter covariant tower. If the gauge-field symbols `∂_p A_μ` have
weight `2 * (1 + |p|)` and the bare family has weight `c + 2 * |t|` at the derivative
multiset `t`, then the `n`-fold covariant derivative has weight `c + 2 * n + 2 * |s|` at
`s`. Each covariant derivative costs two units, whether it lands on the derivative index or
brings down a gauge-field factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_mem_massWeightEigenspace (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) (P : B →ₐ[ℂ] Polynomial B)
    (c : ℕ)
    (hA : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra),
      A p μ ψ ∈ massWeightEigenspace P (2 * (1 + Multiset.card p)))
    (hF : ∀ (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (χ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
      F t χ ∈ massWeightEigenspace P (c + 2 * Multiset.card t))
    {n : ℕ} (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    covDerivIter A act F n l s φ ∈ massWeightEigenspace P (c + 2 * n + 2 * Multiset.card s)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter_mem_anticommuteSubmodule
declarations.doc:
Anything commuting with every gauge-field symbol and anticommuting with every bare symbol
of the family anticommutes with every symbol of its covariant tower, since each term of the
tower is a product of gauge-field symbols with a single bare symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma covDerivIter_mem_anticommuteSubmodule (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) {x : B}
    (hxA : ∀ (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
      (ψ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra), Commute x (A p μ ψ))
    (hxF : ∀ (t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (χ : Module.Dual ℂ V),
      F t χ ∈ anticommuteSubmodule x) :
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
      (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V), covDerivIter A act F n l s φ ∈ anticommuteSubmodule x

modules.title: The derivative of a representation of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
A continuous representation `ρ : G → GL(W)` of a global gauge group differentiates to a
representation `dρ` of its Lie algebra by linear maps on `W`.

## i. Overview

A continuous representation `ρ` of the global gauge group `G` on a finite-dimensional complex
normed space `W` is differentiated to the corresponding representation of the Lie algebra, which
is how gauge fields act on matter. For a generator `X` of `G` this is the derivative
`dρ(X) = d/dt ρ (exp (t X))` at `t = 0`, a linear map on `W`. The matter field `M` of a gauge
theory carries such a representation `M.rep`, and its Lie algebra representation is the
derivative of `M.rep`.

The linear maps `W →L[ℂ] W` form a Banach algebra, and the image `t ↦ ρ (exp (t X))` of a
one-parameter subgroup is a continuous one-parameter subgroup of it. So it is
`t ↦ exp (t dρ(X))`, by `OneParameterSubgroup.apply_eq_exp_smul_deriv`, and `dρ(X)` is the
only linear map with this property, by `OneParameterSubgroup.generator_unique`. The map `dρ`
is a homomorphism of Lie algebras.

* It is real-linear. Compatibility with scalars is a reparametrisation of `t`, and
  additivity follows by applying `ρ` to the Lie product formula
  `exp (t (X + Y)) = lim (exp (t X / n) exp (t Y / n)) ^ n`.
* It intertwines the adjoint actions, `dρ(g X g⁻¹) = ρ(g) dρ(X) ρ(g)⁻¹`, since `ρ` maps
  the one-parameter subgroup of `g X g⁻¹` to the conjugate of that of `X`.
* It preserves the commutator. With `g = exp (s X)`, the intertwining property reads
  `dρ(exp (s X) Y exp (−s X)) = exp (s dρ(X)) dρ(Y) exp (−s dρ(X))`. Both sides are
  differentiable in `s`, `dρ` being linear on a finite-dimensional space. Their derivatives
  at `s = 0` are `dρ(X Y − Y X)` and `dρ(X) dρ(Y) − dρ(Y) dρ(X)`.

The one-parameter subgroups `GlobalGaugeGroup.oneParameterSubgroup` and the adjoint action
`GlobalGaugeGroup.adjoint` of `G` are set up in the `LieAlgebra` directory.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRepFun` : the derivative `dρ(X)` of a representation along a
  generator.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep` : the Lie algebra representation.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.apply_eq_exp_derivRep` : `ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t dρ(X))`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep_eq_of` : `dρ(X)` is the unique linear map with this property.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep_adjoint` : `dρ` intertwines the adjoint actions.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.commute_derivRep` : a linear map commuting with `ρ` commutes with `dρ`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRep` : the Lie algebra representation of a matter
  field, the derivative of its representation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The derivative of a representation along a generator
- B. Linearity
- C. The adjoint action and the commutator
- D. The Lie algebra representation
- E. Matter fields

## iv. References

* B. C. Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, 2nd ed., Springer (2015).

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.instCompleteSpaceW
declarations.doc: A finite-dimensional complex normed space is complete.
declarations.statement: local instance instCompleteSpaceW : CompleteSpace W

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRepFun
declarations.doc:
The derivative `dρ(X) = d/dt ρ (exp (t X))` at `t = 0` of the representation along a
generator `X` of the global gauge group, a linear map on the target space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivRepFun (X : G.lieAlgebra) : W →L[ℂ] W

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep_oneParameterSubgroup
declarations.doc:
The representation maps the one-parameter subgroup of a generator `X` to that of its
derivative `dρ(X)`, `ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t dρ(X))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivRep_oneParameterSubgroup (X : G.lieAlgebra) (t : ℝ) :
    ((ρ (G.oneParameterSubgroup X t) : (W →L[ℂ] W)ˣ) : W →L[ℂ] W) =
      exp (t • derivRepFun ρ X)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep_oneParameterSubgroup_inv
declarations.doc: The inverse of the image of a one-parameter subgroup, `ρ (exp (t X))⁻¹ = exp (−t dρ(X))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivRep_oneParameterSubgroup_inv (X : G.lieAlgebra) (t : ℝ) :
    (↑(ρ (G.oneParameterSubgroup X t) : (W →L[ℂ] W)ˣ)⁻¹ : W →L[ℂ] W) =
      exp (t • -derivRepFun ρ X)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRepFun_eq
declarations.doc:
The derivative `dρ(X)` is the unique linear map `Z` with `ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t Z)` for
all `t`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRepFun_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma derivRepFun_smul (r : ℝ) (X : G.lieAlgebra) :
    derivRepFun ρ (r • X) = r • derivRepFun ρ X

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRepFun_add
declarations.doc:
The derivative of a representation is additive. Applying the representation to the Lie
product formula for `exp (t (X + Y))` gives the Lie product formula for
`exp (t dρ(X) + t dρ(Y))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivRepFun_add (X Y : G.lieAlgebra) :
    derivRepFun ρ (X + Y) = derivRepFun ρ X + derivRepFun ρ Y

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRepLinear
declarations.doc: The derivative of the representation, as a real-linear map on the Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivRepLinear : G.lieAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] W →L[ℂ] W

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRepFun_adjoint
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the representation intertwines the adjoint actions,
`dρ(g X g⁻¹) = ρ(g) dρ(X) ρ(g)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivRepFun_adjoint (g : G.group) (X : G.lieAlgebra) :
    derivRepFun ρ (G.adjoint g X) =
      ((ρ g : (W →L[ℂ] W)ˣ) : W →L[ℂ] W) * derivRepFun ρ X *
        (↑(ρ g : (W →L[ℂ] W)ˣ)⁻¹ : W →L[ℂ] W)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRepFun_commutator
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the representation preserves the commutator. Differentiating the
intertwining property `dρ(exp (s X) Y exp (−s X)) = exp (s dρ(X)) dρ(Y) exp (−s dρ(X))` at
`s = 0` gives `dρ(X Y − Y X) = dρ(X) dρ(Y) − dρ(Y) dρ(X)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivRepFun_commutator (X Y : G.lieAlgebra) :
    derivRepFun ρ ⟨X.1 * Y.1 - Y.1 * X.1, commutator_mem_lieAlgebraOfIsClosed X.2 Y.2⟩ =
      derivRepFun ρ X * derivRepFun ρ Y -
        derivRepFun ρ Y * derivRepFun ρ X

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra representation `dρ : 𝔤 → 𝔤𝔩(W)` of the continuous representation
`ρ : G → GL(W)` of with `ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t dρ(X))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivRep : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ W →L[ℂ] W

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.apply_eq_exp_derivRep
declarations.doc:
The representation maps the one-parameter subgroup of a generator `X` to that of `dρ(X)`,
`ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t dρ(X))`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep_eq_of
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra representation at a generator `X` is the unique linear map `Z` with
`ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t Z)` for all `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivRep_eq_of {X : G.lieSubalgebra} {Z : W →L[ℂ] W}
    (hZ : ∀ (t : ℝ) (g : G.group),
      ((g : GeneralLinearGroup κ ℂ) : Matrix κ κ ℂ) = exp (t • (X : Matrix κ κ ℂ)) →
        ((ρ g : (W →L[ℂ] W)ˣ) : W →L[ℂ] W) = exp (t • Z)) :
    derivRep ρ X = Z

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep_adjoint
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra representation intertwines the adjoint actions,
`dρ(g X g⁻¹) = ρ(g) dρ(X) ρ(g)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivRep_adjoint (g : G.group) (X : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    derivRep ρ ⟨(g.1 : Matrix κ κ ℂ) * X * (↑g.1⁻¹ : Matrix κ κ ℂ),
      conj_mem_lieAlgebraOfIsClosed (hH := G.isClosed) g X.2⟩ =
      ((ρ g : (W →L[ℂ] W)ˣ) : W →L[ℂ] W) * derivRep ρ X *
        (↑(ρ g : (W →L[ℂ] W)ˣ)⁻¹ : W →L[ℂ] W)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.commute_derivRep
declarations.doc:
A linear map commuting with every `ρ(g)` commutes with every `dρ(X)`. Both
`exp (t dρ(X)) L` and `L exp (t dρ(X))` are the same function of `t`, and their derivatives at
`t = 0` are `dρ(X) L` and `L dρ(X)`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRepFun
declarations.doc:
The derivative `dρ(X) = d/dt ρ (exp (t X))` at `t = 0` of the representation of a matter
field along a generator `X` of the global gauge group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lieAlgebraRepFun (X : G.lieAlgebra) : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRepFun_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRepFun_smul (r : ℝ) (X : G.lieAlgebra) :
    lieAlgebraRepFun M (r • X) = r • lieAlgebraRepFun M X

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRepFun_add
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRepFun_add (X Y : G.lieAlgebra) :
    lieAlgebraRepFun M (X + Y) = lieAlgebraRepFun M X + lieAlgebraRepFun M Y

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRepLinear
declarations.doc: The derivative of the representation, as a real-linear map on the Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lieAlgebraRepLinear : G.lieAlgebra →ₗ[ℝ] M.V →L[ℂ] M.V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRepFun_adjoint
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the representation intertwines the adjoint actions,
`dρ(g X g⁻¹) = ρ(g) dρ(X) ρ(g)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRepFun_adjoint (g : G.group) (X : G.lieAlgebra) :
    lieAlgebraRepFun M (G.adjoint g X) =
      ((M.rep g : (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)ˣ) : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V) * lieAlgebraRepFun M X *
        (↑(M.rep g : (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)ˣ)⁻¹ : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRepFun_commutator
declarations.doc: The derivative of the representation preserves the commutator.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRepFun_commutator (X Y : G.lieAlgebra) :
    lieAlgebraRepFun M ⟨X.1 * Y.1 - Y.1 * X.1, commutator_mem_lieAlgebraOfIsClosed X.2 Y.2⟩ =
      lieAlgebraRepFun M X * lieAlgebraRepFun M Y -
        lieAlgebraRepFun M Y * lieAlgebraRepFun M X

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRep
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra representation `dρ : 𝔤 → 𝔤𝔩(V)` of the continuous representation
`ρ : G → GL(V)` of a matter field, with `ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t dρ(X))`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def lieAlgebraRep : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ⁅ℝ⁆ M.V →L[ℂ] M.V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.rep_eq_exp_lieAlgebraRep
declarations.doc:
The representation maps the one-parameter subgroup of a generator `X` to that of `dρ(X)`,
`ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t dρ(X))`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRep_eq_of
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra representation at a generator `X` is the unique linear map `Z` with
`ρ (exp (t X)) = exp (t Z)` for all `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRep_eq_of {X : G.lieSubalgebra} {Z : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V}
    (hZ : ∀ (t : ℝ) (g : G.group),
      ((g : GeneralLinearGroup κ ℂ) : Matrix κ κ ℂ) = exp (t • (X : Matrix κ κ ℂ)) →
        ((M.rep g : (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)ˣ) : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V) = exp (t • Z)) :
    lieAlgebraRep M X = Z

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.commute_lieAlgebraRep
declarations.doc:
A linear map commuting with the representation of every group element commutes with the
Lie algebra representation.

modules.title: The field-derivative space of a matter field
modules.doc:
The span of the derivative symbols of a matter field and their conjugates, with its Lorentz
action, jet derivative and mass-weight scaling.

## i. Overview

For a matter field valued in a complex vector space `V`, the field-derivative space is the span
of the derivative symbols `∂_s ψ_α` and their conjugates `∂_s ψ̄_α`, the local coordinate
functions on the space of jets of the field. This file defines that space and the structure on
it that does not involve a gauge group. This is the Lorentz action, the jet derivative,
functoriality in `V` and the mass-weight scaling. The action of the gauge group is in
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.FieldDerivSpace.GaugeAction`.

## ii. Key results

- `FieldDerivSpace` : the space of component functions of the matter field `M`, the span of the
  symbols `∂_s ψ_α` and their conjugates `∂_s ψ̄_α`, where `α` runs over the target space `M.V`
- `FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup` : the Lorentz action on the field-derivative space
- `FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv` : the derivative of components in the field-derivative space, in the
  direction `μ`, the shift `∂_s ψ_α ↦ ∂_{s + {μ}} ψ_α` of the derivative label, and likewise on the
  conjugate components
- `FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_comm` : total derivatives commute
- `FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_jetDeriv` : the jet derivative is a Lorentz vector on the
  component space
- `FieldDerivSpace.comap` : the component space is contravariant in the target space
- `FieldDerivSpace.comapEquiv` : a relabelling of the target space relabels the component
  functions
- `FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale` : the mass-weight scaling on the field-derivative space of a
  field of mass weight `w` (twice the mass dimension), scaling the generator `∂_s φ_α` and its
  conjugate by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, through the derivative-degree scaling
  `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.gradeScale` on the derivative label
- `FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_massWeightScale` : the mass-weight scaling is natural in the target
  space
- `FieldDerivSpace.fstPiEquiv` : the unconjugated half of the component space of a finite direct
  sum splits
- `FieldDerivSpace.sndPiEquiv` : the conjugate half of the component space of a finite direct sum
  splits, by the same argument applied to the conjugate modules, using that conjugation commutes
  with products

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lorentz action on the component space
- B. The jet derivative
- C. Lorentz covariance of the jet derivative
- D. Functoriality in the target space
- E. The mass-weight scaling
- F. The dual and the conjugate of a finite product

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Lorentz action on the component space
## B. The jet derivative
## C. Lorentz covariance of the jet derivative
## D. Functoriality in the target space

## E. The mass-weight scaling

The mass dimension is tracked multiplicatively, through a scaling action: for a field of
*mass weight* `w` — twice the mass dimension, kept integral so that fermions of dimension
`3/2` carry weight `3` — the generator `∂_s φ_α` scales by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, one factor
of `c ^ 2` per derivative. The scaling on the component space below lifts functorially to
the bosonic and fermionic algebras, where it defines their mass-dimension grading.

## F. The dual and the conjugate of a finite product

The component space of a direct sum of matter fields splits, and both halves split for the same two
reasons: the dual of a finite product is the product of the duals, and conjugation commutes with
products. Neither statement mentions a matter field, so both are recorded here, on a bare family of
modules; the splitting they add up to is
`GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.fieldDerivSpacePiEquiv`, downstream where
`GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi` is available. The index type must be finite — the dual of an
infinite product is strictly larger than the product of the duals, and `TensorProduct.piRight` is an
equivalence only in the finite case.

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace
declarations.doc:
The space of component functions of the matter field `M`, the span of the symbols
`∂_s ψ_α` and their conjugates `∂_s ψ̄_α`, where `α` runs over the target space `M.V`. The
first factor holds the unconjugated symbols, the second the conjugate ones; in each,
`SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ` carries the derivative label `s` and the dual factor the target
component `α`.

Only `M.V` enters the space itself; the field's Lorentz and gauge representations and its
mass weight enter the structure carried on it below. Taking the whole matter field rather
than its value space is what lets that structure be read off `M` instead of being supplied
by hand at each use.
declarations.statement: abbrev FieldDerivSpace (M : G.MatterField) : Type

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the field-derivative space. Under a Lorentz transformation a
matter field transforms as `ψ(x) ↦ ρ(Λ) ψ(Λ⁻¹ x)`, so a derivative symbol `∂_s ψ_α` is
acted on in both of its labels, the derivative multiset `s` by the Lorentz action on
covectors, extended to `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ`, and the target index `α` by the
contragredient of `ρ`.

Unlike the gauge action, this needs no fibrewise-linearity or finite-dimensionality
hypothesis. The two labels transform independently, so the action is simply a tensor
product of representations. The conjugate half is the same with `ρ` replaced by its
conjugate, the symbols `∂_s ψ̄_α` transforming by `star` of the spinor matrix.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup (M : G.MatterField) :
    Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) (FieldDerivSpace M)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_fst (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup M Λ x).1
      = (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.repLorentzGroup.tprod M.repLorentz.dual) Λ x.1

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_snd (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (x : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup M Λ x).2
      = (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.repLorentzGroup.tprod M.repLorentz.conj.dual) Λ x.2

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The derivative of components in the field-derivative space,
in the direction `μ`, the shift `∂_s ψ_α ↦ ∂_{s + {μ}} ψ_α` of the derivative label,
and likewise on the conjugate components.

This is right multiplication by the degree-one element `∂_μ` on the
`SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ` factor, leaving the target index untouched. It uses a basis of
the Lorentz covectors — that is what the index `μ` is — but no basis of `V`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    FieldDerivSpace M →ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace M

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_fst_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_fst_tmul (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ M.V)
    (y : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule M.V)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ (a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, y)).1
      = (a * SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_snd_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_snd_tmul (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ M.V)
    (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule M.V)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ (x, a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)).2
      = (a * SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_comm
declarations.doc:
Total derivatives commute. Mixed partials agree because the derivative labels
live in a *symmetric* algebra; no basis of `V` is involved.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv (M := M) μ).comp (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv ν)
      = (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv (M := M) ν).comp (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_fst (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (v : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ v).1
      = TensorProduct.map
        (LinearMap.mulRight ℂ (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))))
        LinearMap.id v.1

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv_snd (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (v : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ v).2
      = TensorProduct.map
        (LinearMap.mulRight ℂ (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis ({μ} : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))))
        LinearMap.id v.2

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The jet derivative is a Lorentz vector on the component space. Appending `∂_μ` and
then acting is acting and then appending the transformed `∂_μ`, which is a combination of
the `∂_a`. Both halves of the component space are covered by the same argument. The
derivative label lives in the first tensor factor, and what sits in the second factor —
`M.repLorentz.dual` or `M.repLorentz.conj.dual` — plays no role.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup_jetDeriv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (v : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup M Λ (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ v) =
      ∑ a, (((Lorentz.SL2C.toLorentzGroup Λ).1 a μ : ℝ) : ℂ) •
        FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv a (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup M Λ v)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap
declarations.doc:
The component space is contravariant in the target space. A linear map `f : M.V →ₗ N.V`
of target spaces pulls the component functions of the field `N` back to component
functions of the field `M`. A component function is a covector on the target, so it
transposes. The derivative label is untouched, and the conjugate half transposes the
conjugate of `f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.comap (f : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] N.V) :
    FieldDerivSpace N →ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace M

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_fst_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.comap_fst_tmul (f : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] N.V) (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ N.V) (y : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule N.V)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.comap f (a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, y)).1 = a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (φ ∘ₗ f)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_snd_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.comap_snd_tmul (f : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] N.V)
    (x : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ N.V) (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule N.V)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.comap f (x, a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)).2 = a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (φ ∘ₗ ConjModule.map f)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_id
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.comap_id :
    FieldDerivSpace.comap (LinearMap.id : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] M.V) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp
declarations.doc:
Functoriality. Pulling back along `g ∘ f` is pulling back along `g` and then along `f`.
The order reverses, as it must for a contravariant construction.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp {P : G.MatterField}
    (f : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] N.V) (g : N.V →ₗ[ℂ] P.V) :
    FieldDerivSpace.comap (g.comp f)
      = (FieldDerivSpace.comap f).comp (FieldDerivSpace.comap g)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comapEquiv
declarations.doc:
A relabelling of the target space relabels the component functions. An isomorphism
`e : M.V ≃ₗ N.V` of target spaces identifies the two component spaces, contravariantly, so the
component functions of the field `N` become those of the field `M`. This is
`comap` upgraded to an equivalence, the two directions being mutually inverse by
functoriality.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.comapEquiv (e : M.V ≃ₗ[ℂ] N.V) :
    FieldDerivSpace N ≃ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace M

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comapEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.comapEquiv_apply (e : M.V ≃ₗ[ℂ] N.V) (x : FieldDerivSpace N) :
    FieldDerivSpace.comapEquiv e x = FieldDerivSpace.comap e.toLinearMap x

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_repLorentzGroup
declarations.doc:
An equivariant map of target spaces gives an equivariant pullback. If `f : M.V →ₗ N.V`
intertwines the two Lorentz representations then `comap f` intertwines the induced actions on
the component spaces, in the opposite direction. Component functions are covectors, so
the unconjugated half transposes `f` against the contragredient action and the conjugate
half against its conjugate; both reduce to equivariance of `f` at `Λ⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_repLorentzGroup (f : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] N.V)
    (hf : ∀ Λ : SL(2,ℂ), f.comp (M.repLorentz Λ) = (N.repLorentz Λ).comp f)
    (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.comap f).comp (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup N Λ)
      = (FieldDerivSpace.repLorentzGroup M Λ).comp (FieldDerivSpace.comap f)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The pullback commutes with the jet derivative. The two act on different tensor
factors — the derivative label and the target index — so an inclusion of species is a map
of differential algebras.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.comap_jetDeriv (f : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] N.V) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.comap f).comp (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ)
      = (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ).comp (FieldDerivSpace.comap f)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling on the field-derivative space of a field of mass weight `w`
(twice the mass dimension). The generator `∂_s φ_α` and its conjugate are scaled by
`c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`, through the derivative-degree scaling `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.gradeScale`
on the derivative label.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (w : ℕ) (c : ℂ) :
    FieldDerivSpace M →ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace M

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_fst_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
On an unconjugated component function `∂_s φ_α` the mass-weight scaling is
multiplication by `c ^ (w + 2 |s|)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_fst_basis_tmul (w : ℕ) (c : ℂ)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ M.V)
    (y : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule M.V)) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale w c
        ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ, y) : FieldDerivSpace M)).1
      = c ^ (w + 2 * Multiset.card s) • (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_fst (w : ℕ) (c : ℂ) (v : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale w c v).1
      = c ^ w • TensorProduct.map
          (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.gradeScale (c ^ 2)).toLinearMap LinearMap.id v.1

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_snd (w : ℕ) (c : ℂ) (v : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale w c v).2
      = c ^ w • TensorProduct.map
          (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.gradeScale (c ^ 2)).toLinearMap LinearMap.id v.2

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_jetDeriv
declarations.doc:
The total derivative carries mass weight two on the component space. The scaling
intertwines the derivative shift up to a factor `c ^ 2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale_jetDeriv (w : ℕ) (c : ℂ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale (M := M) w c).comp (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ)
      = c ^ 2 • (FieldDerivSpace.jetDeriv μ).comp
          (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale w c)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_massWeightScale
declarations.doc:
The mass-weight scaling is natural in the target space. It commutes with every
pullback, acting as it does on the derivative label and not on the target index. So the
scaling cannot see which part of a target space a component function came from. In
`FieldDerivSpace (∀ i, V i)`, where a species enters through
`comap (LinearMap.proj i)`, every species is scaled by the same weight. This is why the
generator space of a multi-species theory, `GaugeFieldData.FermionGenerators`, records
the weights on a direct sum, one per species, rather than on a single component space of
the product.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_massWeightScale (f : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] N.V) (w : ℕ) (c : ℂ) :
    (FieldDerivSpace.comap f).comp (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale w c)
      = (FieldDerivSpace.massWeightScale w c).comp (FieldDerivSpace.comap f)

declarations.name: prodPiEquiv
declarations.doc:
A pair of families is the same thing as a family of pairs. This is the last step of
the splitting of a component space over a product of target spaces. The two halves split
separately into families, and this puts the two families back together index by index.
Everything is the identity on underlying data, so every law is `rfl`.
declarations.statement:
def prodPiEquiv {A B : ι → Type*} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (A i)] [∀ i, Module ℂ (A i)]
    [∀ i, AddCommGroup (B i)] [∀ i, Module ℂ (B i)] :
    ((∀ i, A i) × (∀ i, B i)) ≃ₗ[ℂ] ∀ i, (A i × B i)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.fstPiEquiv
declarations.doc:
The unconjugated half of the component space of a finite direct sum splits. The
symbols `∂_s ψ_α` of a `(∀ i, E i)`-valued field are the families, over the index, of
the symbols of the summands, since the dual distributes over the finite product and the
derivative label is untouched.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.fstPiEquiv :
    (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (∀ i, E i))
      ≃ₗ[ℂ] ∀ i, SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (E i)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.fstPiEquiv_tmul
declarations.doc:
On a pure symbol the splitting restricts the target index to one summand. The
component `∂_s ψ_α` of the direct sum in the summand `i` is `∂_s` of the covector `φ`
precomposed with the inclusion of that summand.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.fstPiEquiv_tmul (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ (∀ i, E i)) (i : ι) :
    fstPiEquiv E (a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ) i = a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (φ ∘ₗ LinearMap.single ℂ E i)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.sndPiEquiv
declarations.doc:
The conjugate half of the component space of a finite direct sum splits, by the
same argument applied to the conjugate modules, using that conjugation commutes with
products.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def FieldDerivSpace.sndPiEquiv :
    (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (∀ i, E i)))
      ≃ₗ[ℂ] ∀ i, SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (E i))

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.sndPiEquiv_tmul
declarations.doc:
On a pure conjugate symbol the splitting again restricts the target index to one
summand, the inclusion being read through the conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.sndPiEquiv_tmul (a : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ)
    (ψ : Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (∀ i, E i))) (i : ι) :
    sndPiEquiv E (a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] ψ) i
      = a ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (ψ ∘ₗ ConjModule.map (k := ℂ) (LinearMap.single ℂ E i))

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.fstPiEquiv_symm_single
declarations.doc:
The splitting sends the family supported on one summand back to the pullback along
the projection onto that summand. A component function of the summand `i`, read as a
component function of the whole, is `φ ∘ proj i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.fstPiEquiv_symm_single (i : ι)
    (z : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (E i)) :
    (fstPiEquiv E).symm (Pi.single i z)
      = TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Module.Dual.transpose (LinearMap.proj i)) z

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.sndPiEquiv_symm_single
declarations.doc:
The conjugate half of the splitting behaves in the same way, the projection read
through the conjugation.
declarations.statement:
lemma FieldDerivSpace.sndPiEquiv_symm_single (i : ι)
    (z : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule (E i))) :
    (sndPiEquiv E).symm (Pi.single i z)
      = TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id
          (Module.Dual.transpose (ConjModule.map (k := ℂ) (LinearMap.proj i))) z

modules.title: The gauge action on the field-derivative space
modules.doc:
The action of gauge jets on the derivative symbols of a matter field and their conjugates.

## i. Overview

For a matter field valued in `V` with an action `rep` of the jet gauge group
`G.gaugeJetGroup` on its jets `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V`, this file constructs the induced
action of `G.gaugeJetGroup` on the field-derivative space. The construction needs two
hypotheses on `rep`.

* It is fibrewise, `rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z`. A gauge transformation acts on the values
  of the field over the identity on spacetime. This makes the induced action local (a finite
  Leibniz convolution) and makes `rep` determined by its restriction to constant jets.
* The value space `V` is finite-dimensional, so that this restriction is a matrix of power
  series, the coefficient `FieldDerivSpace.jetCoeff rep U` in `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V`.

The coefficient, its multiplicativity and the conjugate action `FieldDerivSpace.repConj` are
set up in `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalFieldAlgebra.JetRep`. Here a
coefficient acts on the symbols by `symbolAction`, the induced action on the unconjugated
symbols is `repDual`, and the action on the whole field-derivative space of a matter field,
conjugate symbols included, is `repJet`. All of these are natural in the value space.

## ii. Key results

- `FieldDerivSpace.symbolAction` : the action of a coefficient on the symbols.
- `FieldDerivSpace.symbolAction_one_tmul` : a coefficient acts on the undifferentiated symbol
  through its value at the base point.
- `FieldDerivSpace.repDual` : the gauge action on the symbols.
- `FieldDerivSpace.repJet` : the gauge action on the field-derivative space of a matter field.
- `FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_repDual`, `FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_repJet` : both actions are
  natural in the value space.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of a coefficient on the symbols
- B. The gauge action on the field-derivative space
- C. Naturality in the value space

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The action of a coefficient on the symbols
## B. The gauge action on the field-derivative space

## C. Naturality in the value space

A component function is a covector on the value space, so a linear map `f : V →ₗ W` of
value spaces pulls the symbols of a `W`-valued field back to those of a `V`-valued field.
If `f` intertwines two fibrewise jet actions then that pullback is equivariant, in the
opposite direction. This is the gauge counterpart of
`FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_repLorentzGroup`, and unlike it, it needs the value spaces to
be finite-dimensional, because the gauge action is defined through the coefficient.

Both halves have to be proved. The unconjugated half is the naturality of `repDual` at
`f`; the conjugate half is the naturality of `repDual` at `ConjModule.map f`, for the
conjugate actions, and is supplied by `FieldDerivSpace.lTensor_comp_repConj`. A conjugate
symbol carries `star` of the gauge matrix, so nothing about it follows from the
unconjugated half.

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.symbolAction
declarations.doc:
The action of a coefficient on the symbols. A coefficient `g ⊗ T` acts by
`jetRingAction g` on the derivative label — the Leibniz convolution redistributing
derivatives between the gauge transformation and the field — and by the transpose `Tᵀ` on
the target index.

A coefficient is allowed to change the value space, so that the symbol action of an
endomorphism and the pullback along a map of value spaces are the same construction; at
`W = V` this is the action on `Module.End ℂ (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗ Module.Dual ℂ V)` that
`repDual` uses.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def symbolAction :
    (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V →ₗ[ℂ] W)) →ₗ[ℂ]
      ((SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ W) →ₗ[ℂ]
        (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ V))

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.symbolAction_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma symbolAction_tmul (g : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] W) :
    symbolAction (g ⊗ₜ[ℂ] T)
      = TensorProduct.map (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.jetRingAction g) (Module.Dual.transpose T)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.symbolAction_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
A coefficient acts on the undifferentiated symbol through its value at the base
point. On `1 ⊗ φ` — the symbol `ψ_φ` carrying no derivatives — only the constant term of
the power-series coefficient survives, so the result is again undifferentiated and the
target index is acted on by the transpose of the base-point value.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbolAction_one_tmul (c : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    symbolAction c ((1 : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)
      = (1 : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℂ]
        Module.Dual.transpose (jetEval ∘ₗ TensorProduct.lift
          ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
