            (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) c) φ

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repDual
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the symbols. Given a fibrewise gauge action on the jets of a
`V`-valued field, this is the induced (contragredient) action on the derivative symbols
`∂_s ψ_α`, which span `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗ Module.Dual ℂ V`.

Multiplicativity is bookkeeping. `coeff_mul_of_smul_comm` makes the coefficient
multiplicative, `symbolAction_mul` makes its action an anti-homomorphism, and the inverse
flips that back.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repDual [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z) :
    Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ ⊗[ℂ] Module.Dual ℂ V)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repDual_one_tmul
declarations.doc:
The undifferentiated symbol transforms by the value of the gauge transformation at
the base point. No derivative of the gauge jet contributes, and the symbol `ψ_φ` is acted on
by the contragredient of `rep U⁻¹` restricted to constant jets and evaluated at the base
point.
declarations.statement:
lemma repDual_one_tmul [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repDual rep hlin U ((1 : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)
      = (1 : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ) ⊗ₜ[ℂ]
        Module.Dual.transpose (jetEval ∘ₗ (rep U⁻¹).comp jetOfConstant) φ

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repJet
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the field-derivative space. The induced action of the jets of
gauge transformations on the full space of component functions of the matter field `M` —
the symbols `∂_s ψ_α` together with their conjugates `∂_s ψ̄_α`.

The unconjugated half is `repDual M.repJet`, the contragredient action on the symbols. The
conjugate half is the same construction applied to `repConj M.repJet`, the action on the
jets of the conjugate field; `repConj_smul_comm` supplies the fibrewise-linearity it needs.
The conjugate half therefore carries `star` of the gauge matrix, which is the physicists'
`ψ̄ ↦ ψ̄ U†`.

Everything the construction needs is carried by the matter field, namely the jet action `M.repJet`,
its fibrewise linearity `M.repJet_smul`, and the freeness and finiteness of `M.V`. Taking
the matter field rather than a bare value space is what removes all three from the
argument list.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repJet (M : G.MatterField) :
    Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (FieldDerivSpace M)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repJet_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_fst (M : G.MatterField) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    (repJet M U x).1 = repDual M.repJet M.repJet_smul U x.1

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repJet_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_snd (M : G.MatterField) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : FieldDerivSpace M) :
    (repJet M U x).2
      = repDual (repConj M.repJet) (repConj_smul_comm M.repJet_smul) U x.2

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.map_transpose_comp_symbolAction
declarations.doc:
Pulling back and then acting is acting and then pulling back, on the symbols of a
coefficient. Precomposing the symbol action of a coefficient of `W` with the pullback
along `f` is the symbol action of the coefficient precomposed with `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma map_transpose_comp_symbolAction (f : V →ₗ[ℂ] W) (y : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ W) :
    (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Module.Dual.transpose f)).comp (symbolAction y)
      = symbolAction (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.lcomp ℂ W f) y)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.symbolAction_comp_map_transpose
declarations.doc:
The companion of `map_transpose_comp_symbolAction` on the other side. Postcomposing
the symbol action of a coefficient of `V` with the pullback along `f` is the symbol
action of the coefficient postcomposed with `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbolAction_comp_map_transpose (f : V →ₗ[ℂ] W) (x : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) :
    (symbolAction x).comp (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Module.Dual.transpose f))
      = symbolAction (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V W f) x)

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_repDual
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the unconjugated symbols is natural in the value space. A
linear map of value spaces intertwining two fibrewise jet actions makes the pullback of
symbols equivariant for the two contragredient actions. The whole content is the naturality
of the coefficient, `FieldDerivSpace.jetCoeff_naturality`, read through the symbol
action; the group element is inverted on both sides alike, so no convention is disturbed
by it.
declarations.statement:
lemma comap_comp_repDual [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    [Module.Free ℂ W] [Module.Finite ℂ W]
    (repV : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hV : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V), repV U
        (χ • z) = χ • repV U z)
    (repW : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W))
    (hW : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] W), repW U
        (χ • z) = χ • repW U z)
    (f : V →ₗ[ℂ] W)
    (hf : ∀ U : G.gaugeJetGroup, (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f).comp (repV U)
      = (repW U).comp (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f)) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Module.Dual.transpose f)).comp (repDual repW hW U)
      = (repDual repV hV U).comp
        (TensorProduct.map LinearMap.id (Module.Dual.transpose f))

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.comap_comp_repJet
declarations.doc:
The gauge action on the field-derivative space is natural in the value space. If
`f : M.V →ₗ N.V` intertwines the two fields' actions on the jets, then the pullback of component
functions along `f` intertwines the induced actions on the component spaces, in the
opposite direction — the pullback of a component function of a `W`-valued field being a
component function of a `V`-valued field.

Both halves are covered and every derivative label is carried. The statement is an equality
of linear maps on the whole component space, not a statement about undifferentiated
symbols. The conjugate half is the unconjugated argument applied to `repConj M.repJet` and
`repConj N.repJet`, whose intertwining is `FieldDerivSpace.lTensor_comp_repConj`.
declarations.statement:
lemma comap_comp_repJet {M N : G.MatterField} (f : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] N.V)
    (hf : ∀ U : G.gaugeJetGroup, (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f).comp (M.repJet U)
      = (N.repJet U).comp (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra f)) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    (comap f).comp (repJet N U) = (repJet M U).comp (comap f)

modules.title: The transformation law of a derivative symbol
modules.doc:
The gauge action on a derivative symbol as a Leibniz convolution of base-point Taylor
coefficients.

## i. Overview

The gauge law of a family of component functions asks that each
derivative symbol transform by the all-orders Leibniz convolution of the base-point Taylor
coefficients `GlobalGaugeGroup.repDualCoeff` of the gauge jet. What the gauge action
on the field-derivative space is built from is `symbolAction`, the action of the coefficient
`jetCoeff rep U⁻¹ : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V` through `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.jetRingAction`
on the derivative label. This file identifies the two, for the jet gauge group
`G.gaugeJetGroup` of a global gauge group `G` acting fibrewise on the jets of the field.

The bridge is `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.jetRingAction_basis_multiset`, which puts the action of
a jet on a derivative monomial into the convolution form of that law. What
remains is to recognise the scalars it produces, the base-point Taylor coefficients of the
jet-ring factor of the gauge coefficient, as `GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff`. That is done by
`jetCoeffAt`, the base-point Taylor coefficient of a jet of endomorphisms, which on the
gauge coefficient reproduces `repCoeff` because `jetCoeff` reproduces `rep U` on constant
jets.

The result, `repDual_basis_tmul`, is stated for an arbitrary fibrewise gauge action `rep`.
The conjugate half of the component space is the same construction at `repConj rep`, so it
is an instance of the same lemma rather than a second proof.

## ii. Key results

- `FieldDerivSpace.jetCoeffAt` : the base-point Taylor coefficient of a jet of
  endomorphisms.
- `FieldDerivSpace.jetCoeffAt_jetCoeff` : on the gauge coefficient it is
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff`.
- `FieldDerivSpace.symbolAction_basis_tmul` : a coefficient acts on a derivative monomial
  by the Leibniz convolution of its base-point Taylor coefficients.
- `FieldDerivSpace.repDual_basis_tmul` : the transformation law of the derivative symbol
  `∂_s ψ_φ`, as a Leibniz convolution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Taylor coefficients of a jet of endomorphisms
  - A.1. The coefficient at a multiset of directions
- B. The transformation law of a derivative symbol
  - B.1. Bookkeeping for transposes and multiset sums
  - B.2. The action of a coefficient on a derivative monomial
  - B.3. The gauge action on a derivative symbol

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Taylor coefficients of a jet of endomorphisms
### A.1. The coefficient at a multiset of directions
## B. The transformation law of a derivative symbol
### B.1. Bookkeeping for transposes and multiset sums
### B.2. The action of a coefficient on a derivative monomial
### B.3. The gauge action on a derivative symbol

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetCoeffAt
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficient at `x` derivatives of a jet of endomorphisms of `V`,
obtained by differentiating `x` times and evaluating at the base point. It is the `V`-valued
jet toolkit applied to the value space `Module.End ℂ V`, and it is what a coefficient in
`SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗ End V` contributes to the derivative symbol `∂_x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def jetCoeffAt (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetCoeffAt_tmul
declarations.doc:
On a pure coefficient `f ⊗ T` the Taylor coefficient is the base-point Taylor
coefficient of `f` times `T`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoeffAt_tmul (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (T : Module.End ℂ V) :
    jetCoeffAt x (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] T)
      = constantCoeff (SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv x f) • T

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetCoeffAt_apply
declarations.doc:
The Taylor coefficient of a jet of endomorphisms, evaluated at a vector, is the Taylor
coefficient of the `V`-valued jet obtained by feeding that vector to the coefficient.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoeffAt_apply (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (c : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    jetCoeffAt x c v = jetEval (jetIteratedDeriv x (TensorProduct.lift
      ((LinearMap.llcomp ℂ V V (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)).comp
        (TensorProduct.mk ℂ SpaceTimeAlgebra V)) c v))

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.jetCoeffAt_jetCoeff
declarations.doc:
The Taylor coefficients of the gauge coefficient are the Taylor coefficients of the
representation. `jetCoeff rep U` reproduces `rep U` on constant jets, and both sides of
this identity read off the same derivative of that.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetCoeffAt_jetCoeff [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jetCoeffAt x (jetCoeff rep U) = GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff rep U x

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.symbolAction_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
A coefficient acts on the derivative symbol `∂_s ψ_φ` by the all-orders Leibniz
convolution of its base-point Taylor coefficients. Each splitting `s = s₁ + s₂` of the
derivative multiset contributes the Taylor coefficient at `s₁` acting on the target index
of the lower symbol `∂_{s₂} ψ_φ`.

This is `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.jetRingAction_basis_multiset` in the derivative label,
together with the identification of the scalars it produces as `jetCoeffAt`; both sides
are additive in the coefficient, so it suffices to check it on a pure tensor.
declarations.statement:
lemma symbolAction_basis_tmul (c : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    symbolAction c (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)
      = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis p.2 ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (jetCoeffAt p.1 c).dualMap φ).sum

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.repDual_basis_tmul
declarations.doc:
The transformation law of the derivative symbol `∂_s ψ_φ` under the jet gauge group,
the all-orders Leibniz convolution of the dual representation coefficients
`GlobalGaugeGroup.repDualCoeff` against lower symbols, with no inhomogeneous term. This is
the identity the gauge laws of the symbols of a matter field rest on.

Nothing here is special to the unconjugated half of the component space, and the conjugate
half is this lemma at `repConj rep`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repDual_basis_tmul [Module.Free ℂ V] [Module.Finite ℂ V]
    (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repDual rep hlin U (SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] φ)
      = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis p.2 ⊗ₜ[ℂ]
            GlobalGaugeGroup.repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ).sum

modules.title: The jet action of a matter field
modules.doc:
The action of gauge jets and of the Lie algebra on the jets of a matter field.

## i. Overview

A matter field `M` of a global gauge group `G` has a continuous representation
`ρ : G → GL(V)` on its target space `V`. The jets of the field are `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V`,
on which the jets of linear maps `SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V →L[ℂ] V)` act fibrewise, `f ⊗ a`
sending `g ⊗ v` to `f g ⊗ a v`. A gauge jet `U` acts through its jet representation `ρ(U)`, of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.JetRep`, and the
Lie algebra through `dρ`.

The physicists' `∂_x ρ(U)|₀` is the base-point Taylor coefficient `M.repCoeff U x` of the jet
action, the base-point derivative of `ρ(U)`. It obeys two laws, which make `dρ` the
infinitesimal action underlying the jet action. The Leibniz law `repCoeff_cons` is the
derivative identity `∂_μ ρ(U) = dρ(ω_μ) ρ(U)` at the base point. The intertwining law
`repCoeff_act` is the equivariance `ρ(U) dρ(c) = dρ(U c U⁻¹) ρ(U)` at the base
point, in terms of the adjoint Taylor coefficients `G.adjointCoeff`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetAction` : the action of jets of linear maps on the
  jets of the field.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJet` : the action of the gauge jets.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repAlgebra` : the action of the Lie algebra, `dρ`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff` : the base-point Taylor coefficients
  `∂_x ρ(U)|₀`, with the laws `repCoeff_cons` and `repCoeff_act`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of jets of linear maps on jets of the field
- B. The jet action of the gauge jets
  - B.1. The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet action
  - B.2. The infinitesimal action

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The action of jets of linear maps on jets of the field
## B. The jet action of the gauge jets
### B.1. The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet action
### B.2. The infinitesimal action

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.toLinearMapAlgHom
declarations.doc: The continuous linear maps on the target space, as linear maps.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def toLinearMapAlgHom : (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V) →ₐ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ M.V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetAction
declarations.doc:
The action of jets of linear maps on the jets of the field, where `f ⊗ a` sends `g ⊗ v` to
`f g ⊗ a v`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetAction : M.EndJet →ₐ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] M.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetAction_tmul_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAction_tmul_tmul (f g : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (a : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V) (v : M.V) :
    jetAction M (f ⊗ₜ[ℂ] a) (g ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v) = (f * g) ⊗ₜ[ℂ] a v

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetAction_smul
declarations.doc: The action is fibrewise, so it commutes with multiplication by scalar jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetAction_smul (T : M.EndJet) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] M.V) :
    jetAction M T (χ • z) = χ • jetAction M T z

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetEval_jetIteratedDeriv_jetAction
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficient along `x` of the action of a jet `T` on a constant is the
base-point derivative of `T` along `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_jetIteratedDeriv_jetAction (T : M.EndJet) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (v : M.V) :
    jetEval (jetIteratedDeriv x (jetAction M T (jetOfConstant v))) = jetDerivValue x T v

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repAlgebra
declarations.doc: The action of the gauge algebra, `dρ` as linear maps on the target space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repAlgebra : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] M.V →ₗ[ℂ] M.V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repAlgebra_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repAlgebra_apply (a : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    repAlgebra M a = ((lieAlgebraRep M a : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V) : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] M.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJet
declarations.doc:
The jet action of the jet gauge group, where a gauge jet `U` acts through its jet
representation `ρ(U)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repJet : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] M.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJet_apply
declarations.statement: lemma repJet_apply (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) : repJet M U = jetAction M (jetRep M U)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJet_smul
declarations.doc: The jet action is fibrewise, so it commutes with multiplication by scalar jets.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJet_smul (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] M.V) : repJet M U (χ • z) = χ • repJet M U z

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff
declarations.doc:
The physicists' `∂_x ρ(U)|₀`, the base-point Taylor coefficient of the jet action of a
gauge jet `U` along the multiset of directions `x`, on constant fields.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repCoeff (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    M.V →ₗ[ℂ] M.V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_eq
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet action are the base-point derivatives of the
jet representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_eq (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repCoeff M U x = ((jetDerivValue x (jetRep M U) : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V) : M.V →ₗ[ℂ] M.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_zero
declarations.doc: The base-point value of the jet action of a gauge jet is `ρ` of its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_zero (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    repCoeff M U 0 =
      ((M.rep (G.evalGaugeJet U) : (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)ˣ) : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRep_evalLie_iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc:
`dρ` of the base-point derivatives of a Lie algebra jet are the base-point derivatives of
its jet `dρ(A)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRep_evalLie_iteratedDeriv (p : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    lieAlgebraRep M (G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p A)) =
      jetDerivValue p (jetLieAlgebraRep M A)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_cons
declarations.doc:
The Leibniz law of the base-point Taylor coefficients, the derivative identity
`∂_μ ρ(U) = dρ(ω_μ) ρ(U)` at the base point.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_cons (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repCoeff M U (μ ::ₘ x) =
      -((x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        repAlgebra M (G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p.1
          (-G.maurerCartan U μ))) ∘ₗ
            repCoeff M U p.2).sum)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_act
declarations.doc:
The intertwining law of the base-point Taylor coefficients, the equivariance
`ρ(U) dρ(c) = dρ(U c U⁻¹) ρ(U)` at the base point.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_act (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (c : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    repCoeff M U x ∘ₗ repAlgebra M c =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        repAlgebra M (G.adjointCoeff U p.1 c) ∘ₗ
          repCoeff M U p.2).sum

modules.title: The infinitesimal action underlying a matter representation
modules.doc:
The compatibility of a Lie-algebra action with a jet representation, and the covariance of the
covariant derivative it implies.

## i. Overview

The covariant derivative `∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + A_ρ · F` of a matter family is built from
an action `act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V` of the gauge algebra on the value space. For the
covariant derivative to transform covariantly, `act` must be the *infinitesimal action*
underlying the representation `rep` of the jet gauge group in which the family
transforms — the physicists' statement that the matrices `i dρ(T^a)` generate `rep`.
This file packages that compatibility as the structure `IsInfinitesimalActionOf`, and
proves the theorem it exists for. Call a family `F` of symbols a gauge tensor of `rep` when
each derivative symbol `[∂_s F^φ]` transforms by the Leibniz convolution of the base-point
Taylor coefficients of `rep` against the lower symbols, with no inhomogeneous term. Then the
covariant derivative of a gauge tensor is again one,
`IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivAction`, and by induction so is every iterated
covariant derivative. The gauge field may be any family transforming as a gauge field,
`GaugeBoson.TransformsAsGaugeField`, under an action of the jet gauge group by multiplicative
maps.

Everything is stated over a global gauge group `G : GlobalGaugeGroup κ`; nothing depends on the
Standard Model choice of it. The last sections show that for a matter field `M` the Lie
algebra action `M.repAlgebra` is the infinitesimal action underlying its jet action `M.repJet`,
that pure jets act trivially at the base point, and record the condition that the gauge and
Lorentz actions on the target space commute. This is `MatterField.GaugeLorentzCommute` for the
group and `MatterField.GaugeLorentzCompatible` for the Lie algebra, and the first implies the
second.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf` : `act` is the infinitesimal action underlying
  `rep`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivAction` : the covariant derivative
  preserves the Leibniz transformation law of a family of symbols.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivIter` : so does every iterated
  covariant derivative, and `repGauge_covDerivIter_zero` is its underived symbol.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.conj` : the conjugate action underlies the
  conjugate representation.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.eq_of_repCoeff_zero` : a fibrewise representation
  is determined by its infinitesimal action and its base-point values.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.isInfinitesimalActionOf` : `dρ` is the infinitesimal
  action underlying the jet action of a matter field.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.repDualCoeff_inv_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval` : if pure jets act trivially at
  the base point, the base-point action of a jet factors through its value.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one` : pure jets act trivially
  at the base point.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.GaugeLorentzCommute`,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.GaugeLorentzCompatible` : the gauge and Lorentz actions
  commute, at the level of the group and of the Lie algebra.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.GaugeLorentzCommute.gaugeLorentzCompatible` : the first
  condition implies the second.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The infinitesimal action underlying a representation
- B. The covariant derivative preserves the transformation law
- C. The conjugate action and the conjugate representation
- D. Uniqueness
- E. Factorization through evaluation
- F. The infinitesimal action of a matter field
- G. Pure jets act trivially
- H. Compatibility of the gauge and Lorentz actions

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The infinitesimal action underlying a representation
## B. The covariant derivative preserves the transformation law
## C. The conjugate action and the conjugate representation

## D. Uniqueness

A representation generated by an infinitesimal action is determined, Taylor coefficient by
Taylor coefficient, by its values at the base point: `repCoeff_cons` expresses each
coefficient through coefficients of lower order.

## E. Factorization through evaluation

If pure jets act trivially at the base point, the base-point action of a jet is that of the
constant jet of its value.

## F. The infinitesimal action of a matter field

For a matter field `M` the action `M.repAlgebra = dρ` of the Lie algebra and the jet
action `M.repJet` form such a pair, by the Leibniz and intertwining laws of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.GaugeJetAction`.
## G. Pure jets act trivially
## H. Compatibility of the gauge and Lorentz actions

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf
declarations.doc:
`act` is the *infinitesimal action* of the gauge algebra underlying the
representation `rep` of the jet gauge group, when the base-point Taylor
coefficients of `rep` satisfy the two laws forced by `rep` being generated by
`act`.

* `repCoeff_cons` is the Leibniz rule in the Maurer–Cartan form. Differentiating
  the representation once produces minus the action of the Maurer–Cartan form,
  with the remaining derivatives distributed over the antidiagonal (for the
  adjoint representation this is `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_cons`);
* `repCoeff_act` says that the transports of `rep` intertwine `act` with the adjoint
  transports, as an antidiagonal convolution (for the adjoint representation this
  is `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointCoeff_lie`); at `x = 0` it is the classical equivariance
  `rep(U)|₀ ∘ act c = act (Ad(U) c)|₀ ∘ rep(U)|₀`.

These are exactly the identities consumed by the proof that the covariant
derivative `covDerivAction` preserves the Leibniz transformation law of a family.
declarations.statement:
structure IsInfinitesimalActionOf (G : GlobalGaugeGroup κ)
    (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)) : Prop where
  repCoeff_cons : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
    repCoeff rep U (μ ::ₘ x) =
      -((x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        act (G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p.1
          (-G.maurerCartan U μ))) ∘ₗ
          repCoeff rep U p.2).sum)
  repCoeff_act : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (c : G.lieSubalgebra),
    repCoeff rep U x ∘ₗ act c =
      ((x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        act (G.adjointCoeff U p.1 c) ∘ₗ repCoeff rep U p.2).sum)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repDualCoeff_cons
declarations.doc:
The dual form of the Leibniz law. The once-more-derived dual coefficient is
minus the antidiagonal convolution of dual coefficients against `act` of the
derived Maurer–Cartan form — the analogue of `GlobalGaugeGroup.adjointDualCoeff_cons`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repDualCoeff_cons
    {act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V}
    {rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V)}
    (h : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repDualCoeff rep U (μ ::ₘ x) φ =
      -((x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        repDualCoeff rep U p.2 (φ ∘ₗ act (G.evalLie
          (G.iteratedDerivJ p.1 (-G.maurerCartan U μ))))).sum)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.actionFam_repDualCoeff
declarations.doc:
The action of families against the dual representation coefficients, the
antidiagonal convolution mixing the adjoint transport on the field slot with the
representation transport on the matter slot — the family-level form of
`IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repCoeff_act`, and the analogue of
`GaugeBoson.bracketFam_adjointDualCoeff`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.actionFam_repDualCoeff
    (h : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup)
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B)
    (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFam act f g (repDualCoeff rep U x φ) =
      (x.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        actionFam act (f ∘ₗ G.adjointDualCoeff U p.1)
          (g ∘ₗ repDualCoeff rep U p.2) φ).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_cons
declarations.doc:
If `F` transforms by the Leibniz law of `rep`, the transformation of its `κ ::ₘ s`-derived
symbols has the extra derivative traced through `IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repDualCoeff_cons`,
giving the Leibniz splittings where `κ` stays a derivative, minus the convolution where `κ`
hits the representation, `act` of the derived Maurer–Cartan form.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_cons (hact : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep)
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hF : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      repGauge U (F s φ) = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => F p.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (κ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U (F (κ ::ₘ s) φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        F (κ ::ₘ p.2) (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum
      - (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          (p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q =>
            F p.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ q.2
              (φ ∘ₗ act (G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ q.1
                (-G.maurerCartan U⁻¹ κ)))))).sum).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.sum_actionFam_conv_eq
declarations.doc:
The action of the transformed gauge-field symbols on the transformed matter symbols,
summed over the antidiagonal, is the antidiagonal convolution of the derived action `A_ρ · F`
against the dual representation coefficients. It is the homogeneous part of the
transformation of `A_ρ · F`, rearranged by the coassociativity of the antidiagonal.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.sum_actionFam_conv_eq (hact : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep)
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
      actionFam act ((p.1.antidiagonal.map fun q =>
          A q.2 ρ ∘ₗ G.adjointDualCoeff U⁻¹ q.1).sum)
        ((p.2.antidiagonal.map fun r =>
          F r.2 ∘ₗ repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ r.1).sum) φ).sum =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        actionFamConv A act ρ F p.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_actionFamConv
declarations.doc:
The all-orders gauge transformation of the derived action `A_ρ · F` for `F`
transforming by the Leibniz law of `rep`. Since `F` transforms homogeneously, only one
cross-term convolution through `act` survives — the analogue of
`GaugeBoson.TransformsInAdjoint.repGauge_bracketFamConv` with a matter field in the second
slot.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_actionFamConv (hact : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep)
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hF : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      repGauge U (F s φ) = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => F p.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U (actionFamConv A act ρ F s φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        actionFamConv A act ρ F p.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum
      + (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
          (p.2.antidiagonal.map fun r =>
            F r.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ r.1
              (φ ∘ₗ act (G.evalLie (G.iteratedDerivJ p.1
                (-G.maurerCartan U⁻¹ ρ)))))).sum).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivAction
declarations.doc:
The covariant derivative preserves the transformation law. If each derivative symbol of `F`
transforms by the Leibniz convolution of the coefficients of `rep`, and `act` is the
infinitesimal action underlying `rep`, then so does each derivative symbol of
`∇_ρ F = [∂_ρ F] + A_ρ · F`. The single inhomogeneous
convolution of `[∂_{ρ ::ₘ s} F]` cancels the single `act` cross-term convolution of
`A_ρ · F` through the coassociativity of the antidiagonal — the matter-field
analogue of `GaugeBoson.TransformsInAdjoint.covDerivAdjoint`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivAction (hact : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep)
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hF : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      repGauge U (F s φ) = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => F p.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repGauge U (GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivAction A act F ρ s φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivAction A act F ρ p.2
        (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
Every iterated covariant derivative preserves the transformation law. If each derivative
symbol of `F` transforms by the Leibniz convolution of the coefficients of `rep`, and `act` is
the infinitesimal action underlying `rep`, then so does each derivative symbol of
`∇_{l 0} ⋯ ∇_{l (n-1)} F`. This is induction on the number `n` of covariant derivatives,
each step being `IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivAction`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivIter (hact : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep)
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hF : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      repGauge U (F s φ) = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => F p.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum)
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repGauge U (GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter A act F n l s φ) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter A act F n l p.2
        (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivIter_zero
declarations.doc:
The underived symbol of an iterated covariant derivative transforms through the
base-point coefficient alone, since the antidiagonal of the empty multiset has a single term.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repGauge_covDerivIter_zero
    (hact : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep)
    {F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B}
    (hF : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)),
      repGauge U (F s φ) = (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => F p.2 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ p.1 φ)).sum)
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repGauge U (GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter A act F n l 0 φ) =
      GlobalGaugeGroup.covDerivIter A act F n l 0 (repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ 0 φ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionConj
declarations.doc:
The conjugate of an infinitesimal action. It is the same maps, read on the conjugate
module, the generators of the conjugate representation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionConj (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) :
    G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] ConjModule V →ₗ[ℂ] ConjModule V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionConj_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma actionConj_apply (act : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] V →ₗ[ℂ] V) (c : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    actionConj act c = ConjModule.endConj (act c)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.conjJetEquiv
declarations.doc:
The identification of the jets of a conjugate field with the conjugates of the
jets. Conjugation is monoidal, and the star of the jet-ring factor absorbs the
twist — `conj (g ⊗ u) ↦ star g ⊗ conj u`. This is the equivalence along which
`FieldDerivSpace.repConj` carries the conjugated representation.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conjJetEquiv :
    ConjModule (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) ≃ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] ConjModule V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.conjJetEquiv_conjEquiv_tmul
declarations.statement:
lemma conjJetEquiv_conjEquiv_tmul (g : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (u : V) :
    conjJetEquiv (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) (g ⊗ₜ[ℂ] u))
      = star g ⊗ₜ[ℂ] conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := V) u

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repConj_conjJetEquiv
declarations.doc: The conjugate representation acts through `conjJetEquiv` by the original maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma repConj_conjJetEquiv (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (w : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) :
    FieldDerivSpace.repConj rep U
        (conjJetEquiv (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) w))
      = conjJetEquiv (conjEquiv (k := ℂ) (M := SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V) (rep U w))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff_repConj
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the conjugate representation are the
conjugated coefficients. The derivative directions are real, so conjugation passes
through `∂_x` and the base-point evaluation untouched.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_repConj (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repCoeff (FieldDerivSpace.repConj rep) U x
      = ConjModule.endConj (repCoeff rep U x)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff_repConj_zero_eq_id
declarations.doc:
The base-point triviality of the zeroth Taylor coefficient passes to the
conjugate representation.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.conj
declarations.doc:
The conjugate of an infinitesimal action underlies the conjugate
representation. Conjugating the Taylor coefficients preserves both the
Maurer–Cartan Leibniz law and the adjoint intertwining, since the gauge-algebra
inputs are real.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.conj (h : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep) :
    IsInfinitesimalActionOf G (actionConj act) (FieldDerivSpace.repConj rep)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repCoeff_eq_of_repCoeff_zero
declarations.doc:
Two representations with the same infinitesimal action and the same base-point values
of a gauge jet have the same Taylor coefficients at that jet.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.repCoeff_eq_of_repCoeff_zero
    (h : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep) (h' : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep')
    {U : G.gaugeJetGroup} (h0 : repCoeff rep U 0 = repCoeff rep' U 0)
      (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repCoeff rep U x = repCoeff rep' U x

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.IsInfinitesimalActionOf.eq_of_repCoeff_zero
declarations.doc:
A fibrewise representation is determined by its infinitesimal action and its
base-point values. Two fibrewise representations generated by the same action, with the
same value `repCoeff · U 0` at every gauge jet, are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsInfinitesimalActionOf.eq_of_repCoeff_zero [FiniteDimensional ℂ V]
    (h : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep) (h' : IsInfinitesimalActionOf G act rep')
    (hs : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) z, rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (hs' : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) z, rep' U (χ • z) = χ • rep' U z)
    (h0 : ∀ U, repCoeff rep U 0 = repCoeff rep' U 0) : rep = rep'

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval
declarations.doc:
If pure jets act trivially at the base point, the zeroth Taylor coefficient of a jet
is that of the constant jet of its value. Every jet is a pure jet times the constant jet
of its value, and the zeroth coefficients are multiplicative for a fibrewise
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval
    (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (hrep : ∀ {W : G.gaugeJetGroup}, G.evalGaugeJet W = 1 → repCoeff rep W 0 = LinearMap.id)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    repCoeff rep U 0 = repCoeff rep (G.gaugeJetOfConstant (G.evalGaugeJet U)) 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repDualCoeff_inv_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval
declarations.doc:
If pure jets act trivially at the base point, the dual base-point coefficient of the
inverse of a jet is that of the inverse of the constant jet of its value.
declarations.statement:
lemma repDualCoeff_inv_zero_eq_ofConstant_eval
    (rep : Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V))
    (hlin : ∀ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] V),
      rep U (χ • z) = χ • rep U z)
    (hrep : ∀ {W : G.gaugeJetGroup}, G.evalGaugeJet W = 1 → repCoeff rep W 0 = LinearMap.id)
    (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    repDualCoeff rep U⁻¹ 0 = repDualCoeff rep (G.gaugeJetOfConstant (G.evalGaugeJet U))⁻¹ 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_repJet
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the jet action are those of the jet action as a
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_repJet (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff M.repJet U x = M.repCoeff U x

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.isInfinitesimalActionOf
declarations.doc:
The action `dρ` of the Lie algebra is the infinitesimal action underlying the jet action
of the gauge jets.
declarations.statement: lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf : G.IsInfinitesimalActionOf M.repAlgebra M.repJet

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one
declarations.doc:
Pure jets act trivially at the base point. A jet of value one has identity zeroth Taylor
coefficient on the target space, for every matter field.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_zero_of_eval_eq_one {W : G.gaugeJetGroup} (hW : G.evalGaugeJet W = 1) :
    GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff M.repJet W 0 = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.GaugeLorentzCommute
declarations.doc: The gauge and Lorentz representations of a matter field commute.
declarations.statement: def GaugeLorentzCommute : Prop

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.GaugeLorentzCompatible
declarations.doc:
The internal gauge symmetry of the matter field commutes with its Lorentz symmetry, that
is, the action of the Lie algebra commutes with the Lorentz representation on the target
space. The covariant derivative adds the term `A_ρ · F`, built from the Lie algebra action, to
the ordinary derivative, so its Lorentz law holds only when this commutation does. The later
algebras of covariant expressions are stable under the Lorentz group for the same reason.
It follows from `GaugeLorentzCommute`, but not conversely. It determines the gauge action
on the identity component alone, so it says nothing about the other components of a
disconnected gauge group.
declarations.statement: def GaugeLorentzCompatible : Prop

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.GaugeLorentzCommute.gaugeLorentzCompatible
declarations.doc:
If the gauge and Lorentz representations commute, so do the Lie algebra action and the
Lorentz representation, the Lie algebra action being the derivative of the gauge
representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma GaugeLorentzCommute.gaugeLorentzCompatible (h : M.GaugeLorentzCommute) :
    M.GaugeLorentzCompatible

modules.title: The jet representation of a matter field
modules.doc:
The continuous representation `ρ : G → GL(V)` of a matter field, extended to the jets
of gauge transformations and to the Lie algebra jets.

## i. Overview

A matter field `M` transforms under the representation `ρ = M.rep` of the global
gauge group `G` on its target space `V`. A gauge transformation `U(x)` acts on it through
`ρ(U(x))`, a function valued in the linear maps on `V`. Its jets are the jets of
`V →L[ℂ] V`-valued functions, `M.EndJet = SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (V →L[ℂ] V)`, an algebra. On
jets, a gauge jet `U` acts through the jet `ρ(U)` of `x ↦ ρ(U(x))`, and a Lie algebra jet `A`
through the jet `dρ(A)` of `x ↦ dρ(A(x))`, with `dρ` the Lie algebra representation of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.MatterField.DerivRep`.

The jet action is built from the Lie algebra action and the Maurer–Cartan form, and not by
applying `ρ` to the power series entries of `U`, because `ρ` is only defined on the group `G`
itself. A jet is formal, so there is no group element `U(x)` to which `ρ` could be applied
and no formula for the jet of `ρ(U(x))` in terms of the entries of `U`. What is available is
the Lie algebra representation `dρ`, which acts on the Lie algebra jets, and the Maurer–Cartan
form `ω_μ = (∂_μ U) U⁻¹`, which carries a gauge jet into them. The derivative of `ρ(U(x))` is
`dρ(ω_μ) ρ(U(x))`, so the jet is recovered as the unique solution of this equation with the
right base-point value.

The jet `dρ(A)` is defined by its base-point derivatives, those of `A` with `dρ` applied, each
lying in the Lie algebra. It commutes with the derivatives, sends constant jets to constant
jets and preserves the commutator, the base-point derivatives of a commutator being sums of
commutators of base-point derivatives.

The jet `ρ(U)` is characterised by its value `ρ(U(0))` and the derivative identity
`∂_μ ρ(U) = dρ(ω_μ) ρ(U)`, with `ω_μ = (∂_μ U) U⁻¹` the Maurer–Cartan form. The flatness of
the Maurer–Cartan form, `∂_μ ω_ν − ∂_ν ω_μ = [ω_μ, ω_ν]`, carries over to `dρ(ω_μ)`, so the
derivative identity has a unique solution with any prescribed value, by the theory of flat
families of jets in `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalFieldTheory.GaugeTheory.LocalFieldAlgebra.Jet`.
Uniqueness then gives `ρ(U V) = ρ(U) ρ(V)` and the equivariance
`dρ(U A U⁻¹) ρ(U) = ρ(U) dρ(A)`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.EndJet` : the jets of linear maps on the target space.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetLieAlgebraRep` : the jet `dρ(A)` of a Lie algebra
  jet.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetRep` : the jet `ρ(U)` of a gauge jet, as a
  homomorphism.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetDeriv_jetRep` : the derivative identity
  `∂_μ ρ(U) = dρ(ω_μ) ρ(U)`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetLieAlgebraRep_adjoint_mul_jetRep` : the equivariance
  `dρ(U A U⁻¹) ρ(U) = ρ(U) dρ(A)`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Lie algebra representation on Lie algebra jets
- B. The jet of a representation along a gauge jet
  - B.1. The flat family `dρ(ω)`
  - B.2. The jet of the representation along a gauge jet
  - B.3. Equivariance and multiplicativity
  - B.4. The jet representation

## iv. References

* B. C. Hall, *Lie Groups, Lie Algebras, and Representations*, 2nd ed., Springer (2015).

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.EndJet
declarations.doc: The jets of linear maps on the target space, an algebra.
declarations.statement: abbrev EndJet : Type

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRepFun_congr
declarations.doc: `dρ` depends on a generator only through its matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRepFun_congr {X Y : G.lieAlgebra} (h : (X : Matrix κ κ ℂ) = Y) :
    lieAlgebraRepFun M X = lieAlgebraRepFun M Y

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetLieAlgebraRepFun
declarations.doc:
The jet `dρ(A)` of a Lie algebra jet `A`, whose base-point derivative along `s` is `dρ` of
that of `A`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetLieAlgebraRepFun (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) : M.EndJet

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetDerivValue_jetLieAlgebraRepFun
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivValue_jetLieAlgebraRepFun (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jetDerivValue s (jetLieAlgebraRepFun M A) =
      lieAlgebraRepFun M ⟨derivValueMatrix s A.1, A.2 s⟩

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetLieAlgebraRep
declarations.doc: The jet `dρ(A)` of a Lie algebra jet, as a real-linear map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetLieAlgebraRep : G.jetLieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] M.EndJet

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetDerivValue_jetLieAlgebraRep
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDerivValue_jetLieAlgebraRep (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    jetDerivValue s (jetLieAlgebraRep M A) = lieAlgebraRepFun M ⟨derivValueMatrix s A.1, A.2 s⟩

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetLieAlgebraRep_ofConstantLie
declarations.doc: The jet `dρ(A)` of a constant Lie algebra jet `A = a` is the constant jet `dρ(a)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetLieAlgebraRep_ofConstantLie (a : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.ofConstantLie a) = jetOfConstant (lieAlgebraRep M a)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetDeriv_jetLieAlgebraRep
declarations.doc: The jet `dρ(A)` commutes with the formal derivatives, `∂_μ dρ(A) = dρ(∂_μ A)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_jetLieAlgebraRep (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    jetDeriv μ (jetLieAlgebraRep M A) = jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.derivJ μ A)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetLieAlgebraRep_lie
declarations.doc:
The jet `dρ` on Lie algebra jets preserves the commutator. The base-point derivatives of
a commutator are sums of commutators of base-point derivatives, each preserved by `dρ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetLieAlgebraRep_lie (A B : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    jetLieAlgebraRep M ⁅A, B⁆ =
      jetLieAlgebraRep M A * jetLieAlgebraRep M B -
        jetLieAlgebraRep M B * jetLieAlgebraRep M A

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetDeriv_jetLieAlgebraRep_maurerCartan_sub
declarations.doc:
The structure equation for `dρ(ω)`, `∂_μ dρ(ω_ν) − ∂_ν dρ(ω_μ) = [dρ(ω_μ), dρ(ω_ν)]`,
so the family `dρ(ω_μ)` is flat.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_jetLieAlgebraRep_maurerCartan_sub (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jetDeriv μ (jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U ν)) -
        jetDeriv ν (jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U μ)) =
      jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U μ) * jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U ν) -
        jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U ν) * jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U μ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetRepFun
declarations.doc:
The jet `ρ(U)` of the representation along a gauge jet `U`, the solution of the
derivative identity `∂_μ ρ(U) = dρ(ω_μ) ρ(U)` with value `ρ(U(0))`, which exists since the
family `dρ(ω_μ)` is flat.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetRepFun (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) : M.EndJet

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetEval_jetRepFun
declarations.doc: The value of `ρ(U)` at the base point is `ρ(U(0))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_jetRepFun (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    jetEval (jetRepFun M U) = ((M.rep (G.evalGaugeJet U) : (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)ˣ) : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetDeriv_jetRepFun
declarations.doc: The derivative identity `∂_μ ρ(U) = dρ(ω_μ) ρ(U)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_jetRepFun (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jetDeriv μ (jetRepFun M U) = jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U μ) * jetRepFun M U

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.eq_jetRepFun
declarations.doc: The jet `ρ(U)` is the only jet with value `ρ(U(0))` satisfying the derivative identity.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_jetRepFun {U : G.gaugeJetGroup} {Y : M.EndJet}
    (hY : ∀ μ, jetDeriv μ Y = jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U μ) * Y)
    (hY0 : jetEval Y = ((M.rep (G.evalGaugeJet U) : (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)ˣ) : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)) :
    Y = jetRepFun M U

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetRepFun_one
declarations.statement: lemma jetRepFun_one : jetRepFun M 1 = 1

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetDeriv_jetLieAlgebraRep_adjointJ
declarations.doc: The derivative of `dρ(U A U⁻¹)` is `dρ(U (∂_μ A) U⁻¹) + [dρ(ω_μ), dρ(U A U⁻¹)]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_jetLieAlgebraRep_adjointJ (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jetDeriv μ (jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.adjointJ U A)) =
      jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.adjointJ U (G.derivJ μ A)) +
        (jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U μ) *
            jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.adjointJ U A) -
          jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.adjointJ U A) *
            jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U μ))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetEval_adjointDefect
declarations.doc:
The equivariance defect `dρ(U A U⁻¹) ρ(U) − ρ(U) dρ(A)` vanishes at the base point, by
`dρ(g X g⁻¹) = ρ(g) dρ(X) ρ(g)⁻¹`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetEval_adjointDefect (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    jetEval (jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.adjointJ U A) * jetRepFun M U -
        jetRepFun M U * jetLieAlgebraRep M A) = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetLieAlgebraRep_adjoint_mul_jetRepFun
declarations.doc:
The equivariance `dρ(U A U⁻¹) ρ(U) = ρ(U) dρ(A)`. The defect vanishes at the base point
and its derivative is the defect of the derivative plus `dρ(ω_μ)` times the defect, so it
vanishes.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetLieAlgebraRep_adjoint_mul_jetRepFun (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.adjointJ U A) * jetRepFun M U =
      jetRepFun M U * jetLieAlgebraRep M A

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetRepFun_mul
declarations.doc: The jet of a representation is multiplicative, `ρ(U V) = ρ(U) ρ(V)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetRepFun_mul (U V : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    jetRepFun M (U * V) = jetRepFun M U * jetRepFun M V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetRep
declarations.doc: The jet representation `U ↦ ρ(U)` of the jet gauge group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def jetRep : G.gaugeJetGroup →* M.EndJet

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetRep_apply
declarations.statement: lemma jetRep_apply (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) : jetRep M U = jetRepFun M U

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetDeriv_jetRep
declarations.doc: The derivative identity `∂_μ ρ(U) = dρ(ω_μ) ρ(U)` of the jet representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetDeriv_jetRep (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    jetDeriv μ (jetRep M U) = jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.maurerCartan U μ) * jetRep M U

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.jetLieAlgebraRep_adjoint_mul_jetRep
declarations.doc: The equivariance `dρ(U A U⁻¹) ρ(U) = ρ(U) dρ(A)` of the jet representation.
declarations.statement:
lemma jetLieAlgebraRep_adjoint_mul_jetRep (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (A : G.jetLieSubalgebra) :
    jetLieAlgebraRep M (G.adjointJ U A) * jetRep M U =
      jetRep M U * jetLieAlgebraRep M A

modules.title: The Lorentz law of the covariant derivatives of a matter family
modules.doc:
How the iterated covariant derivatives of a matter family transform under the Lorentz group.

## i. Overview

The covariant derivative of a matter family adds one ordered derivative slot and the
correction `A_ρ · F`, the derived action `actionFamConv` of the gauge field on the value
index. Expanded in bases, the correction is a scalar combination of Leibniz convolutions of
gauge-field symbols against matter symbols, which gives its Lorentz law and its linearity
in the matter family. The contragredient twist `rep.dual Λ` of the value index passes
through it when the infinitesimal gauge action commutes with the Lorentz action on the
value space, the one hypothesis on the species. These are the inputs of the
abstract induction `Lorentz.repLorentz_tower`, for any family of gauge-field symbols in a
complex algebra `B` with the Lorentz law `GaugeBoson.LorentzTransformsAsGaugeField`, under a
Lorentz action by multiplicative maps.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.repLorentz_covDerivIter` : the Lorentz law of the iterated
  covariant derivative at every derivative multiset.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter`, `..._conj` : the
  covariant tower of a matter family, and of a conjugate family, transforms as the
  covariant derivatives of a Lorentz-covariant field.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Families in the multiset form of the Lorentz law
- B. The derived action family in bases
- C. The Lorentz law of the covariant tower

## iv. References

* None.
