declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.sum_derivConv_sum_fam
declarations.doc:
A scalar combination of convolutions against the gauge field is linear in the
right-hand families.
declarations.statement:
lemma sum_derivConv_sum_fam {ι κ ι' : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] [Fintype ι']
    (f : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (coef : ι → κ → ℂ) (c : ι' → ℂ)
    (g : ι' → κ → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∑ j, ∑ k, coef j k • derivConv (f j) (fun y => ∑ i, c i • g i k y) s =
      ∑ i, c i • ∑ j, ∑ k, coef j k • derivConv (f j) (g i k) s

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repLorentz_eq_lorentzMix
declarations.doc:
A Lorentz law in the tuple form, read on the underlying multisets. The transformed
family mixes by `lorentzMix`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_eq_lorentzMix (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (f g : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (hfg : ∀ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)), repLorentz Λ (f (List.ofFn l)) =
      ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3), (∏ i, L[Λ] (p i) (l i)) • g (List.ofFn p))
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) : repLorentz Λ (f x) = lorentzMix Λ g x 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repLorentz_apply_mix
declarations.doc: The Lorentz law of the gauge-field symbols, in the multiset form.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_apply_mix (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (χ : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) :
    repLorentz Λ (A x μ χ) = lorentzMix Λ (fun t => ∑ a, L[Λ] a μ • A t a χ) x 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.isLorentzDerivTransforms_mix
declarations.doc: The Lorentz law of a family of derivative symbols, in the multiset form.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repLorentz_sum_derivConv
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of a scalar combination of convolutions against the gauge field. The
direction of the gauge field mixes by its own column, the derivative slots by
`lorentzMix`, and the right-hand families are replaced by their transforms.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_sum_derivConv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    {ι κ : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ] (bg : Module.Basis ι ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) (coef : ι → κ → ℂ)
    (g g' : κ → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → B)
    (hg : ∀ k y, repLorentz Λ (g k y) = lorentzMix Λ (g' k) y 0)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    repLorentz Λ (∑ j, ∑ k, coef j k • derivConv (fun x => A x ρ (bg.coord j)) (g k) s) =
      ∑ a, L[Λ] a ρ • lorentzMix Λ
        (fun t => ∑ j, ∑ k, coef j k • derivConv (fun x => A x a (bg.coord j)) (g' k) t)
        s 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_apply_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The action of families expanded in bases of the gauge algebra and the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_apply_eq_sum {ι κ : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
    (bg : Module.Basis ι ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) (bv : Module.Basis κ ℂ V)
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFam act f g φ =
      ∑ j, ∑ k, φ (act (bg j) (bv k)) • (f (bg.coord j) * g (bv.coord k))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFamConv_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The derived action family expanded in bases.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFamConv_eq_sum {ι κ : Type} [Fintype ι] [Fintype κ]
    (bg : Module.Basis ι ℝ G.lieSubalgebra) (bv : Module.Basis κ ℂ V)
    (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (Fm : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFamConv A act ρ Fm s φ = ∑ j, ∑ k, φ (act (bg j) (bv k)) •
      derivConv (fun x => A x ρ (bg.coord j)) (fun y => Fm y (bv.coord k)) s

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFamConv_sum_fam
declarations.doc: The derived action family is linear in the matter family.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFamConv_sum_fam {ι : Type} [Fintype ι] (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (c : ι → ℂ)
    (H : ι → Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFamConv A act ρ (fun t => ∑ i, c i • H i t) s φ =
      ∑ i, c i • actionFamConv A act ρ (H i) s φ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repLorentz_actionFamConv
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of the derived action family. The derivative slots mix, the direction
of the gauge field mixes by its own column, and the value index is carried by the
transformed matter family.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_actionFamConv (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (Fm Fm' : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hG : ∀ y χ, repLorentz Λ (Fm y χ) = lorentzMix Λ (fun t => Fm' t χ) y 0)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repLorentz Λ (actionFamConv A act ρ Fm s φ) =
      ∑ a, L[Λ] a ρ • lorentzMix Λ (fun t => actionFamConv A act a Fm' t φ) s 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.dual_twist
declarations.doc:
The twist of the value index past the gauge action. An endomorphism commuting with
the gauge action may be moved from the dual basis onto the dual vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma dual_twist {κ : Type} [Fintype κ] (bv : Module.Basis κ ℂ V) (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (hT : ∀ (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (v : V), act c (T v) = T (act c v))
    (ψ : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B) (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    ∑ k, φ (act c (bv k)) • ψ (T.dualMap (bv.coord k)) =
      ∑ k, (T.dualMap φ) (act c (bv k)) • ψ (bv.coord k)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFam_comp_dual
declarations.doc:
The contragredient action may be pulled out of an action of families, provided the
gauge action commutes with it on the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFam_comp_dual (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (hT : ∀ (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (v : V), act c (T v) = T (act c v))
    (f : Module.Dual ℝ G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] B) (g : Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFam act f (g ∘ₗ T.dualMap) φ = actionFam act f g (T.dualMap φ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionFamConv_comp_dual
declarations.doc: The contragredient action may be pulled out of a derived action family.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionFamConv_comp_dual (T : V →ₗ[ℂ] V)
    (hT : ∀ (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (v : V), act c (T v) = T (act c v)) (ρ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (K : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    actionFamConv A act ρ (fun t => K t ∘ₗ T.dualMap) s φ =
      actionFamConv A act ρ K s (T.dualMap φ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.repLorentz_covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of the iterated covariant derivative of a matter family. The ordered
covariant slots mix by their own columns and the multiset of plain derivative slots
mixes by `lorentzMix`, while the value index transforms contragrediently.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_covDerivIter {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    (hcomm : ∀ (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V), act c (rep Λ v) = rep Λ (act c v))
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hF : IsLorentzDerivTransforms repLorentz rep F) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (φ : Module.Dual ℂ V) :
    repLorentz Λ (covDerivIter A act F n l s φ) = ∑ p : Fin n → (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3),
      (∏ i, L[Λ] (p i) (l i)) •
        lorentzMix Λ (fun t => covDerivIter A act F n p t (rep.dual Λ φ)) s 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter
declarations.doc:
The iterated covariant derivative of a matter family transforms as the covariant
derivatives of a Lorentz-covariant field, given the Lorentz law of the bare symbols,
the Lorentz law of the gauge field, and the commutation of the infinitesimal gauge
action with the Lorentz action on the value space.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    (hcomm : ∀ (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V), act c (rep Λ v) = rep Λ (act c v))
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ V →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hF : IsLorentzDerivTransforms repLorentz rep F) :
    IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz rep (fun {n} l => covDerivIter A act F n l 0)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.actionConj_comm_repConj
declarations.doc:
Conjugation preserves the commutation of the gauge action with the Lorentz action,
since both are read on the conjugate module through the same underlying maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma actionConj_comm_repConj (rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V)
    (hcomm : ∀ (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V), act c (rep Λ v) = rep Λ (act c v))
    (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : ConjModule V) :
    actionConj act c (rep.conj Λ v) =
      rep.conj Λ (actionConj act c v)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter_conj
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz law of the covariant tower of a conjugate family, from the commutation of
the gauge action with the Lorentz action of the unconjugated species.
declarations.statement:
lemma isLorentzCovDerivTransforms_covDerivIter_conj {rep : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V}
    (hcomm : ∀ (c : G.lieSubalgebra) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (v : V), act c (rep Λ v) = rep Λ (act c v))
    (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → Module.Dual ℂ (ConjModule V) →ₗ[ℂ] B)
    (hF : IsLorentzDerivTransforms repLorentz rep.conj F) :
    IsLorentzCovDerivTransforms repLorentz rep.conj
      (fun {n} l => covDerivIter A (actionConj act) F n l 0)

modules.title: Matter fields from matrix representations of a global gauge group
modules.doc:
Continuous representations of a global gauge group by complex matrices, and the matter fields
they define.

## i. Overview

A model-building table says how a field transforms by writing down a matrix. The field has an
internal index `ι`, and a gauge transformation acts on it by an invertible `ι × ι` complex
matrix. Such a matrix representation of the global gauge group `G` is a continuous
homomorphism `G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ`. Its derivative `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivMat ρ c` is
the matrix by which an element `c` of the Lie algebra acts. It is the matrix version of
`GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep`, and is characterised by the exponential law
`ρ (exp (t c)) = exp (t derivMat ρ c)`.

The representations named in a table are assembled from a few pieces. These are the trivial
representation, the Kronecker product `MatrixRep.kron` and the twist `MatrixRep.charge` by a
power of a character of the gauge group. The derivative of each is computed from the
exponential law.

A matrix representation `ρ` on `ι` gives a matter field on any target space
`V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`, where `S` carries a representation of the Lorentz group. The gauge group
acts by `ρ` on the internal index and the Lorentz group on `S`. This is
`MatterField.ofMatrixRep`. Its action of the Lie algebra is the derivative of `ρ`, and its jet
action is then fixed by the derivative.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivMat` : the derivative of a matrix representation, a matrix for each
  element of the Lie algebra.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.apply_eq_exp_derivMat`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivMat_eq_of` : the exponential
  law, and the uniqueness of the derivative.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.trivial`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.kron`,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.charge` : the trivial representation, the Kronecker product and
  the charge twist.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.derivMat_trivial`, `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.derivMat_kron`,
  `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.derivMat_charge` : their derivatives.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd` : the endomorphism of `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)` defined by a
  matrix on the internal index.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.repLorentz` : the Lorentz action on `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`, which
  commutes with every `valEnd`.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.ofMatrixRep` : the matter field of a matrix
  representation.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.ofMatrixRep_repAlgebra` : its action of the Lie algebra
  is the derivative of the matrix representation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The derivative of a matrix representation
- B. The standard constructions
- C. Endomorphisms from matrices
- D. The matter field of a matrix representation

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The derivative of a matrix representation

A continuous representation of `G` by invertible matrices is differentiated by viewing the
matrices as continuous linear maps of Euclidean space, where `GlobalGaugeGroup.derivRep`
applies.

## B. The standard constructions

A character of the gauge group, such as the hypercharge phase, twists a representation by an
integer power. The derivative of a character `χ` at `c` is a number `z` with
`χ (exp (t c)) = exp (t z)`.

## C. Endomorphisms from matrices

The target space of a field is `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`, where the gauge group acts on the internal
index `ι` and the Lorentz group on `S`. A matrix on `ι` then acts on `V` with `S` untouched.
On a normed target space it acts by a continuous linear map, and a matrix representation
becomes a continuous representation on `V`.

## D. The matter field of a matrix representation

A matrix representation `ρ` gives a matter field on any normed target space
`V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`, with the gauge group acting by `ρ` on the internal index and the Lorentz
group on `S`. Its action of the Lie algebra is the derivative of `ρ`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.unitsMapHom
declarations.doc: The continuous homomorphism of unit groups induced by a continuous monoid homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def unitsMapHom {M N : Type} [Monoid M] [Monoid N] [TopologicalSpace M]
    [TopologicalSpace N] (f : M →* N) (hf : Continuous f) : Mˣ →ₜ* Nˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.matrixCLM
declarations.doc:
The algebra map from complex matrices to the continuous linear endomorphisms of Euclidean
space, a matrix acting on vectors.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def matrixCLM :
    Matrix ι ι ℂ →ₐ[ℂ] (EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →L[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.matrixCLM_injective
declarations.statement: lemma matrixCLM_injective : Function.Injective (matrixCLM (ι := ι))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.matrixCLM_surjective
declarations.statement: lemma matrixCLM_surjective : Function.Surjective (matrixCLM (ι := ι))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.continuous_matrixCLM
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_matrixCLM : Continuous (matrixCLM (ι := ι))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.matrixCLM_exp_smul
declarations.doc: The map `matrixCLM` commutes with the exponential of a real multiple of a matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma matrixCLM_exp_smul (t : ℝ) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) :
    matrixCLM (exp (t • A)) = exp (t • matrixCLM A)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.clmRep
declarations.doc:
A matrix representation of the global gauge group `G`, as a representation on Euclidean
space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def clmRep (ρ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ) :
    G.group →ₜ* (EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →L[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι)ˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivMat
declarations.doc:
The derivative of a continuous matrix representation `ρ` of the global gauge group. It is the
matrix by which an element `c` of the Lie algebra acts, with
`ρ (exp (t c)) = exp (t derivMat ρ c)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivMat (c : G.lieSubalgebra) : Matrix ι ι ℂ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.matrixCLM_derivMat
declarations.statement:
lemma matrixCLM_derivMat (c : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    matrixCLM (derivMat ρ c) = derivRep (clmRep ρ) c

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.apply_eq_exp_derivMat
declarations.doc:
The matrix representation maps the one-parameter subgroup of a generator `c` to the
exponential of its derivative, `ρ (exp (t c)) = exp (t derivMat ρ c)`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.derivMat_eq_of
declarations.doc:
The derivative of a matrix representation at `c` is the unique matrix `Z` with
`ρ (exp (t c)) = exp (t Z)` for all `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_eq_of {c : G.lieSubalgebra} {Z : Matrix ι ι ℂ}
    (hZ : ∀ (t : ℝ) (g : G.group),
      ((g : GL κ ℂ) : Matrix κ κ ℂ) = exp (t • (c : Matrix κ κ ℂ)) →
        ((ρ g : (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ) : Matrix ι ι ℂ) = exp (t • Z)) :
    derivMat ρ c = Z

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.trivial
declarations.doc:
The trivial representation on one internal index. Every gauge transformation acts as the
identity.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def trivial : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix (Fin 1) (Fin 1) ℂ)ˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.derivMat_trivial
declarations.doc: The derivative of the trivial representation is zero.
declarations.statement: lemma derivMat_trivial (c : G.lieSubalgebra) : derivMat (trivial (G := G)) c = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.kroneckerMonoidHom
declarations.doc: The Kronecker product of matrices, as a monoid homomorphism on pairs.
declarations.statement:
def kroneckerMonoidHom :
    Matrix ι₁ ι₁ ℂ × Matrix ι₂ ι₂ ℂ →* Matrix (ι₁ × ι₂) (ι₁ × ι₂) ℂ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.continuous_kroneckerMonoidHom
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_kroneckerMonoidHom :
    Continuous (kroneckerMonoidHom (ι₁ := ι₁) (ι₂ := ι₂))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.kron
declarations.doc:
The Kronecker product of two matrix representations, acting on the product of their
internal indices.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def kron (ρ₁ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι₁ ι₁ ℂ)ˣ) (ρ₂ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι₂ ι₂ ℂ)ˣ) :
    G.group →ₜ* (Matrix (ι₁ × ι₂) (ι₁ × ι₂) ℂ)ˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.kron_val
declarations.doc:
A gauge transformation acts on the Kronecker product by the Kronecker product of its two
actions.
declarations.statement:
lemma kron_val (ρ₁ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι₁ ι₁ ℂ)ˣ) (ρ₂ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι₂ ι₂ ℂ)ˣ)
    (g : G.group) :
    ((kron ρ₁ ρ₂ g : (Matrix (ι₁ × ι₂) (ι₁ × ι₂) ℂ)ˣ) : Matrix (ι₁ × ι₂) (ι₁ × ι₂) ℂ) =
      (ρ₁ g : Matrix ι₁ ι₁ ℂ) ⊗ₖ (ρ₂ g : Matrix ι₂ ι₂ ℂ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.derivMat_kron
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the Kronecker product of two representations is the Kronecker sum of
their derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_kron (ρ₁ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι₁ ι₁ ℂ)ˣ) (ρ₂ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι₂ ι₂ ℂ)ˣ)
    (c : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    derivMat (kron ρ₁ ρ₂) c =
      derivMat ρ₁ c ⊗ₖ (1 : Matrix ι₂ ι₂ ℂ) + (1 : Matrix ι₁ ι₁ ℂ) ⊗ₖ derivMat ρ₂ c

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.scalarUnits
declarations.doc: The scalar matrices, as a homomorphism of unit groups from the nonzero complex numbers.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def scalarUnits (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
    ℂˣ →* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.continuous_scalarUnits
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_scalarUnits (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] :
    Continuous (scalarUnits ι)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.mul_scalarUnits_comm
declarations.doc: Scalar matrices commute with every invertible matrix.
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_scalarUnits_comm (U : (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ) (z : ℂˣ) :
    U * scalarUnits ι z = scalarUnits ι z * U

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.charge
declarations.doc:
The twist of a matrix representation `ρ` by the `n`-th power of a character `χ`. A gauge
transformation `g` acts by `χ(g)ⁿ ρ(g)`. This is how a field of charge `n` under a `U(1)`
factor is built from its neutral part.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def charge (n : ℤ) (χ : G.group →ₜ* ℂˣ) (ρ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ) :
    G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.charge_val
declarations.doc:
A gauge transformation acts on the charge twist by the scalar `χ(g)ⁿ` times its action
on `ρ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma charge_val (n : ℤ) (χ : G.group →ₜ* ℂˣ) (ρ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ) (g : G.group) :
    ((charge n χ ρ g : (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ) : Matrix ι ι ℂ) =
      ((χ g ^ n : ℂˣ) : ℂ) • (ρ g : Matrix ι ι ℂ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.derivMat_charge
declarations.doc:
The derivative of the charge twist. If `z` is the derivative of the character `χ` at `c`,
that is `χ (exp (t c)) = exp (t z)`, the derivative of the twist is `dρ + (n z) 1`.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivMat_charge (n : ℤ) (χ : G.group →ₜ* ℂˣ) (ρ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ)
    {c : G.lieSubalgebra} {z : ℂ}
    (hχ : ∀ (t : ℝ) (g : G.group),
      ((g : GL κ ℂ) : Matrix κ κ ℂ) = exp (t • (c : Matrix κ κ ℂ)) →
        ((χ g : ℂˣ) : ℂ) = Complex.exp (t * z)) :
    derivMat (charge n χ ρ) c = derivMat ρ c + ((n : ℂ) * z) • (1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEndAlgHom
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the target space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)` defined by a complex matrix on
the internal index, as an algebra map.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def valEndAlgHom : Matrix ι ι ℂ →ₐ[ℂ] Module.End ℂ V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd
declarations.doc:
The endomorphism of the target space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)` defined by a complex matrix on
the internal index, with the Lorentz factor untouched.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def valEnd (B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : V →ₗ[ℂ] V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma valEnd_apply (B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (d : V) :
    valEnd e B d = e.symm (LinearMap.lTensor S (Matrix.toLin' B) (e d))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_apply_symm_tmul
declarations.doc: A matrix on the internal index acts on a pure tensor through its action on the vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma valEnd_apply_symm_tmul (B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (s : S) (v : ι → ℂ) :
    valEnd e B (e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)) = e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] (B.mulVec v))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_add
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_add (A B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : valEnd e (A + B) = valEnd e A + valEnd e B

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_smul
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_smul (z : ℂ) (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : valEnd e (z • A) = z • valEnd e A

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_zero
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_zero : valEnd e (0 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) = 0

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_neg
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_neg (A : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : valEnd e (-A) = -valEnd e A

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_multiset_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma valEnd_multiset_sum (m : Multiset (Matrix ι ι ℂ)) :
    valEnd e m.sum = (m.map (valEnd e)).sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_mul
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_mul (A B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) : valEnd e (A * B) = valEnd e A ∘ₗ valEnd e B

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_one
declarations.statement: lemma valEnd_one : valEnd e (1 : Matrix ι ι ℂ) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.repLorentz
declarations.doc:
The Lorentz action on the target space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`, the given action on the Lorentz
factor `S` transported through the identification.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repLorentz (ρ : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) S) : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) V

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.repLorentz_apply_symm_tmul
declarations.doc: The Lorentz action on a pure tensor acts on the Lorentz factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma repLorentz_apply_symm_tmul (ρ : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) S) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ)) (s : S)
    (v : ι → ℂ) : repLorentz e ρ Λ (e.symm (s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)) = e.symm (ρ Λ s ⊗ₜ[ℂ] v)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEnd_comm_repLorentz
declarations.doc:
A matrix on the internal index commutes with the Lorentz action, since the two act on
different tensor factors. This is how the gauge action of a field commutes with its Lorentz
action.
declarations.statement:
lemma valEnd_comm_repLorentz (ρ : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) S) (B : Matrix ι ι ℂ) (Λ : SL(2,ℂ))
    (v : V) : valEnd e B (repLorentz e ρ Λ v) = repLorentz e ρ Λ (valEnd e B v)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEndCLM
declarations.doc:
A matrix on the internal index, as a continuous linear endomorphism of a normed target
space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def valEndCLM : Matrix ι ι ℂ →ₐ[ℂ] (V →L[ℂ] V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.continuous_valEndCLM
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_valEndCLM : Continuous (valEndCLM e)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatrixRep.valEndRep
declarations.doc:
The continuous representation of the global gauge group on `V` by the matrices of a matrix
representation on the internal index.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def valEndRep (ρ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ) : G.group →ₜ* (V →L[ℂ] V)ˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.ofMatrixRep
declarations.doc:
The matter field of a matrix representation `ρ`, on a target space `V ≃ S ⊗ (ι → ℂ)`.
The global gauge group acts by `ρ` on the internal index and the Lorentz group through
`repL` on `S`. The field has mass weight `w` and statistics `σ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def ofMatrixRep (ρ : G.group →ₜ* (Matrix ι ι ℂ)ˣ)
    (repL : Representation ℂ SL(2,ℂ) S) (w : ℕ) (σ : FieldStatistic) : G.MatterField

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRep_ofMatrixRep
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra representation of the matter field of a matrix representation is the
derivative of the matrix representation, acting on the internal index.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRep_ofMatrixRep (c : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    lieAlgebraRep (ofMatrixRep e ρ repL w σ) c = valEndCLM e (derivMat ρ c)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.ofMatrixRep_repAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The action of the Lie algebra on the matter field of a matrix representation is the
derivative of the representation, acting on the internal index.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofMatrixRep_repAlgebra (c : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    (ofMatrixRep e ρ repL w σ).repAlgebra c = valEnd e (derivMat ρ c)

modules.title: The direct sum of a finite family of matter fields
modules.doc:
A finite family of matter fields of one mass weight and statistics as a single matter field.

## i. Overview

`prod` sums two matter fields of the same mass weight and statistics. This file
does the same for a finite family `M : ι → G.MatterField`, producing a single matter
field valued in `∀ i, (M i).V`. It is the operation that turns the several species of a
theory into one field. The fifteen fermionic multiplets of the Standard Model become one
fermion field, carried by `GaugeFieldData.fermionMatterField`.

The binary and indexed versions are the same construction with `LinearMap.prodMap`
replaced by `LinearMap.piMap` and `jetProdEquiv` by `jetPiEquiv`, so the proofs run in
parallel. The representation of the global gauge group is the componentwise one, built as
a continuous homomorphism into the units of the continuous linear maps of the product, and
the infinitesimal and jet gauge actions are derived from it. As in the binary case, the
direct sum is represented by one `MatterField`, which has one mass weight and one
statistic, so the summands must share both. The caller supplies the common values `w` and
`σ`, together with proofs that every summand has them, so the direct sum of an empty family
also has a definite weight and statistics.

Finiteness of `ι` is essential and not merely convenient. `jetPiEquiv`, the
identification of the jets of the product with the product of the jets through which the
jet gauge action is defined, exists only for a finite index type, and finite dimensionality
of the value space would fail for an infinite family in any case.

## ii. Key results

- `repPiUnits` : the componentwise representation of the global gauge group.
- `pi` : the direct sum of a finite family of matter fields of one mass weight and one
  statistic.
- `lieAlgebraRep_pi` : the Lie algebra acts on the direct sum index by index.
- `pi_repAlgebra` and `pi_repJet` : the derived infinitesimal and jet gauge actions are the
  index-by-index ones, `repAlgebraPi` and `repJetPi`.
- `repJetPi_smul` : the jet action is fibrewise, as each summand is.
- `lTensor_proj_repJetPi` : the projection onto a summand intertwines it with that summand's
  own action.
- `repCoeff_repJetPi` : its base-point Taylor coefficients are the family of those of the
  summands.
- `fieldDerivSpacePiEquiv` : the component space of the direct sum is the family of the
  component spaces of the summands.
- `fieldDerivSpacePiEquiv_symm_single` : a summand sits inside it as the pullback along
  the projection onto that summand.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The direct sum of a finite family of matter fields
- B. Diagonal maps of an indexed product
- C. The index-by-index gauge actions
- D. The derived actions of the direct sum
- E. The component space of the direct sum

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The direct sum of a finite family of matter fields

The direct sum acts index by index, so its representation of the global gauge group is the
componentwise one, built as a continuous homomorphism into the units of the continuous linear
maps of the product.

## B. Diagonal maps of an indexed product

Every piece of data of the direct sum acts index by index, that is through
`LinearMap.piMap`. The four facts about that construction used below — that it is
additive, negative-preserving and multiset-sum-preserving in the family, and that it
composes index by index — all hold because `piMap` is evaluated pointwise, so each is a
single `LinearMap.ext`.

## C. The index-by-index gauge actions

The jet gauge action and the infinitesimal gauge action of the direct sum are the families of
those of the summands, and the second generates the first.

## D. The derived actions of the direct sum

The infinitesimal and jet gauge actions that the direct sum inherits from its representation
are the index-by-index ones.

## E. The component space of the direct sum

The direct sum was built so that the several species of a theory can be treated as one
field. Nothing is lost in doing so at the level of component functions either: the
symbols `∂_s ψ_α` and `∂_s ψ̄_α` of the summed field are exactly the families, over the
index, of the symbols of the summands. This is the component-space image of the
identification `jetPiEquiv` that defines the summed jet action, and it is the finite
direct sum case of `FieldDerivSpace.piEquiv`.

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repPi
declarations.doc:
The product of a family of representations, acting index by index. This is the
indexed analogue of `Representation.prod`, which Mathlib provides only in the binary
case.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repPi {W : ι → Type} [∀ i, AddCommGroup (W i)]
    [∀ i, Module ℂ (W i)] {H : Type} [Group H] (ρ : ∀ i, Representation ℂ H (W i)) :
    Representation ℂ H (∀ i, W i)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.piMapRingHom
declarations.doc:
The family of continuous linear maps `f i` as the continuous linear map of the product acting
index by index, a ring homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def piMapRingHom :
    (∀ i, (M i).V →L[ℂ] (M i).V) →+* ((∀ i, (M i).V) →L[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.piMapRingHom_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma piMapRingHom_apply (f : ∀ i, (M i).V →L[ℂ] (M i).V) (v : ∀ i, (M i).V) (i : ι) :
    piMapRingHom M f v i = f i (v i)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.continuous_piMapRingHom
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_piMapRingHom : Continuous (piMapRingHom M)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repPiUnits
declarations.doc:
The direct sum `g ↦ (ρ_{M i}(g))ᵢ` of the representations of a family of matrix matter
fields.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repPiUnits : G.group →ₜ* ((∀ i, (M i).V) →L[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V))ˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repPiUnits_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repPiUnits_apply (g : G.group) :
    ((repPiUnits M g : ((∀ i, (M i).V) →L[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V))ˣ) :
        (∀ i, (M i).V) →L[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V)) =
      piMapRingHom M fun i => ((M i).rep g : (M i).V →L[ℂ] (M i).V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi
declarations.doc:
The direct sum of a finite family of matter fields with common mass weight `w` and
common statistics `σ`, given with proofs that every summand has them. It is one field
valued in `∀ i, (M i).V`, of weight `w` and statistics `σ`, with every action acting index
by index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def pi (w : ℕ) (_h : ∀ i, (M i).massWeight = w) (σ : FieldStatistic)
    (_hσ : ∀ i, (M i).statistic = σ) : G.MatterField

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi_repLorentz
declarations.statement: lemma pi_repLorentz : (pi M w h σ hσ).repLorentz = repPi fun i => (M i).repLorentz

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi_massWeight
declarations.statement: lemma pi_massWeight : (pi M w h σ hσ).massWeight = w

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi_statistic
declarations.statement: lemma pi_statistic : (pi M w h σ hσ).statistic = σ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJetPi
declarations.doc:
The jet gauge action of an indexed direct sum, the family of actions read
through the identification of the jets of `∀ i, (M i).V` with the family of jets.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repJetPi :
    Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJetPi_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetPi_apply (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V)) :
    repJetPi M U z = (jetPiEquiv fun i => (M i).V).symm
      (fun i => (M i).repJet U (jetPiEquiv (fun i => (M i).V) z i))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJetPi_smul
declarations.doc:
The jet gauge action of an indexed direct sum is fibrewise. It acts index by
index, and each summand is fibrewise, so multiplication by a scalar jet passes through
the splitting untouched. This is the statement `repJet_smul` for `pi`, stated
separately so that it can be used without fixing a common mass weight.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetPi_smul (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V)) :
    repJetPi M U (χ • z) = χ • repJetPi M U z

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lTensor_proj_repJetPi
declarations.doc:
A summand is a subrepresentation of the jet gauge action of the direct sum. The
projection onto the value space of one summand, applied to the jets, intertwines the
summed action with that summand's own, since the summed action is the family of the actions,
and reading off a summand of the jets is the projection on the value factor.
declarations.statement:
lemma lTensor_proj_repJetPi (i : ι) (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) :
    (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.proj i)).comp (repJetPi M U)
      = ((M i).repJet U).comp (LinearMap.lTensor SpaceTimeAlgebra (LinearMap.proj i))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repAlgebraPi
declarations.doc:
The infinitesimal action of an indexed direct sum, the family of actions, one on
each summand.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repAlgebraPi :
    G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] (∀ i, (M i).V) →ₗ[ℂ] (∀ i, (M i).V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repAlgebraPi_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repAlgebraPi_apply (c : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    repAlgebraPi M c = LinearMap.piMap fun i => (M i).repAlgebra c

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_repJetPi
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the summed jet action are the family of the
coefficients of the summands, since `jetOfConstant`, `jetIteratedDeriv` and `jetEval` all act
index by index through `jetPiEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_repJetPi (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff (repJetPi M) U x =
      LinearMap.piMap fun i => GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff (M i).repJet U x

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.isInfinitesimalActionOf_repAlgebraPi
declarations.doc:
The index-by-index algebra action generates the index-by-index jet action. Both
laws of `IsInfinitesimalActionOf` are the corresponding laws of the summands, read
through `repCoeff_repJetPi`, since `piMap` is additive in the family and composes index
by index.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf_repAlgebraPi :
    G.IsInfinitesimalActionOf (repAlgebraPi M) (repJetPi M)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRep_pi
declarations.doc: The Lie algebra acts on a direct sum index by index.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRep_pi (X : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    lieAlgebraRep (pi M w h σ hσ) X = piMapRingHom M fun i => lieAlgebraRep (M i) X

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi_repAlgebra
declarations.doc: The Lie algebra of a direct sum acts index by index.
declarations.statement: lemma pi_repAlgebra : (pi M w h σ hσ).repAlgebra = repAlgebraPi M

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.pi_repJet
declarations.doc: The gauge jets act on a direct sum index by index.
declarations.statement: lemma pi_repJet : (pi M w h σ hσ).repJet = repJetPi M

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.fieldDerivSpacePiEquiv
declarations.doc:
The component space of a direct sum of matter fields splits. A component function
of `pi M w h σ hσ` is exactly a family, one component function per summand. Both
halves split by `FieldDerivSpace.fstPiEquiv` and `FieldDerivSpace.sndPiEquiv`, and
the pair of families is reassembled into a family of pairs index by index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def fieldDerivSpacePiEquiv :
    FieldDerivSpace (pi M w h σ hσ) ≃ₗ[ℂ] ∀ i, FieldDerivSpace (M i)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.fieldDerivSpacePiEquiv_symm_single
declarations.doc:
The summand of one species is the pullback along the projection onto it. A
component function of the summand `i`, placed in the family and read back as a component
function of the direct sum, is that function precomposed with the projection onto the
summand. This is what identifies the splitting with the species inclusions of a direct
sum of component spaces.
declarations.statement:
lemma fieldDerivSpacePiEquiv_symm_single (i : ι) (x : FieldDerivSpace (M i)) :
    (fieldDerivSpacePiEquiv M w h σ hσ).symm (Pi.single i x)
      = FieldDerivSpace.comap
        (LinearMap.proj (φ := fun i => (M i).V) i :
          (pi M w h σ hσ).V →ₗ[ℂ] (M i).V) x

modules.title: The direct sum of two matter fields
modules.doc:
Two matter fields of one mass weight and statistics as a single matter field.

## i. Overview

Two matter fields of a gauge theory with the same mass weight and the same declared
statistics combine into one, valued in the product of their value spaces. This is the
operation that lets a multiplet be described either as one field or as its summands: three
generations of a fermion type, or the two chiralities of a Dirac field, are the direct sum
of their pieces.

Every piece of data acts componentwise. The Lorentz representation and the infinitesimal
gauge action are `LinearMap.prodMap` of the two; the jet gauge action is the pair of the
two, read through the identification `jetProdEquiv` of the jets of a product with the
product of the jets. The direct sum is one `MatterField`, with one mass weight and one
statistic, so it takes as hypotheses that the two fields have the same mass weight and the
same statistics.

The gauge group acts through `repProd`, a continuous homomorphism into the units of the
continuous linear maps of the product. The infinitesimal and jet gauge actions of the direct
sum are derived from it, and what has to be proved is that they are the componentwise ones,
`prod_repAlgebra` and `prod_repJet`.

## ii. Key results

- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJetProd` : the jet gauge action of a direct sum.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repAlgebraProd` : the infinitesimal gauge action of a direct
  sum.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_repJetProd` : its base-point Taylor coefficients are
  the pair of those of the summands.
- `GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prod` : the direct sum of two matter fields of the same mass
  weight and statistics.
- `FieldDerivSpace.prodEquiv` : the component space of a direct sum splits.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The direct sum of two matter fields
- B. The componentwise gauge actions
- C. The derived actions of the direct sum
- D. The component space of a direct sum

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The direct sum of two matter fields

Two matter fields of the same mass weight and statistics combine into one, valued in the
product of their value spaces. The global gauge group and the Lorentz group act componentwise,
and the weight and statistics are those of the first summand.

## B. The componentwise gauge actions

Every other piece of data acts componentwise. The infinitesimal gauge action is
`LinearMap.prodMap` of the two, and the jet gauge action is read through the identification
`jetProdEquiv` of the jets of a product with the product of the jets. What has to be checked
is the last field, that the componentwise algebra action still generates the componentwise
jet action.

## C. The derived actions of the direct sum

The Lie algebra action and the jet gauge action that the direct sum inherits from its
representation are the componentwise ones.
## D. The component space of a direct sum

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prodMapRingHom
declarations.doc:
The pair of continuous linear maps `(f, g)` as the continuous linear map `f × g` of the
product, a ring homomorphism.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def prodMapRingHom :
    (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V) × (N.V →L[ℂ] N.V) →+* ((M.V × N.V) →L[ℂ] (M.V × N.V))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.continuous_prodMapRingHom
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_prodMapRingHom : Continuous (prodMapRingHom M N)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repProd
declarations.doc: The direct sum `g ↦ ρ_M(g) × ρ_N(g)` of the representations of two matter fields.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repProd : G.group →ₜ* ((M.V × N.V) →L[ℂ] (M.V × N.V))ˣ

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repProd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repProd_apply (g : G.group) :
    ((repProd M N g : ((M.V × N.V) →L[ℂ] (M.V × N.V))ˣ) : (M.V × N.V) →L[ℂ] (M.V × N.V)) =
      ((M.rep g : (M.V →L[ℂ] M.V)ˣ) : M.V →L[ℂ] M.V).prodMap
        ((N.rep g : (N.V →L[ℂ] N.V)ˣ) : N.V →L[ℂ] N.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prod
declarations.doc:
The direct sum of two matter fields of the same mass weight and statistics, as one
field valued in `M.V × N.V`, on which the global gauge group and the Lorentz group act
componentwise, with the weight and statistics of `M`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def prod (_h : M.massWeight = N.massWeight) (_hσ : M.statistic = N.statistic) :
    G.MatterField

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prod_V
declarations.statement: lemma prod_V : (prod M N h hσ).V = (M.V × N.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prod_repLorentz
declarations.statement: lemma prod_repLorentz : (prod M N h hσ).repLorentz = M.repLorentz.prod N.repLorentz

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prod_massWeight
declarations.statement: lemma prod_massWeight : (prod M N h hσ).massWeight = M.massWeight

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prod_statistic
declarations.statement: lemma prod_statistic : (prod M N h hσ).statistic = M.statistic

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJetProd
declarations.doc:
The jet gauge action of a direct sum, the two actions read through the
identification of the jets of `M.V × N.V` with the pair of jets.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def repJetProd :
    Representation ℂ G.gaugeJetGroup (SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (M.V × N.V))

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJetProd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetProd_apply (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (M.V × N.V)) :
    repJetProd M N U z =
      jetProdEquiv.symm (M.repJet U (jetProdEquiv z).1, N.repJet U (jetProdEquiv z).2)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repAlgebraProd
declarations.doc: The infinitesimal action of a direct sum, the two actions on the two summands.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def repAlgebraProd : G.lieSubalgebra →ₗ[ℝ] (M.V × N.V) →ₗ[ℂ] (M.V × N.V)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repAlgebraProd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma repAlgebraProd_apply (c : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    repAlgebraProd M N c = (M.repAlgebra c).prodMap (N.repAlgebra c)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repCoeff_repJetProd
declarations.doc:
The base-point Taylor coefficients of the summed jet action are the pair of the
coefficients of the summands, since `jetOfConstant`, `jetIteratedDeriv` and `jetEval` all act
componentwise through `jetProdEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma repCoeff_repJetProd (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (x : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff (repJetProd M N) U x =
      (GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff M.repJet U x).prodMap
        (GlobalGaugeGroup.repCoeff N.repJet U x)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.repJetProd_smul
declarations.doc: The componentwise jet action is fibrewise.
declarations.statement:
lemma repJetProd_smul (U : G.gaugeJetGroup) (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra)
    (z : SpaceTimeAlgebra ⊗[ℂ] (M.V × N.V)) : repJetProd M N U (χ • z) = χ • repJetProd M N
      U z

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.isInfinitesimalActionOf_repAlgebraProd
declarations.doc:
The componentwise algebra action generates the componentwise jet action. Both laws
of `IsInfinitesimalActionOf` are the corresponding laws of the summands, read through
`repCoeff_repJetProd`, since `prodMap` is additive in both slots at once and composes
componentwise.
declarations.statement:
lemma isInfinitesimalActionOf_repAlgebraProd :
    G.IsInfinitesimalActionOf (repAlgebraProd M N) (repJetProd M N)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.lieAlgebraRep_prod
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra acts on a direct sum componentwise, since the exponential of `dρ_M(X) × dρ_N(X)`
is the pair of exponentials.
declarations.statement:
lemma lieAlgebraRep_prod (X : G.lieSubalgebra) :
    lieAlgebraRep (prod M N h hσ) X = (lieAlgebraRep M X).prodMap (lieAlgebraRep N X)

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prod_repAlgebra
declarations.doc: The Lie algebra of a direct sum acts componentwise.
declarations.statement: lemma prod_repAlgebra : (prod M N h hσ).repAlgebra = repAlgebraProd M N

declarations.name: GlobalGaugeGroup.MatterField.prod_repJet
declarations.doc:
The gauge jets act on a direct sum componentwise, since both actions are generated by the
componentwise action of the Lie algebra, and agree at the base point.
declarations.statement: lemma prod_repJet : (prod M N h hσ).repJet = repJetProd M N

declarations.name: FieldDerivSpace.prodEquiv
declarations.doc:
The component space of a direct sum splits. The component functions of the direct
sum `M.prod N h hσ` are those of `M` together with those of `N`, since the dual and the conjugate
both distribute over the finite product, and the derivative label is untouched. Only the
value spaces enter, so the hypotheses `h` and `hσ` are carried along and not used.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def _root_.FieldDerivSpace.prodEquiv (M N : G.MatterField)
    (h : M.massWeight = N.massWeight) (hσ : M.statistic = N.statistic) :
    FieldDerivSpace (M.prod N h hσ) ≃ₗ[ℂ] FieldDerivSpace M × FieldDerivSpace N

modules.title: Green operators and causally supported fields
modules.doc:
Retarded and advanced Green operators of a local operator.

## i. Overview

Retarded and advanced Green operators of a local operator. Fields with spacelike compact, future or
past compact support.

## ii. Key results

- `spacelikeCompactFields` : Admissible fields with support contained in the causal hull of a
  compact set.
- `futureSupportedFields` : Fields supported in the future of a compact set.
- `futureSupportedOperator` : Restrict the field equation to fields supported to the future of
  compact sets.
- `spacelikeCompactSolution` : Spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
- `spacelikeCompactOperator` : The field equation restricted to spacelike-compact admissible fields.
- `RetardedGreenOperator` : A retarded two-sided inverse on compact sources with future causal
  support.
- `AdvancedGreenOperator` : An advanced two-sided inverse on compact sources with past causal
  support.
- `GreenOperators` : A pair of causal Green inverses for the same field equation.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Linear field equations and compact sources
- B. Retarded and advanced Green operators
- C. Past-compact and future-compact support

## iv. References

None.

## A. Linear field equations and compact sources

- `spacelikeCompactFields` : Admissible fields with support contained in the causal hull of a
  compact set.
- `futureSupportedFields` : Fields supported in the future of a compact set.
- `futureSupportedOperator` : Restrict the field equation to fields supported to the future of
  compact sets.
- `spacelikeCompactSolution` : Spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
- `spacelikeCompactOperator` : The field equation restricted to spacelike-compact admissible fields.

Lemmas: `operator_mem_futureSupportedFields`, `operator_mem_spacelikeCompactFields`,
`futureSupportedFields_le_spacelikeCompactFields`, `pastSupportedFields_le_spacelikeCompactFields`.

## B. Retarded and advanced Green operators

- `RetardedGreenOperator` : A retarded two-sided inverse on compact sources with future causal
  support.
- `AdvancedGreenOperator` : An advanced two-sided inverse on compact sources with past causal
  support.
- `GreenOperators` : A pair of causal Green inverses for the same field equation.
- `reverse` : Reverse time orientation and exchange the Green operators.

## C. Past-compact and future-compact support

- `pastCompactFields` : The full past-compact admissible source and field space.
- `pastCompactOperator` : The field equation restricted to the full past-compact support class.

Lemmas: `operator_mem_pastCompactFields`, `futureSupportedFields_le_pastCompactFields`.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.RetardedGreenOperator
declarations.doc: A retarded two-sided inverse on compact sources with future causal support.
declarations.statement:
structure RetardedGreenOperator (C : CausalRelation M) (P : LocalOperator S) where
  /-- Compact sources produce admissible fields without a compact support requirement. -/
  toLinearMap : P.compactSources →ₗ[𝕜] S
  /-- The response solves the prescribed sourced equation. -/
  solves : ∀ f, P.operator (toLinearMap f) = f.val
  /-- Compact fields are recovered from their equation of motion. -/
  comp_operator : ∀ f, toLinearMap (P.compactOperator f) = f.val
  /-- Retarded propagation is supported in the source's causal future. -/
  support : ∀ f, tsupport (toLinearMap f : M → V) ⊆
    C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

  /-- Compact sources produce unrestricted admissible fields. -/
  toLinearMap : P.compactSources →ₗ[𝕜] S
  /-- The response solves the prescribed sourced equation. -/
  solves : ∀ f, P.operator (toLinearMap f) = f.val
  /-- Compact fields are recovered from their equation of motion. -/
  comp_operator : ∀ f, toLinearMap (P.compactOperator f) = f.val
  /-- Advanced propagation is supported in the source's causal past. -/
  support : ∀ f, tsupport (toLinearMap f : M → V) ⊆
    C.causalPast (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

modules.title: The causal propagator and causal uniqueness
modules.doc:
The difference of the retarded and advanced response solves the homogeneous equation.

## i. Overview

The difference of the retarded and advanced response solves the homogeneous equation. Uniqueness of
one-sided solutions follows from the support of the response.

## ii. Key results

- `causalPropagator` : The causal propagator uses the sign convention retarded minus advanced.
- `toSolutionSpace` : The causal propagator with its proven solution-space codomain.
- `HasCausalCutoffs` : Temporal cutoff splitting of spacelike-compact admissible fields.
- `eq_of_local_truncations` : Compact truncations agreeing with the same field in the observation's
  causal past give identical retarded responses.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The causal propagator and compact source kernel
- B. Causal splitting and one-sided uniqueness
- C. Local field equations and causal agreement

## iv. References

None.

## A. The causal propagator and compact source kernel

- `causalPropagator` : The causal propagator uses the sign convention retarded minus advanced.
- `toSolutionSpace` : The causal propagator with its proven solution-space codomain.

Lemmas: `causalPropagator_solves`, `causalPropagator_comp_operator`, `causalPropagator_support`,
`causalPropagator_mem_solution`, `range_compactOperator_le_ker`, `compactOperator_injective`,
`retarded_compact_of_causalPropagator_eq_zero`, `mem_range_of_causalPropagator_eq_zero`,
`causalPropagator_ker`, `toSolutionSpace_ker`.

## B. Causal splitting and one-sided uniqueness

- `HasCausalCutoffs` : Temporal cutoff splitting of spacelike-compact admissible fields.

Lemmas: `futureSupported_unique`, `retarded_mem_futureSupportedFields`,
`advanced_mem_futureSupportedFields_reverse`, `retarded_eq_of_futureSupported`,
`advanced_eq_of_pastSupported`.

## C. Local field equations and causal agreement

Lemmas: `eq_zero_of_no_causal_source`, `eq_of_no_causal_difference`, `eq_of_local_truncations`.

Equations of motion are in the kernel of the causal propagator.
The reverse inclusion requires causal compactness and additional arguments.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.causalPropagator_ker

The proof uses compact causal diamonds rather than an assumed exactness hypothesis.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.RetardedGreenOperator.eq_of_local_truncations
declarations.doc:
Compact truncations agreeing with the same field in the observation's causal past give
identical retarded responses. Equality is needed as germs to control topological support.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_local_truncations (f g : P.compactSources) (u : S) {x : M}
    (hf : ∀ y : M, C.Precedes y x → (f.val : M → V) =ᶠ[𝓝 y] (u : M → V))

    (G.toLinearMap f : M → V) x = (G.toLinearMap g : M → V) x

modules.title: Localization and extension of retarded responses
modules.doc:
A past compact source is cut off to compact pieces.

## i. Overview

A past compact source is cut off to compact pieces. The retarded responses to the pieces define a
response to the whole source.

## ii. Key results

- `PastLocalization` : The geometric and cutoff data for localizing past-compact sections to compact
  test sections.
- `sourceAt` : Each source has a compact truncation adapted to the observation event.
- `retardedValue` : The pointwise retarded response obtained from observation-adapted compact
  truncations.
- `retardedSection` : The glued retarded field as an admissible section.
- `retardedExtension` : The two-sided linear Green extension to all past-compact sources.
- `truncationRadius` : A positive ball radius enclosing the relevant compact part of the source.
- `truncationBump` : A smooth compact bump equal to one near the relevant source intersection.
- `bumpTruncate` : A bump truncation is a compact admissible source, not an assumed larger-support
  solution.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Compact localization of past-compact sources
- B. Constructing Green extensions by local compact truncation
- C. Compact source localization by smooth bump functions

## iv. References

None.

## A. Compact localization of past-compact sources

- `PastLocalization` : The geometric and cutoff data for localizing past-compact sections to compact
  test sections.
- `sourceAt` : Each source has a compact truncation adapted to the observation event.
- `retardedValue` : The pointwise retarded response obtained from observation-adapted compact
  truncations.

Lemmas: `mem_past_bound`, `sourceAt_agrees`, `predecessor_mem_past_bound`,
`retardedValue_eq_on_past_bound`, `retardedValue_eventuallyEq`, `retardedValue_mem`,
`homogeneous_eq_zero`, `pastCompactOperator_injective`.

## B. Constructing Green extensions by local compact truncation

- `retardedSection` : The glued retarded field as an admissible section.
- `retardedExtension` : The two-sided linear Green extension to all past-compact sources.

Lemmas: `retardedSection_solves`, `retardedValue_support`, `retardedSection_support`,
`retardedSection_mem_pastCompactFields`, `pastCompactOperator_surjective`,
`retardedExtension_solves`, `retardedExtension_eq_section`, `retardedExtension_support`,
`pastCompact_unique`, `futureSupportedOperator_injective` and more.

## C. Compact source localization by smooth bump functions

- `truncationRadius` : A positive ball radius enclosing the relevant compact part of the source.
- `truncationBump` : A smooth compact bump equal to one near the relevant source intersection.
- `bumpTruncate` : A bump truncation is a compact admissible source, not an assumed larger-support
  solution.
- `ofBumpFunctions` : Construct all local compact-source truncation data from bump stability and
  causal topology.

Lemmas: `truncationRadius_pos`, `mem_truncation_ball`, `bumpTruncate_support`,
`bumpTruncate_agrees`.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization
declarations.doc: The geometric and cutoff data for localizing past-compact sections to compact test sections.
declarations.statement:
structure PastLocalization (C : CausalRelation M) (P : LocalOperator S) where
  /-- Compact observation bounds whose causal pasts are neighborhoods. -/
  bound : M → Set M
  /-- Every observation bound is compact. -/
  bound_compact : ∀ x, IsCompact (bound x)
  /-- The causal past of an observation bound contains a neighborhood of the event. -/
  bound_neighborhood : ∀ x, C.causalPast (bound x) ∈ 𝓝 x
  /-- Admissible fields glue from local representatives. -/
  local_fields : IsLocalFieldSpace S
  /-- The causal future of a compact set is closed. -/
  closed_compact_future : ∀ K : Set M, IsCompact K → IsClosed (C.causalFuture K)
  /-- Compact source truncation near the causal past of a compact observation set. -/
  truncate : P.pastCompactFields C → (K : Set M) → IsCompact K → P.compactSources
  /-- Truncation agrees as germs with the source throughout that causal past. -/
  truncate_agrees : ∀ f K hK x, x ∈ C.causalPast K →
    ((truncate f K hK).val : M → V) =ᶠ[𝓝 x] (f.val : M → V)
  /-- Compact truncation introduces no support outside the original source. -/
  truncate_support : ∀ f K hK,
    tsupport ((truncate f K hK).val : M → V) ⊆ tsupport (f.val : M → V)

declarations.statement: lemma mem_past_bound (x : M) : x ∈ C.causalPast (L.bound x)

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedValue_eq_on_past_bound
declarations.doc:
Retarded responses of different admissible truncations agree locally.
No limit or convergence of the truncation family is required.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedValue_eq_on_past_bound (G : RetardedGreenOperator C P)
    (f : P.pastCompactFields C) (x : M) {y : M}

    L.retardedValue G f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] (G.toLinearMap (L.sourceAt f x) : M → V)

declarations.statement:

One-sided uniqueness is a consequence of local compact truncation and the compact Green

declarations.statement:

declarations.statement: def retardedSection (f : P.pastCompactFields C) : S

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedSection_solves
declarations.doc: The glued field solves the full past-compact source equation.
declarations.statement:

    P.operator (L.retardedSection G f) = f.val

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedValue_support
declarations.doc: Pointwise support of the glued response lies in the future of the source.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedValue_support (f : P.pastCompactFields C) :
    Function.support (L.retardedValue G f) ⊆ C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedSection_support
declarations.doc: The topological support bound follows from the closed future of a past-compact source.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedSection_support (f : P.pastCompactFields C) :
    tsupport (L.retardedSection G f : M → V) ⊆ C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedSection_mem_pastCompactFields
declarations.doc:
Causal support and compact diamonds put the constructed response in the full past-compact
class.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedSection_mem_pastCompactFields (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds)
    (f : P.pastCompactFields C) : L.retardedSection G f ∈ P.pastCompactFields C

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.pastCompactOperator_surjective
declarations.doc: Existence on the larger support class is constructed from local compact responses.
declarations.statement:
lemma pastCompactOperator_surjective (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) :
    Function.Surjective (P.pastCompactOperator C)

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedExtension
declarations.doc: The two-sided linear Green extension to all past-compact sources.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def retardedExtension (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) :
    P.pastCompactFields C ≃ₗ[𝕜] P.pastCompactFields C

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedExtension_solves
declarations.doc: The constructed extension solves the source equation.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedExtension_solves (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) (f : P.pastCompactFields C) :
    P.pastCompactOperator C (L.retardedExtension G hC f) = f

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedExtension_eq_section
declarations.doc: The abstract linear inverse equals the explicitly glued local response.
declarations.statement:
lemma retardedExtension_eq_section (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds)
    (f : P.pastCompactFields C) :
    (L.retardedExtension G hC f).val = L.retardedSection G f

declarations.name: GreenOperator.PastLocalization.retardedExtension_support
declarations.doc: The full past-compact extension retains the sharp causal support bound.
declarations.statement:

modules.title: Smooth spacetime fields as Green operator input
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Smooth fields on spacetime admit past and future localization and temporal cutoffs.

## ii. Key results

- `pastLocalization` : Retarded localization for every admissible field space with local gluing and
  bump stability.
- `futureLocalization` : Advanced localization uses the same field hypotheses and the reversed
  verified causal geometry.
- `smoothPastLocalization` : All past-compact smooth fields admit the compact truncations required
  by the general theory.
- `smoothFutureLocalization` : The same analytic field class supplies advanced localization after
  causal reversal.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Localization of admissible fields in Minkowski spacetime
- B. Localization of smooth spacetime fields
- C. Temporal cutoffs of spacelike-compact smooth fields

## iv. References

None.

## A. Localization of admissible fields in Minkowski spacetime

- `pastLocalization` : Retarded localization for every admissible field space with local gluing and
  bump stability.
- `futureLocalization` : Advanced localization uses the same field hypotheses and the reversed
  verified causal geometry.

## B. Localization of smooth spacetime fields

- `smoothPastLocalization` : All past-compact smooth fields admit the compact truncations required
  by the general theory.
- `smoothFutureLocalization` : The same analytic field class supplies advanced localization after
  causal reversal.

Lemmas: `smoothFields_bumpStable`.

## C. Temporal cutoffs of spacelike-compact smooth fields

Lemmas: `isCompact_causalPast_inter`, `isCompact_causalFuture_inter`, `tsupport_cutoff_subset`,
`tsupport_cutoff_sub_subset`, `smoothHasCausalCutoffs`.

modules.title: Uniqueness and the causal exact sequence
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Existence and uniqueness of retarded solutions and the exact sequence of compact sources and
spacelike compact fields.

## ii. Key results

- `sourceOfCausalSplit` : The compact source obtained from a causal splitting of a homogeneous
  field.
- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotient` : Compact test fields modulo the equation of motion are equivalent to
  spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotientOfLocalization` : Homogeneous spacelike-compact solutions are source
  classes, with one-sided inverse and uniqueness hypotheses discharged by local compact
  constructions.
- `toSpacelikeCompact` : The causal propagator with the support codomain required in the exact
  sequence.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. One-sided uniqueness for weak solutions
- B. Homogeneous solutions as source classes
- C. The causal Green exact sequence
- D. General sourced field equations

## iv. References

None.

## A. One-sided uniqueness for weak solutions

Lemmas: `distribution_eq_zero_of_retarded`.

## B. Homogeneous solutions as source classes

- `sourceOfCausalSplit` : The compact source obtained from a causal splitting of a homogeneous
  field.
- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotient` : Compact test fields modulo the equation of motion are equivalent to
  spacelike-compact homogeneous solutions.
- `solutionSpaceEquivQuotientOfLocalization` : Homogeneous spacelike-compact solutions are source
  classes, with one-sided inverse and uniqueness hypotheses discharged by local compact
  constructions.

Lemmas: `compact_equation_of_causal_split`, `causalPropagator_sourceOfCausalSplit`,
`toSolutionSpace_surjective`, `solutionSpaceEquivQuotient_symm_mk`,
`solutionSpaceEquivQuotient_toSolutionSpace`, `spacelikeCompactOperator_surjective_of_localization`.

## C. The causal Green exact sequence

- `toSpacelikeCompact` : The causal propagator with the support codomain required in the exact
  sequence.

Lemmas: `toSpacelikeCompact_ker`, `exact_compactSources`, `exact_spacelikeCompactFields`,
`causalGreen_exactSequence`.

## D. General sourced field equations

Lemmas: `existsUnique_retardedSolution`, `existsUnique_retardedSolution_of_localization`.

declarations.name: GreenOperator.distribution_eq_zero_of_retarded
declarations.doc:
Compact advanced Green data and causal localization force a retarded weak homogeneous
solution to vanish. The native test model preserves the underlying scalar test fields.
declarations.statement:
lemma distribution_eq_zero_of_retarded
    (e : P.compactSources ≃ₗ[ℝ] _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : Opens E) ℝ ⊤)
    (he : ∀ f : P.compactSources, (e f : E → ℝ) = f.val.val)
    (G : AdvancedGreenOperator C P) (L : PastLocalization C.reverse P)
    (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) (K : Set E) (hK : IsCompact K)
    (T : Distribution (⊤ : Opens E) V ⊤)
    (hT : Distribution.IsVanishingOn T (C.causalFuture K)ᶜ)
    (hzero : ∀ f : P.compactSources, T (e (P.compactOperator f)) = 0) : T = 0

declarations.name: GreenOperator.GreenOperators.causalGreen_exactSequence
declarations.doc:
The full causal Green sequence, including injectivity and terminal surjectivity.
The larger-support inverses and uniqueness are derived from compact Green data and localization.
declarations.statement:
lemma causalGreen_exactSequence
    (Lret : PastLocalization C P) (Ladv : PastLocalization C.reverse P)
    (hC : C.HasCompactCausalDiamonds) (hcut : P.HasCausalCutoffs C) :
    Function.Injective P.compactOperator ∧
      Function.Exact P.compactOperator G.toSpacelikeCompact ∧

      Function.Surjective (P.spacelikeCompactOperator C)

declarations.name: GreenOperator.RetardedGreenOperator.existsUnique_retardedSolution
declarations.doc:
A source has exactly one sharply retarded solution when the future-supported homogeneous
kernel vanishes. Existence follows from the supplied Green operator.
declarations.statement:
lemma existsUnique_retardedSolution
    (huniq : Function.Injective (P.futureSupportedOperator C)) (f : P.compactSources) :
    ∃! u : S, P.operator u = f.val ∧
      tsupport (u : M → V) ⊆ C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

declarations.doc: Local compact-cutoff geometry proves the uniqueness hypothesis of the compact-source theorem.
declarations.statement:

    ∃! u : S, P.operator u = f.val ∧
      tsupport (u : M → V) ⊆ C.causalFuture (tsupport (f.val : M → V))

modules.title: The Klein–Gordon equation
modules.doc:
This file sets up the Klein–Gordon equation on spacetime for smooth fields and for distributions.

## i. Overview

Spacetime is `SpaceTime d` with the speed of light equal to one. The operator `operator m` is the
wave operator plus `m ^ 2` on smooth fields. The mass parameter `m` is any real number. The
operator does not enlarge support, so `equation m` packages it as a local operator. The operator
extends to distributions as `distributionOperator m`. The file `Solution` states the solution.

## ii. Key results

- `operator` : the Klein–Gordon operator on smooth fields.
- `equation` : the Klein–Gordon operator as a local operator.
- `distributionOperator` : the Klein–Gordon operator on distributions.
- `testOperator` : the Klein–Gordon operator on compactly supported smooth test functions.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The operator on smooth fields
- B. The operator on distributions

## iv. References

None.

## A. The operator on smooth fields

`operator m` is `smoothWaveOperator + m ^ 2 • id`. The mass enters as a zeroth order term. The
field type and the dimension are unchanged. `equation m` records that the operator does not
enlarge support.

## B. The operator on distributions

`distributionOperator m` is the wave operator plus `m ^ 2` on `DistributionField d V`. On a test
function it is given by the same operator `testOperator m`, and `distributionOperator_apply`
states this.

declarations.doc: The massive wave operator, with mass measured in inverse spacetime-length units.
declarations.statement: def operator (m : ℝ) : smoothFields d V →ₗ[ℝ] smoothFields d V

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.equation
declarations.doc: Klein–Gordon is a local equation on the existing smooth spacetime field class.
declarations.statement: def equation (m : ℝ) : LocalOperator (smoothFields d V)

declarations.doc: The Klein–Gordon operator on native distributions.
declarations.statement: def distributionOperator (m : ℝ) : DistributionField d V →L[ℝ] DistributionField d V

declarations.name: KleinGordon.Spacetime.distributionOperator_apply
declarations.doc: The positive second-order operator has the same transpose on test functions.
declarations.statement:
lemma distributionOperator_apply (m : ℝ) (T : DistributionField d V)
    (φ : _root_.TestFunction (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (SpaceTime d)) ℝ ⊤) :
    distributionOperator m T φ = T (testOperator m φ)

modules.title: The massive sine evolution through the massless one
modules.doc:
The massive sine evolution is the massless sine evolution plus a Bessel average of the massless
sine evolutions at smaller radii. This holds in every space dimension.

## i. Overview

The massive multiplier is a Bessel average of the massless cosine multipliers
(`Real.integral_besselSq_cos`). So the massive sine evolution is the Bessel average of the massless
cosine evolution. The massless cosine evolution is the derivative of the massless sine evolution.
Integration by parts moves the derivative to the Bessel weight.

## ii. Key results

- `cosineFourier` : the massless cosine evolution as a Fourier integral.
- `sineEvolution_mass_cos` : the massive sine evolution as a Bessel average of it.
- `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_zero` : the cosine evolution is the derivative of the sine evolution.
- `sineEvolution_mass_zero` : the massive sine evolution through the massless one.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Bessel average of the cosine evolution
- B. The derivative of the sine evolution
- C. Integration by parts

## iv. References

None.

## A. The Bessel average of the cosine evolution

- `cosineFourier` : the massless cosine evolution as a Fourier integral.
- `sineEvolution_mass_cos` : the massive sine evolution as a Bessel average of it.

## B. The derivative of the sine evolution

- `hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_zero` : the cosine evolution is the derivative of the sine evolution.

## C. Integration by parts

- `sineEvolution_mass_zero` : the massive sine evolution through the massless one.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cosineFourier
declarations.doc: The cosine evolution of the massless wave equation, as a Fourier integral.
declarations.statement: def cosineFourier (u : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) : ℂ

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_mass_cos
declarations.doc: **The massive sine evolution is a Bessel average of the massless cosine evolution.**
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_mass_cos {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (m : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r (m ^ 2) g x =
      ∫ u in (-r)..r, ((1 / 2 * Real.besselSq (m ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        cosineFourier u g x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_zero
declarations.doc: **The cosine evolution is the derivative of the sine evolution.**
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_sineEvolution_zero (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) (u₀ : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun u : ℝ => sineEvolution ℂ u 0 g x) (cosineFourier u₀ g x) u₀

declarations.name: KleinGordon.cosineFourier_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma cosineFourier_neg (u : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) :
    cosineFourier (-u) g x = cosineFourier u g x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.continuous_cosineFourier
declarations.statement: lemma continuous_cosineFourier (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) : Continuous fun u => cosineFourier u g x

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_mass_zero
declarations.doc:
**The massive sine evolution in terms of the massless one.** The massive sine evolution is the
massless one at the radius plus a Bessel average of the massless sine evolution over smaller
radii.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_mass_zero {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (m : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(E, ℂ)) (x : E) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r (m ^ 2) g x = sineEvolution ℂ r 0 g x +
      ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..r, ((2 * m ^ 2 * u * Real.besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        sineEvolution ℂ u 0 g x

modules.title: The retarded solution of the Klein–Gordon equation on the line
modules.doc:
The retarded Green function in one space dimension is `½ Θ(t - |x|) J₀(m √(t² - x²))`.

## i. Overview

A multiplier that is the cosine transform of an even continuous kernel on `[-r, r]` is the
convolution with that kernel. The Bessel identity says that the multiplier of the massive sine
evolution is the cosine transform of `½ J₀(m √(r² - u²))`. So the sine evolution on the line is the
average of the data against the Bessel kernel over `[x - r, x + r]`. The Duhamel integral then gives
the retarded solution as the integral of the source against the retarded Green function over the
backward light cone. For `m = 0` this is the d'Alembert formula.

## ii. Key results

- `sineEvolution_of_kernel` : a cosine-transform multiplier is a convolution.
- `sineEvolution_mass_line` : the sine evolution with mass on the line.
- `solution_mass_line` : the retarded solution with mass on the line.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Convolution kernels
- B. The Bessel kernel

## iv. References

None.

## A. Convolution kernels

- `sineEvolution_of_kernel` : a cosine-transform multiplier is a convolution.

## B. The Bessel kernel

- `sineEvolution_mass_line` : the sine evolution with mass on the line.
- `solution_mass_line` : the retarded solution with mass on the line.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_of_kernel
declarations.doc: **A multiplier that is a cosine transform is a convolution.**
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_of_kernel {μ r : ℝ} (hμ : 0 ≤ μ) (hr : 0 ≤ r) (w : ℝ → ℝ) (W : ℝ)
    (hw : Continuous w) (hwb : ∀ u, |w u| ≤ W) (hwe : ∀ u, w (-u) = w u)
    (hm : ∀ ξ : ℝ, multiplier r μ ξ =
      ((∫ u in (-r)..r, w u * Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * ξ * u) : ℝ) : ℂ))
    (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (x : ℝ) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r μ g x = ∫ u in (-r)..r, (w u : ℂ) * g (x + u)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_mass_line
declarations.doc:
**The massive sine evolution on the line.** The sine evolution of the mass `m` is the average
of the data against the Bessel kernel `½ J₀ (m √(r² - u²))` over the interval of radius `r`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_mass_line {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 ≤ r) (m : ℝ) (g : 𝓢(ℝ, ℂ)) (x : ℝ) :
    sineEvolution ℂ r (m ^ 2) g x =
      ∫ u in (-r)..r, ((1 / 2 * Real.besselSq (m ^ 2 * (r ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) * g (x + u)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_mass_line
declarations.doc:
**The retarded solution of the Klein–Gordon equation on the line.** The retarded solution at
`(t, x)` is the integral of the source against the retarded Green function
`½ Θ(t - s - |u|) J₀ (m √((t - s)² - u²))` over the backward light cone.
declarations.statement:
lemma solution_mass_line (m : ℝ) (ψ : TestFunction (⊤ : Opens (ℝ × ℝ)) ℂ ⊤) (t x : ℝ) :
    solution ℂ ψ (m ^ 2) t x = ∫ s in Set.Iic t, ∫ u in (-(t - s))..(t - s),
      ((1 / 2 * Real.besselSq (m ^ 2 * ((t - s) ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) * ψ (s, x + u)

modules.title: The retarded Green function with mass in three space dimensions
modules.doc:
The retarded Green function in three space dimensions is
`δ(t - r) / (4π r) - m J₁(m √(t² - r²)) / (4π √(t² - r²)) Θ(t - r)`.

## i. Overview

Dimension raising turns the one-dimensional Green function `½ Θ J₀(m √(t² - x²))` into the
three-dimensional one by `-(1 / (2π r)) ∂ᵣ`. The derivative of the step gives the shell
`δ(t - r) / (4π r)`. The derivative of `J₀` gives the tail with `J₁`.

## ii. Key results

- `sineEvolution_origin_radialSource` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution at
  the origin.
- `solution_origin_radialSource_space` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution on
  `Space 3`.
- `solution_origin_radialSource_besselJ1` : the same formula with `J₁`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The formula at the origin

## iv. References

None.

## A. The formula at the origin

- `sineEvolution_origin_radialSource` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution at
  the origin.
- `solution_origin_radialSource` : the formula for the retarded solution on Euclidean three-space.
- `solution_origin_radialSource_space` : the Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution on
  `Space 3`.
- `solution_origin_radialSource_besselJ1` : the same formula with `J₁`.

declarations.name: KleinGordon.sineEvolution_origin_radialSource
declarations.doc:
**The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the sine evolution at the origin.** For a radial source with
the profile `Φ` the massive sine evolution at the origin is
`τ Φ(τ) + 2 m² ∫₀^τ u² κ(m² (τ² - u²)) Φ(u) du`, where `κ = -J₁(z) / (2z)` at `y = z²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sineEvolution_origin_radialSource (m : ℝ) {τ : ℝ} (hτ : 0 ≤ τ)
    (P : 𝓓((⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (ℝ × ℝ)), ℂ)) (s : ℝ) :
    sineEvolution ℂ τ (m ^ 2) (slice ℂ (radialSource Eucl3 (liftProfile P)) s) 0 =
      (τ : ℂ) * liftProfile P (s, τ ^ 2) + ((2 * m ^ 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ∫ u in (0 : ℝ)..τ, ((u ^ 2 * Real.besselSqDeriv (m ^ 2 * (τ ^ 2 - u ^ 2)) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
          liftProfile P (s, u ^ 2)

declarations.name: KleinGordon.solution_origin_radialSource
declarations.doc:
**The Kirchhoff–Bessel formula for the retarded solution at the origin.** For a radial source
